7:16: God Almighty informs us that when He warned Iblis until the Day they are resurrected and Iblis was certain of that, he began to be stubborn and rebellious, so he said Then because You have led me astray, I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path meaning just as You have led me astray. Ibn Abbas said: Just as You have led me astray. Another said: Just as You have destroyed me, I will surely sit in wait for Your servants whom You create from the offspring of this one because of whom You have distanced me on Your straight path meaning the path of truth and the path of salvation, I will lead them astray from it so that they will not worship You or believe in You alone because of Your leading me astray. Some grammarians said: The ba' here is a divisive particle as if He is saying, Then because You have led me astray, I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path. Mujahid said: Your straight path means the truth. Muhammad ibn Suqah said on the authority of Awn ibn Abdullah: It means the path of Mecca. Ibn Jarir said: The correct view is that the straight path is more general than that. I said when Imam Ahmad narrated: Hashim ibn al-Qasim told us, Abu Uqayl told us, meaning Al-Thaqafi Abdullah bin Aqil, Musa bin Al-Musayyab told us, Salim bin Abi Al-Jaad told me, on the authority of Sabra bin Abi Al-Fakih, who said: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The devil lies in wait for the son of Adam in his paths, so he lies in wait for him on the path of Islam, and he says: Will you submit and abandon your religion and the religion of your fathers? He said: So he disobeyed him and submitted.” He said: “He lies in wait for him on the path of migration and he says: Will you migrate and abandon your land and your sky? The example of the migrant is like that of a horse in height, so he disobeyed him and migrated. Then he lies in wait for him on the path of jihad, which is jihad of the soul and wealth, and he says: You will fight and be killed, then you will marry the woman and divide the wealth. He said: So he disobeyed him and fought.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever among them does that and dies, it is a right upon God to admit him into Paradise. If he is killed, it is a right upon God to admit him into Paradise. If he drowns, it is a right upon God to admit him into Paradise, or if a beast falls on him, it is a right upon God to admit him into Paradise.” And His statement, Then I will come to them from before them and from behind them, the verse. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Then I will come to them from before them, making them doubt their Hereafter, and from behind them, making them desire their worldly life, and from their right, confusing their religious affairs, and from their left, making them desire sins. Ibn Abi Talhah said in the narration of Al-Awfi, both of them on the authority of Ibn Abbas: As for from before them, it is in front of their worldly life, and as for from behind them, it is in front of their Hereafter, and as for their right, it is in front of their good deeds, and as for their left, it is in front of their bad deeds. Saeed bin Abi Arubah said on the authority of Qatada, He came to them from before them and informed them that there is no resurrection, no Paradise, and no Hellfire, and from behind them. From the command of the world, He made it attractive to them and called them to it, and from their right, before their good deeds, He made them slow to do so, and from their left, He made evil deeds and transgressions attractive to them, and called them to them and commanded them to do them. He came to you, O son of Adam, from every direction, except that He did not come to you from above you. He was not able to stand between you and the mercy of God. And this is what was narrated from Ibrahim al-Nakha’i, al-Hakam ibn Utaybah, al-Suddi, and Ibn Jurayj, except that they said: Before them is the world, and behind them is the Hereafter. Mujahid said: From before them and from their right from where they see, and from behind them and from their left from where they do not see. Ibn Jarir chose: What is meant is all the paths of good and evil, so goodness turns them away from it and evil makes it good for them. Al-Hakam bin Abaan said on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, Then I will come to them from before them and from behind them and from their right and from their left, and he did not say from above them, because mercy descends from above them. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And You will not find most of them grateful, he said: monotheists. And this statement of Satan is only a conjecture and imagination from him, and it is in accordance with this reality, as God Almighty said: “And Satan proved true about them his conjecture, so they followed him, except for a party of the believers. * And he had no authority over them except that We might make evident who believes in the Hereafter from who is in doubt about it. And your Lord is Guardian over all things.” That is why it was mentioned in the hadith seeking refuge from the control of Satan over man from all sides, as Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said in his Musnad: Nasr bin Ali told us, Amr ibn Mujammi’ narrated to us, on the authority of Yunus ibn Khabab, on the authority of Ibn Jubayr ibn Mut’im, meaning Nafi’ ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and Umar ibn al-Khattab, meaning al-Sijistani, narrated to us, Ubayd God ibn Ja’far narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Amr narrated to us, on the authority of Zayd ibn Abi Anisa, on the authority of Yunus ibn Khabab, on the authority of Ibn Jubayr ibn Mut’im, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to supplicate, “O God, I ask You for forgiveness and well-being in my religion, my worldly life, my family, and my wealth. O God, cover my faults, protect me from fear, and preserve me from before me, behind me, to my right, to my left, and above me. And I seek refuge in You, O God, from being attacked from beneath me.” Al-Bazzar alone transmitted this hadith and deemed it hasan. Imam Ahmad said: Wakee’ told us, Ubadah bin Muslim Al-Fazari told us, Jarir bin Abi Sulayman bin Jubair bin Mut’im told me, I heard Abdullah bin Umar say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would not omit these supplications when he woke up and when he went to bed: “O God, I ask You for well-being in this world and the hereafter. O God, I ask You for forgiveness and well-being in my religion, my world, my family and my wealth. O God, cover my faults and keep me safe from fear. O God, protect me from before me and behind me, from my right and from my left and from above me, and I seek refuge in Your greatness from being attacked from beneath me.” Wakee’ said: From beneath me meaning the sinking of the earth. Abu Dawud, Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Hibban and Al-Hakim narrated it on the authority of Ubadah bin Muslim, and Al-Hakim said: Its chain of transmission is sound.
7:17: God Almighty informs us that when He warned Iblis until the Day they are resurrected and Iblis was certain of that, he began to be stubborn and rebellious, so he said Then because You have led me astray, I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path meaning just as You have led me astray. Ibn Abbas said: Just as You have led me astray. Another said: Just as You have destroyed me, I will surely sit in wait for Your servants whom You create from the offspring of this one because of whom You have distanced me on Your straight path meaning the path of truth and the path of salvation, I will lead them astray from it so that they will not worship You or believe in You alone because of Your leading me astray. Some grammarians said: The ba' here is a divisive particle as if He is saying, Then because You have led me astray, I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path. Mujahid said: Your straight path means the truth. Muhammad ibn Suqah said on the authority of Awn ibn Abdullah: It means the path of Mecca. Ibn Jarir said: The correct view is that the straight path is more general than that. I said when Imam Ahmad narrated: Hashim ibn al-Qasim told us, Abu Uqayl told us, meaning Al-Thaqafi Abdullah bin Aqil, Musa bin Al-Musayyab told us, Salim bin Abi Al-Jaad told me, on the authority of Sabra bin Abi Al-Fakih, who said: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The devil lies in wait for the son of Adam in his paths, so he lies in wait for him on the path of Islam, and he says: Will you submit and abandon your religion and the religion of your fathers? He said: So he disobeyed him and submitted.” He said: “He lies in wait for him on the path of migration and he says: Will you migrate and abandon your land and your sky? The example of the migrant is like that of a horse in height, so he disobeyed him and migrated. Then he lies in wait for him on the path of jihad, which is jihad of the soul and wealth, and he says: You will fight and be killed, then you will marry the woman and divide the wealth. He said: So he disobeyed him and fought.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever among them does that and dies, it is a right upon God to admit him into Paradise. If he is killed, it is a right upon God to admit him into Paradise. If he drowns, it is a right upon God to admit him into Paradise, or if a beast falls on him, it is a right upon God to admit him into Paradise.” And His statement, Then I will come to them from before them and from behind them, the verse. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Then I will come to them from before them, making them doubt their Hereafter, and from behind them, making them desire their worldly life, and from their right, confusing their religious affairs, and from their left, making them desire sins. Ibn Abi Talhah said in the narration of Al-Awfi, both of them on the authority of Ibn Abbas: As for from before them, it is in front of their worldly life, and as for from behind them, it is in front of their Hereafter, and as for their right, it is in front of their good deeds, and as for their left, it is in front of their bad deeds. Saeed bin Abi Arubah said on the authority of Qatada, He came to them from before them and informed them that there is no resurrection, no Paradise, and no Hellfire, and from behind them. From the command of the world, He made it attractive to them and called them to it, and from their right, before their good deeds, He made them slow to do so, and from their left, He made evil deeds and transgressions attractive to them, and called them to them and commanded them to do them. He came to you, O son of Adam, from every direction, except that He did not come to you from above you. He was not able to stand between you and the mercy of God. And this is what was narrated from Ibrahim al-Nakha’i, al-Hakam ibn Utaybah, al-Suddi, and Ibn Jurayj, except that they said: Before them is the world, and behind them is the Hereafter. Mujahid said: From before them and from their right from where they see, and from behind them and from their left from where they do not see. Ibn Jarir chose: What is meant is all the paths of good and evil, so goodness turns them away from it and evil makes it good for them. Al-Hakam bin Abaan said on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, Then I will come to them from before them and from behind them and from their right and from their left, and he did not say from above them, because mercy descends from above them. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And You will not find most of them grateful, he said: monotheists. And this statement of Satan is only a conjecture and imagination from him, and it is in accordance with this reality, as God Almighty said: “And Satan proved true about them his conjecture, so they followed him, except for a party of the believers. * And he had no authority over them except that We might make evident who believes in the Hereafter from who is in doubt about it. And your Lord is Guardian over all things.” That is why it was mentioned in the hadith seeking refuge from the control of Satan over man from all sides, as Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said in his Musnad: Nasr bin Ali told us, Amr ibn Mujammi’ narrated to us, on the authority of Yunus ibn Khabab, on the authority of Ibn Jubayr ibn Mut’im, meaning Nafi’ ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and Umar ibn al-Khattab, meaning al-Sijistani, narrated to us, Ubayd God ibn Ja’far narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Amr narrated to us, on the authority of Zayd ibn Abi Anisa, on the authority of Yunus ibn Khabab, on the authority of Ibn Jubayr ibn Mut’im, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to supplicate, “O God, I ask You for forgiveness and well-being in my religion, my worldly life, my family, and my wealth. O God, cover my faults, protect me from fear, and preserve me from before me, behind me, to my right, to my left, and above me. And I seek refuge in You, O God, from being attacked from beneath me.” Al-Bazzar alone transmitted this hadith and deemed it hasan. Imam Ahmad said: Wakee’ told us, Ubadah bin Muslim Al-Fazari told us, Jarir bin Abi Sulayman bin Jubair bin Mut’im told me, I heard Abdullah bin Umar say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would not omit these supplications when he woke up and when he went to bed: “O God, I ask You for well-being in this world and the hereafter. O God, I ask You for forgiveness and well-being in my religion, my world, my family and my wealth. O God, cover my faults and keep me safe from fear. O God, protect me from before me and behind me, from my right and from my left and from above me, and I seek refuge in Your greatness from being attacked from beneath me.” Wakee’ said: From beneath me meaning the sinking of the earth. Abu Dawud, Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Hibban and Al-Hakim narrated it on the authority of Ubadah bin Muslim, and Al-Hakim said: Its chain of transmission is sound.
7:18: God Almighty emphasized upon him the curse, expulsion, banishment and banishment from the place of the highest assembly, by saying: Get out of it, disgraced and banished. Ibn Jarir said: As for the disgraced, he is the one who is disgraced, and the blame is not stressed in the defect, it is said: he blamed him, he blames him, he is blamed, and they leave the hamza and say: I blame him, I blame him, blameworthy and blameworthy, and the blame and the blame are more expressive in the defect than the blame, he said: The banished and the excluded, is the banished and expelled, and Abd al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said: We do not know the disgraced and the blameworthy except one, and Sufyan al-Thawri said: On the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of al-Tamimi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Get out of it, disgraced and banished, he said: detested, and Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: small and detested, and al-Suddi said: detested and expelled, and Qatadah said: cursed and detested, and Mujahid said: banished and expelled, and al-Rabi’ said: Ibn Anas: The one who is censured and banished and the one who is defeated is the diminutive. And the Almighty’s saying: For whoever of them follows you, I will surely fill Hell with you all, is like His saying: “He said, ‘Go! And whoever of them follows you, indeed, Hell will be your recompense - an ample recompense. And incite whomever you can among them with your voice and assault them with your cavalry and infantry and share with them in wealth and children and promise them. But Satan promises them nothing but delusion. Indeed, over My servants you have no authority. And sufficient is your Lord as Disposer of affairs.’”
7:19: The Almighty mentions that He permitted Adam, peace be upon him, and his wife Eve to eat from all of the fruits of Paradise except for one tree. We have already discussed this in Surat Al-Baqarah. At that time, Satan envied them and sought to deceive, whisper, and trick them in order to take away from them the blessings and beautiful clothing they were in. And he said, falsely and slanderously, Your Lord did not forbid you from this tree except that you should become angels, meaning so that you would not become angels or immortal here. If you had eaten from it, you would have achieved that, like His statement, He said, ‘O Adam, shall I guide you to the tree of immortality and possession that will not decay?’ meaning so that you would not be angels, like His statement, God makes clear to you, lest you go astray, meaning so that you would not go astray. And He has cast into the earth firm mountains, lest it should shift with you, meaning so that it would not shift with you. Ibn Abbas and Yahya ibn Abi Katheer used to read except that you should become angels with a kasra on the lam, and the majority read it. By opening it, and he swore to them meaning he swore to them by God that I am to you both among the sincere advisers for I am here before you and I know this place, and this is from the chapter of reciprocity, and what is meant is one of the two parties, as Khalid bin Zuhair, the cousin of Abu Dhu’ayb, said: And share with them, by God, the effort, for you are sweeter than quails when We resurrect them. That is, he swore to them by God on that until he deceived them. And the believer may be deceived by God. Qatada said about the verse: He swore by God that I was created before you and I am more knowledgeable than you, so follow me and I will guide you. And some of the people of knowledge used to say that whoever deceives us by God, we will be deceived by him.

7:22: Saeed bin Abi Arubah said on the authority of Qatada on the authority of Al-Hasan on the authority of Abi bin Kaab, may God be pleased with him, who said: Adam was a tall man like a palm tree with a lot of hair on his head. When he committed the sin he committed, his private parts became apparent to him but he could not see them. He ran away in Paradise and a tree from the trees of Paradise caught hold of his head. He said to it: Let me go. It said: I will not let you go. Then his Lord, the Almighty, called out to him: O Adam, do you want to flee from me? He said: O Lord, I felt shy before You. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through various chains of transmission on the authority of Al-Hasan on the authority of Abi bin Kaab on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet is more authentic. Abdul Razzaq said: On the authority of Sufyan bin Uyaynah and Ibn al-Mubarak, on the authority of al-Hasan bin Amara, on the authority of al-Munhal bin Amr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The tree that God forbade Adam and his wife from was the ear of corn. When they ate from it, their private parts became apparent to them, and what had hidden their private parts were their fingernails. They began to fasten together over themselves from the leaves of Paradise, the leaves of figs, sticking them together. Then Adam, peace be upon him, set out in Paradise, and a tree from Paradise hung over his head. God called out to him: O Adam, are you fleeing from me? He said: No, but I was ashamed of You, O Lord. He said: Did you not have in what I granted you of Paradise and permitted you from it an alternative to what I forbade you? He said: Yes, O Lord, but by Your glory, I did not think that anyone would swear by You falsely. He said: And this is the saying of God Almighty: And he swore to them, ‘Indeed, I am to you both of you,’ He said: By My glory, I will send you down to the earth, and you will not attain life except with difficulty. He said: So he was sent down from Paradise, and they were eating from it in abundance, then he was sent down to something other than abundance of food and drink. So he learned the craft of iron and was ordered to plough, so he ploughed and planted, then watered until he harvested, then he trampled it, then winnowed it, then ground it, then kneaded it, then baked it, then ate it. But he did not reach it until he reached what God wanted him to reach. Al-Thawri said: On the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Al-Munhal bin Amr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And they began to fasten together, over themselves, from the leaves of Paradise. He said: Fig leaves. It is authentically attributed to him. Mujahid said: They began to sew together leaves from Paradise, he said: Like a garment. Wahb ibn Munabbih said regarding His statement: Their clothing would be stripped from them, he said: The clothing of Adam and Eve was a light on their private parts, so that this one could see the private parts of this one and that one the private parts of this one. Then when they ate from the tree, their private parts became apparent to them. Ibn Jarir narrated it with a sound chain of transmission going back to him. Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar told us on the authority of Qatadah, he said: Adam said: O Lord, have you seen if you repent and seek forgiveness? He said: Then I will admit you to Paradise. As for Iblis, he did not ask him for repentance and asked him for a reprieve, so he gave each of them what he asked for. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Ibad ibn al-Awwam told us, on the authority of Sufyan ibn al-Husayn, on the authority of Ya`la ibn Muslim, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: When Adam ate from the tree, he was asked: Why did you eat from the tree that I forbade you from? He said: Eve commanded me. He said: Then I have followed her so that she will not become pregnant except with reluctance and will not give birth except with reluctance. He said: Eve was afraid at that, and it was said to her: May you and your children be cursed. Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim said regarding his statement: Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers, these are the words that Adam received from his Lord.

7:24: It was said that what is meant by the address in descend is Adam, Eve, Satan, and the serpent. Some of them did not mention the serpent, and God knows best. The mainstay of the enmity is Adam and Satan, and for this reason God Almighty said in Surat Taha, Descend from it, all of you the verse, and Eve is subordinate to Adam, and the serpent, if its mention is correct, is subordinate to Satan. The commentators have mentioned the places where each of them descended, and the result of those reports goes back to the Israelite stories, and God knows best about their authenticity. If there was any benefit in specifying those places that would return to those charged with the matter of their religion or their worldly life, God Almighty would have mentioned them in His Book or His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. His saying, And for you on the earth is a place of settlement and provision for a time means a settlement and ages set for known terms, which the pen has written and fate has counted and written in the first book. Ibn Abbas said, The place of settlement is the graves, and from him he said, The place of settlement is above the earth and below it, both of them were narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. His saying, He said, in it you will live And in it you die and from it you will be brought forth.” As God Almighty says: From it We created you, and into it We will return you, and from it We will bring you forth another time. God Almighty informs us that He made the earth a home for the children of Adam for the duration of worldly life. In it is their life, in it is their death and their graves, and from it is their resurrection on the Day of Resurrection, on which God will gather the first and the last and reward each according to his deeds.

7:26: God Almighty bestows His blessings upon His servants by giving them clothing and feathers. Clothing is the covering of private parts, which are the bad things, and feathers and feathers are what one adorns oneself with outwardly. The first is from the necessities and feathers are from the completions and additions. Ibn Jarir said: In the speech of the Arabs, feathers are furniture and what is apparent from the clothes. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and Al-Bukhari narrated it on his authority: feathers are money, and this is what Mujahid, Urwah bin Al-Zubayr, Al-Suddi, Al-Dahhak and others said. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: feathers are clothing, living and comfort. Abd Al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said: feathers are beauty. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid bin Harun told us, Asba’ told us on the authority of Abu Al-Ala Al-Shami, who said: Abu Umamah put on a new garment, and when it reached his collarbone, he said: Praise be to God who clothed me with what I cover my private parts with and adorn myself with in my life. Then he said: I heard Omar bin Al-Khattab say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever gets a new garment and wears it, then he says when it reaches His collarbone: Praise be to God who clothed me with what I can cover my nakedness with and beautify myself with in my life. Then he took the old garment and gave it in charity, and he was in God’s protection and in God’s care, alive and dead.” Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah on the authority of Yazid bin Harun on the authority of Asba’, who is Ibn Zayd Al-Juhani. Yahya bin Ma’in and others authenticated him, and his sheikh Abu Al-Ala Al-Shami is not known except for this hadith, but no one narrated it, and God knows best. Imam Ahmad also said: Muhammad bin Ubaid told us, Mukhtar bin Nafi’ al-Tammar told us, on the authority of Abu Matar, that he saw Ali, may God be pleased with him, come to a young boy and buy a shirt from him for three dirhams and wear it from the wrists to the ankles, saying when he put it on: Praise be to God who has provided me with feathers with which I can adorn myself before people and cover my nakedness. It was said: This is something you narrate from yourself or from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: This is something I heard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he was given clothing: Praise be to God who has provided me with feathers with which I can adorn myself before people and cover my nakedness. Imam Ahmad narrated it. God the Almighty said: And the clothing of righteousness - that is best. Some of them read the clothing of righteousness in the accusative case, while others read it in the nominative case as the subject, and that is best is its predicate. The commentators differed about its meaning. Ikrimah said: It is said that it is what the righteous will wear on the Day of Resurrection. It was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Zaid bin Ali, al-Suddi and Qatadah said: Ibn Jurayj said: The garment of piety is faith. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Righteous deeds. Al-Diyal bin Amr said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It is the good appearance on the face. Urwah bin Al-Zubayr said: The garment of piety is fear of God. Abd Al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said: The garment of piety is to fear God and cover one’s private parts, so that is the garment of piety. They are all close together. This is supported by the hadith narrated by Ibn Jarir where he said: Al-Muthanna told me, Ishaq bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Ishaq bin Ismail told me on the authority of Sulayman bin Arqam on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: I saw Uthman bin Affan, may God be pleased with him, on the pulpit of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wearing a shirt with its buttons unbuttoned. I heard him order the killing of dogs and forbid playing with pigeons. Then he said: O people, fear God in these secrets, for I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “By the One in Whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, no one conceals a secret except that God dresses him in its garment publicly. If it is good, then good, and if it is evil, then evil.” Then he recited this verse: And feathers. And the clothing of piety is the best of those are the signs of God.” He said: The good appearance. This is how Ibn Jarir narrated it from the narration of Sulayman ibn Arqam, and it is weak. The imams al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, and al-Bukhari narrated in the Book of Etiquette from authentic chains of transmission on the authority of al-Hasan al-Basri that he heard the Commander of the Faithful, Uthman ibn Affan, order the killing of dogs and the slaughtering of pigeons on Friday from the pulpit. As for the hadith that was attributed to the Prophet, al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani narrated in his great dictionary a corroborating hadith from another chain of transmission where he said: He told us.
7:27: God Almighty warns the children of Adam against Satan and his tribe, explaining to them his ancient enmity towards the father of mankind, Adam, peace be upon him, in his efforts to expel him from Paradise, which is the abode of bliss, to the abode of toil and suffering, and causing his nakedness to be exposed after it had been covered from him. This is nothing but a definite enmity, and this is like the Almighty’s saying: Then will you take him and his descendants as allies instead of Me while they are enemies to you? An evil exchange for the wrongdoers.
7:28: Mujahid said: The polytheists used to circumambulate the House naked, saying, We circumambulate as our mothers bore us. Then the woman would place a leaf or something on her vagina and say: Today some or all of it appears, and whatever appears of it I do not permit. Then God revealed: “And when they commit an immorality, they say, ‘We found our fathers doing it, and God has commanded us to do it. ’” The Quraish I said: The Arabs, except for the Quraysh, did not circumambulate the House in the clothes they wore, interpreting that as meaning that they did not circumambulate in clothes in which they disobeyed God. The Quraysh, who were the Hams, used to circumambulate in their clothes. Whoever was lent a garment by an Hamsidi, circumambulated in it. Whoever had a new garment, circumambulated in it and then threw it away, and no one owned it. Whoever did not find a new garment, nor was lent a garment by an Hamsidi, circumambulated naked. Sometimes a woman would circumambulate naked, and she would put something over her private parts to cover it somewhat, and she would say: Today some or all of it appears, and whatever appears of it I do not permit. Most of what women used to do was circumambulate naked at night, and this was something they had invented on their own and followed their fathers in it, and they believed that the actions of their fathers were based on a command from God and a law, so God Almighty denounced them for that, and said: “And when they commit an immorality, they say: We found our fathers doing it, and God has commanded us to do it.” So God Almighty said in response to them: Say, meaning O Muhammad, to the one who claimed that, Indeed, God does not command immorality, meaning that what you are doing is an abhorrent immorality, and God does not command such a thing. Do you say about God that which you do not know? meaning do you attribute to God statements that you do not know to be true? And God Almighty said: “Say: My Lord has commanded justice,” meaning justice and righteousness, And set your faces at every mosque and call upon Him, sincere to Him in religion, meaning He has commanded you to be steadfast in worshipping Him in its proper places, which is following the messengers who were supported by miracles, in what they reported about God and what they brought of laws, and to be sincere to Him in worshipping Him, for God Almighty does not accept a deed until it combines these two pillars, that it be Correct, in accordance with Sharia, and free from polytheism. And the Almighty’s saying: As He began you, you will return to His saying misguidance. There is a difference of opinion regarding the meaning of His saying: As He began you, you will return. Ibn Abi Nujayh said: On the authority of Mujahid: As He began you, you will return means He will revive you after your death. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: As He began you in this world, so will you return on the Day of Resurrection alive. Qatada said: As He began you, you will return means: He began and created them and they were nothing, then they went away, then He will return them. Abd Al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said: As He began you first, so will He return you last. Abu Ja`far bin Jarir chose this statement, and he supported it with what he narrated from the hadith of Sufyan Al-Thawri and Shu`bah bin Al-Hajjaj, both of them on the authority of Al-Mughirah bin Al-Nu`man on the authority of Sa`id bin Jubayr on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up among us to give a sermon and said: “O people, you will be gathered before God barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised. As We began the first creation, We will return it. It is a promise binding upon Us. Indeed, We will do it.” This hadith is narrated in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Shu`bah, and in Sahih Al-Bukhari also from the hadith of Al-Thawri. And Warqa’ bin Iyas Abu Yazid said on the authority of Mujahid, As He began you, you will return, meaning He will send the Muslim as a Muslim and the disbeliever as a disbeliever. Abu Al-Aaliyah said, As He began you, you will return, they will be returned to His knowledge of them. Sa’id bin Jubayr said, As He began you, you will return, as He decreed for you to be, and in another narration, As you were upon, you will be. Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi said: In His Almighty’s saying, As He began you, you will return, whoever God began his creation upon misery will become as He began his creation upon, even if he does the deeds of the people of happiness. And whoever began his creation upon happiness will become as He began his creation upon, even if he does the deeds of the people of misery, just as the magicians did the deeds of the people of misery and then became as they began. Al-Suddi said, As He began you, you will return * A group He guided and a group upon whom error was decreed, meaning, As He began you, you will return, just as We created you as a group guided and a group astray, thus you return and emerge from the wombs of your mothers. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: His statement, As He began you, you will return * A party He has guided and a party upon whom error is due. He said: God Almighty began the creation of the son of Adam as believers and disbelievers, as He said, It is He who created you, and among you is a disbeliever and among you is a believer. Then He will return them on the Day of Resurrection as He began them, as believers and disbelievers. I said: This statement is supported by the hadith of Ibn Masoud in Sahih al-Bukhari: “By the One besides whom there is no god, one of you may do the deeds of the people of Paradise until there is only a cubit or an arm’s length between him and it, then the Book overtakes him and he does the deeds of the people of Hell and enters it. And one of you may do the deeds of the people of Hell until there is only a cubit or an arm’s length between him and it, then the Book overtakes him and he does the deeds of the people of Paradise and enters Paradise.” Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi said: Ali ibn al-Ja`d told us, Abu Ghassan told us, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Sahl ibn Sa`d, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “A servant may do, in what people see, the deeds of the people of Paradise, but he is one of the people of Hellfire. And he may do, in what people see, the deeds of the people of Hellfire, but he is one of the people of Paradise.” This is part of a hadith of al-Bukhari from the hadith of Abu Ghassan Muhammad ibn Mutraf al-Madani in the story of the two dwarves on the day of Uhud. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashar told me, Abd al-Rahman told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-A`mash, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Every soul will be resurrected in the state in which it was. This hadith was narrated by Muslim and Ibn Majah from other sources, on the authority of al-A`mash, with the same wording: Every servant will be resurrected in the state in which he died. And from Ibn Abbas, similarly. I said: It is supported by the hadith of Ibn Mas`ud. I said: It is necessary to reconcile this statement, if it is what is meant by the verse, with the words of God, the Most High: “So direct your face toward the religion, inclining toward truth. [Adhere to] the nature of God upon which He has created mankind.” And what came in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Every child is born in a state of fitrah, but his parents make him a Jew, a Christian, or a Zoroastrian. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Iyad ibn Himar, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God the Most High says: I created My servants as monotheists, but the devils came to them and led them astray from their religion. The hadith. The reason for the combination in this is that God the Most High created them so that some of them would be believers and some would be disbelievers in the second instance, even though He created all of creation with the knowledge and oneness of Him and the knowledge that there is no god but Him, as He took a covenant from them to do so and made it in their instincts and nature. Despite this, He decreed that some of them would be wretched and some would be happy. It is He who created you, and among you are disbelievers and among you are believers. And in the hadith: All people go forth in the morning, selling their souls, either freeing them or ruining them. And God’s decree is effective in His creation, for He is the One who decreed and guided and the One who gave everything its nature and then guided. And in the two Sahihs: “As for those among you who are among the people of happiness, He will make it easy for them to do the work of the people of happiness, and as for those among the people of misery, He will make it easy for them to do the work of the people of misery.” For this reason, God the Most High said: A group He has guided and a group upon whom error is due. Then He explained that by saying: They have taken the devils as allies instead of God verse. Ibn Jarir said: This is one of the clearest indications of the error of those who claim that God does not punish anyone for a sin he has committed or a misguidance he believes in, unless he commits it after knowing that it is correct and commits it out of stubbornness towards his Lord in it, because if that were the case, there would be no difference between the group of misguidance who went astray while thinking that they were guided, and the group of guidance, and God Almighty has distinguished between their names and their rulings in this verse.

And in the two Sahihs: “As for those among you who are among the people of happiness, He will make it easy for them to do the work of the people of happiness, and as for those among the people of misery, He will make it easy for them to do the work of the people of misery.” For this reason, God the Most High said: A group He has guided and a group upon whom error is due. Then He explained that by saying: They have taken the devils as allies instead of God verse. Ibn Jarir said: This is one of the clearest indications of the error of those who claim that God does not punish anyone for a sin he has committed or a misguidance he believes in, unless he commits it after knowing that it is correct and commits it out of stubbornness towards his Lord in it, because if that were the case, there would be no difference between the group of misguidance who went astray while thinking that they were guided, and the group of guidance, and God Almighty has distinguished between their names and their rulings in this verse.
7:31: This noble verse is a response to the polytheists regarding what they used to do, which was to circumambulate the House naked, as narrated by Muslim, Al-Nasa’i, and Ibn Jarir, and the wording is his from the hadith of Shu’bah on the authority of Salamah bin Kuhayl on the authority of Muslim Al-Batin on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He said: They used to circumambulate the House naked, men and women, the men during the day and the women at night, and the woman would say: Today some or all of it appears, and whatever appears of it I do not permit. God the Almighty said: Take your adornment at every mosque. Al-Awfi said: On the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: Take your adornment at every mosque, the verse, he said: There were men who would circumambulate the House naked, so God commanded them to adorn themselves. Adornment is clothing, which is what covers the private parts and other than that of good clothes and goods, so they were commanded to take their adornment at every mosque. This is what Mujahid, Ata’, Ibrahim al-Nakha’i, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, Qatadah, al-Suddi, al-Dahhak, and Malik said, on the authority of al-Zuhri and more than one of the imams of the Salaf, in their interpretation of it, that it was revealed about the polytheists circumambulating the House naked. Al-Hafiz ibn Mardawayh narrated from the hadith of Sa’id ibn Bashir and al-Awza’i, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Anas, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, that it was revealed about prayer in sandals, but its authenticity is questionable, and God knows best. For this verse and what has been reported in its meaning from the Sunnah, it is recommended to beautify oneself at prayer, especially on Friday and the day of Eid, and to use perfume because it is an adornment and to use the siwak because it is part of that. And the best clothing is white, as Imam Ahmad said: Ali bin Asim told us, Abdullah bin Othman bin Khathim told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, and he authenticated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Wear white clothing, for it is the best of your clothing, and shroud your dead in it. The best of your kohl is antimony, for it clears the vision and makes the hair grow.” This is a hadith with a good chain of transmission, and its men meet the conditions of Muslim. It was narrated by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and Ibn Majah on the authority of Abdullah bin Othman bin Khathim, and al-Tirmidhi said: It is good and authentic. Imam Ahmad also narrated it, and the people of the Sunnah, with a good chain of transmission, on the authority of Samurah bin Jundub, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Wear white clothing, for it is the purest and best, and shroud your dead in it. Al-Tabarani narrated with a sound chain of transmission on the authority of Qatadah on the authority of Muhammad bin Sirin: That Tamim al-Dari bought a cloak for a thousand and used to pray in it. And the words of God, the Most High, and eat and drink verse, some of the predecessors said that God gathered all medicine in half. Verse: And eat and drink, but be not excessive. Al-Bukhari said: Ibn Abbas said: Eat whatever you wish and wear whatever you wish, as long as two things escape you: extravagance and conceit. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: God has permitted eating and drinking as long as it is not extravagance or conceit. Its chain of transmission is sound. Imam Ahmad said: Buhaiz told us, Hammam told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Amr ibn Shu’ayb, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Eat, drink, dress, and give charity without conceit or extravagance, for God loves to see His favor upon His servant. Al-Nasa’i and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Qatadah, on the authority of Amr ibn Shu’ayb, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Eat, give charity, and dress without extravagance or conceit. Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Mughira told us, Sulayman ibn Salim al-Kalbi told us, Yahya ibn Jabir al-Ta’i told us, I heard Al-Muqaddam bin Ma’dikarib Al-Kindi said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “The son of Adam has not filled a vessel worse than his stomach. It is sufficient for the son of Adam to have a few mouthfuls to keep him going. If he must do so, then a third for his food, a third for his drink, and a third for his breath.” Al-Nasa’i and Al-Tirmidhi narrated it through various chains of transmission on the authority of Yahya bin Jabir, and Al-Tirmidhi said: It is good, and in one copy it is good and authentic. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la al-Mawsili said in his Musnad: Suwaid bin Abdul Aziz told us, Baqiyah told us, on the authority of Yusuf bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of Nuh bin Dhakwan, on the authority of al-Hasan, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is extravagance to eat whatever you desire. Ad-Daraqutni narrated it in al-Afrad, and he said: This is a strange hadith that was narrated only by Baqiyah. As-Suddi said: Those who circumambulated the House naked were forbidden to eat fat as long as they stayed during the season, so God Almighty said to them: Eat and drink the verse, meaning do not be extravagant in forbidding. Mujahid said: He ordered them to eat and drink from what God had provided for them. Abd al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said: And do not be extravagant means: do not eat what is forbidden, that is extravagance. Ata’ al-Khurasani said: Ibn Abbas said: His statement: “And eat and drink, but be not extravagant. Indeed, He does not like those who are extravagant” in food and drink. Ibn Jarir said: His statement: Indeed, He does not like those who are extravagant means God Almighty says: Indeed, God does not like those who transgress His limits. In what is permissible or forbidden, the extremists are in what is permissible by making permissible what is forbidden or by making permissible what is forbidden, but he loves to make permissible what is permissible and forbid what is forbidden, and that is the justice that he commanded.
7:33: Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu'awiyah told us, Al-A'mash told us, on the authority of Shaqiq, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "No one is more jealous than God, and for this reason He has forbidden indecencies, both apparent and hidden. No one loves praise more than God." They both included it in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Sulayman ibn Mihran Al-A'mash, on the authority of Shaqiq, on the authority of Abu Wa'il, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud. The discussion of what is related to indecencies, both apparent and hidden, was presented in Surat Al-An'am and His statement: And sin and oppression without right. Al-Suddi said: As for sin, it is disobedience, and oppression is to oppress people without right. Mujahid said: Sin is all transgressions, and he informed us that the oppressor oppresses himself. The gist of what sin is interpreted as is that it is the sins related to the doer himself, and oppression is transgression against people, so God has forbidden this and that. And His statement, the Most High: And that you associate with God that for which He has not sent down authority, meaning that you make partners for Him in His worship, And that you say about God that which you do not know. From the slander and lies of claiming that he has a son and the like of what you have no knowledge of, such as his saying, So avoid the uncleanness of idols (verse).
7:34: God Almighty says: And for every nation meaning a century and generation “is a term. So when their term comes” meaning their appointed time they will not remain behind an hour, nor will they precede it. Then God Almighty warned the children of Adam that He would send to them messengers who would recite to them His verses and give them good tidings and caution, saying: So whoever fears God and reforms meaning abandons forbidden things and performs acts of obedience “there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve. * But those who deny Our verses and are arrogant toward them” meaning their hearts deny them and are arrogant about acting upon them they are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally meaning they will remain therein forever.
7:35: God Almighty says: And for every nation meaning a century and generation “is a term. So when their term comes” meaning their appointed time they will not remain behind an hour, nor will they precede it. Then God Almighty warned the children of Adam that He would send to them messengers who would recite to them His verses and give them good tidings and caution, saying: So whoever fears God and reforms meaning abandons forbidden things and performs acts of obedience “there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve. * But those who deny Our verses and are arrogant toward them” meaning their hearts deny them and are arrogant about acting upon them they are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally meaning they will remain therein forever.
7:36: God Almighty says: And for every nation meaning a century and generation “is a term. So when their term comes” meaning their appointed time they will not remain behind an hour, nor will they precede it. Then God Almighty warned the children of Adam that He would send to them messengers who would recite to them His verses and give them good tidings and caution, saying: So whoever fears God and reforms meaning abandons forbidden things and performs acts of obedience “there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve. * But those who deny Our verses and are arrogant toward them” meaning their hearts deny them and are arrogant about acting upon them they are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally meaning they will remain therein forever.
7:37: He says, So who is more unjust than he who invents a lie against God or denies His revelations? That is, no one is more unjust than he who invents a lie against God or denies His revealed revelations. Those will receive their share of the Book. The commentators differed about its meaning. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: What was written for them will be written for those who lied about God will be blackened. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, saying: Their share of deeds is that whoever does good will be rewarded for it, and whoever does evil will be rewarded for it. Mujahid said: What they were promised of good and evil. Qatada, Ad-Dahhak, and more than one said the same. Ibn Jarir chose this. Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said, Those will receive their share of the Book. He said, His work, provision, and lifespan. This is also what al-Rabi' ibn Anas and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said. This statement is strong in meaning, and the context indicates it, which is His statement, Until, when Our messengers come to them, they take their souls. Similar in meaning in this verse is His statement, "Indeed, those who invent falsehood against God will not succeed. Enjoyment in this world, then to Us is their return. Then We will make them taste the severe punishment for what they used to disbelieve." And His statement, "And whoever disbelieves, let not his disbelief grieve you. To Us is their return, and We will inform them of what they did. Indeed, God is Knowing of that within the breasts. We will give them enjoyment for a little." And His statement, Until, when Our messengers come to them, they take their souls. The Almighty informs us that when the angels take the souls of the polytheists, they frighten them at death and take their souls to the Fire, saying to them, Where are those with whom you used to associate partners in this worldly life, and whom you used to call upon and worship instead of God? Call upon them to save you from what you are in. They say, They have gone astray. About us means they left us, so we do not hope for their benefit or good. And they testified against themselves means they acknowledged and confessed against themselves that they were disbelievers.
7:38: The Almighty says, informing about what He says to these polytheists, those who slander Him and deny His signs, Enter among nations that is, of your likes and characteristics, that have passed on before you that is, of the previous disbelieving nations, of jinn and mankind in the Fire may be a substitute for His saying among nations, and it may be that it is among nations, that is, with nations. And His saying, Whenever a nation enters, it curses its sister as Abraham, peace be upon him, said, Then on the Day of Resurrection, some of you will disbelieve in others the verse, and His saying, the Almighty: “When those who followed disown those who followed, and they see the punishment, and all ties are severed from them. And those who followed say, ‘If only we had another chance, we could disown them as they disowned us.’ Thus will God show them their deeds as regrets for them, and they will not emerge from the Fire.” And His saying, Until they are all overtaken therein that is, they are all gathered therein, The last of them will say to the first of them that is, the last of them to enter, and they are The followers are for their first ones, and they are the ones who are followed, because they are more sinful than their followers, so they entered before them, and the followers will complain about them to God on the Day of Resurrection because they are the ones who led them astray from the straight path, and they will say, Our Lord, these led us astray, so give them a double punishment in the Fire, meaning, make the punishment double for them, as God Almighty said: “On the Day when their faces will be turned over in the Fire, they will say, ‘Oh, if only we had obeyed God and obeyed the Messenger.’ And they will say, ‘Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our masters and our dignitaries, and they led us astray from the way. Our Lord, give them double the punishment,’” the verse. And His statement, He said, ‘For each double,’ means that We did that and punished each according to his condition, like His statement, Those who disbelieved and averted [people] from the way of God - We will increase for them the punishment,’ the verse. And His saying, And they will bear their own burdens and other burdens besides their own burdens, and His saying, And of the burdens of those whom they misguide without knowledge, the verse, And the first of them will say to the last of them, meaning the ones who are followed will say to the ones who follow, So you had no advantage over us, Al-Suddi said: You have gone astray as we have gone astray, So taste the punishment for what you used to earn, and this state is as God Almighty has informed us about them in the state of their gathering in His saying, “And if you could but see when the wrongdoers are made to stand before their Lord, returning their words to one another. Those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant, “Had it not been for you, we would have been believers.” Those who were arrogant will say to those who were oppressed, Did we avert you from guidance after it had come to you? Rather, you were criminals. And those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant, Rather, it was [your] plotting by night and by day when you ordered us to disbelieve in God and attribute to Him equals. And they will conceal their regret when they see the punishment, and We will place shackles on the necks of those who disbelieve. Are they recompensed except for what they used to do?” "
