And they will conceal their regret when they see the punishment, and We will place shackles on the necks of those who disbelieve. Are they recompensed except for what they used to do?” "
7:40: His saying, The gates of heaven will not be opened for them. It was said that what is meant is that no good deed or supplication will be raised for them from it. This was said by Mujahid and Saeed bin Jubair, and it was narrated by Al-Awfi and Ali bin Abi Talhah from Ibn Abbas, and it was also narrated by Al-Thawri from Laith from Ata’ from Ibn Abbas. It was also said that what is meant is that the gates of heaven will not be opened for their souls. This was narrated by Ad-Dahhak from Ibn Abbas, and it was said by As-Suddi and others, and it is supported by what Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Abu Bakr bin Ayyash told us from Al-A’mash from Al-Munhal, who is Ibn Amr, from Zadhan from Al-Bara’ that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned the taking of the soul of the wicked, and that it ascends with it to heaven and they ascend with it, and it does not pass by a group of angels except that they say, What is this evil soul? They say, So-and-so, using the worst names he was called by in this world, until they reach the heavens and ask for its gates to be opened for him, but they do not open them for him. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited, The gates of heaven will not be opened for them, the verse. This is how he narrated it, and it is part of a long hadith narrated by Abu Dawud, al-Nasa’i, and Ibn Majah through various chains of transmission on the authority of al-Munhal ibn Amr. Imam Ahmad narrated it in full, saying: Abu Muawiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Al-Munhal bin Amr, on the authority of Zadhan, on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib, who said: We went out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the funeral of a man from the Ansar, and we reached the grave and it had not yet been dug. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sat down and we sat around him as if there were birds on our heads, and in his hand was a stick with which he was poking the ground. He raised his head and said: Seek refuge with God from the punishment of the grave - two or three times. Then he said: When the believing servant is cut off from this world and turning to the Hereafter, angels descend to him from the heavens with white faces as if their faces were the sun, with them a shroud from the shrouds of Paradise and embalming from the embalming of Paradise until they sit near him as far as the eye can see. Then the Angel of Death comes and sits at his head and says: O good soul, come out to forgiveness from God and His pleasure - he said: So it comes out flowing as a drop flows from the mouth of a waterskin, and he takes it, and when he takes it, he does not leave it in his hand for the blink of an eye until they take it and put it in that shroud and in That is the embalming and from it comes out the most fragrant scent of musk found on the face of the earth. They ascend with it and they do not pass by a group of angels except that they say, What is this fragrant soul? They say, So-and-so, son of so-and-so, using the best of the names by which they used to call him in the world, until they reach the lowest heaven. They ask permission for him, and it is opened for him. Then those closest to him accompany him from each heaven to the heaven next to it, until he reaches the seventh heaven. Then God, the Almighty, the Majestic, says, Write the book of My servant in ‘Illiyeen and return him to the earth, for from it I created them, and into it I will return them, and from it I will extract them another time. He said: Then his soul is restored and two angels come to him and make him sit and say to him: Who is your Lord? He says: My Lord is God. They say to him: What is your religion? He says: My religion is Islam. They say to him: Who is this man who was sent among you? He says: He is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. They say to him: What is your work? He says: I read the Book of God and believed in it and believed. Then a voice calls from the heaven: My servant has spoken the truth, so furnish him from Paradise and clothe him from Paradise and open for him a door to Paradise. Its fragrance and goodness come to him, and his grave is expanded for him as far as the eye can see. He said: Then a man with a handsome face, handsome clothes and a pleasant scent comes to him and says: Receive good tidings of that which will please you. This is the day which you were promised. He says to him: Who are you, for your face is a face that brings good? He says: I am your righteous work. He says: O Lord, bring about the Hour. O Lord, bring about the Hour so that I may return to my family and my wealth. He said: And when the disbelieving servant is in a state of separation from this world and turning to the Hereafter, angels with black faces descend to him from the heavens, carrying sackcloth, and they sit near him as far as the eye can see. Then the Angel of Death comes and sits at his head and says: O wicked soul, come out to the wrath and anger of God. He said: So it spreads through his body and pulls it out as a skewer is pulled out of wet wool, and he takes it. When he takes it, he does not leave it in his hand for the blink of an eye until they put it in that sackcloth, and it comes out of it like the most foul odor of a corpse found on the face of the earth. They ascend with it and they do not pass by a group of angels except that they say: What is this wicked soul? They say: So-and-so, son of so-and-so, using the ugliest names he was called by in this world, until he reaches the lowest heaven and asks for permission, but it is not opened for him. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: The gates of heaven will not be opened for them, nor will they enter Paradise until a camel passes through the eye of a needle. Then God, the Almighty, says: Write his record in a prison in the lowest earth. Then his soul is thrown out. Then he recited: And whoever associates with God a partner, God will not be granted permission. By God, it is as if he had fallen from the sky and been snatched by birds or blown away by the wind to a far off place. Then his soul is returned to his body and two angels come to him and make him sit up and say to him, Who is your Lord? He says, Huh, huh? I do not know. They say, What is your religion? He says, Huh, huh? I do not know. They say, Who is this man who was sent among you? He says, Huh, huh? I do not know. Then a voice calls from the sky, My servant has lied, so spread out for him a bed from the Fire and open for him a door to the Fire. Then some of its heat and its poisonous winds come to him and his grave becomes narrow for him until his ribs overlap. Then a man comes to him with an ugly face, ugly clothes, and a foul odor and says, “Give me good tidings of that which will grieve you. This is the Day which you were promised.” He says, Who are you? Your face is the face that brings evil. He says, I am your evil deeds. He says, My Lord, do not establish the Hour. Imam Ahmad also said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Yunus ibn Khabab, on the authority of al-Munhal ibn Amr, on the authority of Zadhan, on the authority of al-Bara’ ibn Azib, who said: We went out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to a funeral, and he mentioned something similar to it, and in it until his soul departed, every angel of the heavens and the earth and every angel in the heavens prayed for him, and the gates of the heavens were opened for him, and there is no one among the people of a gate except that they call upon God, the Almighty, the Majestic, to ascend with his soul before them, and at the end of it, then a blind, deaf, and mute man is appointed for him, in whose hand is a hammer, if he struck a mountain with it, it would be dust, so he strikes it once and it becomes dust, then God, the Almighty, the Majestic, returns him as he was and strikes him another blow, so he cries out a cry that everything hears except the two heavy things, al-Bara’ said: Then a door of Hell is opened for him and a bed of Hell is prepared for him, and in the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad, al-Nasa’i, Ibn Majah, and Ibn Jarir, and the wording is his, from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Ata’, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Yasar, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The dead person is attended by… The angels, if it is a righteous man, say: Come out, O reassured soul, you were in a good body, come out praiseworthy and receive good tidings of spirit and fragrance and a Lord who is not angry. They say that until it ascends to heaven and it is opened for it. It is said: Who is this? They say: So-and-so. It is said: Welcome to the good soul that was in the good body. Enter praiseworthy and receive good tidings of spirit and fragrance and a Lord who is not angry. It is said that to it until it reaches the heaven in which God, the Almighty, is. But if it is a bad man, they say: Come out, O evil soul that was in an evil body, come out reprehensible and receive good tidings of boiling water and pus and other similar pairs. They say that until it comes out and then it ascends to heaven and it is opened for it. It is said: Who is this? They say: So-and-so. They say: No, welcome to the evil soul that was in the evil body. Go back reprehensible, for the gates of heaven were not opened for you. So it is sent between heaven and earth and it goes to the grave. Ibn Jurayj said about His statement, The gates of heaven will not be opened for them, they will not be opened for their deeds or their souls. This combines the two statements, and God knows best. God Almighty’s statement, And they will not enter Paradise until a camel passes through the eye of a needle, is how the majority read it and interpreted it as meaning the camel. Ibn Mas’ud said: It is the camel, the son of the she-camel. In another narration, it is the husband of the she-camel. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: Until the camel passes through the eye of a needle. Abu al-Aaliyah and al-Dahhak said the same. Ali ibn Abi Talhah al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas. Mujahid and Ikrimah said from Ibn Abbas: He used to read it, The camel passes through the eye of a needle, with a damma on the jim and a shaddah on the mim, meaning the thick rope through the eye of a needle. This is the choice of Sa’id ibn Jubayr. In another narration, he read, Until the camel passes through, meaning the hulls of ships, which are thick ropes. God Almighty’s statement, For them are beds from Hell, Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi said, For them are beds from Hell, al-Farsh said, And above them are coverings, al-Lahf said, and al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim and al-Suddi said, And likewise. We will reward the wrongdoers.
7:41: His saying, The gates of heaven will not be opened for them. It was said that what is meant is that no good deed or supplication will be raised for them from it. This was said by Mujahid and Saeed bin Jubair, and it was narrated by Al-Awfi and Ali bin Abi Talhah from Ibn Abbas, and it was also narrated by Al-Thawri from Laith from Ata’ from Ibn Abbas. It was also said that what is meant is that the gates of heaven will not be opened for their souls. This was narrated by Ad-Dahhak from Ibn Abbas, and it was said by As-Suddi and others, and it is supported by what Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Abu Bakr bin Ayyash told us from Al-A’mash from Al-Munhal, who is Ibn Amr, from Zadhan from Al-Bara’ that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned the taking of the soul of the wicked, and that it ascends with it to heaven and they ascend with it, and it does not pass by a group of angels except that they say, What is this evil soul? They say, So-and-so, using the worst names he was called by in this world, until they reach the heavens and ask for its gates to be opened for him, but they do not open them for him. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited, The gates of heaven will not be opened for them, the verse. This is how he narrated it, and it is part of a long hadith narrated by Abu Dawud, al-Nasa’i, and Ibn Majah through various chains of transmission on the authority of al-Munhal ibn Amr. Imam Ahmad narrated it in full, saying: Abu Muawiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Al-Munhal bin Amr, on the authority of Zadhan, on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib, who said: We went out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the funeral of a man from the Ansar, and we reached the grave and it had not yet been dug. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sat down and we sat around him as if there were birds on our heads, and in his hand was a stick with which he was poking the ground. He raised his head and said: Seek refuge with God from the punishment of the grave - two or three times. Then he said: When the believing servant is cut off from this world and turning to the Hereafter, angels descend to him from the heavens with white faces as if their faces were the sun, with them a shroud from the shrouds of Paradise and embalming from the embalming of Paradise until they sit near him as far as the eye can see. Then the Angel of Death comes and sits at his head and says: O good soul, come out to forgiveness from God and His pleasure - he said: So it comes out flowing as a drop flows from the mouth of a waterskin, and he takes it, and when he takes it, he does not leave it in his hand for the blink of an eye until they take it and put it in that shroud and in That is the embalming and from it comes out the most fragrant scent of musk found on the face of the earth. They ascend with it and they do not pass by a group of angels except that they say, What is this fragrant soul? They say, So-and-so, son of so-and-so, using the best of the names by which they used to call him in the world, until they reach the lowest heaven. They ask permission for him, and it is opened for him. Then those closest to him accompany him from each heaven to the heaven next to it, until he reaches the seventh heaven. Then God, the Almighty, the Majestic, says, Write the book of My servant in ‘Illiyeen and return him to the earth, for from it I created them, and into it I will return them, and from it I will extract them another time. He said: Then his soul is restored and two angels come to him and make him sit and say to him: Who is your Lord? He says: My Lord is God. They say to him: What is your religion? He says: My religion is Islam. They say to him: Who is this man who was sent among you? He says: He is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. They say to him: What is your work? He says: I read the Book of God and believed in it and believed. Then a voice calls from the heaven: My servant has spoken the truth, so furnish him from Paradise and clothe him from Paradise and open for him a door to Paradise. Its fragrance and goodness come to him, and his grave is expanded for him as far as the eye can see. He said: Then a man with a handsome face, handsome clothes and a pleasant scent comes to him and says: Receive good tidings of that which will please you. This is the day which you were promised. He says to him: Who are you, for your face is a face that brings good? He says: I am your righteous work. He says: O Lord, bring about the Hour. O Lord, bring about the Hour so that I may return to my family and my wealth. He said: And when the disbelieving servant is in a state of separation from this world and turning to the Hereafter, angels with black faces descend to him from the heavens, carrying sackcloth, and they sit near him as far as the eye can see. Then the Angel of Death comes and sits at his head and says: O wicked soul, come out to the wrath and anger of God. He said: So it spreads through his body and pulls it out as a skewer is pulled out of wet wool, and he takes it. When he takes it, he does not leave it in his hand for the blink of an eye until they put it in that sackcloth, and it comes out of it like the most foul odor of a corpse found on the face of the earth. They ascend with it and they do not pass by a group of angels except that they say: What is this wicked soul? They say: So-and-so, son of so-and-so, using the ugliest names he was called by in this world, until he reaches the lowest heaven and asks for permission, but it is not opened for him. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: The gates of heaven will not be opened for them, nor will they enter Paradise until a camel passes through the eye of a needle. Then God, the Almighty, says: Write his record in a prison in the lowest earth. Then his soul is thrown out. Then he recited: And whoever associates with God a partner, God will not be granted permission. By God, it is as if he had fallen from the sky and been snatched by birds or blown away by the wind to a far off place. Then his soul is returned to his body and two angels come to him and make him sit up and say to him, Who is your Lord? He says, Huh, huh? I do not know. They say, What is your religion? He says, Huh, huh? I do not know. They say, Who is this man who was sent among you? He says, Huh, huh? I do not know. Then a voice calls from the sky, My servant has lied, so spread out for him a bed from the Fire and open for him a door to the Fire. Then some of its heat and its poisonous winds come to him and his grave becomes narrow for him until his ribs overlap. Then a man comes to him with an ugly face, ugly clothes, and a foul odor and says, “Give me good tidings of that which will grieve you. This is the Day which you were promised.” He says, Who are you? Your face is the face that brings evil. He says, I am your evil deeds. He says, My Lord, do not establish the Hour. Imam Ahmad also said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Yunus ibn Khabab, on the authority of al-Munhal ibn Amr, on the authority of Zadhan, on the authority of al-Bara’ ibn Azib, who said: We went out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to a funeral, and he mentioned something similar to it, and in it until his soul departed, every angel of the heavens and the earth and every angel in the heavens prayed for him, and the gates of the heavens were opened for him, and there is no one among the people of a gate except that they call upon God, the Almighty, the Majestic, to ascend with his soul before them, and at the end of it, then a blind, deaf, and mute man is appointed for him, in whose hand is a hammer, if he struck a mountain with it, it would be dust, so he strikes it once and it becomes dust, then God, the Almighty, the Majestic, returns him as he was and strikes him another blow, so he cries out a cry that everything hears except the two heavy things, al-Bara’ said: Then a door of Hell is opened for him and a bed of Hell is prepared for him, and in the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad, al-Nasa’i, Ibn Majah, and Ibn Jarir, and the wording is his, from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Ata’, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Yasar, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The dead person is attended by… The angels, if it is a righteous man, say: Come out, O reassured soul, you were in a good body, come out praiseworthy and receive good tidings of spirit and fragrance and a Lord who is not angry. They say that until it ascends to heaven and it is opened for it. It is said: Who is this? They say: So-and-so. It is said: Welcome to the good soul that was in the good body. Enter praiseworthy and receive good tidings of spirit and fragrance and a Lord who is not angry. It is said that to it until it reaches the heaven in which God, the Almighty, is. But if it is a bad man, they say: Come out, O evil soul that was in an evil body, come out reprehensible and receive good tidings of boiling water and pus and other similar pairs. They say that until it comes out and then it ascends to heaven and it is opened for it. It is said: Who is this? They say: So-and-so. They say: No, welcome to the evil soul that was in the evil body. Go back reprehensible, for the gates of heaven were not opened for you. So it is sent between heaven and earth and it goes to the grave. Ibn Jurayj said about His statement, The gates of heaven will not be opened for them, they will not be opened for their deeds or their souls. This combines the two statements, and God knows best. God Almighty’s statement, And they will not enter Paradise until a camel passes through the eye of a needle, is how the majority read it and interpreted it as meaning the camel. Ibn Mas’ud said: It is the camel, the son of the she-camel. In another narration, it is the husband of the she-camel. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: Until the camel passes through the eye of a needle. Abu al-Aaliyah and al-Dahhak said the same. Ali ibn Abi Talhah al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas. Mujahid and Ikrimah said from Ibn Abbas: He used to read it, The camel passes through the eye of a needle, with a damma on the jim and a shaddah on the mim, meaning the thick rope through the eye of a needle. This is the choice of Sa’id ibn Jubayr. In another narration, he read, Until the camel passes through, meaning the hulls of ships, which are thick ropes. God Almighty’s statement, For them are beds from Hell, Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi said, For them are beds from Hell, al-Farsh said, And above them are coverings, al-Lahf said, and al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim and al-Suddi said, And likewise. We will reward the wrongdoers.
7:42: When God the Almighty mentioned the state of the wretched, He followed it up by mentioning the state of the happy, saying, And those who believed and did righteous deeds, meaning their hearts believed and they did righteous deeds with their limbs, as opposed to those who disbelieved in the verses of God and were arrogant towards them. God the Almighty points out that belief and acting upon it are easy, because God the Almighty said, “We do not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity. Those are the companions of Paradise, they will abide therein eternally. And We will remove whatever is in their breasts of resentment,” meaning envy and hatred, as came in Sahih al-Bukhari from the hadith of Qatadah on the authority of Abu al-Mutawakkil al-Naji on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When the believers are saved from the Fire, they will be detained on a bridge between Paradise and the Fire, and retribution will be taken against them for the injustices that were between them in this world. Then, when they are refined and purified, they will be permitted to enter Paradise. By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, one of them will be more worthy of his home in Paradise than of his home in this world.” Al-Suddi said about His statement, And We will remove whatever is in their breasts of resentment, beneath them rivers flow, the verse, that when the people of Paradise are driven to Paradise, they will find At its gate is a tree at the base of its trunk two springs. They drank from one of them, and it removed whatever rancor was in their hearts, and it was the pure drink. They washed themselves from the other, and the freshness of bliss flowed upon them, and they were never disheveled or pale after that ever. Abu Ishaq narrated on the authority of Asim on the authority of the Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abi Talib something similar to this, as will come in the words of God Almighty: And those who feared their Lord will be led to Paradise in groups, God willing. In Him is the trust and upon Him is reliance. Qatada said: Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: I hope that I, Uthman, Talha, and Al-Zubayr will be among those about whom God Almighty said: And We will remove whatever is in their breasts of resentment. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Abd Al-Razzaq said: Ibn Uyaynah told us on the authority of Isra’il who said: I heard Al-Hasan say: Ali said: By God, it was about us, the people of Badr, that And We will remove whatever is in their breasts of resentment. Al-Nasa’i and Ibn Mardawayh narrated, and the wording is his, from the hadith of Abu Bakr Ibn Ayyash on the authority of Al-A’mash on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Abu Hurairah who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Everyone in Paradise will see his seat in Hell and say: ‘If only God had guided me,’ and that will be a sign of gratitude for him. Every one of the people of Hell will see his seat in Paradise and say: ‘If only God had guided me,’ and that will be a sign of regret for him.” For this reason, when the people of Hell were inherited the seats of the people of Hell in Paradise, they were called out: This is Paradise, which you inherited because of what you used to do, meaning that because of your deeds, mercy was bestowed upon you, so you entered Paradise and were assigned your homes according to your deeds. It is necessary to interpret this as it was proven in the two Sahihs that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Know that none of you will enter Paradise because of his deeds. They said: Not even you, O Messenger of God? He said: Not even me, unless God covers me with His mercy and grace.

7:44: The Almighty tells us what He will address the people of Hell with in a way of rebuke and reprimand when they settle in their homes: Indeed, we have found what our Lord promised us to be true. Here, that is an explanation of the omitted statement, and qad is for confirmation, meaning that they said to them, “Indeed, we have found what our Lord promised us to be true. Have you found what your Lord promised to be true?” They said, Yes. Just as the Almighty told us in Surat As-Saffat about the one who had a companion from among the disbelievers: “So he looked and saw him in the midst of Hellfire. He said, “By God, you were almost doomed to perish. And had it not been for the grace of my Lord, I would have been among those brought forth. Are we not to die? Except for our first death, and we are not to be punished.” That is, He denounces his statement that he says in this world and rebukes him for what has befallen him of punishment and torment. Likewise, the angels rebuke them, saying to them: “This is the Fire which you used to deny. Is this magic, or do you not see? Enter it, and be patient or do not be patient. It is all the same to you. You are only being recompensed for what you used to do.” And likewise, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, rebuked the dead of Al-Qalib. On the day of Badr, he called out, O Abu Jahl bin Hisham, O Utbah bin Rabi’ah, and O Shaiba bin Rabi’ah - and he named their heads - Have you found what your Lord promised to be true? I have found what my Lord promised me to be true. Umar said, O Messenger of God, are you addressing people who have rotted away? He said, By the One in Whose hand is my soul, you are not more attentive to what I say than they are, but they are unable to respond. And the Almighty said: Then a crier will proclaim among them meaning a teacher will know and a crier will call out that the curse of God is upon the wrongdoers meaning it will be settled upon them. Then He described them by saying those who hinder [people] from the way of God and seek to make it crooked meaning they hinder people from following the way of God and His law and what the prophets brought and they seek for the way to be crooked and not straight so that no one will follow it and they are disbelievers in the Hereafter meaning they are disbelievers in meeting God in the Hereafter meaning they are ungrateful and deny that and do not believe in it or have faith in it. For this reason they do not care about what they do of evil words and deeds because they do not fear being held accountable for it or being punished. They are the worst of people in words and deeds.

7:46: When God the Almighty mentioned the people of Paradise addressing the people of Hell, He pointed out that there is a veil between Paradise and Hell, which is the barrier preventing the people of Hell from reaching Paradise. Ibn Jarir said: It is the wall about which God the Almighty said: And a wall will be set up between them having a door, inside of which is mercy, but outside of it is punishment before it, and it is Al-A'raf. About which God the Almighty said: And on the heights are men, then he narrated with his chain of transmission on the authority of Al-Suddi that he said regarding His the Almighty's saying: And between them is a veil, which is the wall, which is Al-A'raf. Mujahid said that Al-A'raf is a veil between Paradise and Hell, a wall with a door. Ibn Jarir said: Al-A'raf is the plural of 'urf, and every elevated area of land among the Arabs is called 'urf, and the rooster's crest is called 'urf because of its height. Sufyan ibn Wakee’ narrated to us, Ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, on the authority of Ubayd God ibn Abi Yazid, who heard Ibn Abbas say: Al-A’raf is a high place. Ath-Thawri narrated on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Al-A’raf is a wall like a rooster’s comb. In another narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Al-A’raf is a hill between Paradise and Hell, on which some sinners were held between Paradise and Hell. In another narration on his authority, it is a wall between Paradise and Hell. Ad-Dahhak and more than one of the scholars of tafsir said the same. As-Suddi said: Al-A’raf is called Al-A’raf because its people know people. The commentators differed in their expressions about who the people of Al-A’raf are. All of these are close and go back to one meaning, which is that they are people whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal. This was stated by Hudhayfah, Ibn Abbas, Ibn Mas`ud, and more than one of the early and later generations, may God have mercy on them. It was mentioned in a hadith with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, narrated by Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Ibn Mardawayh: Abdullah Ibn Ismail told us, Ubayd Ibn Al-Husayn told us, Sulayman Ibn Dawud told us, An-Nu`man Ibn Abd Al-Salam told us, an old man of ours called Abu `Ibad told us, on the authority of Abdullah Ibn Muhammad Ibn `Aqil, on the authority of Jabir Ibn `Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about those whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal, so he said: “Those are the companions of Al-A`raf. They will not enter it, and they are hopeful.” This is a strange hadith from this perspective. And he narrated it from another chain of transmission on the authority of Saeed bin Salamah on the authority of Abu Al-Hussam on the authority of Muhammad bin Al-Munkadir on the authority of a man from Muzaynah who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about those whose good deeds and bad deeds were equal, so he said: They are people who went out as sinners without the permission of their fathers and were killed in the cause of God. And Saeed bin Mansour said: Abu Ma’shar told us, Yahya bin Shibl told us on the authority of Yahya bin Abd Al-Rahman Al-Muzani on the authority of his father who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about the people of Al-A’raf, so he said: “They are people who were killed in the cause of God due to the disobedience of their fathers, and their disobedience to their fathers prevented them from entering Paradise, and their killing in the cause of God prevented them from the Fire.” And Ibn Mardawayh, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it through various chains of transmission on the authority of Abu Ma’shar, and Ibn Majah also narrated it with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri and Ibn Abbas. And God knows best about the authenticity of these reports with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, and the most they can be said is that they are attributed to the Prophet, and in them is evidence for what was mentioned. Ibn Jarir said: Yaqub told me, Hisham told us, Husayn told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Hudhayfah, that he was asked about the people of Al-A’raf. He said: They are people whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal, so their bad deeds kept them from Paradise and their good deeds kept them from Hell. He said: So they stood there on the wall until God judged them. And he narrated it from another chain of transmission more simply than this. He said: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya ibn Wadh told us, Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq told us: Al-Sha’bi said: Abd Al-Hamid ibn Abd Al-Rahman sent for me and Abu Al-Zinad Abd God ibn Dhakwan, a freedman of Quraysh, was with him. They mentioned a mention of the people of Al-A’raf that was not as they had mentioned. So I said to them: If you wish, I will tell you what Hudhayfah mentioned. They said: Bring it. So I said: Hudhayfah mentioned the people of Al-A’raf and said: Their good deeds kept them from Hell and their bad deeds kept them from Paradise. “And when their eyes are turned toward the companions of the Fire, they will say: Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people.” While they were like that, your Lord appeared to them and said: Go. Enter Paradise, for I have forgiven you. Abdullah bin Mubarak said on the authority of Abu Bakr Al-Hudhali that Saeed bin Jubair said while narrating that on the authority of Ibn Masoud that he said: People will be held to account on the Day of Resurrection, so whoever’s good deeds outweigh his bad deeds by one will enter Paradise, and whoever’s bad deeds outweigh his good deeds by one will enter Hell. Then he recited the words of God: But whose scales are heavy 2:130, then he said: The scale will be made lighter by the weight of a grain, and it will be heavier. He said: And whoever’s good deeds and bad deeds are equal will be among the people of Al-A’raf. Then they will stand on the Sirat and then they will recognize the people of Paradise and the people of Hell. When they look at the people of Paradise, they will call out, “Peace be upon you.” And when they turn their eyes to their left, they will look at the people of Hell. They will say, ‘Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people.’ They sought refuge in God from their homes. He said: As for the people of good deeds, they will be given a light with which they will walk in front of them and on their right, and every slave will be given a light on that Day, and every nation will be given a light. Then when they come to the Sirat, God will take away the light of every hypocrite, male and female. When the people of Paradise saw what the hypocrites had endured, they will say, Our Lord, perfect for us our light. As for the people of A’raf, the light was in their hands and was not taken away. So God Almighty says: They did not enter it while they were hoping. So hope was an entry. He said: Ibn Masoud said: If a servant does a good deed, ten are written for him, but if he does a bad deed, only one is written for him. Then he says: He is doomed whose ones outweigh his tens. 7:48: God the Almighty says, informing us about the rebuke of the people of A'raf to men from the leaders of the polytheists and their leaders whom they will recognize in Hell by their features: Your multitude has not availed you, nor you were arrogant meaning your multitude and your crowds will not benefit you from God’s punishment, rather you have reached the punishment and torment you are in. Are these the ones you swore God would not grant them mercy? Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, meaning the people of A'raf. Enter Paradise, no fear for you, nor shall you grieve. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, my father told me, my uncle told me, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas. They said, ‘Your multitude has not availed you,’ the verse. He said: When they said to them what God had decreed that they would say, meaning the people of A'raf, about the people of Paradise and the people of Hell, God said to the people of arrogance and wealth: Are these the ones you swore God would not grant them mercy? Enter Paradise, no fear for you, nor shall you grieve. You are sad. Hudhayfah said: The people of A'raf were a people whose deeds had increased so much that their good deeds kept them short of Paradise and their bad deeds kept them short of Hellfire. They were on A'raf and people were known by their marks. When God judged between the servants, He gave them permission to ask for intercession. They came to Adam and said: O Adam, you are our father, so intercede for us with your Lord. He said: Do you know of anyone whom God created with His hand and breathed into him of His spirit, and whose mercy preceded his wrath, and to whom the angels prostrated, other than me? They said: No. He said: I do not know its true nature. I cannot intercede for you, but go to my son Ibrahim. So they go to Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and ask him to intercede for them with their Lord. He said: Do you know of anyone whom God took as a friend? Do you know of anyone whom his people burned in fire for the sake of God other than me? They will say, No. He will say, “I do not know its true nature; I cannot intercede for you. But go to my son Moses.” So they will go to Moses, peace be upon him, and he will say, Do you know of anyone to whom God spoke directly and brought him close in private conversation other than me? They will say, No. He will say, “I do not know its true nature; I cannot intercede for you. But go to Jesus.” So they will go to him, peace be upon him, and say, Intercede for us with your Lord. He will say, Do you know of anyone whom God created without a father? They will say, No. He will say, Do you know of anyone who healed the blind and the leper and raised the dead by God’s permission other than me? He said: They say: No. He says: I am the pilgrim of my soul, I do not know its essence, I cannot intercede for you, but go to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. So they come to me, and I strike my hand on my chest and say: I am for it. Then I walk until I stand before the Throne and come to my Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, and He opens for me praise the like of which the listeners have never heard before. Then I prostrate and it is said to me: O Muhammad, raise your head and ask and you will be given, and intercede and your intercession will be accepted. So I raise my head and praise my Lord, the Mighty and Sublime. Then I prostrate and it is said to me: Raise your head and ask and you will be given, and intercede and your intercession will be accepted. So I raise my head and say: My Lord, my nation. He says: They are for you, for there will not remain a prophet sent and an angel brought near except that he will envy me for that station, which is the praised station. So I bring them to Paradise and ask for permission, and it will be opened for me and for them. Then they are taken to a river called the River of Life, its banks are reeds crowned with pearls, its soil is musk and its pebbles are rubies. They wash in it and the colors of the people of Paradise and the fragrance of the people of Paradise return to them and they become like shining stars and it remains in their chests. White moles by which they are known as the poor people of Paradise.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Nasr bin Ali told us, Musa bin Al-Mughira told us, Abu Musa Al-Saffar told us in the house of Amr bin Muslim, he said: I asked Ibn Abbas or he was asked which charity is best? He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The best charity is water. Didn’t you hear the people of Hell when they called for help from the people of Paradise? They said: Pour upon us some water or from whatever God has provided you.” He also said: Ahmad bin Sinan told us, Abu Muawiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, he said: When Abu Talib fell ill, they said to him: Why don’t you send for your nephew so that he can send you a cluster of grapes from Paradise, perhaps it will cure you. So the Messenger came to him and Abu Bakr was with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr said: God has forbidden them to the disbelievers. Then God the Almighty described the disbelievers with what they relied on in this world, by taking religion as a pastime and a game, and being deceived by this world, its adornments and its decorations, instead of what they were commanded to do of working for the Hereafter. His statement, So today We will forget them as they forgot the meeting of this Day of theirs, means that He will treat them as one who forgot them, because nothing is outside His knowledge and He will not forget it, as God the Almighty said, “It is in a Book. My Lord does not err, nor does He forget.” Rather, God the Almighty said this as a way of contrast, like His statement, They forgot God, so He forgot them, and He said, Thus did Our signs come to you, and you forgot them, and thus will you be forgotten today. And God the Almighty said, And it will be said, ‘Today We will forget you as you forgot the meeting of this Day of yours.’ Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement, So today We will forget them as they forgot the meeting of this Day of theirs, that God forgot them of goodness, but He did not forget them of evil. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said, We will leave them as they forgot the meeting of this Day of theirs. Mujahid said, We will leave them in the Fire. Al-Suddi said, We will leave them from mercy as they forgot to work for the meeting of their Day. This, and in the authentic hadith, it is stated that God the Almighty will say to the servant on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:Did I not marry you? Did I not honor you? Did I not subject the horses and camels to you and let you rule and sit on the throne? He will say: Yes. He will say: Did you think that you would meet Me? He will say: No. God the Almighty will say: So today I will forget you as you forgot Me?
7:51: God Almighty tells us about the humiliation of the people of Hell and their asking the people of Paradise for their food and drink, and that they will not be answered in that. Al-Suddi said, And the companions of the Fire will call out to the companions of Paradise, ‘Pour upon us some water or whatever God has provided you,’ meaning food. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said, They will seek food from them and ask them for water. Al-Thawri said, on the authority of Uthman al-Thaqafi, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, regarding this verse, he said, “A man will call out to his father or brother and say to him, ‘I have been burned, so pour some water on me.’ They will be told, ‘Answer them,’ and they will say, ‘God has forbidden them to the disbelievers.’” It was narrated from another source on the authority of Saeed on the authority of Ibn Abbas, something similar. 7:52: God Almighty says, informing about His excuse to the polytheists by sending messengers to them with the book that the Messenger brought and that it is a detailed and clear book, as He says, A Book whose verses are perfected and then detailed Al-An’am 2:17, and His saying, We have detailed it with knowledge for the worlds, meaning with knowledge from Us of what We have detailed it with, as He says, He sent it down with His knowledge. Ibn Jarir said, This verse is a response to His saying, “A Book sent down to you, so let there not be in your breast discomfort therefrom Al-An’am 2:17, And We have certainly brought them a Book Al-An’am 2:17, and what He said is questionable, because the separation was long and there is no evidence for it. Rather, the matter is that when He informed them of what they had become of loss in the Hereafter, He mentioned that He had removed their excuses in this world by sending messengers and sending down books, as He says, And We never punish until We have sent a messenger. For this reason He said, Do they await except its interpretation? meaning what they were promised of punishment, chastisement, Paradise, and Hell. This was said by Mujahid and more than one person. Malik said: Its reward. Al-Rabi’ said: “Its interpretation will continue to come until the Day of Judgment is completed, until the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of Hell enter Hell, and its interpretation will be completed on that day.” His statement, The Day its interpretation comes, means the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abbas said, Those who forgot it before will say, meaning they abandoned acting upon it and forgot about it in this worldly life, “The messengers of our Lord have come with the truth. So are there for us any intercessors who will intercede for us?” meaning for our salvation from what we have come to, from what we are in. Or will we be returned to this worldly life so that we may do other than what we used to do? like His statement, “And if you could but see when they are made to stand before the Fire and say, ‘Oh, would that we could be sent back and not deny the signs of our Lord and be among the believers.’ Rather, what they used to conceal before will appear to them. And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed, they are liars.” Just as He said here, They have lost themselves, and lost from them is that which they used to invent. That is, they have lost themselves by entering the Fire and remaining in it forever. And lost from them is that which they used to invent. That is, what they used to worship besides God has gone away from them, so they will not intercede for them nor will they intercede for them. They support them but do not save them from what they are in.

7:54: God Almighty tells us that He created the world, its heavens and its earth and everything in between, in six days, as He has told us in more than one verse of the Qur’an. The six days are: Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday. On that day, all creation gathered, and on that day, Adam, peace be upon him, was created. They differed about these days: is each day like these days, as comes to mind, or is each day like a thousand years, as Mujahid and Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal stated, and this is narrated from the narration of Ad-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas? As for Saturday, no creation occurred on it because it is the seventh day, and from that it was called Saturday, which means cutting off. As for the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad, where he said: Hajjaj told us, Ibn Jurayj told us, Ismail ibn Umayyah told me, on the authority of Ayoub ibn Khalid, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Rafi’, the freed slave of Umm Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took my hand and said: “God created the soil on Saturday, and He created the mountains in it on Sunday, and He created the trees in it on Monday, and He created the detestable on Tuesday, and He created the light on Wednesday, and He spread the animals in it on Thursday, and He created Adam after the afternoon on Friday, and He was the last of creation, in the last hour of the hours of Friday, between the afternoon and the night.” Muslim ibn Hajjaj narrated it in his Sahih, and al-Nasa’i from more than one chain of transmission on the authority of Hajjaj, who is Ibn Muhammad al-A’war, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on his authority, and it includes the seven days, and God Almighty said in six days. For this reason, al-Bukhari and more than one of the hadith masters spoke about this hadith and attributed it to the narration of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of Ka’b al-Ahbar, not to the Prophet, and God knows best. As for the saying of God the Almighty: Then He rose over the Throne, people have many opinions on this subject, and this is not the place to elaborate on them. Rather, we follow the doctrine of the righteous predecessors, Malik, Al-Awza’i, Al-Thawri, Al-Layth bin Sa’d, Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, Ishaq bin Rahawayh, and others from the imams of the Muslims, past and present, which is to pass it on as it came without any description, likening, or nullifying it. The apparent meaning that comes to the minds of those who liken God to something is negated, and nothing of His creation resembles Him. There is nothing like Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing. Rather, the matter is as the imams said, including Nu’aym bin Hammad Al-Khuza’i, the Sheikh of Al-Bukhari, who said: Whoever likens God to His creation has committed blasphemy, and whoever denies what God described Himself with has committed blasphemy. There is no likening in what God described Himself with, nor in what His Messenger described Himself with. So whoever affirms for God the Almighty what is mentioned in the clear verses and authentic reports in the manner that befits the majesty of God, and denies the shortcomings of God the Almighty, has followed the path of guidance. And the saying of God the Almighty: The night covers the day, pursuing it rapidly, means that the darkness of this one is dispelled by the light of this one and the light of that one. In the darkness of this, each of them seeks the other urgently, meaning quickly, not delayed from it, but if this goes, this comes, and the opposite is like His saying: “And a sign for them is the night. We strip thereof the day, and at once they are in darkness. And the sun runs to a resting place for it. That is the determination of the Almighty, the Knowing. And the moon - We have determined for it phases until it returns [like] an old palm branch. It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day. Each, in an orbit, floats.” So His saying: Nor does the night outstrip the day, means that it does not escape it by a time that is delayed from it, but rather it follows it without an intermediary between them. For this reason He said: He seeks it urgently, and the sun, the moon, and the stars are subjected by His command. Some of them used the accusative and some used the nominative, and both are close in meaning, meaning that all are under His control, subjection, and will. For this reason He said, drawing attention: Is not His the creation and the command? That is His the kingdom and the disposition. Blessed be God, Lord of the worlds, like His saying: Blessed be He who has placed constellations in the heaven. The verse. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna told me, Ishaq told us, Hisham Abu Abd al-Rahman told us, Baqiyah ibn al-Waleed told us, Abd al-Ghaffar ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Ansari told us, on the authority of Abd al-Aziz al-Shami, on the authority of his father, who was a companion of the Prophet, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever does not praise God for the righteous deeds he has done and praises himself has disbelieved and his deeds have been rendered worthless. Whoever claims that God has given the servants any part of the matter has disbelieved in what God has revealed to His prophets,” because of His saying: “To Him belongs creation and command. Blessed be God, Lord of the worlds.” And in the supplication narrated on the authority of Abu al-Darda’, and it was narrated with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, “O God, all dominion is Yours, all praise is Yours, and to You returns all matters. I ask You for all good and I seek refuge in You from all evil.”
7:55: God the Almighty guided His servants to supplicate Him, which is their well-being in this world and the next, so He said, “Call upon your Lord humbly and in secret.” It was said that its meaning is humility and submission, and secretly like His saying, And remember your Lord within yourself, the verse. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash’ari, he said that the people raised their voices in supplication, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “O people, be gentle with yourselves, for you are not calling upon one who is deaf or absent. Indeed, the One you call upon is All-Hearing, Near,” the hadith. Ibn Jurayj said, on the authority of Ata’ al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying, in secret and in secret, he said, in secret. Ibn Jarir said, in humility, submission, and submission to His obedience, and secretly, meaning with the humility of your hearts and the soundness of certainty in His Oneness and Lordship between you and Him, not out loud for show. Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak ibn Fadala said, on the authority of al-Hasan, he said, If a man has collected the Qur’an, people do not realize it, and if a man has understood a great deal of jurisprudence, people do not realize it. People are like that, even if a man prays a long prayer in his house and has visitors and they do not notice them. We have known people who did not do any work on earth that they could do in secret, but it would always be done in public. The Muslims used to strive hard in supplication, but no voice was heard from them. It was only a whisper between them and their Lord. This is because God Almighty says, Call upon your Lord humbly and in secret. This is because God mentioned a righteous servant whose action He was pleased with, saying, When he called upon his Lord a call in secret. Ibn Jurayj said, raising one’s voice, calling, and shouting in supplication is disliked, and one is commanded to be humble and submissive. Then it was narrated on the authority of Ata’ al-Khurasani on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, He does not love transgressors in supplication or otherwise. Abu Majlaz said, He does not love transgressors does not ask for the status of the prophets. Ahmad said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Ziyad ibn Mukhraq, I heard Abu Na’amah on the authority of a freed slave of Sa’d that Sa’d heard his son supplicating and saying, O God, I ask You for Paradise and its delights and its brocade and something similar to this, and I seek refuge in You from the Fire and its chains and shackles. He said, “I have asked God for much good and I have sought refuge in Him from much evil. I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say, ‘There will be people who transgress in supplication’ – and in another version – they transgress in purification and supplication – and he recited this verse, ‘Call upon your Lord humbly’ – and it is sufficient for you to say, ‘O God, I ask You for Paradise and whatever brings one closer to it in word or deed, and I seek refuge in You from the Fire and whatever brings one closer to it in word or deed. ’” Abu Dawud narrated it on the authority of Shu’bah on the authority of Ziyad ibn Mukhraq, on the authority of Abu Na’amah, on the authority of a freed slave of Sa’d, on the authority of Sa’d, and he mentioned it, and God knows best. Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, Al-Hariri told us, on the authority of Abu Na’amah, that Abdullah bin Mughaffal heard his son say, O God, I ask You for the white palace on the right of Paradise when I enter it. He said, “O my son, ask God for Paradise and seek refuge with Him from the Fire, for I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say, ‘There will be people who go to extremes in supplication and purification.’” And this is how Ibn Majah narrated it, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah, on the authority of Affan, on his authority. Abu Dawud narrated it on the authority of Musa bin Ismail, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Sa’id bin Iyas Al-Jariri, on the authority of Abu Na’amah, whose name is Qais bin Ubayyah Al-Hanafi Al-Basri, and it is a good chain of transmission, there is nothing wrong with it, and God knows best. God the Almighty says, And do not cause corruption on the earth after its reformation, God the Almighty forbids corruption on the earth and what harms it after its reformation. If things are going well and then corruption occurs after that, it is the most harmful thing for the servants. God the Almighty forbade that and commanded worshipping Him, calling upon Him, beseeching Him, and humbled himself before Him. He said, And call upon Him in fear and hope, meaning fear of what He has of severe punishment and hope for what He has of abundant reward. Then He said, Indeed, the mercy of God is near to the doers of good, meaning that His mercy is waiting for the doers of good who follow His commands and abandon His prohibitions, as God the Almighty said, And My mercy encompasses all things, so I will prescribe it for those who fear God, the verse. He said near and did not say near because He included the meaning of reward in mercy or because it is attributed to God, so that is why He said near to the doers of good. Matar al-Warraq said, Fulfill the promise of God by obeying Him, for He has decreed that His mercy is near to the doers of good. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

7:57: When the Almighty mentioned that He is the Creator of the heavens and the earth and that He is the Disposer, the Ruler, the Manager, the One who is subservient, and He guided us to call upon Him because He is able to do whatever He wills, the Almighty pointed out that He is the Provider and that He will restore the dead on the Day of Resurrection, so He said, And it is He who sends the winds as good tidings, meaning they spread out before the clouds carrying rain. Some of them read good tidings, as in His statement, And among His signs is that He sends the winds as good tidings, and His statement, before His mercy, meaning before the rain, as in His statement, And it is He who sends down the rain after they have despaired and spreads His mercy, and He is the Protector, the Praiseworthy, and He said, “Then look at the traces of God’s mercy, how He revives the earth after its death. Indeed, that is the One who revives the dead, and He is over all things competent.” And His statement, Until, when they carry heavy clouds, meaning the winds carry heavy clouds, meaning because of the abundance of water in them, they are heavy, close to the earth, and dark, as Zayd ibn Amr ibn Nufayl, may God have mercy on him, said: I surrender my face to the one to whom the rains surrender, carrying pure sweet water. I surrendered my face to the one to whom the earth surrendered, carrying heavy rocks. And His saying, We drove it to a dead land, meaning to a barren, dead land with no vegetation, like His saying, “And a sign for them is the dead land. We have given it life,” the verse. And for this reason He said, “And We brought forth thereby all kinds of fruits. Thus do We bring forth the dead,” meaning, just as We brought this land to life after its death, thus do We bring forth the bodies after they have become dust. On the Day of Resurrection, God Almighty will send down water from the sky, and it will rain on the land for forty days, and the bodies will grow from it in their graves, just as seeds grow in the ground. This meaning is common in the Qur’an. God gives an example of the Day of Resurrection by bringing the land to life after its death, and for this reason He said, Perhaps you will remember. And His saying, And the good land - its vegetation comes forth by permission of its Lord, meaning, and the good land - its vegetation comes forth quickly and well, like His saying, And He caused it to grow a good vegetation, “And that which is bad brings forth nothing but bad,” Mujahid and others said, like salt marshes and the like. And Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse: This is an example that God gave for the believer and the disbeliever. 7:59: When the Almighty mentioned the story of Adam at the beginning of the Surah and what is related to that and connected to it and finished with it, the Almighty began to mention the stories of the prophets, peace be upon them, the first and the last. He began by mentioning Noah, peace be upon him, for he was the first messenger whom God sent to the people of the earth after Adam, peace be upon him. He is Noah, son of Lamech, son of Methuselah, son of Enoch, and he is Idris the Prophet, peace be upon him, according to what they claim. He was the first to write with a pen, son of Burd, son of Mahlil, son of Qanin, son of Yanish, son of Seth, son of Adam, peace be upon them. This is how Muhammad ibn Ishaq and more than one of the imams of lineage traced his lineage. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: No prophet from his people suffered as much harm as Noah, except for a prophet who was killed. Yazid al-Ruqashi said: He was called Noah because of the amount of time he mourned for himself. There were ten centuries between Adam and the time of Noah, peace be upon them, all of them Muslims. Abdullah bin Abbas and more than one of the scholars of interpretation said: The first time idols were worshipped was when righteous people died, so their people built mosques over them and made pictures of those people in them so that they would remember their state and their worship and resemble them. When time passed, they made bodies in those pictures. When time passed, they worshipped those idols and named them after the names of those righteous al-Nas 114:Wadd, Suwa’, Yaghuth, Ya’uq, and Nasr. When the matter became serious, God Almighty, praise and thanks be to Him, sent His Messenger Noah, who commanded them to worship God alone, with no partner for Him. He said: “O my people, worship God; you have no god other than Him. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a tremendous Day.” That is, the punishment of the Day of Resurrection when you meet God while you are associating partners with Him. The leaders of the His people, meaning the public, the masters, the leaders and the notables among them, “Indeed, we see you in manifest error, meaning in your calling us to abandon the worship of these idols that we found our fathers upon. This is the state of the wicked. They only see the righteous in error, as He says, And when they see them, they say, ‘Indeed, these are the ones who have gone astray.’ “And those who disbelieve say to those who believe, ‘If it had been good, they would not have preceded us to it.’ And since they were not guided by it, they will say, ‘This is an ancient falsehood.’” And other verses, He said, ‘O my people, there is no error in me, but I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds.’ That is, I am not astray, but I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of everything and its King. I convey to you the messages of my Lord and advise you, and I know from God that which you do not know. This is the nature of the Messenger, that he be an eloquent, sincere conveyor of God, knowledgeable of God, whom none of God’s creation can reach in these qualities, as it came in Sahih Muslim that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to his companions on the Day of Arafah, and they were the most numerous and most numerous, O people, you are asked about me, so what will you say? They said, We bear witness that you have conveyed the message, fulfilled your duty, and given sincere advice. So he raised his finger to the sky and lowered it to them, saying, “O God, bear witness. O God, bear witness.”

The verse, meaning do not be amazed by this, for this is not surprising that God would inspire a man from among you with mercy, kindness, and goodness to you, to warn you and so that you may fear God’s vengeance and not associate others with Him, and perhaps you will receive mercy. God Almighty says, But they denied him, meaning they persisted in denying him and opposing him, and only a few of them believed with him, as He stated in another place. So We saved him and those with him in the ark, meaning the ship, as He said: So We saved him and the people of the ark, and We drowned those who denied Our signs, as He said, Because of their sins they were drowned, so they were put into the Fire, and they found for themselves no helpers besides God. And His statement, Indeed, they were a blind people, meaning from the truth, they did not see it nor were they guided to it. So God Almighty explained in this story that He took revenge for His friends from His enemies and saved His Messenger and the believers and destroyed their enemies from the disbelievers, as He said: We will surely support Our messengers the verse. This is the way of God with His servants in this world and the hereafter, that the outcome is for the righteous, and victory and triumph are theirs, just as He destroyed the people of Noah by drowning, and saved Noah and his believing companions. Malik said on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, The people of Noah found the plains and mountains too narrow for them. Abd al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said, God did not punish the people of Noah except that the earth was filled with them, and there was no spot on earth that did not have a possessor or a possessor. Ibn Wahb said, It reached me on the authority of Ibn Abbas that eighty men were saved with Noah in the ship, one of whom was a Jurhum, and his tongue was Arabic. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim, and it was narrated in a connected chain of transmission from another source on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both.

The Hadrami said: What is the matter with him, O Commander of the Faithful? He said: In it is the grave of Hud, peace be upon him. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. 7:70: The Almighty tells about their rebellion, tyranny, stubbornness and denial of Hud, peace be upon him, They said, ‘Have you come to us so that we may worship God alone?’ The verse is like the words of the infidels of Quraysh, When they said, ‘O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment.’ Muhammad ibn Ishaq and others mentioned that they used to worship idols, one of which was called Samad, another called Samud, and another called Al-Haba. For this reason, Hud, peace be upon him, said, There has fallen upon you from your Lord an impurity and wrath. That is, because of your statement, an impurity from your Lord has fallen upon you. It is said that it is inverted from rajz. According to Ibn Abbas, it means anger and wrath. Do you argue with me about names that you and your fathers have named? That is, do you argue with me about these idols that you and your fathers have named as gods, and they do not harm or benefit, and God has not given you any proof or evidence for their worship. For this reason, he said, God has not sent down any authority for them? So wait, for I am with you. “From those who are waiting.” This is a threat and warning from the Messenger to his people, and that is why he followed it up by saying, So We saved him and those with him by mercy from Us, and We eliminated the root of those who denied Our signs and were not believers. God the Almighty mentioned the description of their destruction in other places in the Qur’an, that He sent upon them a barren wind that left nothing it came upon except that it made it like ashes, as He said in another verse: “As for ‘Aad, they were destroyed by a furious, violent wind. He subjected it to them for seven nights and eight days in succession. So you would see the people therein fallen down as if they were hollow trunks of palm trees. Do you see any remnant of them?” When they rebelled and were insolent, God destroyed them with a violent wind that would lift a man among them and raise him up in the air, then turn him over on his head and smash his head until it separated him from his body. For this reason He said: As if they were hollow trunks of palm trees. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said that they lived in Yemen between Oman and Hadhramaut, and despite that, they had spread throughout the land and subdued its people by virtue of the strength that God had given them. They were idolaters who worshipped them instead of God, so God sent to them Hud, peace be upon him, who was from the most noble of them in lineage and the best of them in position. He commanded them to unify God and not to associate others with Him. And they refused and denied him and said, Who is stronger than us in strength? And a group of them followed him, but they were few in number, concealing their faith. But when 'Aad rebelled against God and denied His Prophet and spread corruption in the land and acted tyrannically and built on every high place a sign in vain, without benefit. Hud spoke to them and said, "Do you build on every high place a sign, amusingly? And take for yourselves lofty palaces that you may live forever? And when you strike, you strike like tyrants. So fear God and obey me." They said, "O Hud, you have not brought us clear proof, nor will we abandon our gods because of your word, nor will we believe you. We only say that some of our gods have afflicted you with evil," meaning madness. He said, "Indeed, I call God to witness, and you to witness, that I am innocent of what you associate with Him. So plot against me all together, then do not respite. Indeed, I have put my trust in God, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature but that He holds it by the forelock. Indeed, my Lord is on a straight path." Muhammad bin Ishaq said: When they refused to disbelieve in him, God withheld rain from them for three years, as they claim, until that exhausted them. He said: When people were exhausted by a matter at that time and asked God for relief in it, they only asked Him for the sanctity and location of His House, which was well-known among the people of that time. The Amalekites resided there, and they were from the lineage of Amalek bin Lawdh bin Sam bin Noah. Their master at that time was a man called Hal Muawiyah bin Bakr, and he had a mother from the people of Aad, and her name was Kalhada bint Al-Khaibari. He said: So Aad sent a delegation of about seventy men to the sanctuary to pray for rain for them at the sanctuary. They passed by Muawiyah bin Bakr outside Mecca, and they descended upon him and stayed with him for a month, drinking wine and being sung to by two locusts: two female singers belonging to Muawiyah. They had reached him in a month. When their stay with him was prolonged and he was overcome by compassion for his people and was too shy to order them to leave, he composed a poem in which he urged them to leave and ordered the two female singers to sing it to them, so he said: Oh Qayl, woe to you! Get up and sleep, perhaps God will make us cloudy in the morning. And he waters the land of Aad, for Aad have become speechless. From extreme thirst, and we do not hope for it for the old man or the young man Their women were fine, but now their women are poor. The beasts come to them openly, and they do not fear the arrows of the enemy. And you are here, doing whatever you desire, all day and all night. Your delegation is worse than the delegation of a people who did not receive greetings and peace. He said: Then the people became aware of what they came for, so they rose up at the sanctuary and called out for their people. Their caller, who was Qayl ibn Anz, called out, and God created three clouds, white, black, and red. Then a caller from the sky called out to him, Choose for yourself or your people from this cloud. He said, I have chosen this black cloud, for it contains the most water. Then a caller called out to him, “You have chosen ashes and ash. It will not leave anyone from ‘Ad, neither father nor son, except that you will make them Hamdan, except for Banu al-Lawdhiyyah al-Muhandis.” He said, Banu al-Lawdhiyyah is a clan of ‘Ad who reside in Mecca, but what happened to their people did not happen to them. He said, And they are the ones who remained of their descendants and offspring, the ‘Ad of the Hereafter. He said, “And God drove the black cloud, as they say, which Qayl ibn ‘Az chose, with all the punishment in it, to ‘Ad until it emerged upon them from a valley called al-Mughith. When they saw it, they were filled with joy and said, ‘This is a cloud bringing us rain.’ He said, “Rather, it is that which you were hastening upon, a wind in which is a painful punishment. It destroys everything.” That is, it destroys everything. It passed by him and the first to see what was in it and knew that it was a wind, as they say, was a woman from Aad called Mumaid. When she realized what was in it, she cried out and then fainted. When she regained consciousness, they said, What did you see, O Mumaid? She said, A wind in which there was something like fire, with men leading it. So God subjected it to them for seven nights and eight days in decisive battle, as God Almighty said. And the decisive battles are permanent and did not leave anyone from Aad except that they perished. And Hud, peace be upon him, and the believers with him secluded themselves in a pen, as I was told, and nothing befell him or those with him except that which softens the skins and delights the souls. And it would pass by Aad in the desert between the sky and the earth and crush them with stones. And he mentioned the entire story in its entirety, and it is a strange context with many benefits. And God Almighty said: And when Our command came, We saved Hud and those who believed with him by mercy from Us, and We saved them from a severe punishment. It was reported in the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad, similar to what was reported by Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar, may God have mercy on him. Imam Ahmad said: Zaid ibn al-Habbab told us, Abu al-Mundhir Salam ibn Sulayman al-Nahwi told us, Asim ibn Abi al-Najud told us, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of al-Harith al-Bakri, who said: I went out to complain to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about al-Ala’ ibn al-Hadrami. I passed by al-Rabdhah, and there was an old woman from Banu Tamim who was stranded there. She said to me: O servant of God, I have a need from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Will you deliver it to him? I carried her and came to Madinah. There was a mosque full of people, a black banner fluttering, and Bilal was wearing a sword in front of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. I said: What is the matter with the people? They said: He wants to send Amr ibn al-Aas as a commander. I sat down and he entered his house, or he said his tent, and I asked permission to enter, and he gave me permission. I entered and greeted him, and he said: Is there anything between you and Tamim? I said: Yes, and we had the upper hand over them. I passed by an old woman from Banu Tamim who was stranded there and she asked me to carry her to you. Here she is at the door, so give her permission and she entered. I said, O Messenger of God, if you see that you should make a barrier between us and Tamim, then make it Dahna. The old woman became angry and became agitated and said, O Messenger of God, where will your needy person go? He said, “I am like what the first one said: A goat that carried its death, carried this one and I do not feel that it was an opponent to me. I seek refuge in God and His Messenger from being like the delegation of ‘Ad.” He said to me, And what is the delegation of ‘Ad? He was more knowledgeable about hadith than him, but he tasted it. I said, “‘Ad suffered a drought, so they sent a delegation of theirs called Qil. He passed by Mu’awiyah ibn Bakr and stayed with him for a month, giving him wine to drink and singing to him two girls called the two jaradats. When the month had passed, he went out to the mountains of Mahra and said, ‘O God, You know that I have not come to a sick person to treat him, nor to a prisoner to ransom him.’” O God, give ‘Aad what you used to give them to drink. Then black clouds passed by him and he was called from among them, Choose. So he pointed to one of the black clouds and he was called from among them, Take it, ashes, blackened, do not leave anyone from ‘Aad. He said, I did not hear that God sent upon them a wind except as much as runs through this ring of mine, until they perished. Abu Wa’il said, and he was truthful. He said: When a man or a woman sent a delegation to them, they would say, Do not be like the delegation of ‘Ad. This is how Imam Ahmad narrated it in Al-Musnad. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Abd ibn Humayd on the authority of Zayd ibn Al-Habbab, with a similar chain of transmission. Al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Salam ibn Abi Al-Mundhir on the authority of Asim, who is Ibn Bahdalah. Ibn Majah also narrated it on the authority of Abu Wa’il on the authority of Al-Harith ibn Hassan Al-Bakri on his authority. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Abu Kurayb on the authority of Zayd ibn Hubab, with a chain of transmission that he had, on the authority of Al-Harith ibn Yazid Al-Bakri, so he mentioned it. He also narrated it on the authority of Abu Kurayb on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash on the authority of Asim on the authority of Al-Harith ibn Hassan Al-Bakri, so he mentioned it. I did not see Abu Wa’il in the copy, and God knows best.
