I seek refuge in God and His Messenger from being like the delegation of ‘Ad.” He said to me, And what is the delegation of ‘Ad? He was more knowledgeable about hadith than him, but he tasted it. I said, “‘Ad suffered a drought, so they sent a delegation of theirs called Qil. He passed by Mu’awiyah ibn Bakr and stayed with him for a month, giving him wine to drink and singing to him two girls called the two jaradats. When the month had passed, he went out to the mountains of Mahra and said, ‘O God, You know that I have not come to a sick person to treat him, nor to a prisoner to ransom him.’” O God, give ‘Aad what you used to give them to drink. Then black clouds passed by him and he was called from among them, Choose. So he pointed to one of the black clouds and he was called from among them, Take it, ashes, blackened, do not leave anyone from ‘Aad. He said, I did not hear that God sent upon them a wind except as much as runs through this ring of mine, until they perished. Abu Wa’il said, and he was truthful. He said: When a man or a woman sent a delegation to them, they would say, Do not be like the delegation of ‘Ad. This is how Imam Ahmad narrated it in Al-Musnad. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Abd ibn Humayd on the authority of Zayd ibn Al-Habbab, with a similar chain of transmission. Al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Salam ibn Abi Al-Mundhir on the authority of Asim, who is Ibn Bahdalah. Ibn Majah also narrated it on the authority of Abu Wa’il on the authority of Al-Harith ibn Hassan Al-Bakri on his authority. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Abu Kurayb on the authority of Zayd ibn Hubab, with a chain of transmission that he had, on the authority of Al-Harith ibn Yazid Al-Bakri, so he mentioned it. He also narrated it on the authority of Abu Kurayb on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash on the authority of Asim on the authority of Al-Harith ibn Hassan Al-Bakri, so he mentioned it. I did not see Abu Wa’il in the copy, and God knows best.
7:72: The Almighty tells about their rebellion, tyranny, stubbornness and denial of Hud, peace be upon him, They said, ‘Have you come to us so that we may worship God alone?’ The verse is like the words of the infidels of Quraysh, When they said, ‘O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment.’ Muhammad ibn Ishaq and others mentioned that they used to worship idols, one of which was called Samad, another called Samud, and another called Al-Haba. For this reason, Hud, peace be upon him, said, There has fallen upon you from your Lord an impurity and wrath. That is, because of your statement, an impurity from your Lord has fallen upon you. It is said that it is inverted from rajz. According to Ibn Abbas, it means anger and wrath. Do you argue with me about names that you and your fathers have named? That is, do you argue with me about these idols that you and your fathers have named as gods, and they do not harm or benefit, and God has not given you any proof or evidence for their worship. For this reason, he said, God has not sent down any authority for them? So wait, for I am with you. “From those who are waiting.” This is a threat and warning from the Messenger to his people, and that is why he followed it up by saying, So We saved him and those with him by mercy from Us, and We eliminated the root of those who denied Our signs and were not believers. God the Almighty mentioned the description of their destruction in other places in the Qur’an, that He sent upon them a barren wind that left nothing it came upon except that it made it like ashes, as He said in another verse: “As for ‘Aad, they were destroyed by a furious, violent wind. He subjected it to them for seven nights and eight days in succession. So you would see the people therein fallen down as if they were hollow trunks of palm trees. Do you see any remnant of them?” When they rebelled and were insolent, God destroyed them with a violent wind that would lift a man among them and raise him up in the air, then turn him over on his head and smash his head until it separated him from his body. For this reason He said: As if they were hollow trunks of palm trees. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said that they lived in Yemen between Oman and Hadhramaut, and despite that, they had spread throughout the land and subdued its people by virtue of the strength that God had given them. They were idolaters who worshipped them instead of God, so God sent to them Hud, peace be upon him, who was from the most noble of them in lineage and the best of them in position. He commanded them to unify God and not to associate others with Him. And they refused and denied him and said, Who is stronger than us in strength? And a group of them followed him, but they were few in number, concealing their faith. But when 'Aad rebelled against God and denied His Prophet and spread corruption in the land and acted tyrannically and built on every high place a sign in vain, without benefit. Hud spoke to them and said, "Do you build on every high place a sign, amusingly? And take for yourselves lofty palaces that you may live forever? And when you strike, you strike like tyrants. So fear God and obey me." They said, "O Hud, you have not brought us clear proof, nor will we abandon our gods because of your word, nor will we believe you. We only say that some of our gods have afflicted you with evil," meaning madness. He said, "Indeed, I call God to witness, and you to witness, that I am innocent of what you associate with Him. So plot against me all together, then do not respite. Indeed, I have put my trust in God, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature but that He holds it by the forelock. Indeed, my Lord is on a straight path." Muhammad bin Ishaq said: When they refused to disbelieve in him, God withheld rain from them for three years, as they claim, until that exhausted them. He said: When people were exhausted by a matter at that time and asked God for relief in it, they only asked Him for the sanctity and location of His House, which was well-known among the people of that time. The Amalekites resided there, and they were from the lineage of Amalek bin Lawdh bin Sam bin Noah. Their master at that time was a man called Hal Muawiyah bin Bakr, and he had a mother from the people of Aad, and her name was Kalhada bint Al-Khaibari. He said: So Aad sent a delegation of about seventy men to the sanctuary to pray for rain for them at the sanctuary. They passed by Muawiyah bin Bakr outside Mecca, and they descended upon him and stayed with him for a month, drinking wine and being sung to by two locusts: two female singers belonging to Muawiyah. They had reached him in a month. When their stay with him was prolonged and he was overcome by compassion for his people and was too shy to order them to leave, he composed a poem in which he urged them to leave and ordered the two female singers to sing it to them, so he said: Oh Qayl, woe to you! Get up and sleep, perhaps God will make us cloudy in the morning. And he waters the land of Aad, for Aad have become speechless. From extreme thirst, and we do not hope for it for the old man or the young man Their women were fine, but now their women are poor. The beasts come to them openly, and they do not fear the arrows of the enemy. And you are here, doing whatever you desire, all day and all night. Your delegation is worse than the delegation of a people who did not receive greetings and peace. He said: Then the people became aware of what they came for, so they rose up at the sanctuary and called out for their people. Their caller, who was Qayl ibn Anz, called out, and God created three clouds, white, black, and red. Then a caller from the sky called out to him, Choose for yourself or your people from this cloud. He said, I have chosen this black cloud, for it contains the most water. Then a caller called out to him, “You have chosen ashes and ash. It will not leave anyone from ‘Ad, neither father nor son, except that you will make them Hamdan, except for Banu al-Lawdhiyyah al-Muhandis.” He said, Banu al-Lawdhiyyah is a clan of ‘Ad who reside in Mecca, but what happened to their people did not happen to them. He said, And they are the ones who remained of their descendants and offspring, the ‘Ad of the Hereafter. He said, “And God drove the black cloud, as they say, which Qayl ibn ‘Az chose, with all the punishment in it, to ‘Ad until it emerged upon them from a valley called al-Mughith. When they saw it, they were filled with joy and said, ‘This is a cloud bringing us rain.’ He said, “Rather, it is that which you were hastening upon, a wind in which is a painful punishment. It destroys everything.” That is, it destroys everything. It passed by him and the first to see what was in it and knew that it was a wind, as they say, was a woman from Aad called Mumaid. When she realized what was in it, she cried out and then fainted. When she regained consciousness, they said, What did you see, O Mumaid? She said, A wind in which there was something like fire, with men leading it. So God subjected it to them for seven nights and eight days in decisive battle, as God Almighty said. And the decisive battles are permanent and did not leave anyone from Aad except that they perished. And Hud, peace be upon him, and the believers with him secluded themselves in a pen, as I was told, and nothing befell him or those with him except that which softens the skins and delights the souls. And it would pass by Aad in the desert between the sky and the earth and crush them with stones. And he mentioned the entire story in its entirety, and it is a strange context with many benefits. And God Almighty said: And when Our command came, We saved Hud and those who believed with him by mercy from Us, and We saved them from a severe punishment. It was reported in the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad, similar to what was reported by Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar, may God have mercy on him. Imam Ahmad said: Zaid ibn al-Habbab told us, Abu al-Mundhir Salam ibn Sulayman al-Nahwi told us, Asim ibn Abi al-Najud told us, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of al-Harith al-Bakri, who said: I went out to complain to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about al-Ala’ ibn al-Hadrami. I passed by al-Rabdhah, and there was an old woman from Banu Tamim who was stranded there. She said to me: O servant of God, I have a need from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Will you deliver it to him? I carried her and came to Madinah. There was a mosque full of people, a black banner fluttering, and Bilal was wearing a sword in front of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. I said: What is the matter with the people? They said: He wants to send Amr ibn al-Aas as a commander. I sat down and he entered his house, or he said his tent, and I asked permission to enter, and he gave me permission. I entered and greeted him, and he said: Is there anything between you and Tamim? I said: Yes, and we had the upper hand over them. I passed by an old woman from Banu Tamim who was stranded there and she asked me to carry her to you. Here she is at the door, so give her permission and she entered. I said, O Messenger of God, if you see that you should make a barrier between us and Tamim, then make it Dahna. The old woman became angry and became agitated and said, O Messenger of God, where will your needy person go? He said, “I am like what the first one said: A goat that carried its death, carried this one and I do not feel that it was an opponent to me. I seek refuge in God and His Messenger from being like the delegation of ‘Ad.” He said to me, And what is the delegation of ‘Ad? He was more knowledgeable about hadith than him, but he tasted it. I said, “‘Ad suffered a drought, so they sent a delegation of theirs called Qil. He passed by Mu’awiyah ibn Bakr and stayed with him for a month, giving him wine to drink and singing to him two girls called the two jaradats. When the month had passed, he went out to the mountains of Mahra and said, ‘O God, You know that I have not come to a sick person to treat him, nor to a prisoner to ransom him.’” O God, give ‘Aad what you used to give them to drink. Then black clouds passed by him and he was called from among them, Choose. So he pointed to one of the black clouds and he was called from among them, Take it, ashes, blackened, do not leave anyone from ‘Aad. He said, I did not hear that God sent upon them a wind except as much as runs through this ring of mine, until they perished. Abu Wa’il said, and he was truthful. He said: When a man or a woman sent a delegation to them, they would say, Do not be like the delegation of ‘Ad. This is how Imam Ahmad narrated it in Al-Musnad. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Abd ibn Humayd on the authority of Zayd ibn Al-Habbab, with a similar chain of transmission. Al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Salam ibn Abi Al-Mundhir on the authority of Asim, who is Ibn Bahdalah. Ibn Majah also narrated it on the authority of Abu Wa’il on the authority of Al-Harith ibn Hassan Al-Bakri on his authority. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Abu Kurayb on the authority of Zayd ibn Hubab, with a chain of transmission that he had, on the authority of Al-Harith ibn Yazid Al-Bakri, so he mentioned it. He also narrated it on the authority of Abu Kurayb on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash on the authority of Asim on the authority of Al-Harith ibn Hassan Al-Bakri, so he mentioned it. I did not see Abu Wa’il in the copy, and God knows best.
7:73: The scholars of interpretation and genealogy said that Thamud bin Aathir bin Iram bin Sam bin Noah, who is the brother of Jadis bin Aathir, and the same was true of the tribe of Tasam. All of these were living Arabs before Abraham, peace be upon him. Thamud came after Aad, and their dwellings were famous between the Hijaz and the Levant to Wadi al-Qura and what was around it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by their homes and dwellings while he was going to Tabuk in the year nine. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Samad told us: Sakhr ibn Juwayriyah told us: Nafi’ told us: Ibn Umar said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, descended with the people to Tabuk, he descended with them to al-Hijr near the houses of Thamud. The people drew water from the wells from which Thamud used to drink, and they kneaded from them and set up pots for them. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered them to pour out the pots and feed the dough to the camels. Then he set out with them until he descended with them to the well from which the she-camel used to drink. He forbade them from entering upon the people who had been tortured, and said: I fear that you will be afflicted with what afflicted them, so do not enter upon them. Ahmad also said: Affan told us: Abd al-Aziz ibn Muslim told us: Abdullah ibn Dinar told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said while he was at al-Hijr 15:“Do not enter upon these tortured people unless you are crying. If you are not crying, then do not enter upon them, lest you be afflicted with what afflicted them.” The origin of this hadith is reported in the two Sahihs from more than one source. Imam Ahmad also said: Yazid bin Harun Al-Masoudi told us on the authority of Ismail bin Awsat on the authority of Muhammad bin Abi Kabsha Al-Anmari on the authority of his father who said: When there was a battle in Tabuk, people rushed to the people of Al-Hijr to enter upon them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard about that, so he called out to the al-Nas 114:Prayer is in congregation. He said: So I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he was holding a goat and he was saying: Why do you enter upon a people with whom God is angry? A man from among them called out to him: We are amazed at them, O Messenger of God? He said: “Shall I not inform you of something more amazing than that? A man from among yourselves informs you of what happened before you and what will happen after you, so be upright and steadfast, for God does not care about your punishment at all. There will come a people who will not defend themselves at all.” None of the authors of the Sunnah narrated it. Abu Kabsha’s name is Umar ibn Sa’d, and it is said that his name is Aamer ibn Sa’d, and God knows best. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Uthman ibn Khathim, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by al-Hijr, he said: “Do not ask for signs, for the people of Salih asked for them, and it - meaning the she-camel - used to come back from this pass and go forth from that pass, but they rebelled against the command of their Lord and hamstrung it. It used to drink their water one day and they used to drink its milk one day, so they hamstrung it, and a shout seized them, and God extinguished from them all from under the sky except for one man who was in the sanctuary of God.” They said: Who is he, O Messenger of God? He said: Abu Righal, when he left the sanctuary, what happened to his people happened to him. This hadith is not in any of the six books, and it meets the conditions of Muslim. God the Almighty said: And to Thamud meaning, We had certainly sent to the tribe of Thamud their brother Salih. He said, ‘O my people, worship God; you have no deity other than Him.’ All the messengers called to worship God alone, with no partner, as God the Almighty said: And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him, ‘There is no deity except Me, so worship Me.’ And He said: And We have certainly sent to every nation a messenger, [saying], ‘Worship God and avoid false deities.’ And His statement: “There has come to you a clear proof from your Lord. This is the she-camel of God, a sign for you.” Meaning, there has come to you a proof from God that what I have brought you is true. They were the ones who asked Salih to bring them a sign, and they suggested to him that a she-camel should come out for them from a solid rock that they had identified themselves, and it was a separate rock in the corner of the rock called Al-Katibah. They asked him to bring out for them from it a pregnant she-camel that was giving birth. So Salih took covenants and pledges from them that if God answered their question and answered their request, they would believe in him and follow him. When they gave him their covenants and pledges, Salih stood up. Peace be upon him, he went to his prayer and called upon God Almighty, so that rock moved and then split open revealing a hollow she-camel and Bara’a’s fetus moving between her sides as they had asked. Then their leader Junda’ bin Amr and those who were with him believed in his command. The rest of the nobles of Thamud wanted to believe, but they were stopped by Dhu’ab bin Amr bin Labid, Al-Habbab, the owner of their idols, and Rbab bin Samar bin Jalhas. Junda’ bin Amr had a cousin called Shihab bin Khalifa bin Mukhalla bin Labid bin Jawas, who was one of the nobles and best of Thamud. He also wanted to convert to Islam, but those people forbade him, but he obeyed them. A man from the believers of Thamud called Mahwish bin Uthma bin Ad-Dumayl, may God have mercy on him, said about that: A group of the Al Amr family followed the religion of the Prophet and called him Shahab. Aziz Thamud, all of them together, understood that he should answer, so if they answered So that Saleh would become dear to us, and they would not treat their companion as equals. But the seducers of the Al-Hajar family turned away after their maturity as wolves. The she-camel and her foal stayed among them for a period of time, drinking from her well one day and leaving it for them the next. They would drink her milk the day they drank it, milking it and filling their vessels and containers as they wished, as He said in the other verse: And inform them that the water is to be divided among them, each drinking in turn. And the Most High said: This is a she-camel, for her is a drink, and for you is a drink on a known day. And she used to graze in some of those valleys, coming from one pass and coming from another, so that it would suffice her, because she used to get her fill of water. And as mentioned, she was a formidable creature and a wonderful sight. When that went on for a long time and their denial of the Prophet’s favor became intense, they resolved to kill her so that they could keep the water for themselves every day. It is said that they all agreed to kill her. Qatada said: It reached me that the one who killed her went around to them all, and they were satisfied with killing her, even the women in their chambers and the children. I said: This is what is apparent from the words of the Most High: But they denied him, so they hamstrung her, so their Lord destroyed them for their sin and leveled her. He said, And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign, but they wronged her. And he said, So they hamstrung the she-camel. So he attributed that to the entire tribe, which indicates that all of them were satisfied with that, and God knows best. Imam Abu Jaafar bin Jarir and other scholars of interpretation mentioned that the reason for her killing was that a woman from them called Unayzah bint Ghanim bin Majlaz, who was nicknamed Umm Ghanim, was an old infidel and was one of the most hostile people to Salih, peace be upon him. She had beautiful daughters and a lot of money. Her husband was Dhu’ab bin Amr, one of the chiefs of Thamud. There was another woman called Saduf bint Al-Muhaya bin Zuhair bin Al-Mukhtar, who was of noble lineage, money and beauty. She was married to a Muslim man from Thamud, but she left him. They used to make a promise to whoever pledged to them to kill the she-camel. Saduf called a man called Al-Habbab and offered herself to him if he would hamstring the she-camel, but he refused. She called her cousin called Musadd’ bin Mihraj bin Al-Muhaya, and he agreed to do so. Unayzah bint Ghanim called Qadar bin Salaf bin Jad’a, who was a short, red-haired man. They claimed that he was the son of fornication and that he was not from his father, to whom he was attributed, who is Salaf, but rather from a man called Sahyad, but he was born on Salaf’s bed. She said to him, I will give you any of my daughters you wish, provided that you hamstring the she-camel. Then, Qudar bin Salaf and Musda’ bin Muharij set out and seduced the seducers of Thamud. Seven men followed them, and they became nine men, and they are the ones about whom God Almighty said: And there were in the city nine men who spread corruption in the land and did not reform. They were leaders among their people, so they won over the entire disbelieving tribe, and they obeyed them in that. They set out and watched the she-camel when she came out of the water. Qudar bin Salaf had ambushed her at the base of a rock on her way, and Musda’ had ambushed her at the base of another. She passed by Musda’, so he shot her with an arrow, and it pierced her leg muscle. Umm Ghanem of Unaizah came out and ordered her daughter, who was one of the most beautiful people, to uncover her face for Qudar and his arm. He attacked the she-camel with the sword, uncovering her hock, so she fell to the ground and bellowed once, fearing her foal. Then he stabbed her in the heart and slaughtered her, and her foal, which was her young foal, set out until he came. A fortified mountain, so he climbed the highest rock in it and roared. Abdul Razzaq narrated on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of someone who heard Al-Hasan Al-Basri, that he said: O Lord, where is my mother? And it is said that he roared three times and that he entered a rock and disappeared in it. And it is said that they followed him and hamstrung him and his mother, and God knows best. So when they did that and finished hamstringing the she-camel, the report reached Salih, peace be upon him, so he came to them while they were gathered. When he saw the she-camel, he cried and said: Enjoy yourselves in your home for three days the verse. And they killed the she-camel on Wednesday, and when the evening came, those nine men resolved to kill Salih and said: If he is truthful, we will hasten him before us, and if he is lying, we will catch up with his she-camel. They said, “Swear by God that we will surely kill him and his family by night, and then we will say to his heir, ‘We did not witness the destruction of his family, and indeed, we are truthful.’ And they planned a plan, and We planned a plan, and they did not perceive. So see how was the end of their plan.” The verse. So when they resolved to do that and conspired to do it and came at night to kill the Prophet of God, God Almighty - and to Him belongs glory and to His Messenger - sent upon them stones that crushed them in advance and hastened before their people. And Thamud woke up on Thursday, which was the first day of the days of reprieve, and their faces were yellow as Salih had promised them, and they woke up on the second day of the days of postponement, which was Friday, and their faces were red, and they woke up on the third day of the days of enjoyment, which was Saturday, and their faces were black. So when they woke up on Sunday, they had embalmed themselves and sat down. They are waiting for the vengeance and punishment of God, may God protect us from that. They do not know what will happen to them or how the punishment will come to them. The sun rose and a shout came to them from the sky and a violent tremor from below them, so the souls departed and the spirits were lost in one hour. So they became in their homes, prostrated, meaning dead, with no souls in them. Not one of them escaped, neither young nor old, male nor female. They said: Except for a girl who was crippled and her name was Kalba bint al-Salq, and she was called al-Zariqa. She was a disbeliever and a fierce enemy of Salih, peace be upon him. When she saw what she saw of the punishment, she released her legs and she ran as fast as anything. She came to a neighborhood and told them what she had seen and what had happened to her people. Then she asked them for water, but when she drank, she died. The scholars of interpretation said: None of the descendants of Thamud remained except Salih, peace be upon him, and those who followed him, may God be pleased with them, except for a man called Abu Righal, who, when the punishment befell his people, was staying at that time in the sanctuary and nothing happened to him. Then when he went out to the open area one day, a stone came from the sky and killed him. The hadith of Jabir ibn Abdullah about that was mentioned at the beginning of the story, and they mentioned that this Abu Righal was the father of Thaqeef who lived in Taif. Abd al-Razzaq said on the authority of Muammar: Ismail ibn Umayya informed me that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by the grave of Abu Righal and said, Do you know who this is? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: “This is the grave of Abu Righal, a man from Thamud who was in the sanctuary of God, but the sanctuary of God prevented him from the punishment of God. When he came out, what happened to his people happened to him, so he was buried here, and with him was buried a branch of gold. The people came down and rushed to him with their swords, and they searched for it and extracted the branch.” And Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar said: al-Zuhri said: Abu Righal is Abu Thaqif. This is mursal from this source. It was narrated in a connected manner from another source, as Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: On the authority of Ismail ibn Umayyah, on the authority of Bajir ibn Abi Bajir, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Amr say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: When we went out with him to Taif, we passed by a grave, and he said: “This is the grave of Abu Righal, who is Abu Thaqeef, and he was from Thamud, and he was in this sanctuary, so he was protected from it. When he went out, the punishment that befell his people in this place befell him, so he was buried in it, and the sign of that is that a branch of gold was buried with him. If you dig it up, you will find it. So the people rushed to it and extracted the branch from it.” And this is how Abu Dawud narrated it, on the authority of Yahya ibn Ma’een, on the authority of Wahb ibn Jarir ibn Hazim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on his authority. Our Sheikh Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mizzi said: It is a good and noble hadith. I said Bajir ibn Abi Bajir was the only one who connected it, and he is a sheikh who is not known except for this hadith. Yahya ibn Ma’een said: I did not hear anyone narrate from him except Ismail ibn Umayyah. I said Based on this, it is feared that there was a mistake in raising it. This hadith. It could be from the words of Abdullah bin Amr, from what he took from the two Zamilites. Our Sheikh Abu Al-Hajjaj said after I presented that to him, and this is possible, and God knows best.
7:74: The scholars of interpretation and genealogy said that Thamud bin Aathir bin Iram bin Sam bin Noah, who is the brother of Jadis bin Aathir, and the same was true of the tribe of Tasam. All of these were living Arabs before Abraham, peace be upon him. Thamud came after Aad, and their dwellings were famous between the Hijaz and the Levant to Wadi al-Qura and what was around it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by their homes and dwellings while he was going to Tabuk in the year nine. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Samad told us: Sakhr ibn Juwayriyah told us: Nafi’ told us: Ibn Umar said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, descended with the people to Tabuk, he descended with them to al-Hijr near the houses of Thamud. The people drew water from the wells from which Thamud used to drink, and they kneaded from them and set up pots for them. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered them to pour out the pots and feed the dough to the camels. Then he set out with them until he descended with them to the well from which the she-camel used to drink. He forbade them from entering upon the people who had been tortured, and said: I fear that you will be afflicted with what afflicted them, so do not enter upon them. A man from among yourselves informs you of what happened before you and what will happen after you, so be upright and steadfast, for God does not care about your punishment at all. There was another woman called Saduf bint Al-Muhaya bin Zuhair bin Al-Mukhtar, who was of noble lineage, money and beauty. She was married to a Muslim man from Thamud, but she left him. She called her cousin called Musadd’ bin Mihraj bin Al-Muhaya, and he agreed to do so. Unayzah bint Ghanim called Qadar bin Salaf bin Jad’a, who was a short, red-haired man. They claimed that he was the son of fornication and that he was not from his father, to whom he was attributed, who is Salaf, but rather from a man called Sahyad, but he was born on Salaf’s bed. Seven men followed them, and they became nine men, and they are the ones about whom God Almighty said: And there were in the city nine men who spread corruption in the land and did not reform. They were leaders among their people, so they won over the entire disbelieving tribe, and they obeyed them in that. They set out and watched the she-camel when she came out of the water. Qudar bin Salaf had ambushed her at the base of a rock on her way, and Musda’ had ambushed her at the base of another. She passed by Musda’, so he shot her with an arrow, and it pierced her leg muscle. Umm Ghanem of Unaizah came out and ordered her daughter, who was one of the most beautiful people, to uncover her face for Qudar and his arm. He attacked the she-camel with the sword, uncovering her hock, so she fell to the ground and bellowed once, fearing her foal. And it is said that he roared three times and that he entered a rock and disappeared in it. And it is said that they followed him and hamstrung him and his mother, and God knows best. So when they did that and finished hamstringing the she-camel, the report reached Salih, peace be upon him, so he came to them while they were gathered. When he saw the she-camel, he cried and said: Enjoy yourselves in your home for three days the verse. And they killed the she-camel on Wednesday, and when the evening came, those nine men resolved to kill Salih and said: If he is truthful, we will hasten him before us, and if he is lying, we will catch up with his she-camel. They said, “Swear by God that we will surely kill him and his family by night, and then we will say to his heir, ‘We did not witness the destruction of his family, and indeed, we are truthful.’ And they planned a plan, and We planned a plan, and they did not perceive. So see how was the end of their plan.” The verse. So when they resolved to do that and conspired to do it and came at night to kill the Prophet of God, God Almighty - and to Him belongs glory and to His Messenger - sent upon them stones that crushed them in advance and hastened before their people. And Thamud woke up on Thursday, which was the first day of the days of reprieve, and their faces were yellow as Salih had promised them, and they woke up on the second day of the days of postponement, which was Friday, and their faces were red, and they woke up on the third day of the days of enjoyment, which was Saturday, and their faces were black. So when they woke up on Sunday, they had embalmed themselves and sat down. They are waiting for the vengeance and punishment of God, may God protect us from that. They do not know what will happen to them or how the punishment will come to them. The sun rose and a shout came to them from the sky and a violent tremor from below them, so the souls departed and the spirits were lost in one hour. So they became in their homes, prostrated, meaning dead, with no souls in them. Not one of them escaped, neither young nor old, male nor female. They said: Except for a girl who was crippled and her name was Kalba bint al-Salq, and she was called al-Zariqa. She was a disbeliever and a fierce enemy of Salih, peace be upon him. When she saw what she saw of the punishment, she released her legs and she ran as fast as anything. She came to a neighborhood and told them what she had seen and what had happened to her people. Then she asked them for water, but when she drank, she died. Then when he went out to the open area one day, a stone came from the sky and killed him. Abd al-Razzaq said on the authority of Muammar: Ismail ibn Umayya informed me that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by the grave of Abu Righal and said, Do you know who this is? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: “This is the grave of Abu Righal, a man from Thamud who was in the sanctuary of God, but the sanctuary of God prevented him from the punishment of God. When he came out, what happened to his people happened to him, so he was buried here, and with him was buried a branch of gold. The people came down and rushed to him with their swords, and they searched for it and extracted the branch.” And Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar said: al-Zuhri said: Abu Righal is Abu Thaqif. This is mursal from this source. It was narrated in a connected manner from another source, as Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: On the authority of Ismail ibn Umayyah, on the authority of Bajir ibn Abi Bajir, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Amr say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: When we went out with him to Taif, we passed by a grave, and he said: “This is the grave of Abu Righal, who is Abu Thaqeef, and he was from Thamud, and he was in this sanctuary, so he was protected from it. When he went out, the punishment that befell his people in this place befell him, so he was buried in it, and the sign of that is that a branch of gold was buried with him. If you dig it up, you will find it. So the people rushed to it and extracted the branch from it.” And this is how Abu Dawud narrated it, on the authority of Yahya ibn Ma’een, on the authority of Wahb ibn Jarir ibn Hazim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on his authority. Our Sheikh Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mizzi said: It is a good and noble hadith. I said Bajir ibn Abi Bajir was the only one who connected it, and he is a sheikh who is not known except for this hadith. Yahya ibn Ma’een said: I did not hear anyone narrate from him except Ismail ibn Umayyah. I said Based on this, it is feared that there was a mistake in raising it. This hadith. It could be from the words of Abdullah bin Amr, from what he took from the two Zamilites. Our Sheikh Abu Al-Hajjaj said after I presented that to him, and this is possible, and God knows best.

The people came down and rushed to him with their swords, and they searched for it and extracted the branch.” And Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar said: al-Zuhri said: Abu Righal is Abu Thaqif. This is mursal from this source. It was narrated in a connected manner from another source, as Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: On the authority of Ismail ibn Umayyah, on the authority of Bajir ibn Abi Bajir, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Amr say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: When we went out with him to Taif, we passed by a grave, and he said: “This is the grave of Abu Righal, who is Abu Thaqeef, and he was from Thamud, and he was in this sanctuary, so he was protected from it. When he went out, the punishment that befell his people in this place befell him, so he was buried in it, and the sign of that is that a branch of gold was buried with him. If you dig it up, you will find it. So the people rushed to it and extracted the branch from it.” And this is how Abu Dawud narrated it, on the authority of Yahya ibn Ma’een, on the authority of Wahb ibn Jarir ibn Hazim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on his authority. Our Sheikh Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mizzi said: It is a good and noble hadith. I said Bajir ibn Abi Bajir was the only one who connected it, and he is a sheikh who is not known except for this hadith. Yahya ibn Ma’een said: I did not hear anyone narrate from him except Ismail ibn Umayyah. I said Based on this, it is feared that there was a mistake in raising it. This hadith. It could be from the words of Abdullah bin Amr, from what he took from the two Zamilites. Our Sheikh Abu Al-Hajjaj said after I presented that to him, and this is possible, and God knows best.
7:78: The scholars of interpretation and genealogy said that Thamud bin Aathir bin Iram bin Sam bin Noah, who is the brother of Jadis bin Aathir, and the same was true of the tribe of Tasam. All of these were living Arabs before Abraham, peace be upon him. Thamud came after Aad, and their dwellings were famous between the Hijaz and the Levant to Wadi al-Qura and what was around it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by their homes and dwellings while he was going to Tabuk in the year nine. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Samad told us: Sakhr ibn Juwayriyah told us: Nafi’ told us: Ibn Umar said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, descended with the people to Tabuk, he descended with them to al-Hijr near the houses of Thamud. The people drew water from the wells from which Thamud used to drink, and they kneaded from them and set up pots for them. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered them to pour out the pots and feed the dough to the camels. Then he set out with them until he descended with them to the well from which the she-camel used to drink. He forbade them from entering upon the people who had been tortured, and said: I fear that you will be afflicted with what afflicted them, so do not enter upon them. Ahmad also said: Affan told us: Abd al-Aziz ibn Muslim told us: Abdullah ibn Dinar told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said while he was at al-Hijr 15:“Do not enter upon these tortured people unless you are crying. If you are not crying, then do not enter upon them, lest you be afflicted with what afflicted them.” The origin of this hadith is reported in the two Sahihs from more than one source. Imam Ahmad also said: Yazid bin Harun Al-Masoudi told us on the authority of Ismail bin Awsat on the authority of Muhammad bin Abi Kabsha Al-Anmari on the authority of his father who said: When there was a battle in Tabuk, people rushed to the people of Al-Hijr to enter upon them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard about that, so he called out to the al-Nas 114:Prayer is in congregation. He said: So I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he was holding a goat and he was saying: Why do you enter upon a people with whom God is angry? A man from among them called out to him: We are amazed at them, O Messenger of God? He said: “Shall I not inform you of something more amazing than that? A man from among yourselves informs you of what happened before you and what will happen after you, so be upright and steadfast, for God does not care about your punishment at all. There will come a people who will not defend themselves at all.” None of the authors of the Sunnah narrated it. Abu Kabsha’s name is Umar ibn Sa’d, and it is said that his name is Aamer ibn Sa’d, and God knows best. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Uthman ibn Khathim, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by al-Hijr, he said: “Do not ask for signs, for the people of Salih asked for them, and it - meaning the she-camel - used to come back from this pass and go forth from that pass, but they rebelled against the command of their Lord and hamstrung it. It used to drink their water one day and they used to drink its milk one day, so they hamstrung it, and a shout seized them, and God extinguished from them all from under the sky except for one man who was in the sanctuary of God.” They said: Who is he, O Messenger of God? He said: Abu Righal, when he left the sanctuary, what happened to his people happened to him. This hadith is not in any of the six books, and it meets the conditions of Muslim. God the Almighty said: And to Thamud meaning, We had certainly sent to the tribe of Thamud their brother Salih. He said, ‘O my people, worship God; you have no deity other than Him.’ All the messengers called to worship God alone, with no partner, as God the Almighty said: And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him, ‘There is no deity except Me, so worship Me.’ And He said: And We have certainly sent to every nation a messenger, [saying], ‘Worship God and avoid false deities.’ And His statement: “There has come to you a clear proof from your Lord. This is the she-camel of God, a sign for you.” Meaning, there has come to you a proof from God that what I have brought you is true. They were the ones who asked Salih to bring them a sign, and they suggested to him that a she-camel should come out for them from a solid rock that they had identified themselves, and it was a separate rock in the corner of the rock called Al-Katibah. They asked him to bring out for them from it a pregnant she-camel that was giving birth. So Salih took covenants and pledges from them that if God answered their question and answered their request, they would believe in him and follow him. When they gave him their covenants and pledges, Salih stood up. Peace be upon him, he went to his prayer and called upon God Almighty, so that rock moved and then split open revealing a hollow she-camel and Bara’a’s fetus moving between her sides as they had asked. Then their leader Junda’ bin Amr and those who were with him believed in his command. The rest of the nobles of Thamud wanted to believe, but they were stopped by Dhu’ab bin Amr bin Labid, Al-Habbab, the owner of their idols, and Rbab bin Samar bin Jalhas. Junda’ bin Amr had a cousin called Shihab bin Khalifa bin Mukhalla bin Labid bin Jawas, who was one of the nobles and best of Thamud. He also wanted to convert to Islam, but those people forbade him, but he obeyed them. A man from the believers of Thamud called Mahwish bin Uthma bin Ad-Dumayl, may God have mercy on him, said about that: A group of the Al Amr family followed the religion of the Prophet and called him Shahab. Aziz Thamud, all of them together, understood that he should answer, so if they answered So that Saleh would become dear to us, and they would not treat their companion as equals. But the seducers of the Al-Hajar family turned away after their maturity as wolves. The she-camel and her foal stayed among them for a period of time, drinking from her well one day and leaving it for them the next. They would drink her milk the day they drank it, milking it and filling their vessels and containers as they wished, as He said in the other verse: And inform them that the water is to be divided among them, each drinking in turn. And the Most High said: This is a she-camel, for her is a drink, and for you is a drink on a known day. And she used to graze in some of those valleys, coming from one pass and coming from another, so that it would suffice her, because she used to get her fill of water. And as mentioned, she was a formidable creature and a wonderful sight. When that went on for a long time and their denial of the Prophet’s favor became intense, they resolved to kill her so that they could keep the water for themselves every day. It is said that they all agreed to kill her. Qatada said: It reached me that the one who killed her went around to them all, and they were satisfied with killing her, even the women in their chambers and the children. I said: This is what is apparent from the words of the Most High: But they denied him, so they hamstrung her, so their Lord destroyed them for their sin and leveled her. He said, And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign, but they wronged her. And he said, So they hamstrung the she-camel. So he attributed that to the entire tribe, which indicates that all of them were satisfied with that, and God knows best. Imam Abu Jaafar bin Jarir and other scholars of interpretation mentioned that the reason for her killing was that a woman from them called Unayzah bint Ghanim bin Majlaz, who was nicknamed Umm Ghanim, was an old infidel and was one of the most hostile people to Salih, peace be upon him. She had beautiful daughters and a lot of money. Her husband was Dhu’ab bin Amr, one of the chiefs of Thamud. There was another woman called Saduf bint Al-Muhaya bin Zuhair bin Al-Mukhtar, who was of noble lineage, money and beauty. She was married to a Muslim man from Thamud, but she left him. They used to make a promise to whoever pledged to them to kill the she-camel. Saduf called a man called Al-Habbab and offered herself to him if he would hamstring the she-camel, but he refused. She called her cousin called Musadd’ bin Mihraj bin Al-Muhaya, and he agreed to do so. Unayzah bint Ghanim called Qadar bin Salaf bin Jad’a, who was a short, red-haired man. They claimed that he was the son of fornication and that he was not from his father, to whom he was attributed, who is Salaf, but rather from a man called Sahyad, but he was born on Salaf’s bed. She said to him, I will give you any of my daughters you wish, provided that you hamstring the she-camel. Then, Qudar bin Salaf and Musda’ bin Muharij set out and seduced the seducers of Thamud. Seven men followed them, and they became nine men, and they are the ones about whom God Almighty said: And there were in the city nine men who spread corruption in the land and did not reform. They were leaders among their people, so they won over the entire disbelieving tribe, and they obeyed them in that. They set out and watched the she-camel when she came out of the water. Qudar bin Salaf had ambushed her at the base of a rock on her way, and Musda’ had ambushed her at the base of another. She passed by Musda’, so he shot her with an arrow, and it pierced her leg muscle. Umm Ghanem of Unaizah came out and ordered her daughter, who was one of the most beautiful people, to uncover her face for Qudar and his arm. He attacked the she-camel with the sword, uncovering her hock, so she fell to the ground and bellowed once, fearing her foal. Then he stabbed her in the heart and slaughtered her, and her foal, which was her young foal, set out until he came. A fortified mountain, so he climbed the highest rock in it and roared. Abdul Razzaq narrated on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of someone who heard Al-Hasan Al-Basri, that he said: O Lord, where is my mother? And it is said that he roared three times and that he entered a rock and disappeared in it. And it is said that they followed him and hamstrung him and his mother, and God knows best. So when they did that and finished hamstringing the she-camel, the report reached Salih, peace be upon him, so he came to them while they were gathered. When he saw the she-camel, he cried and said: Enjoy yourselves in your home for three days the verse. And they killed the she-camel on Wednesday, and when the evening came, those nine men resolved to kill Salih and said: If he is truthful, we will hasten him before us, and if he is lying, we will catch up with his she-camel. They said, “Swear by God that we will surely kill him and his family by night, and then we will say to his heir, ‘We did not witness the destruction of his family, and indeed, we are truthful.’ And they planned a plan, and We planned a plan, and they did not perceive. So see how was the end of their plan.” The verse. So when they resolved to do that and conspired to do it and came at night to kill the Prophet of God, God Almighty - and to Him belongs glory and to His Messenger - sent upon them stones that crushed them in advance and hastened before their people. And Thamud woke up on Thursday, which was the first day of the days of reprieve, and their faces were yellow as Salih had promised them, and they woke up on the second day of the days of postponement, which was Friday, and their faces were red, and they woke up on the third day of the days of enjoyment, which was Saturday, and their faces were black. So when they woke up on Sunday, they had embalmed themselves and sat down. They are waiting for the vengeance and punishment of God, may God protect us from that. They do not know what will happen to them or how the punishment will come to them. The sun rose and a shout came to them from the sky and a violent tremor from below them, so the souls departed and the spirits were lost in one hour. So they became in their homes, prostrated, meaning dead, with no souls in them. Not one of them escaped, neither young nor old, male nor female. They said: Except for a girl who was crippled and her name was Kalba bint al-Salq, and she was called al-Zariqa. She was a disbeliever and a fierce enemy of Salih, peace be upon him. When she saw what she saw of the punishment, she released her legs and she ran as fast as anything. She came to a neighborhood and told them what she had seen and what had happened to her people. Then she asked them for water, but when she drank, she died. The scholars of interpretation said: None of the descendants of Thamud remained except Salih, peace be upon him, and those who followed him, may God be pleased with them, except for a man called Abu Righal, who, when the punishment befell his people, was staying at that time in the sanctuary and nothing happened to him. Then when he went out to the open area one day, a stone came from the sky and killed him. The hadith of Jabir ibn Abdullah about that was mentioned at the beginning of the story, and they mentioned that this Abu Righal was the father of Thaqeef who lived in Taif. Abd al-Razzaq said on the authority of Muammar: Ismail ibn Umayya informed me that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by the grave of Abu Righal and said, Do you know who this is? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: “This is the grave of Abu Righal, a man from Thamud who was in the sanctuary of God, but the sanctuary of God prevented him from the punishment of God. When he came out, what happened to his people happened to him, so he was buried here, and with him was buried a branch of gold. The people came down and rushed to him with their swords, and they searched for it and extracted the branch.” And Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar said: al-Zuhri said: Abu Righal is Abu Thaqif. This is mursal from this source. It was narrated in a connected manner from another source, as Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: On the authority of Ismail ibn Umayyah, on the authority of Bajir ibn Abi Bajir, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Amr say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: When we went out with him to Taif, we passed by a grave, and he said: “This is the grave of Abu Righal, who is Abu Thaqeef, and he was from Thamud, and he was in this sanctuary, so he was protected from it. When he went out, the punishment that befell his people in this place befell him, so he was buried in it, and the sign of that is that a branch of gold was buried with him. If you dig it up, you will find it. So the people rushed to it and extracted the branch from it.” And this is how Abu Dawud narrated it, on the authority of Yahya ibn Ma’een, on the authority of Wahb ibn Jarir ibn Hazim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on his authority. Our Sheikh Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mizzi said: It is a good and noble hadith. I said Bajir ibn Abi Bajir was the only one who connected it, and he is a sheikh who is not known except for this hadith. Yahya ibn Ma’een said: I did not hear anyone narrate from him except Ismail ibn Umayyah. I said Based on this, it is feared that there was a mistake in raising it. This hadith. It could be from the words of Abdullah bin Amr, from what he took from the two Zamilites. Our Sheikh Abu Al-Hajjaj said after I presented that to him, and this is possible, and God knows best.
7:79: This is a rebuke from Salih, peace be upon him, to his people, when God destroyed them for their disobedience to him and their rebellion against God and their refusal to accept the truth and their turning away from guidance to blindness. Salih said this to them after their destruction, as a rebuke and a rebuke while they were listening to it, as it was established in the two Sahihs that when the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, defeated the people of Badr, he stayed there for three days, then he ordered his mount to be saddled after three days at the end of the night, so he mounted it and then walked until he stopped at the well, the well of Badr, and he began to say, O Abu Jahl bin Hisham, O Utbah bin Rabi’ah, O Shaiba bin Rabi’ah, and O so-and-so, did you find what your Lord promised to be true? For I found what my Lord promised me to be true. So Omar said to him: O Messenger of God, what do you speak of people who have become corpses? He said, By Him in Whose Hand is my soul, you are not more attentive to what I say than they are, but they do not respond. In the biography, he, peace be upon him, said to them, “What a bad tribe you were to your Prophet! You called me a liar, yet the people believed me. You expelled me, yet the people gave me shelter. You fought me, yet the people supported me. So what a bad tribe you were to your Prophet.” Thus, Salih, peace be upon him, said to his people, I have conveyed to you the message of my Lord and advised you, meaning, you did not benefit from that because you do not love the truth and do not follow an advisor. That is why he said, But you do not love advisors. Some commentators have mentioned that every prophet whose nation perished would go and reside in the sanctuary, the sanctuary of Mecca. And God knows best. Imam Ahmad said: Waki’ told us, Zam’ah ibn Salih told us, on the authority of Salamah ibn Wahram, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by Wadi Usfan when he performed Hajj, he said, O Abu Bakr, what valley is this? He said, This is Wadi Usfan. He said, “Hud and Salih, peace be upon them, passed by it on camels with muzzles of palm fiber, their belts were cloaks and their robes were leopard print, chanting the talbiyah, performing Hajj to the Ancient House.” This is a strange hadith from this source, and none of them narrated it.
7:81: God Almighty says, And We sent Lot or its meaning is And remember Lot when he said to his people and Lot is the son of Haran bin Azar and he is the nephew of Abraham the friend of God, peace be upon them, and he had believed with Abraham, peace be upon him, and migrated with him to the land of Ash-Sham, so God sent him to the people of Sodom and the surrounding villages, calling them to God Almighty and commanding them to do good and forbidding them from what they were committing of sins, prohibitions and obscenities that they had invented and no one from the children of Adam or others had preceded them in, which is intercourse with males without females, and this is something that the children of Adam were not familiar with nor familiar with nor did it cross their minds, until the people of Sodom did it, may God's curses be upon them. Amr ibn Dinar said about his statement, No one in the worlds has preceded you with it, he said: No male has copulated with another male until the people of Lot. Al-Walid ibn Abd al-Malik, the Umayyad Caliph who built the Great Mosque of Damascus, said: If God Almighty had not told us the story of the people of Lot, I would not have thought that a male would mount another male. That is why Lot, peace be upon him, said to them, Do you commit such immorality as no one in the worlds has preceded you with? Indeed, you approach men with desire instead of women. That is, you have turned away from women and what your Lord created for you from them to men. This is extravagance and ignorance on your part because he put the thing in the wrong place. That is why he said to them in the other verse, These are my daughters, if you are to do so. So he directed them to their women, but they apologized to him by saying that they did not desire them. “They said, ‘Indeed, you know that we have no right to your daughters, and indeed, you know what we want. ’” That is, you know that we have no interest in women or desire, and indeed, you know what we want from your guests. The commentators mentioned that the men had become satisfied with each other, and their women had also become satisfied with each other. They also dispensed with each other.
7:82: That is, they did not respond to Lot except that they intended to expel him and those with him from among them, but God Almighty expelled him safely and destroyed them in their land, humiliated and disgraced. And the Almighty’s statement: Indeed, they are a people who purify themselves. Qatada said: They criticized them without any fault. Mujahid said: They are a people who purify themselves from the anuses of men and the anuses of women. And something similar was narrated from Ibn Abbas as well.
7:83: The Almighty says: "So We saved Lot and his family, and none of them believed in him except his family only, as the Almighty said: "So We brought out whoever was there of the believers. And We found therein not a single house of Muslims" except his wife, for she did not believe in him, but rather she was of the religion of her people, conspiring with them against him and informing them of who was coming to him from his guests by signs between her and them. For this reason, when Lot, peace be upon him, was ordered to travel with his family, he was ordered not to inform her or to expel her from the city. Some of them say: Rather, she followed them, and when the punishment came, she turned around and what happened to them happened to her. It is more apparent that she did not leave the city, nor did Lot inform her, but rather she remained with them. For this reason, He said here: "Except his wife, she was among those who remained behind" meaning those who remained, and it was said that she was among those who perished, and this is an interpretation of the necessary, and His statement: "And We rained down upon them a rain" is explained by His statement: "And We rained down upon them stones of hard clay, in layers, marked from your Lord, and she is not far from the wrongdoers" and for this reason He said: Then see how was the end of the criminals. That is, see, O Muhammad, how was the end of those who dared to disobey God Almighty and lied about His messengers. Imam Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, said that the sodomite should be thrown from a high place and stoned as was done to the people of Lot. Other scholars said that he should be stoned whether he is married or not. This is one of the two opinions of Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him. The evidence is what Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated from the hadith of Al-Darawardi on the authority of Amr ibn Abi Amr ibn Abi Umar on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever you find doing the work of the people of Lot, kill the one who does it and the one to whom it is done. Others said that he is like the adulterer. If he is married, he should be stoned, and if he is not married, he should be flogged one hundred times. This is the other opinion of Al-Shafi’i. As for having intercourse with women in the anus, this is minor sodomy, and it is forbidden by the consensus of scholars, except for a strange opinion of some of the early Muslims. Many hadiths have been narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prohibiting it, and we have discussed them in Surat Al-Baqarah.
7:84: The Almighty says: "So We saved Lot and his family, and none of them believed in him except his family only, as the Almighty said: "So We brought out whoever was there of the believers. And We found therein not a single house of Muslims" except his wife, for she did not believe in him, but rather she was of the religion of her people, conspiring with them against him and informing them of who was coming to him from his guests by signs between her and them. For this reason, when Lot, peace be upon him, was ordered to travel with his family, he was ordered not to inform her or to expel her from the city. Some of them say: Rather, she followed them, and when the punishment came, she turned around and what happened to them happened to her. It is more apparent that she did not leave the city, nor did Lot inform her, but rather she remained with them. For this reason, He said here: "Except his wife, she was among those who remained behind" meaning those who remained, and it was said that she was among those who perished, and this is an interpretation of the necessary, and His statement: "And We rained down upon them a rain" is explained by His statement: "And We rained down upon them stones of hard clay, in layers, marked from your Lord, and she is not far from the wrongdoers" and for this reason He said: Then see how was the end of the criminals. That is, see, O Muhammad, how was the end of those who dared to disobey God Almighty and lied about His messengers. Imam Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, said that the sodomite should be thrown from a high place and stoned as was done to the people of Lot. Other scholars said that he should be stoned whether he is married or not. This is one of the two opinions of Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him. The evidence is what Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated from the hadith of Al-Darawardi on the authority of Amr ibn Abi Amr ibn Abi Umar on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever you find doing the work of the people of Lot, kill the one who does it and the one to whom it is done. Others said that he is like the adulterer. If he is married, he should be stoned, and if he is not married, he should be flogged one hundred times. This is the other opinion of Al-Shafi’i. As for having intercourse with women in the anus, this is minor sodomy, and it is forbidden by the consensus of scholars, except for a strange opinion of some of the early Muslims. Many hadiths have been narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prohibiting it, and we have discussed them in Surat Al-Baqarah.
7:85: Muhammad bin Ishaq said: They are from the lineage of Madyan bin Ibrahim and Shuaib, who is the son of Mikil bin Yashjar. He said: His name in Syriac is Jethro. (I said) Madyan refers to the tribe and to the city, which is near Ma'an on the Hijaz road. God Almighty said: And when he came to the water of Madyan, he found there a group of people watering their land. They are the people of the thicket, as we will mention, God willing, and in Him is trustworthiness. He said, 'O my people, worship God; you have no god other than Him.' This is the call of all the messengers. Clear evidence has come to you from your Lord, meaning God has established the arguments and proofs for the truth of what I have brought to you. Then He admonished them in their dealings with people to fulfill the measure and the scale and not to defraud people of their things, meaning not to betray people in their money and take it in a defrauding manner, which is a reduction in the measure and the scale and deception, as God Almighty said: "Woe to those who give short measure, who, when they take by measure from people, take in full, but when they measure or weigh for them, give less. Do they not think that they are wrong?" Sent * for a mighty Day * the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the Worlds. This is a severe threat and a definite warning. We ask God to protect us from it. Then God Almighty said, informing us about Shu`ayb, who was called the orator of the prophets because of the eloquence of his expression and the strength of his sermon.
7:86: Shu'aib, peace be upon him, forbade them from cutting off the physical and spiritual path by saying: And do not sit on every path, threatening meaning threatening people with killing if they do not give you their money. Al-Suddi and others said: They were tax collectors. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and others said: And do not sit on every path, threatening meaning threatening the believers who came to Shu'aib to follow him. The first is more evident because he said on every path which is the road. This second is his saying: And you hinder from the way of God those who believe in Him, and you seek to make it crooked meaning you wish for the way of God to be crooked and crooked. And remember when you were few and He made you many meaning you were weak because of your fewness and then you became powerful because of your large number. So remember God’s blessing upon you in that. And see how was the end of the corrupters meaning of the past nations and the past centuries and what befell them of torment and punishment because of their daring to disobey God and deny His messengers. 7:87: Shu'aib, peace be upon him, forbade them from cutting off the physical and spiritual path by saying: And do not sit on every path, threatening meaning threatening people with killing if they do not give you their money. Al-Suddi and others said: They were tax collectors. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and others said: And do not sit on every path, threatening meaning threatening the believers who came to Shu'aib to follow him. The first is more evident because he said on every path which is the road. This second is his saying: And you hinder from the way of God those who believe in Him, and you seek to make it crooked meaning you wish for the way of God to be crooked and crooked. And remember when you were few and He made you many meaning you were weak because of your fewness and then you became powerful because of your large number. So remember God’s blessing upon you in that. And see how was the end of the corrupters meaning of the past nations and the past centuries and what befell them of torment and punishment because of their daring to disobey God and deny His messengers. 7:88: This is report from God Almighty about what the infidels confronted His Prophet Shuaib and those who were with him from the believers with in their threat to him and those with him with banishment from the village or coercion to return to their religion and enter with them in what they are in, and this is addressed to the Messenger and what is meant is his followers who were with him in the religion, and His saying or even if we were reluctant means or you are doing that even if we were reluctant to what you are calling us to, then if we return to your religion and enter with you in what you are in, then we have greatly slandered God in making the partners with Him equals, and this is an expression from Him about following them, and it is not for us to return to it except if God, our Lord, wills and this is a return to the will, for He knows everything and has encompassed everything with knowledge, upon God we have put our trust meaning in our affairs, what we do of them and what we leave, Our Lord, judge between us and our people in truth meaning judge between us and our people and grant us victory over them, and You are the best of judges meaning the best of judges, for You are the Just One who never wrongs.

7:90: The Almighty tells about the severity of their disbelief, rebellion, and insolence, and what they are in of misguidance and what their hearts were created with of opposition to the truth, and for this reason they swore and said, If you follow Shu'aib, indeed, you will be losers. For this reason, He followed it with His saying, So the earthquake seized them, and they became within their homes, fallen down. The Almighty informed here that the earthquake seized them, just as they had shaken Shu'aib and his companions, and He threatened them with exile, just as He informed about them in Surat Hud, saying, And when Our command came, We saved Shu'aib and those who believed with him, by mercy from Us, and the shriek seized those who did wrong, and they became within their homes, fallen down. The relevance there, and God knows best, is that when they mocked him in their saying, Your prayer commands you, the verse, the shriek came and silenced them. The Almighty said, informing about them in Surat Ash-Shu'ara', "But they denied him, so the punishment of the Day of Shadow seized them. Indeed, it was the punishment of a tremendous Day." And that is only because they said to Him in the context of the story Then let down upon us fragments of the sky the verse. Then He informed that the punishment of the Day of the Shadow had befallen them, and all of that had gathered upon them. Then the punishment of the Day of the Shadow seized them. It was a cloud that shaded them with sparks of fire, flames, and a great blaze. Then a shout came to them from the sky and a violent tremor from the earth from below them, so the souls were lost, the spirits departed, and the bodies were extinguished. So they became in their homes, prostrate. Then the Most High said: As if they had never prospered therein. That is, as if when the punishment befell them, they had not stayed in their homes from which they had wanted to expel the Messenger and his companions. Then the Most High said, in response to what they said: Those who denied Shu`ayb were the losers.

7:93: That is, Shu'aib, peace be upon him, turned away from them after the torment, punishment, and humiliation that befell them, and he said, rebuking and rebuking them, O my people, I have conveyed to you the messages of my Lord and have given you sincere advice. That is, I have conveyed to you what I was sent with, so I should not feel sorry for you, since you have disbelieved in what I brought to you. For this reason, he said, How can I feel sorry for a disbelieving people?
7:94: The Almighty says, informing about what He tested the past nations to whom the prophets were sent with hardship and distress, meaning by hardship what befalls them in their bodies of diseases and illnesses, and hardship what befalls them of poverty and need and the like, so that they may humble themselves, meaning that they may supplicate, be humble and implore God Almighty to remove what has befallen them. The meaning of the speech is that He tested them with hardship so that they would humble themselves, but they did not do anything that He wanted from them, so He turned the situation for them to ease in order to test them with it. For this reason, He said, Then We replaced the bad with good, meaning We changed the situation from hardship to ease, from sickness and illness to health and wellness, and from poverty to wealth so that they would be thankful for that, but they did not do it. His saying, until they became abundant, means that they multiplied and their wealth and children multiplied. It is said that something became abundant if it became abundant. And they said, ‘Our fathers have been touched by hardship and prosperity.’ So We seized them suddenly while they perceived not. God the Almighty says: We tested them with this and that so that they would humble themselves and turn to God, but neither this nor that worked for them, nor did they stop with this or that. Rather, they said, ‘We have been touched by hardship and prosperity, followed by prosperity like that which befell our fathers in ancient times and ages.’ But time is only passing by at times, and at times. Rather, they did not realize God’s command regarding them, nor did they sense God’s testing them in both situations. This is in contrast to the state of the believers who thank God for prosperity and are patient in adversity, as is proven in the two Sahihs: “It is amazing that God does not decree for him a decision except that it is good for him. If adversity befalls him, he is patient, and that is good for him. If ease befalls him, he is grateful, and that is good for him.” So the believer is the one who realizes what God has tested him with of adversity and prosperity. For this reason, it is stated in the hadith: “The believer will continue to be afflicted until he emerges cleansed of his sins. The hypocrite is like a donkey who does not know where he is tied up.” His family nor for what they had sent him,” or something like that. That is why he followed this description with his saying, So We seized them suddenly while they did not perceive, meaning, We seized them with the punishment suddenly, meaning suddenly, and without them realizing it, meaning, We seized them suddenly, as in the hadith, Sudden death is a mercy for the believer and a sorrowful seizure for the disbeliever.

7:96: The Almighty tells us about the lack of faith of the people of the villages to whom the messengers were sent, as He the Almighty says: "Why was there not a village that believed and its faith benefited it, except the people of Jonah? When they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world and gave them enjoyment for a time." That is, no village believed in its entirety except the people of Jonah, for they believed after they witnessed the punishment, as He the Almighty says: "And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more. So they believed, so We gave them enjoyment for a time." And He the Almighty says: And We did not send to any city a warner verse, and He the Almighty says: And if only the people of the cities had believed and feared God that is, their hearts believed in what the messengers brought and believed in it and followed it, and feared God by doing acts of obedience and avoiding forbidden things We would have opened upon them blessings from the heaven and the earth that is, the rain from the sky and the plants of the earth. God the Almighty says: But they denied, so We seized them for what they were earning that is, but they denied their messengers, so We punished them with destruction for what they earned of Sins and prohibitions, then the Almighty said, frightening and warning against disobeying His commands and daring to disobey His prohibitions: “Do the people of the towns feel secure against Our punishment coming to them by night while they are asleep? Or do the people of the towns feel secure against Our punishment coming to them by daylight while they are playing?” That is, while they are busy and heedless. Do they feel secure against the plan of God? That is, His punishment, vengeance, and power over them and taking them while they are heedless and heedless. No one feels secure against the plan of God except the losing people. For this reason, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, may God have mercy on him, said: The believer does acts of obedience while he is fearful, anxious, and afraid, while the wicked person does acts of disobedience while he is secure.
