7:100: Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said in his statement, Has it not become clear to those who inherit the earth after its people? or has it not become clear to them that if We willed, We could afflict them for their sins? Mujahid and others said the same. Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir said in his interpretation of it: God the Almighty says, “Has it not become clear to those who are succeeded by successors on the earth after the destruction of others before them who were its people, so they followed their ways and did their deeds and rebelled against their Lord, “that if We willed, We could afflict them for their sins.” He says, if We willed, We could do to them as We did to those before them. And set a seal upon their hearts, he says, and seal their hearts. So they do not hear, an admonition or a reminder. I said And thus God the Almighty said, Has it not become clear to them how many generations We destroyed before them, who walked about in their dwellings? Indeed in that are signs for those of understanding. And God the Almighty said, Has it not become clear to them how many generations We destroyed before them, who walked about in their dwellings? Indeed in that are signs. Do they not hear? He said, Did you not swear before that you would not perish? And you dwelt in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves. The verse. And God Almighty said, And how many generations before them have We destroyed? Do you perceive anyone of them or hear a sound from them? That is, do you see a person of theirs or hear a sound from them? God the Almighty said: “Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them whom We had established in the earth as We have not established you? And We sent down upon them abundant rain and made rivers flow beneath them. Then We destroyed them for their sins and brought forth after them another generation.” And God the Almighty said after mentioning the destruction of the ‘Aad: “So they became such that nothing could be seen except their dwellings. Thus do We recompense the criminal people. And We had certainly established them in that in which We had not established you, and We gave them hearing and sight and hearts. But their hearing and sight and hearts availed them nothing when they denied the signs of God, and that which they used to ridicule encompassed them. And We had certainly destroyed the towns around you and diversified the signs that perhaps they would return.” God the Almighty said: “And those before them denied, and they did not attain a tenth of what We gave them. So they denied My messengers. So how was My reproach?” God the Almighty said: And those before them denied, so how was My reproach? God the Almighty said: “And how many a town have We destroyed while it was in wrongdoing, so it is desolate upon its roofs, and a well unused, and a lofty palace? Have they not traveled through the land and had hearts by which to reason, or ears by which to hear? Indeed, it is not eyes that are blinded, but blinded are the hearts which are within the breasts.” God the Almighty said: And messengers before you were mocked, but that which they used to mock encompassed those who mocked them. And other verses indicating the descent of His vengeance upon His enemies and the attainment of His blessings upon His friends. For this reason, He followed up with His saying: He is the most truthful of speakers and the Lord of the worlds.
7:101: When God the Almighty told His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the story of the people of Noah, Hud, Salih, Lot, and Shuaib, and what happened of his destruction of the disbelievers and his saving of the believers, and that God the Almighty excused them by explaining to them the truth with arguments on the tongues of the messengers, may God's prayers be upon them all, God the Almighty said: These towns - We relate to you meaning, O Muhammad, of their report meaning of their report and their messengers had already come to them with clear proofs meaning the arguments for their truthfulness in what they told them, as God the Almighty said: And We never punish until We have sent a messenger and God the Almighty said: "That is from the report of the towns - We relate it to you, of them standing and harvested. And We did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves" and God the Almighty said: So they were not to believe in what they denied before the ba is causal, meaning they were not to believe in what the messengers brought them because of their denial of the truth when it first came to them, as Ibn Atiyah, may God have mercy on him, narrated it, and it is a good and appropriate statement like his saying: "And what makes you realize that when it comes, they will not believe? And We will turn Their hearts and their eyes, just as they did not believe in Him the first time verse, and for this reason He said here, “Thus does God set a seal upon the hearts of the disbelievers. And We did not find for most of them” meaning for most of the past nations any covenant, and indeed We found most of them to be wicked meaning, We found most of them to be wicked, outside of obedience and compliance. The covenant that He took is what He created them upon and created them upon, and He took from them in their loins that He is their Lord and King, and that there is no god but Him, so they acknowledged that and bore witness against themselves to it, and they disobeyed it and left it behind them and worshipped other than Him with God without evidence or argument from reason or law, and in the sound nature there is the opposite of that, and the noble messengers from the first of them to the last of them came with the prohibition of that as it came in Sahih Muslim, God the Most High says: Indeed, I created My servants as monotheists, but the devils came to them and led them astray from their religion and prohibited for them what I had made lawful for them Sahih Muslim. And in the two Sahihs, Every child is born in a state of fitrah, then his parents make him a Jew, a Christian, or a Zoroastrian Hadith. And God the Almighty said in His Noble Book: And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him, ‘There is no god except Me, so worship Me.’ And His Almighty said: “And ask those We sent before you of Our messengers: ‘Did We appoint other gods to be worshipped besides the Most Merciful?’” And His Almighty said: And We have certainly sent among every nation a messenger, [saying], ‘Worship God and avoid false deities.’ And other verses. It has been said in the interpretation of His Almighty’s saying: So they were not to believe in what they denied before, what Abu Ja`far al-Razi narrated on the authority of al-Rabi` ibn Anas on the authority of Abu al-`Aliyah on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka`b in His saying: So they were not to believe in what they denied before, he said it was in His Almighty’s knowledge on the day they acknowledged the covenant to Him, meaning they were not to believe because God knew that from them. And this is what al-Rabi` ibn Anas said on the authority of Abu al-`Aliyah on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka`b on the authority of Anas, and Ibn Jarir chose it. Al-Suddi said: So they were not to believe in what they denied before, he said: That was on the day the covenant was taken from them, so they believed unwillingly. And Mujahid said in His saying: So they were not to believe in what they denied before, To believe in what they denied before. This is like His saying, And if they were returned, they would return verse.

And in the two Sahihs, Every child is born in a state of fitrah, then his parents make him a Jew, a Christian, or a Zoroastrian Hadith. And God the Almighty said in His Noble Book: And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him, ‘There is no god except Me, so worship Me.’ And His Almighty said: “And ask those We sent before you of Our messengers: ‘Did We appoint other gods to be worshipped besides the Most Merciful?’” And His Almighty said: And We have certainly sent among every nation a messenger, [saying], ‘Worship God and avoid false deities.’ And other verses. It has been said in the interpretation of His Almighty’s saying: So they were not to believe in what they denied before, what Abu Ja`far al-Razi narrated on the authority of al-Rabi` ibn Anas on the authority of Abu al-`Aliyah on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka`b in His saying: So they were not to believe in what they denied before, he said it was in His Almighty’s knowledge on the day they acknowledged the covenant to Him, meaning they were not to believe because God knew that from them. And this is what al-Rabi` ibn Anas said on the authority of Abu al-`Aliyah on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka`b on the authority of Anas, and Ibn Jarir chose it. Al-Suddi said: So they were not to believe in what they denied before, he said: That was on the day the covenant was taken from them, so they believed unwillingly. And Mujahid said in His saying: So they were not to believe in what they denied before, To believe in what they denied before. This is like His saying, And if they were returned, they would return verse.
7:103: The Almighty says: Then We sent after them meaning the messengers mentioned earlier, such as Noah, Hud, Salih, Lot, and Shuaib, may the blessings and peace of God be upon them and upon all of God's prophets, Moses with Our signs meaning with Our clear proofs and evidence to Pharaoh, who was the king of Egypt at the time of Moses, and his chiefs meaning his people, but they wronged them meaning they denied and disbelieved in them out of injustice and stubbornness on their part, and as God Almighty says: "And they denied them, while their souls were convinced thereof, out of injustice and arrogance. So see how was the end of the corrupters" meaning those who turned people away from the path of God and denied His messengers, meaning see how We dealt with them, we drowned them all in front of Moses and his people, and this is more eloquent in punishing Pharaoh and his people and more healing for the hearts of the friends of God, Moses and his people, of the believers in him.
7:104: God Almighty tells about Moses' debate with Pharaoh and his bridling him with argument and showing him clear signs in the presence of Pharaoh and his people from the Copts of Egypt. God Almighty said: And Moses said, 'O Pharaoh, indeed I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds.' That is, He who is the Creator of everything, its Lord and its King, sent me. It is right for me not to say about God except the truth. Some of them said: Its meaning is right for me not to say about God except the truth, that is, worthy of that and deserving of it. They said: The prepositions ba and ala alternate. It is said: I shot with the bow and on the bow, and he came in a good state and in a good state. Some of the commentators said: Its meaning is that I am keen not to say about God except the truth. Others from the people of Medina read: It is right for me in the sense of obligatory and it is right for me that I not speak about Him except what is true and honest, because I know of His majesty and great status. I have come to you with a clear proof from your Lord. That is, with a decisive proof from God that He gave me as evidence of my truthfulness in what I have come to you. So send with me the Children of Israel. That is, release them from your captivity. And he subdued you, and left them and the worship of your Lord and their Lord, for they are from the lineage of the noble prophet Israel, and he is Jacob, son of Isaac, son of Abraham, the friend of the Most Merciful. He said, ‘If you have come with a sign, then produce it, if you should be of the truthful.’ That is, Pharaoh said, I will not believe you in what you said, nor will I obey you in what you asked, so if you have an argument, then present it so that we may see it, if you are truthful in what you claimed.

7:107: Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement a clear serpent the male snake, and this is what Al-Suddi and Al-Dahhak said. In the hadith of Al-Fitun narrated by Yazid bin Harun on the authority of Al-Asbagh bin Zaid on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abi Ayoub on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said So he threw down his staff and it turned into a huge serpent with its mouth open, rushing towards Pharaoh. When Pharaoh saw that it was heading towards him, he rushed from his bed and called upon Moses to stop it from him, so he did. Qatada said: It turned into a huge serpent like the city. Al-Suddi said regarding his statement And behold, it was a clear serpent the male serpent from the snakes, opening its mouth and placing its lower jaw on the ground and its upper jaw on the wall of the palace, then it headed towards Pharaoh to take him. When he saw it, he was terrified by it and jumped up and started talking, and he had never done so before, and he shouted, O Moses, take it and I will believe in you and send the Children of Israel with you. So Moses, peace be upon him, took it and it turned into a staff. It was narrated on the authority of Ikrimah On the authority of Ibn Abbas, something similar to this. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: When Moses entered upon Pharaoh, Pharaoh said to him: Do I know you? He said: Yes. He said: Did We not raise you among us as a child? He said: So Moses returned to him what he had returned, and Pharaoh said: Take him. So Moses hastened, and he threw down his staff, and behold, it was a clear serpent. So it charged at the people, and they fled from it, and twenty-five thousand of them died, killing one another, and Pharaoh stood up in defeat until he entered the House. It was narrated by Ibn Jarir, Imam Ahmad, in his book Az-Zuhd, and Ibn Abi Hatim, and there is something strange in its context, and God knows best. And his saying, And he took out his hand, and behold, it was white to the beholders, meaning he took his hand out of his armor after he had put it in it, and behold, it was white, shining without leprosy or disease, as God Almighty said, And put your hand into the bosom of your garment; it will come out white without disease, the verse. And Ibn Abbas said in the hadith of the trials: without disease, meaning without leprosy. Then he put it back into his sleeve, and it returned to its original color. And Mujahid and more than one other said the same.

7:109: That is, the chiefs, who were the masses and the masters of Pharaoh's people, agreed with what Pharaoh said about him after his terror returned to him and he settled on the throne of his kingdom. After that, he said to the chiefs around him, This is indeed a learned magician. So they agreed and said the same as he said and consulted about his matter, what they should do about him and what their trick would be to extinguish his light and extinguish his word and reveal his lies and fabrications. They feared that he would win people over with his magic in what they believed, and that would be a reason for his appearance over them and his expulsion of them from their land. What they feared they fell into, as God Almighty said: And We showed Pharaoh and Haman and their soldiers from them that which they had been wary of. So when they consulted about his matter and deliberated about what was in it, their opinion agreed on what God Almighty narrated about them in His Almighty saying.

If they defeated Moses, He would reward them and give them a generous gift. So He promised them and promised them that He would give them what they wanted and make them among his companions and those close to him. But when they were certain of Pharaoh, God cursed him.

7:115: This is a duel between the magicians and Moses, peace be upon him, in their saying, Either you throw or we will be the ones who throw meaning before you, as He said in the other verse, Or we will be the first to throw, so Moses, peace be upon him, said to them, Throw meaning you will be the first. It was said that the wisdom in this, and God knows best, is for people to see their actions and reflect. Then, when they finished with their dazzle and their tricks, the clear and evident truth would come to them after they sought it and waited for it to come, so that it would be more effective in their souls. And that is how it was, and for this reason, God Almighty said, So when they threw, they bewitched the eyes of the people and struck terror into them meaning they made it seem to the eyes that what they had done to him was real in reality, and it was nothing but a mere artifice and imagination, as God Almighty said, "And behold, their ropes and their staffs appeared to him, because of their magic, to be crawling. So Moses felt fear within himself. We said, "Fear not; indeed, you are the superior. And throw down what is in your right hand; it will swallow up what they have made. What they have made is only the trick of a magician, and the magician will not succeed, wherever he goes." Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said: Abu Saeed narrated to us from Ikrimah from Ibn Abbas: They threw thick ropes and long pieces of wood. He said: So it came and it seemed to him from their magic that it was moving. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: A row of fifteen thousand magicians, each with his own ropes and staffs. Moses, peace be upon him, went out with his brother leaning on his staff until he reached the assembly and Pharaoh was in his council with the nobles of his kingdom. Then the magicians said: O Moses, either you throw or we will be the first to throw. He said: Rather, throw. Then behold, their ropes and staffs.” So the first thing they took away with their magic was the sight of Moses and the sight of Pharaoh, then the sight of the people after that. Then each man threw what he had in his hand of ropes and staffs, and behold, serpents like mountains had filled the valley, riding on each other. Al-Suddi said: They were thirty-two thousand men, and there was not a man among them who did not have a rope and staff. So when they threw, they bewitched the eyes of the people and terrified them. He said: They scattered them, that is, from the groups. Ibn Jarir said: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us: Hisham al-Dastawai narrated to us: al-Qasim narrated to us. Ibn Abi Bazza said: Pharaoh gathered seventy thousand magicians and they threw down seventy thousand ropes and seventy thousand sticks until he thought that their magic was moving. That is why God Almighty said: And they brought a great magic.

7:117: God Almighty tells us that He revealed to His servant and messenger Moses, peace be upon him, in that great situation in which God Almighty distinguished between truth and falsehood, ordering him to throw down what was in his right hand, which was his staff. And behold, it swallowed up meaning it devoured what they were fabricating meaning what they were throwing down and making them think was truth when it was false. Ibn Abbas said: “It did not pass by anything of their ropes or wood except that it swallowed it up. The magicians knew that this was something from the sky and that this was not magic, so they fell down in prostration and said: ‘We believe in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Moses and Aaron.’” Muhammad bin Ishaq said: I kept following those ropes and sticks one by one until nothing could be seen in the valley, little or much of what they had thrown. Then Moses took it and behold, it was a stick in his hand as it had been, and the magicians fell down in prostration. They said: We believe in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Moses and Aaron. If this were a magician, he would not have defeated us. Al-Qasim bin Abi Bazza said: God revealed to him: Throw down your stick. So he threw down his stick and behold, it was a clear serpent, its mouth open, swallowing their ropes and sticks. Then the magicians fell down in prostration, and they did not raise their heads until they saw Paradise and Hell and the reward of their people.

The magicians knew that this was something from the sky and that this was not magic, so they fell down in prostration and said: ‘We believe in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Moses and Aaron.’” Muhammad bin Ishaq said: I kept following those ropes and sticks one by one until nothing could be seen in the valley, little or much of what they had thrown. Then Moses took it and behold, it was a stick in his hand as it had been, and the magicians fell down in prostration. They said: We believe in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Moses and Aaron. If this were a magician, he would not have defeated us. Al-Qasim bin Abi Bazza said: God revealed to him: Throw down your stick. So he threw down his stick and behold, it was a clear serpent, its mouth open, swallowing their ropes and sticks. Then the magicians fell down in prostration, and they did not raise their heads until they saw Paradise and Hell and the reward of their people.
7:123: God Almighty tells us about what Pharaoh, may God curse him, threatened the magicians with when they believed in Moses, peace be upon him, and what he showed the people of his plot and deceit in His statement, This is indeed a plot that you have plotted in the city to expel its people from it, meaning that his defeat of you on this day was only after consultation between you and your approval of it, as He said in the other verse, Indeed, he is your leader who taught you magic, and he knows, as does everyone who has a mind, that what he said is the most false of falsehoods, for Moses, peace be upon him, as soon as he came from Madyan, called Pharaoh to God and showed dazzling miracles and conclusive evidence of the truth of what he brought. At that time, Pharaoh sent to the cities of his kingdom and the affairs of his sultanate, and gathered magicians scattered from all the regions of Egypt, whom he and the leaders of his people had chosen, and brought them to him and promised them generous gifts. For this reason, they were among the most eager people for that and for appearing in their position and advancing with Pharaoh. Moses, peace be upon him, did not know any of them, nor did he see them, nor did he meet them, and Pharaoh knew that. He only said this to cover up and deceive the ignorant people of his state, as God Almighty said: So he made light of his people, and they obeyed him. For a people who believed him in his saying, I am your Lord, the Most High, were among the most ignorant and misguided of God’s creation. Al-Suddi said in his interpretation with his famous chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Masoud, Ibn Abbas and other companions regarding the words of God Almighty: This is indeed a plot which you have plotted in the city. He said: Moses, peace be upon him, and the chief magician met and Moses said to him: Tell me, if I defeat you, will you believe in me and testify that what you have brought is the truth? The magician said: “We will come tomorrow with magic that no magic can defeat. By God, if you defeat me, I will believe in you and testify that you are the truth.” And Pharaoh looked at them and said: This is why he said what he said. And His words: So that you may expel from it its people means that you and he will gather and you will have a state and influence and you will expel from it the great and leaders and the state and control will be yours. Then you will soon know means what I will do with you. Then he interpreted this threat by saying: I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides meaning that he will cut off the right hand of a man and his left foot or vice versa. Then I will crucify you all. And he said in the other verse: On the trunks of palm trees meaning on the trunks. Ibn Abbas said: He was the first to be crucified and the first to have his hands and feet cut off from the opposition of Pharaoh. The magicians said: To our Lord we will return, meaning we have realized that we will return to Him, and His punishment is more severe than your punishment and His punishment for what you call us to today, and what you forced us to do of magic is greater than your punishment. So we will be patient today with your punishment so that we may be saved from the punishment of God. For this reason they said: Our Lord, pour out upon us patience, meaning, make us patient in your religion and steadfast in it, and let us die as Muslims, meaning following your Prophet Moses, peace be upon him. They said to Pharaoh: “Then decide what you will decide. You can only decide this worldly life. Indeed, we have believed in our Lord that He may forgive us our sins and what you forced us to do of magic. And God is better and more lasting. Indeed, whoever comes to his Lord as a criminal, for him is Hell; he will neither die therein nor live. And whoever comes to Him as a believer having done righteous deeds, for those will be the highest degrees.” So they were magicians at the beginning of the day, but at the end of it they became righteous martyrs. Ibn Abbas, Ubayd ibn Umayr, Qatadah, and Ibn Jurayj said: They were magicians at the beginning of the day and at the end of it Martyrs.

7:127: God Almighty tells us about what Pharaoh and his people conspired to do and what they harbored for Moses, peace be upon him, and his people of harm and hatred. And the chiefs of Pharaoh’s people said meaning to Pharaoh, Will you leave Moses and his people? meaning will you leave them to spread corruption in the land, meaning to corrupt your subjects and call them to worship their Lord instead of you? Oh my God, how amazing it is that these people are afraid of the corruption of Moses and his people! Indeed, Pharaoh and his people are the corruptors, but they do not realize it. That is why they said, And leave you and your gods. Some of them said that the waw here is a circumstantial particle, meaning will you leave him and his people to spread corruption in the land when he has abandoned worshipping you? Abi bin Kaab read it as: And they have left you to worship you and your gods. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Others said: It is a conjunction, meaning: Do you allow them to do the corruption that you have approved of them doing and to abandon your gods? Some of them read: your gods, meaning: your worship. This was narrated from Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and others. According to the first reading, some of them said: Pharaoh had a god that he worshipped. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: Pharaoh had a god that he worshipped in secret. He said in another narration: He had a noose around his neck that he would prostrate to. Al-Suddi said about the Almighty’s statement: And he leaves you and your gods, and his gods, according to what Ibn Abbas claimed, were that whenever they saw a beautiful cow, Pharaoh would order them to worship it. For this reason, the Samaritan brought out for them a calf with a body that mooed. So Pharaoh answered their question by saying: We will kill their sons and spare their women. This was a second command with this action. He had tormented them before the birth of Moses, peace be upon him, out of caution from his presence, so it was contrary to what he sought and against what Pharaoh intended. And this is how he was treated in his actions when he wanted to humiliate and subjugate the Children of Israel, but the matter came out contrary to what he wanted: God honored them and humiliated him, and made him angry and drowned him and his soldiers. And when Pharaoh insisted on what he mentioned of harming the Children of Israel, “Moses said to his people, ‘Seek help from God and be patient. ’” And he promised them the outcome and that the home would be theirs in his saying, “Indeed, the earth belongs to God. He causes it to inherit whomever He wills of His servants. And the [best] outcome is for the righteous. They said, “We were harmed before you came to us and after you came to us.” That is, they did to us what you saw of humiliation and disgrace before you came, O Moses, and after that. So he said, alerting them to their present state and what they would become in the second state, Perhaps your Lord will destroy your enemy. This is a specification for them to resolve to be grateful when blessings come and calamities are removed.

Abu Ishaq said on the authority of Raja bin Haywah that the palm tree would only bear one fruit "that perhaps they would be reminded. But when good comes to them" meaning fertility and provision they say, 'This is for us' meaning this is for us because of what we deserve and if evil befalls them meaning drought and famine they regard Moses and those with him as an evil omen meaning this is because of them and what they brought unquestionably, their omen is only with God Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas unquestionably, their omen is only with God meaning their misfortunes are with God but most of them do not know Ibn Jurayj said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said unquestionably, their omen is only with God meaning except from God.

7:132: This is a report from God Almighty about the rebellion of the people of Pharaoh, their arrogance, their stubbornness towards the truth, and their insistence on falsehood in their saying, No matter what sign you bring us to bewitch us with, we will not believe in you. They say, Whatever sign you bring us, evidence, and proof you present, we will reject it, and we will not accept it from you, nor will we believe in you or what you have brought. God Almighty said, So We sent upon them the flood. They differed in its meaning. According to Ibn Abbas in a narration, it means abundant, torrential rains that destroy crops and fruits, and Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim said the same. According to Ibn Abbas in another narration, it means abundant death, and so said Ata'. Mujahid said, The flood is water and plague in any case. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hisham Al-Rafa’i told us, Yahya bin Yaman told us, Al-Munhal bin Khalifa told us, on the authority of Al-Hajjaj, on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Mina’, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The flood is death. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it in the same way from the hadith of Yahya bin Yaman, and it is a strange hadith. Ibn Abbas said in another narration: It is a command from God that swept over them, then he recited: And a company from your Lord swept over them while they were asleep. As for locusts, they are well-known and famous, and they are edible, as is proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abu Ya’fur, who said: I asked Abdullah bin Abi Awfa about locusts, and he said: We participated in seven battles with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we ate locusts. Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad bin Hanbal, and Ibn Majah narrated from the hadith of Abd Al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Umar on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Two dead things and two types of blood have been made lawful for us: fish and locusts, and the liver and the spleen.” Abu Al-Qasim Al-Baghawi narrated it on the authority of Dawud bin Rashid on the authority of Suwaid bin Abd Al-Aziz on the authority of Abu Tamam Al-Ayli. On the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of Ibn Omar, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, similarly. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Muhammad bin al-Faraj, on the authority of Muhammad bin Zubarqan al-Ahwazi, on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Uthman, on the authority of Salman, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about locusts, and he said: Most of God’s soldiers, I do not eat them nor forbid them. He, peace be upon him, only left them because he was disgusted by them, just as his noble soul was disgusted by eating the monitor lizard, and he permitted it. Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir narrated in a section he collected on locusts from the hadith of Abu Saeed Al-Hassan bin Ali Al-Adawi, who said: Nasr bin Yahya bin Saeed told us, Yahya bin Khalid told us on the authority of Ibn Jurayj on the authority of Ata’ on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not eat locusts, kidneys, or monitor lizards without forbidding them. As for locusts, they are a punishment and a torment, and as for kidneys, they are close to urine. As for the monitor lizard, he said: I fear that it may be transformed. Then he said: It is strange that I did not write it except from this source. The Commander of the Faithful, Umar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, desired and loved them. Abdullah bin Dinar narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar: Umar was asked about locusts, and he said: I wish we had a handful or two of them to eat. Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir narrated in a section he collected on locusts from the hadith of Abu Saeed Al-Hassan bin Ali Al-Adawi, who said: Nasr bin Yahya bin Saeed told us, Yahya bin Khalid told us on the authority of Ibn Jurayj on the authority of Ata’ on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not eat locusts, kidneys, or monitor lizards without forbidding them. As for locusts, they are a punishment and a torment, and as for kidneys, they are close to urine. As for the monitor lizard, he said: I fear that it may be transformed. Then he said: It is strange that I did not write it except from this source. The Commander of the Faithful, Umar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, desired and loved them. Abdullah bin Dinar narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar: Umar was asked about locusts, and he said: I wish we had a handful or two of them to eat. Ibn Majah narrated: Ahmad bin Mani’ told us on the authority of Sufyan bin Uyaynah on the authority of Abu Saad Saeed bin Al-Marzban Al-Baqqal, who heard Anas bin Malik say: The wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to give each other locusts on plates. Abu Al-Qasim Al-Baghawi said: Dawud bin Rashid told us. Baqiyya bin Al-Waleed narrated to us on the authority of Yahya bin Yazid Al-Qa’nabi, my father narrated to me on the authority of Sadi bin Ajlan on the authority of Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Mary, daughter of Imran, peace be upon her, asked her Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, to feed her meat without blood, so He fed her locusts. She said: O God, let him live without breastfeeding and keep him alive without being separated.” Numayr said: Sedition is sound. Abu Bakr bin Abi Dawud said: Abu Taqi Hisham bin Abdul Malik Al-Muzani narrated to us, Baqiyya bin Al-Waleed narrated to us, Ismail bin Ayyash narrated to us on the authority of Damdam bin Zur’ah on the authority of Shureih bin Ubayd on the authority of Abu Zuhair Al-Numairi, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not fight the locusts, for they are the greatest soldiers of God. Very strange. Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid regarding the Almighty’s statement: So We sent upon them the flood and the locusts, he said: They ate the nails of their doors and left the wood. We have already mentioned at God the Almighty said: Lawful to you is game from the sea and its food as provision for you and for the travelers. The hadith of Hammad bin Salamah on the authority of Abu Al-Muhzam on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: We went out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for Hajj or Umrah, and we encountered a swarm of locusts, so we began to hit them with sticks while we were in ihram. So we asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: There is nothing wrong with game from the sea. Ibn Majah narrated on the authority of Harun Al-Hammal on the authority of Hisham bin Al-Qasim on the authority of Ziyad bin Abdullah bin Alatha on the authority of Musa bin Muhammad bin Ibrahim Al-Taimi on the authority of his father on the authority of Anas and Jabir on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that when he supplicated against locusts, he would say: O God, destroy their adults, kill their young, spoil their eggs, cut off their roots, and seize our livelihoods and provisions by their mouths, for You are the Hearer of supplication. Jabir said to him: O Messenger of God, are you supplicating against one of God’s soldiers to cut off their roots? He said, It is only the eggs of a whale in the sea. Hisham said, Ziyad told me that someone who saw it being scattered by a whale told him. Whoever verified this said that when a fish lays eggs on the seashore, the water dries up and it appears to the sun that it all hatches into flying locusts. We have presented, when he said, Except for nations like you, the hadith of Omar, may God be pleased with him, that God created a thousand nations, six hundred in the sea and four hundred on land, and that the first of them to perish would be locusts. Abu Bakr bin Abi Dawud said, Yazid bin Mubarak told us, Abd al-Rahman bin Qais told us, Salim bin Salim told us, Abu al-Mughira al-Jawzjani Muhammad bin Malik told us, on the authority of al-Bara’ bin Azib, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, There is no epidemic with the sword, and there is no escape with locusts. A strange hadith. As for lice, according to Ibn Abbas, they are the weevils that emerge from wheat, and according to him, they are the small locusts that have no wings. Mujahid, Ikrimah, Qatadah, and according to al-Hasan and Saeed bin Jubayr, lice are small black insects. Abd al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said: Lice are fleas. Ibn Jarir said, “Lice is the plural of a louse, and it is an insect that resembles lice and that camels eat, as far as I have been informed. It is what al-A’sha meant when he said: A people who treat their children with lice, chains are more effective, and a closed door He said: Some of the people of Basra who were knowledgeable about the Arabic language claimed that lice among the Arabs were called hamnan, the singular of which is hamnanah, and they are small monkeys above the qamqamah. Abu Ja`far Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid Al-Razi told us, Ya`qub Al-Qummi told us on the authority of Ja`far Ibn Abi Al-Mughira on the authority of Sa`id Ibn Jubayr who said: When Moses, peace be upon him, came to Pharaoh, he said to him: Send the Children of Israel with me, but he did not send them. Then God sent upon them the flood, which is rain, and poured some of it upon them. They feared that it was a punishment, so they said to Moses: Call upon your Lord to remove the rain from us, so we will believe in you and send the Children of Israel with you. So he called upon his Lord, and He removed it from them, but they did not believe and did not send the Children of Israel with him. So he caused to grow for them in that year something that had not grown before of crops, fruits and pastures. They said: This is what we wished for. So God sent upon them locusts and let them destroy the pastures. When they saw their traces in the pastures, they knew that they would not leave the crops. So they said: O Moses, call upon your Lord to remove the locusts from us, so we will believe in you and send the Children of Israel with you. So he called upon his Lord, and He removed the locusts from them, but they did not believe and did not send the Children of Israel with them. They trampled and took refuge in the houses, but they said: We have taken refuge. So God sent upon them Lice, which are mites that come out of it, so the man would take ten bags to the mill, but only three would return. They said, “O Moses, call upon your Lord to remove the lice from us, so that we may believe in you and send the Children of Israel with you.” So he called upon his Lord, and He removed them, but they refused to send the Children of Israel with him. While he was sitting with Pharaoh, he heard the croaking of a frog, so he said to Pharaoh, What do you and your people suffer from this? He said, What could be the plot of this? They did not spend the night before a man was sitting up to his chin among the frogs, and about to speak, a frog jumped into his mouth. They said to Moses, Call upon your Lord to remove these frogs from us, so that we will believe in you and send the Children of Israel with you. So he called upon his Lord, and He removed them, but they did not believe. God sent blood upon them, so whatever they drew from the rivers and wells and whatever was in their vessels, they found it to be thick blood. They complained to Pharaoh and said, We have been afflicted with blood and we have no drink. He said, He has bewitched you. They said, From where did he bewitch us when we do not find any water in our vessels except that we find it to be thick blood? They came to him and said, O Moses, call upon your Lord to remove this blood from us, so that we will believe in you and send the Children of Israel with you. So he called upon his Lord, and He removed them, but they did not believe and did not send the Children of Israel with him. Thus, Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yasar, may God have mercy on him, said: “The enemy of God, Pharaoh, returned when the magicians believed, defeated and shackled. Then he refused to do anything except remain in disbelief and persist in evil. So God continued to send signs upon him, so He seized him with years and sent upon him the flood, then locusts, then lice, then frogs, then blood, detailed signs. So He sent the flood, which is water, and it overflowed the face of the earth, then it stagnated, and they were unable to plow or do anything until they were exhausted from hunger. When that reached them, “They said, ‘O Moses, call upon your Lord for us according to what He has promised you: If you remove this punishment from us, we will believe in you and send with you the Children of Israel. ’” So Moses called upon his Lord, and He removed it from them, but they did not fulfill anything of what they said. So God sent upon them locusts, and they ate the trees, as I have heard, until they were eating the iron nails of doors until their houses and dwellings collapsed. They said as they said, so he called upon his Lord, and He removed it from them, but they did not fulfill anything of what they said. So God sent upon them lice. It was mentioned to me that Moses, peace be upon him, was commanded to walk to a sand dune and strike it. With his staff, he walked to a huge hill of Ahil and struck it with it, and lice swarmed upon them until they covered the houses and food and prevented them from sleeping and resting. When he exhausted them, they said the same as they had said, so he called upon his Lord, and He removed them, but they did not fulfill anything of what they had said. So God sent frogs upon them, and they filled the houses, food, and vessels. No one uncovered a garment or food except that he found frogs in it, and they had overwhelmed it. When he exhausted them, they said the same as they had said, so he called upon his Lord, and He removed them, but they did not fulfill anything of what they had said. So God sent blood upon them, and the waters of Pharaoh’s people became blood. They did not draw water from a well or a river, nor did they scoop from a vessel, but it became foul blood. So God replaced it with the coolest water that He knew of, and made their croaking glorification of God. And it was narrated on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, something similar. Zayd ibn Aslam said: He meant nosebleeds by blood. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

They say, Whatever sign you bring us, evidence, and proof you present, we will reject it, and we will not accept it from you, nor will we believe in you or what you have brought. God Almighty said, So We sent upon them the flood. They differed in its meaning. According to Ibn Abbas in a narration, it means abundant, torrential rains that destroy crops and fruits, and Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim said the same. According to Ibn Abbas in another narration, it means abundant death, and so said Ata'. Mujahid said, The flood is water and plague in any case. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hisham Al-Rafa’i told us, Yahya bin Yaman told us, Al-Munhal bin Khalifa told us, on the authority of Al-Hajjaj, on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Mina’, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The flood is death. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it in the same way from the hadith of Yahya bin Yaman, and it is a strange hadith. Ibn Abbas said in another narration: It is a command from God that swept over them, then he recited: And a company from your Lord swept over them while they were asleep. 7:136: God Almighty informs us that when they rebelled and rebelled, despite His testing them with successive signs one after the other, He took revenge on them by drowning them in the sea, which is the sea that He parted for Moses, so he crossed it and the Children of Israel with him, then Pharaoh and his soldiers returned to it after them, and when they had completed it, it crashed upon them and they drowned, all of them, because of their denial of God’s signs and their neglect of them. God Almighty informed us that He gave the people who were oppressed, namely the Children of Israel, the east and west of the earth inheritance, as God Almighty said: “And We desired to bestow a favor upon those who were oppressed in the land and make them leaders and make them heirs * And establish them in the land and show Pharaoh and Haman and their soldiers from them that which they feared.” God Almighty also said: How many gardens and springs did they leave behind * And crops and noble positions * And comfort in which they used to delight * Thus We caused another people to inherit it. And from Al-Hasan Al-Basri and Qatadah in His statement the easts of the earth and its wests which We blessed it meaning Ash-Sham. And His statement, And the good word of your Lord was fulfilled for the Children of Israel because of their patience Mujahid and Ibn Jarir said that it is the statement of God Almighty: “And We desired to bestow a favor upon those who were oppressed in the land and make them leaders and make them inheritors * And establish them in the land and show Pharaoh and Haman and their soldiers from them that which they had feared.” And His statement, And We destroyed what Pharaoh and his people had made meaning, We destroyed what Pharaoh and his people had made of buildings and farms. And what they had erected Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said, Erected means built.
7:137: God Almighty informs us that when they rebelled and rebelled, despite His testing them with successive signs one after the other, He took revenge on them by drowning them in the sea, which is the sea that He parted for Moses, so he crossed it and the Children of Israel with him, then Pharaoh and his soldiers returned to it after them, and when they had completed it, it crashed upon them and they drowned, all of them, because of their denial of God’s signs and their neglect of them. God Almighty informed us that He gave the people who were oppressed, namely the Children of Israel, the east and west of the earth inheritance, as God Almighty said: “And We desired to bestow a favor upon those who were oppressed in the land and make them leaders and make them heirs * And establish them in the land and show Pharaoh and Haman and their soldiers from them that which they feared.” God Almighty also said: How many gardens and springs did they leave behind * And crops and noble positions * And comfort in which they used to delight * Thus We caused another people to inherit it. And from Al-Hasan Al-Basri and Qatadah in His statement the easts of the earth and its wests which We blessed it meaning Ash-Sham. And His statement, And the good word of your Lord was fulfilled for the Children of Israel because of their patience Mujahid and Ibn Jarir said that it is the statement of God Almighty: “And We desired to bestow a favor upon those who were oppressed in the land and make them leaders and make them inheritors * And establish them in the land and show Pharaoh and Haman and their soldiers from them that which they had feared.” And His statement, And We destroyed what Pharaoh and his people had made meaning, We destroyed what Pharaoh and his people had made of buildings and farms. And what they had erected Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said, Erected means built.
7:138: God Almighty tells us what the ignorant children of Israel said to Moses, peace be upon him, when they crossed the sea and saw the signs of God and His great power, and they came meaning they passed by a people who were devoted to their idols. Some commentators said that they were Canaanites, and it was said that they were Lakhm. Ibn Jarir said: They used to worship idols in the form of cows, so that raised doubts for them in their worship of the calf after that, so they said, O Moses, make for us a god as they have gods. He said, Indeed, you are a people behaving ignorantly, meaning you are ignorant of the greatness and majesty of God and what He must be free from of partners and equals. Indeed, what they are in will perish, meaning they will perish, and what they used to do will be in vain. Imam Abu Ja`far Ibn Jarir narrated in his interpretation of this verse from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, `Aqil, and Mu`ammar, all on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Sinan ibn Abi Sinan, on the authority of Abu Waqid al-Laythi, “that they went out from Mecca with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Hunayn. He said, “And the infidels had a lote tree near which they would devote themselves and hang their weapons on, called Dhat Anwat.” He said, So we passed by a great green lote tree. He said, So we said, O Messenger of God, make for us a Dhat Anwat as they have a Dhat Anwat. He said, “You said, by the One in Whose hand is my soul, as the people of Moses said to Moses, ‘Make for us a god as they have a Dhat Anwat. ’ He said, ‘You said, by the One in Whose hand is my soul, as the people of Moses said to Moses, ‘Make for us a god as they have a Dhat Anwat. ’” They have gods. He said, “Indeed, you are a people behaving ignorantly. Indeed, what they are doing is lost, and what they have been doing is futile.” Imam Ahmad said: “Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Sinan ibn Abi Sinan al-Dailami, on the authority of Abu Waqid al-Laythi, who said: We went out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, before Hunayn, and we passed by a lote-tree. I said, “O Prophet of God, make this for us a Dhat Anwat, as the infidels have a Dhat Anwat.” The infidels used to hang their weapons on a lote-tree and devote themselves around it. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “God is Great. This is like what the Children of Israel said to Moses, ‘Make for us a god as they have gods. You are following the ways of those before you.’” Ibn Jarir included it and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of Katheer ibn Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Awf al-Muzani, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet.

7:140: Moses, peace be upon him, reminds them of God’s blessings upon them, such as saving them from Pharaoh’s captivity and oppression, and the humiliation and disgrace they were in, and the glory and satisfaction they have gained from their enemy, and looking at him in his state of humiliation, destruction, drowning, and devastation. The explanation of this has been presented in Surat Al-Baqarah.
7:141: Moses, peace be upon him, reminds them of God’s blessings upon them, such as saving them from Pharaoh’s captivity and oppression, and the humiliation and disgrace they were in, and the glory and satisfaction they have gained from their enemy, and looking at him in his state of humiliation, destruction, drowning, and devastation. The explanation of this has been presented in Surat Al-Baqarah.
7:142: The Almighty says, thanking the Children of Israel for the guidance they received by speaking to Moses, peace be upon him, and giving him the Torah, which contains their rulings and details of their law. The Almighty mentioned that He promised Moses thirty nights. The commentators said that Moses, peace be upon him, fasted and completed them. When the appointed time was completed, he used the bark of a tree, and the Almighty commanded him to complete forty with ten. The commentators differed about what these ten are. Most of them say that the thirty is Dhul-Qi'dah, and the ten is Dhul-Hijjah. This was said by Mujahid, Masruq, and Ibn Jurayj. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas and others. Based on this, the appointed time was completed on the Day of Sacrifice, and speaking to Moses, peace be upon him, occurred on it, and on it God completed the religion for Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as the Almighty said: This day I have perfected your religion for you, completed My favor upon you, and have approved for you Islam as religion. When the appointed time was completed and Moses resolved to go to the mountain, as the Almighty said: O Children of Israel, We have saved you from your enemy and made an appointment with you on the right side of the mountain. The verse, then Moses, peace be upon him, appointed his brother Aaron as his successor over the Children of Israel and commanded him to reform and not cause corruption. This is a warning and a reminder. Otherwise, Aaron, peace be upon him, is a noble and honorable prophet with God, and he has prestige and majesty. May God’s prayers and peace be upon him and upon all the prophets.
7:143: God Almighty tells us about Moses, peace be upon him, that when he came to his appointed time with God Almighty and God Almighty spoke to him, he asked God Almighty to look at him and said, My Lord, show me, that I may look at You. He said, You will never see Me. The letter lan here has been confusing to many scholars because it is used to negate eternity, so the Mu'tazila used it as evidence to negate seeing in this world and the hereafter. This is the weakest of the opinions because the hadiths from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, have been transmitted that the believers will see God in the hereafter, as we will mention when God Almighty says, Some faces, that Day, will be radiant, looking at their Lord. And the Almighty said, informing about the disbelievers, No indeed, they will be veiled from their Lord that Day. It was said that it is to deny eternity in this world, combining this verse with the conclusive evidence for the validity of the vision in the Hereafter. It was said that this statement in this context is like the statement in the Almighty’s statement, “No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps all vision. He is the Subtle, the Acquainted.” This was mentioned previously in Al-An’am and in the previous books that God the Almighty said to Moses, peace be upon him, O Moses, no living thing sees Me except that it dies, and no dry thing except that it crumbles. For this reason, God the Almighty said, But when his Lord revealed Himself to the mountain, He rendered it level, and Moses fell unconscious. Abu Ja’far ibn Jarir al-Tabari said in his interpretation of this verse, Ahmad ibn Suhayl al-Wasiti told us, Qurrah ibn Isa told us, al-A’mash told us, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, who said: When his Lord revealed Himself to the mountain, He pointed with His finger and rendered it level. Abu Ismail showed us with his index finger, this chain of transmission contains an unknown man who was not named, then he said Al-Muthanna told me, Hajjaj bin Munhal told us, Hammad told us on the authority of Laith on the authority of Anas that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse: But when his Lord revealed Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble. He said: This is how he said it with his finger, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, placed his thumb on the upper joint of the little finger, and the mountain crumbled. This is how it was mentioned in this narration: Hammad bin Salamah on the authority of Laith on the authority of Anas, and the famous one is Hammad bin Salamah on the authority of Thabit on the authority of Anas, as Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna told me, Hudbah bin Khalid told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us on the authority of Thabit on the authority of Anas, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: But when his Lord revealed Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble. He said: And he placed his thumb close to the tip of his little finger. He said: The mountain crumbled. Hamid said to Thabit: He says this, so Thabit raised his hand and struck Hamid’s chest and said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, says this, and Anas says this, and I conceal it? And thus Imam Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad: Abu Al-Muthanna Muadh bin Muadh Al-Anbari told us: Hammad bin Salamah told us: Thabit Al-Banani told us: Anas bin Malik told us: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said regarding his statement: Then when his Lord revealed Himself to the mountain, he said: He said: Like this, meaning that he stuck out the tip of his little finger. Ahmad said: Muadh showed us, and Humayd Al-Tawil said to him: What do you want with this, O Abu Muhammad? He said: He struck his chest hard and said: Who are you, O Humayd, and what are you, O Humayd? Anas bin Malik tells me this from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: What do you want with this? And thus it was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi in his interpretation of this verse on the authority of Abdul-Wahhab bin Al-Hakam Al-Warraq on the authority of Muadh bin Muadh on his authority, and on the authority of Abdullah bin Abdul-Rahman Al-Darimi on the authority of Sulayman bin Harb on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah on his authority, then he said: This is a good, authentic, strange hadith that we do not know except from the hadith of Hammad. And thus it was narrated by Al-Hakim in his Mustadrak from various chains of narration on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah on his authority, and he said: This is an authentic hadith according to the conditions of Muslim, and they did not include it. And it was narrated by Abu Muhammad bin Al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin Ali Al-Khalal on the authority of Muhammad bin Ali bin Suwaid on the authority of Abu Al-Qasim Al-Baghawi on the authority of Hudbah bin Khalid on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, and he mentioned it and said: This is an authentic chain of narration with no defect in it. And Dawud bin Al-Muhayyir narrated it on the authority of Shu’bah on the authority of Thabit on the authority of Anas, with a chain of narration traceable to the Prophet, and this is nothing, because Dawud bin Al-Muhayyir is a liar. It was narrated by the two Hafizs Abu Al-Qasim Al-Tabarani and Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh through two chains of narration on the authority of Sa’id bin Abi ‘Aruba on the authority of Qatadah on the authority of Anas, with a chain of narration traceable to the Prophet, in a similar manner. And it was narrated by Ibn Mardawayh on the authority of Ibn Al-Bilamani on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn ‘Umar, with a chain of narration traceable to the Prophet, and there is no… It is also authentic. It was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi and authenticated by Al-Hakim, who said it meets the conditions of Muslim. Al-Suddi said on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the statement of God the Almighty: So when his Lord revealed Himself to the mountain, he said, He revealed only the size of a little finger from it, “He made it crumble, he said, Dust, “And Moses fell unconscious,” he said, unconscious. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Qatada said, And Moses fell unconscious, he said, dead. Sufyan al-Thawri said, The mountain sank into the earth until it fell into the sea, so it goes with it. Sunayd said on the authority of Hajjaj bin Muhammad al-A’war on the authority of Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, So when his Lord revealed Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble, it sank and went under the earth, so it will not appear until the Day of Resurrection. It came in some reports that it sank into the earth, so it will fall into it until the Day of Resurrection. Narrated by Ibn Mardawayh. Ibn Abi Hatim said, Umar bin Shabbah told us, Muhammad bin Yahya Abu Ghassan al-Kinani told us, Abdul Aziz bin Imran told us, on the authority of Mu’awiyah bin Abdullah, on the authority of al-Jild bin Ayyub, on the authority of Mu’awiyah bin Qurrah, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, When God revealed Himself to the mountains, they flew away. For his greatness, six mountains fell, three in Medina and three in Mecca: in Medina, Uhud, Warqan and Radwa, and in Mecca, Hira, Thabir and Thawr fell. This is a strange hadith, rather it is rejected. Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was mentioned on the authority of Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Abi Al-Thalj, who told us, Al-Haitham bin Kharijah told us, Uthman bin Husayn bin Al-Alaaf told us, on the authority of Urwah bin Ruwaim, who said: The mountains were solid and smooth before God revealed Himself to Moses on the mountain. When God revealed Himself to Moses on the mountain, they were crushed and the mountains split, creating cracks and caves. Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said: But when his Lord revealed Himself to the mountain, He rendered it level and Moses fell unconscious. This is because when the cover was removed and the mountain saw the light, it became like a piece of dust. Some of them said that it was made level, meaning a trial. Mujahid said about his statement: But look at the mountain; if it remains in its place, then you will see Me, that it is larger than you and more powerful in creation. But when his Lord revealed Himself to the mountain, so he looked at the mountain and could not control himself, and the mountain turned and was crushed on its head. Moses saw what the mountain was doing and fell down. A stun. Ikrimah said, He made it level. He said, God looked at the mountain and it became a desert of dust. Some reciters read this reading, and Ibn Jarir chose it. A hadith attributed to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was narrated about it by Ibn Mardawayh. What is known is that stun is fainting here, as Ibn Abbas and others interpreted it, not as Qatadah interpreted it as death, even though it is correct in the language, like the Almighty’s statement: “And the Trumpet will be blown, and all who are in the heavens and the earth will fall unconscious except whom God wills. Then it will be blown again, and at once they will be standing, looking on.” There is an indication that indicates death, just as here there is an indication that indicates fainting. It is His statement, So when he regained consciousness, and regaining consciousness only occurs after fainting. He said, ‘Glory be to You,’ as a sign of glorification, magnification, and reverence that no one in this world would see Him except that he would die. And his saying, I repent to You, Mujahid said, that I ask You to see me, “and I am the first of the believers,” Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said, from the Children of Israel, and Ibn Jarir chose it. In another narration from Ibn Abbas, and I am the first of the believers, that no one sees You. And Abu al-Aaliyah said the same, there were believers before him, but he says, I am the first to believe in You, that no one from Your creation sees You until the Day of Resurrection. This is a good statement that has a direction. Muhammad ibn Jarir mentioned in his interpretation here a long trace in which there are strange and amazing things on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar, and it seems that he received it from the Israelites, and God knows best. And his saying, and Moses fell unconscious, in it is Abu Saeed and Abu Hurairah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. As for the hadith of Abu Saeed, al-Bukhari attributed it in his Sahih here, and he said, Muhammad ibn Yusuf told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Yahya al-Mazini, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Saeed al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, who said, “A Jewish man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he had slapped his face,” and he said, O Muhammad, a man from your companions from the Ansar slapped my face. He said, Call him, so they called him. He said, Why did you slap him in the face? He said, "O Messenger of God, I passed by the Jew and heard him say, 'By Him who chose Moses over mankind.' He said, 'And also Muhammad?' I said, 'And also Muhammad.' And I became angry and slapped him. He said, 'Do not choose me among the prophets, for people will fall unconscious on the Day of Resurrection and I will be the first to regain consciousness. Then I will see Moses holding one of the pillars of the Throne and I will not know whether he regained consciousness before me or was rewarded with the stun of Mount Mount.'" Al-Bukhari narrated it in many places in his Sahih, and Muslim in Hadith of the Prophets, and Abu Dawud in the Book of the Sunnah from his Sunan, through various chains of transmission on the authority of Amr ibn Yahya ibn 'Ammarah ibn Abi al-Hasan al-Mazini al-Ansari al-Madani, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Sa'id Sa'd ibn Malik ibn Sinan al-Khudri, on his authority. As for the hadith of Abu Hurairah, Imam Ahmad said in his Musnad: Abu Kamil told us, Ibrahim bin Saad told us, Ibn Shihab told us, on the authority of Abu Salamah bin Abd al-Rahman and Abd al-Rahman al-A’raj, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: Two men quarreled, a Muslim man and a Jewish man. The Muslim said: By Him Who chose Muhammad over all the worlds. The Jew said: By Him Who chose Moses over all the worlds. The Muslim became angry with the Jew and slapped him. The Jew came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him. He told him, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called him and he confessed to that. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Do not give me precedence over Moses, for the people will faint on the Day of Resurrection and I will be the first to regain consciousness. Then Moses will be holding on to the side of the Throne, and I do not know whether he was among those who fainted and regained consciousness before me or whether he was among those whom God Almighty excepted.” They both included it in their Sahihs on the authority of al-Zuhri. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr bin Abi Al-Dunya, may God have mercy on him, narrated that the one who slapped the Jew in this case was Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him. However, it was mentioned in the two Sahihs that he was a man from the Ansar, and this is more correct and clear, and God knows best. The discussion of his saying, peace be upon him: Do not give me precedence over Moses is like the discussion of his saying, Do not give me precedence over the prophets or over Jonah, son of Matta. It was said that it was out of humility, and it was said that it was before he knew about that, and it was said that he forbade giving precedence over them out of anger and fanaticism, and it was said that it was said out of mere opinion and desire, and God knows best. As for his saying, Then people will be struck dumb on the Day of Resurrection, it appears that this striking will take place on the plains of Resurrection, and something will happen that will cause them to be struck dumb, and God knows best about it. This may be if the Lord, Blessed and Exalted be He, came to pass judgment and revealed Himself to the creatures as the King, the Judge, as Moses was struck dumb by the revelation of the Lord, Blessed and Exalted be He. For this reason, he, peace be upon him, said, I do not know whether he regained consciousness before me or was rewarded by the thunderbolt of the mountain. Judge Iyad narrated in the beginning of his book Al-Shifa’ on the authority of Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Marzouq, who said, “Qatadah told us, Al-Hasan told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Yahya ibn Waththab, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said, ‘When God revealed Himself to Moses, peace be upon him, he could see an ant on a rock on a dark night, a distance of ten farsakhs.’ Then he said, ‘It is not far-fetched that our Prophet was singled out for what we have mentioned in this regard after the Night Journey and the blessing of what he saw of the great signs of his Lord.’ This is the end of what he said. It seems that he authenticated this hadith, and there is doubt about its authenticity. The men in its chain of transmission are not free of unknowns who are not known. Such a thing is only accepted from the narration of a just and accurate person from his like until it reaches its end. And God knows best.
7:144: The Almighty mentions that He addressed Moses, saying that He chose him over the people of his time with His messages and His speech. There is no doubt that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is the master of the children of Adam from the first to the last. For this reason, God Almighty singled him out by making him the Seal of the Prophets and Messengers, whose law will continue until the Day of Judgment. His followers are more numerous than the followers of all the other prophets and messengers. After him in honor and virtue is Abraham, the friend of God, peace be upon him, then Moses, son of Imran, the one who spoke to the Most Merciful, peace be upon him. For this reason, God Almighty said to him: So take what I have given you, meaning of speech and intimate conversation, and be among the grateful, meaning for that and do not ask for what you cannot bear. Then the Almighty informed that He wrote for him on the tablets of everything, an admonition and a detailed explanation of everything. It was said that the tablets were made of a substance and that God Almighty wrote for him in them admonitions and detailed rulings explaining what was permissible and what was forbidden. These tablets included the Torah, about which God Almighty said: And We gave Moses the Scripture after We destroyed the former generations as insight for the people. It was said that the tablets were given to Moses before The Torah, and God knows best. In any case, it was like compensation for what he asked for in terms of seeing God and was prevented from seeing Him, and God knows best. And His saying, Take it with strength, meaning with determination to obey, and command your people to take the best of it. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said, Abu Saeed told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said, “Moses, peace be upon him, was commanded to take the most severe of what he commanded his people.” And His saying, I will show you the abode of the wicked, meaning, you will see the consequences of those who disobey My command and rebel against My obedience, how they will end up in destruction, devastation, and ruin. Ibn Jarir said, “He only said, ‘I will show you the abode of the wicked,’ as someone says to someone he is addressing, ‘I will show you tomorrow,’ as a threat and warning to those who disobey Him and oppose His command.” Then the meaning of that was transmitted from Mujahid and Al-Hasan Al-Basri, and it was said that its meaning was, I will show you the abode of the wicked, meaning, of the people of Ash-Sham, and I will give it to you. It was also said, The dwellings of the people of Pharaoh, and the first is more appropriate, and God knows best, because this was after Moses and his people had separated from the land of Egypt, and it was addressed to the Children of Israel before they entered the wilderness, and God knows best.

Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said, Abu Saeed told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said, “Moses, peace be upon him, was commanded to take the most severe of what he commanded his people.” And His saying, I will show you the abode of the wicked, meaning, you will see the consequences of those who disobey My command and rebel against My obedience, how they will end up in destruction, devastation, and ruin. Ibn Jarir said, “He only said, ‘I will show you the abode of the wicked,’ as someone says to someone he is addressing, ‘I will show you tomorrow,’ as a threat and warning to those who disobey Him and oppose His command.” Then the meaning of that was transmitted from Mujahid and Al-Hasan Al-Basri, and it was said that its meaning was, I will show you the abode of the wicked, meaning, of the people of Ash-Sham, and I will give it to you. It was also said, The dwellings of the people of Pharaoh, and the first is more appropriate, and God knows best, because this was after Moses and his people had separated from the land of Egypt, and it was addressed to the Children of Israel before they entered the wilderness, and God knows best.
7:146: God the Almighty says: I will turn away from My signs those who are arrogant on earth without right meaning I will prevent the understanding of the arguments and evidence indicating My greatness, My law and My rulings from the hearts of the arrogant from obeying Me and they will act arrogantly towards people without right, meaning just as they were arrogant without right, God will humiliate them with ignorance as God the Almighty says: And We will turn away their hearts and their eyes just as they did not believe in it the first time and God the Almighty says: So when they deviated, God caused their hearts to deviate and some of the predecessors said: Knowledge is not attained by the modest or the arrogant, and another said: Whoever does not endure the humiliation of learning for an hour will remain in that ignorance forever, and Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said in His statement: I will turn away from My signs those who are arrogant on earth without right he said: I will take away from them the understanding of the Qur'an and turn them away from My signs, Ibn Jarir said: This indicates that this address is for this nation, I said this is not necessary because Ibn Uyaynah only meant that this is general for every nation and there is no difference between anyone And one in this, and God knows best. And His statement, And if they see every sign, they will not believe in it, as God the Most High said, Indeed, those against whom the word of your Lord has come into effect will not believe, even if every sign came to them, until they see the painful punishment. And His statement, And if they see the path of right guidance, they will not take it as a way, meaning, even if the path of right guidance, meaning the path of salvation, appears to them, they will not follow it, and if the path of destruction and misguidance appears to them, they will take it as a way. Then He explained their fate in this state by His statement, That is because they denied Our signs, meaning their hearts denied them, and were heedless of them, meaning, they did not know anything of what was in them. And His statement, And those who denied Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter, their deeds have become worthless, meaning, whoever among them did that and continued in it until death, his deeds have become worthless. And His statement, Are they recompensed except for what they used to do? Meaning, We will only recompense them according to the deeds they did before, if good, then good, and if evil, then evil, and as you judge, you will be judged.

7:148: The Almighty tells about the misguidance of those who went astray from the Children of Israel in their worship of the calf that the Samaritan made for them, from the ornaments of the Copts that they had borrowed from them, so he shaped it into a calf for them, then he threw into it the handful of dirt that he had taken from the trace of Gabriel’s horse, peace be upon him, so it became a calf with a body that mooed: and the mooing is the sound of cows, and this was from them after Moses went to meet his Lord, the Almighty, so God informed him of that while he was on the mountain, where the Almighty says, informing about His noble self, He said, ‘We have indeed tried your people after you, and the Samaritan has led them astray.’ The commentators differed about this calf, did it become flesh and blood that mooed, or did it remain made of gold except that air entered it and it made a sound like a cow, according to two opinions, and God knows best. It is said that when the calf made a sound to them, they danced around it and were fascinated by it and said, This is your god and the god of Moses, but he forgot. God Almighty said: Do they not see that it does not return to them a word and that it does not possess for them any harm or benefit? And He said in this noble verse: Have they not seen that it does not speak to them or guide them to a way? God Almighty denounces them for their misguidance with the calf and their neglect of the Creator of the heavens and the earth, the Lord of everything and its King, that they worshipped with it a calf with a body that mooed and did not speak to them or guide them to good, but the blindness of ignorance and misguidance covered the eyes of their insight, as mentioned in the narration of Imam Ahmad and Abu Dawud on the authority of Abu al-Darda’, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Loving something blinds and deafens. And his saying, And when it fell into their hands, meaning they regretted what they did, and saw that they had gone astray, they said, ‘If our Lord does not have mercy on us and forgive us,’ and some of them read, If you do not have mercy on us with the double ta’ above, our Lord is the vocative. And forgive us, lest we be among the losers.” That is, among the doomed. This is an admission of their sin and a resort to God Almighty.
