7:150: God the Almighty tells us that when Moses, peace be upon him, returned to his people from his intimate conversation with his Lord, the Almighty, he was angry and sad. Abu Darda said that sadness is the most intense anger. He said, ‘How evil is that which you have done in replacing me after me.’ He said, How evil is that which you have done in worshipping the calf after I left you. And His statement, Did you hasten the command of your Lord? He said, You hastened my coming to you, which was decreed by God the Almighty. And His statement, And he threw down the tablets and seized his brother by the head, dragging him toward him. It was said that the tablets were made of emerald, and it was said that they were made of ruby, and it was said that they were made of hail. This is evidence of what came in the hadith: Hearing is not like seeing. Then the apparent context is that he only threw down the tablets out of anger at his people, and this is the statement of the majority of scholars, past and present. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Qatada a strange statement regarding this, the chain of transmission of which is not valid to the account of Qatada. Ibn Atiyah and more than one of the scholars rejected it, and it is worthy of rejection, as if Qatada received it from some of the People of the Book, among whom were liars, fabricators, slanderers, and heretics. And his saying, And he took hold of his brother’s head, dragging him towards him, was out of fear that he had fallen short in forbidding them, as He said in the other verse, “He said, ‘O Aaron, what prevented you, when you saw them going astray, from following me? Did you disobey my command?’ He said, ‘O son of my mother, do not seize me by my beard or by my head. Indeed, I feared that you would say, ‘You have divided the Children of Israel and did not respect my word.’” And He said here, “O son of my mother, indeed the people have weakened me and almost killed me. So do not let the enemies rejoice over me and do not place me with the wrongdoing people.’” That is, do not lead me into their path and place me with them. Rather, He said, O son of my mother, so that it would be more gentle and effective for him, otherwise he would be his brother through his father and mother. So when Moses, peace be upon him, was certain of the innocence of Aaron, peace be upon him, as God Almighty said, And Aaron had already said to them before, ‘O my people, you are only being tested by it, and your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me and obey my command.’ At that time, Moses said, ‘My Lord, forgive me and my brother and admit us into Your mercy, for You are the Most Merciful of the merciful.’ And Ibn Abi Hatim said, Al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin Al-Sabah told us, Affan narrated to us Abu Awana on the authority of Abu Bishr on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “May God have mercy on Moses. The one who witnesses is not like the one who is informed. His Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, informed him that his people would be tempted after him, but he did not throw up the tablets. But when he saw them and witnessed them, he threw down the tablets.”

7:152: As for the anger that befell the Children of Israel in worshipping the calf, it is that God Almighty did not accept their repentance until they killed each other, as mentioned in Surat al-Baqarah 2:“So repent to your Creator and kill yourselves. That is better for you in the sight of your Creator. Then He will forgive you. Indeed, He is the Accepter of Repentance, the Most Merciful.” As for humiliation, that was followed by humiliation and disgrace in this worldly life. His statement: And thus do We recompense the slanderers is a result of everyone who invents an innovation, for the humiliation of innovation and opposition to guidance is connected from his heart to his shoulders, as Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: The humiliation of innovation is on their shoulders, even if the mules groan with them and the mules clatter with them. And thus Ayoub Al-Sakhtiyani narrated on the authority of Abu Qilabah Al-Jarmi that he recited this verse: And thus do We recompense the slanderers and said: By God, it is for every slanderer until the Day of Resurrection. Sufyan bin Uyaynah said: Every innovator is humiliated. Then God Almighty alerted His servants and guided them to the fact that He accepts Repentance of His servants from any sin, even if it was disbelief, polytheism, hypocrisy or discord. That is why He followed this story with His saying: And those who have committed evil deeds and then repented thereafter and believed - indeed, your Lord is, thereafter, Forgiving and Merciful. That is, O Muhammad, O Messenger of repentance and Prophet of Mercy, thereafter that is, after that action, is Forgiving and Merciful. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Muslim bin Ibrahim told us, Aban told us, Qatadah told us, on the authority of Azra, on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Arni, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, that he was asked about that, meaning about a man who commits adultery with a woman and then marries her, so he recited this verse: And those who have committed evil deeds and then repented thereafter and believed - indeed, your Lord is, thereafter, Forgiving and Merciful. Abdullah recited it ten times, but he did not command them to do it or forbid them from it.

7:154: God Almighty says: And when Moses' anger subsided meaning his anger at his people he took the tablets meaning the ones he had thrown down out of intense anger at their worship of the calf out of jealousy for God and anger for Him and in their inscription was guidance and mercy for those who fear their Lord Many commentators say that when he threw them down they were broken and then he put them together after that and for this reason some of the predecessors said that he found in them guidance and mercy, and as for the details, they went and claimed that their pieces remained in the treasuries of the kings of the Children of Israel until the Islamic state and God knows best the correctness of this. As for the clear evidence that they were broken when he threw them down and they are from the essence of Paradise, God Almighty informed us that when he took them after he threw them down he found in them guidance and mercy for those who fear their Lord He included fear in the meaning of submission, and for this reason it is transitive with the preposition lam. Qatada said: Regarding the Almighty’s saying: He took the tablets, he said: “My Lord, indeed I find in the tablets a nation, the best nation produced for mankind. They enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, so make them my nation.” He said: That is the nation of Ahmad. He said: My Lord, indeed I find in the tablets a nation who are the last and the foremost, meaning the last in creation, the first in entering Paradise. My Lord, make them my nation. He said: That is the nation of Ahmad. He said: “My Lord, indeed I find in the tablets a nation whose Gospels are in their chests, which they read. And those before them used to read their books, looking until, when they lifted them up, they did not memorize a thing nor did they recognize it. And God gave them a degree of memorization that He had not given to any other nation.” He said: My Lord, make them my nation. He said: That is the nation of Ahmad. He said: My Lord, indeed I find in the tablets a nation who believe in the first book and the last book and fight the factions of misguidance until they fight the one-eyed liar, so make them my nation. He said: That is the nation of Ahmad. He said, "My Lord, indeed I find in the Tablets a nation whose charity they consume in their bellies and are rewarded for it. And there were nations before them who, if they gave charity and it was accepted from them, God would send upon it a fire which would consume it, but if it was returned to them, it would be left and eaten by wild beasts and birds. And God has taken their charity from their rich for their poor." He said, My Lord, then make them my nation. He said, That is the nation of Ahmad. He said, "My Lord, indeed I find in the Tablets a nation who, if one of them intended to do a good deed but did not do it, a good deed would be recorded for him, and if he did it, ten like it would be recorded for him, up to seven hundred. My Lord, make them my nation." He said, That is the nation of Ahmad. He said, My Lord, indeed I find in the Tablets a nation who are the intercessors and for whom intercession is made, so make them my nation. He said, That is the nation of Ahmad. Qatada said, "It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, Moses, peace be upon him, threw away the Tablets and said, "O God, make me from the nation of Ahmad."
7:155: Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas in the interpretation of this verse, God had commanded him to choose seventy men from his people, so he chose seventy men and they went out to call upon their Lord. Among what they called upon God was that they said, O God, give us what You have not given to anyone before us and will not give to anyone after us. God disliked that from their call, so the earthquake took them. He said, 'My Lord, if You had willed, You could have destroyed them before and me' verse. Al-Suddi said: God commanded Moses to come to Him with thirty of the Children of Israel to apologize to Him for worshipping the calf, and He promised them an appointment. And Moses chose from his people seventy men in front of his eyes, then he went with them to apologize. When they reached that place, they said, We will not believe in you O Moses, until we see God plainly for you have spoken to Him, so show Him. So the thunderbolt took them and they died. Moses stood up crying and calling upon God, saying, My Lord, what shall I say to the Children of Israel when I meet them, and You have destroyed the best of them? "My Lord, if You had willed, You could have destroyed them before and me" verse. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: Moses chose from the Children of Israel seventy good men, one after the other, and said: Go to God and repent to Him for what you have done and ask Him to forgive those of your people whom you have left behind you. Fast and purify yourselves and purify your clothes. So he went out with them to Mount Sinai for the appointed time that his Lord had set for him. He would not come to it except with His permission and knowledge. So the seventy said to him, as I have mentioned, when they did what he had commanded them to do and went out with him to meet his Lord to Moses: Ask for us to hear the speech of our Lord. He said: I will do it. So when Moses approached the mountain, a pillar of cloud fell upon him until it covered the entire mountain. Moses approached and entered it and said to the al-Nas 114:Come closer. And when God spoke to Moses, a bright light fell upon Moses’ forehead that no one from the children of Adam could look at. So a veil was placed between him and the people approached, until when they entered the cloud, they fell in prostration and they heard him speaking to Moses, commanding him and forbidding him to do and not to do. So when he finished with his command to him and the cloud cleared from Moses, he came to them and they said: O Moses, we will not believe you until we see God. Then the thunderbolt struck them openly, and their souls met and they all died. Then Moses stood up, beseeching his Lord, calling upon Him, and beseeching Him, saying, My Lord, if You had willed, You could have destroyed them before and me. They had acted foolishly, so will You destroy those of the Children of Israel who come after me? Sufyan al-Thawri said: Abu Ishaq told me on the authority of Ammarah ibn Ubayd al-Saluli on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, who said: Moses, Aaron, Shiber, and Shabir set out and went to the foot of a mountain. Aaron slept on a bed, and God Almighty took him. When Moses returned to the Children of Israel, they said to him: Where is Aaron? He said: God Almighty took him. They said: You killed him. You envied us for his character and his gentleness, or something similar. He said: Then choose whomever you wish. He said: So they chose seventy men. He said: This is what God Almighty said: And Moses chose from his people seventy men. When they came to him, they said: O Aaron, who killed you? He said: No one killed me, but God caused me to die. They said: O Moses, you will never disobey again from today onwards. So the earthquake seized them. Moses began to turn right and left and said: O Lord, “If You had willed, You could have destroyed them and me before. Will You destroy us for what the fools among us have done? It is only Your trial by which You lead astray whom You will and guide whom You will.” He said: So God revived them and made them all prophets. This is a very strange narration. I do not know this Ammarah ibn Ubayd. Shu`bah narrated it on the authority of Abu Ishaq on the authority of a man from Banu Salul on the authority of Ali, and he mentioned it. Ibn Abbas, Qatada, Mujahid and Ibn Jarir said: The earthquake took them because they did not abandon their people in their worship of the calf or forbid them. This statement is supported by the words of Moses: Will You destroy us for what the fools among us have done? and his words: It is only Your trial, meaning your trial, test and examination. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Saeed bin Jubayr, Abu Al-Aaliyah, Al-Rabi’ bin Anas and more than one of the scholars of the Salaf and Khalaf. It has no meaning other than that. He says that the matter is only Your matter and the judgment is only Yours, so whatever You will is. You misguide whomever You will and guide whomever You will. There is no guide for whomever You misguide, nor can there be a misguider for whomever You guide, nor can there be a giver of what You prevent, nor can there be a preventer of what You give. So all of the kingdom is Yours and all of the judgment is Yours. You have creation and command. And His saying, You are our protector, so forgive us and have mercy upon us, and You are the best of forgivers. Forgiveness is covering and not holding one accountable for sin. When mercy is paired with forgiveness, it means that He will not cause him to fall into the same sin in the future. And You are the best of forgivers, meaning that no one forgives sin except You. And decree for us in this world [that which is] good and in the Hereafter. The first chapter of the supplication is to repel the forbidden. This is to achieve the intended purpose. And decree for us in this world [that which is] good and in the Hereafter, meaning make obligatory for us and establish for us in both of them good. The interpretation of good has already been presented in Surat Al-Baqarah. Indeed, we have been guided to You, meaning we have repented, returned, and turned to You. Ibn Abbas, Saeed bin Jubayr, Mujahid, Abu Al-Aaliyah, Ad-Dahhak, Ibrahim At-Taymi, As-Suddi, Qatadah, and more than one said: It is like this in language. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakee’ told us, my father told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Abdullah bin Yahya, on the authority of Ali, who said: The Jews were only called that because they said, Indeed, we have been guided to You. Jabir is the son of Yazid Al-Ja’fi, weak.
7:156: The Almighty says, answering Himself in His statement, It is only Your trial verse, He said, My punishment - I afflict with it whom I will, and My mercy encompasses all things verse, meaning I do what I will and I rule what I want, and I have wisdom and justice in all of that, glory be to Him, there is no god but Him. And the Almighty's statement, And My mercy encompasses all things verse is of great comprehensiveness and generality, like the Almighty's statement, informing about the bearers of the Throne and those around it, that they say, Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Samad told us, my father told us, al-Jariri told us on the authority of Abu Abdullah al-Jashmi, Jundub, who is the son of Abdullah al-Bajali, may God be pleased with him, told us: A Bedouin came and dismounted his camel, then tied it up, then prayed behind the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had finished praying, he came to his camel, untied its halter, mounted it, and called out, O God, have mercy on me and Muhammad, and do not associate anyone with Our mercy. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “Do you say, ‘This one is more astray or his camel? Did you not hear what he said?’ They said, ‘Yes.’ He said, ‘You have preserved a vast mercy. God Almighty created one hundred mercies, then sent down a mercy by which He sympathizes with His creation, jinn, humans, and animals. He kept ninety-nine mercies with Him. Do you say, ‘He is more astray or his camel?’” It was narrated by Ahmad and Abu Dawud, on the authority of Ali ibn Nasr, on the authority of Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Warith, on his authority. Imam Ahmad also said: Yahya ibn Sa`id narrated to us, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of Abu Uthman, on the authority of Salman, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God, the Almighty, has one hundred mercies, one of which is mercy by which creation is merciful to one another, and by which wild beasts are kind to their young. He has reserved ninety-nine for the Day of Resurrection.” Muslim is the only one to narrate it, as he narrated it from the hadith of Sulayman, who is Ibn Tarkhan, and Dawud ibn Abi Hind, both of them on the authority of Abu Uthman, whose name is Abd al-Rahman ibn Mal, on the authority of Salman, who is al-Farisi, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on his authority. Imam Ahmad said: Affan narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, on the authority of Asim ibn Bahdalah, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God has one hundred mercies, ninety-nine of which He has placed with you one by which you are merciful to one another between the jinn and mankind and between the creation. When the Day of Resurrection comes, He will gather them to Himself.” Ahmad is the only one to narrate it from this source. Ahmad said: Affan told us, Abdul Wahid told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Saeed, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God has one hundred mercies, and He divided one portion of them among His creation, by which people, beasts, and birds show mercy to one another. Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Abu Mu’awiyah, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on his authority. Al-Hafiz Abu Al-Qasim Al-Tabarani said: Muhammad bin Uthman bin Abi Shaybah told us, Ahmad bin Yunus told us, Sa’d Abu Ghailan Al-Shaybani told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Abi Sulayman, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Silah bin Zafar, on the authority of Hudhayfah bin Al-Yaman, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, the one who is wicked in his religion and foolish in his livelihood will enter Paradise. By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, the one whose sin has filled him with Hell will enter Paradise. By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, God will forgive on the Day of Resurrection a forgiveness that Satan will long for, hoping that it will reach him.” This is a very strange hadith, and I do not know this Sa’d. His statement, Then I will prescribe it for those who fear God, the verse, means, Then I will make My mercy obligatory. As a favor and kindness from Me to them, as the Almighty said: Your Lord has prescribed mercy for Himself. And His saying, for those who fear God, means I will make it for those who are characterized by these qualities, and they are the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Those who fear God, meaning polytheism and major sins. His saying, and give zakat, it was said that it is the zakat of souls, and it was said that it is money. It is possible that it is general for both of them, as the verse is Meccan. And those who believe in Our verses, meaning they confirm.
7:157: Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, whom they find written in what they have of the Torah and the Gospel. This is the description of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the books of the prophets. They gave good tidings to their nations of his mission and commanded them to follow him, and his descriptions are still present in their books, known by their scholars and rabbis. Imam Ahmad narrated: Ismail told us, on the authority of Al-Jariry, on the authority of Abu Sakhr Al-Uqaili, who said: A Bedouin told me: I brought a milking cow to Madinah during the lifetime of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. When I finished selling it, I said: I will meet this man and hear from him. He met me between Abu Bakr and Umar, walking, so I followed them until they came to a Jewish man spreading the Torah and reciting it, consoling himself for the death of his son, the most handsome and best of youths. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I ask you by Him who sent down the Torah, do you find in this book of yours my description and my coming out? He nodded like this, meaning no. His son said: Yes, by Him who sent down the Torah, we find in our book your description and your coming out, and I bear witness that there is no god but God and I bear witness that you are the Messenger of God. He said: Rescue the Jew from your brother. Then he took charge of shrouding him and praying over him. This is a good, strong hadith with a corroborating evidence in Sahih on the authority of Anas. Al-Hakim, the author of Al-Mustadrak, said: “Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Ishaq Al-Baghawi told us, Ibrahim bin Al-Haitham Al-Baldi told us, Abdul Aziz bin Muslim bin Idris told us, Abdullah bin Idris told us, on the authority of Shurahbil bin Muslim, on the authority of Abu Umamah Al-Bahili, on the authority of Hisham bin Al-Aas Al-Umawi, who said: I and another man were sent to Heraclius, the ruler of the Romans, to invite him to Islam. We went out until we reached Ghouta, meaning the Ghouta of Damascus, and we stayed with Jabalah bin Al-Ayham Al-Ghassani. We entered upon him and found him on a bed of his. He sent his messenger to us to speak to him. We said: By God, we will not speak to a messenger, but we have been sent to the king. If he gives us permission, we will speak to him, otherwise we will not speak to the messenger. The messenger returned to him and informed him of that. He said: So he gave us permission, and he said: Speak. So Hisham bin Al-Aas spoke to him and invited him to Islam. He was wearing black clothes. Hisham said to him: What are these that you are wearing? He said: I put them on and swore that I would not take them off until I expel you from Ash-Sham. We said: By God, this is your meeting, we will take it from you and we will take the kingdom of the greatest king, God willing. He told us: Our Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: You are not like them, but they are a people who fast during the day and stand in prayer at night, so how is your fast? So we told him, and his face was filled with blackness and he said: Get up, and he sent a messenger with us to the king, so we went out until we were close to the city, and the one with us said to us: These beasts of yours do not enter the city of the king, so if you wish we will carry you on mules and mules, we said by God we will not enter except on them, so they sent to the king that they refuse that, so he ordered them to enter on our mounts, so we entered on them with our swords girdled until we reached a room of his, so we knelt at its base while he was looking at us, so we said there is no god but God and God is greatest, and God knows that the room shook until it became like a palm branch fluttering with the winds, he said: So send to us, it is not for you to speak your religion openly against us, and he sent to us to enter, so we entered upon him while he was on his bed and with him were patriarchs of the Romans, and everything in his seat was red and everything around him was red, and he was wearing red clothes, so we approached him and he laughed and said: What is wrong with you if You greeted me with the greeting you greet among yourselves? And there was a man with him who was fluent in Arabic and talked a lot. So we said, “Our greeting among ourselves is not permissible for you, and the greeting with which you greet, it is not permissible for us to greet you with.” He said, How do you greet among yourselves? We said, “Peace be upon you.” He said, How do you greet your king? We said, It is like this. He said, How does he respond to you? We said, It is like this. He said, What is the greatest of your words? We said, There is no god but God and God is the Greatest. When we said it, and God knows best, the room shook until he raised his head to it. He said, So this word that you said where the room shook? Every time you say it in your houses, your rooms shake against you? We said, No, we have never seen it do this except with you. He said, I wish that whenever you say it, everything would shake against you, and I have left half of my kingdom. We said, Why? He said, Because it would have been easier for its matter and more appropriate for it not to be from the matter of prophethood and for it to be from the tricks of the people. Then he asked us what he wanted and we informed him. Then he said, How is your prayer and fasting? So we told him, and he said: Get up and he ordered for us a good place to stay and a lot of accommodation. So we stayed for three days, then he sent for us at night and we entered upon him and he repeated our words and we repeated them. Then he called for something like a large square gilded with small rooms on them with doors. He opened a room and a lock and took out a black silk cloth and spread it out and in it was a red picture, and in it was a man with large eyes and large buttocks. I have never seen a neck as long as his, and he had no beard and two braids, the most beautiful of what God created. He said: Do you know this? We said: No. He said: This is Adam, peace be upon him, and he is the hairiest of people. Then he opened another door and took out a black silk cloth and in it was a white picture. He had hair like a cat’s hair, red eyes, a large head and a beautiful beard. He said: Do you know this? We said: No. He said: This is Noah, peace be upon him. Then he opened another door and took out a black silk cloth and in it was a man with very white hair, beautiful eyes, a straight forehead, long cheeks and a white beard as if he was smiling. He said: Do you know this? We said: No. He said: This is Abraham, peace be upon him. Then he opened another door and in it was a white picture, and by God, it is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: Do you know this? We said: Yes, this is Muhammad, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: And we cried. He said: By God, he stood up and then sat down and said: By God, it is funny. We said: Yes, it is funny as if you are looking at it. He paused for a while looking at it and then said: It was the last of the houses, but I hastened it for you to see what you have. Then he opened another door and took out a black silk cloth and in it was a picture of a dark-skinned man with sunken eyes, a sharp gaze, a scowl, overlapping teeth, and a contracted lip as if he was angry. He said: Do you know this? We said: No. He said: This is Moses, peace be upon him, and next to him was a picture resembling him except that his head was oiled and his forehead was broad, and there was nobility in his eyes. He said: Do you know this? We said: No. He said: This is Aaron, son of Imran, peace be upon him. Then he opened another door and took out a white silk cloth and in it was a picture of a dark-skinned man, stocky and as if he was angry. He said: Do you know this? We said: No. He said: This is Lot, peace be upon him. Then he opened another door and took out a white silk cloth and in it was a picture of a white man with a reddish complexion, a hooked nose, light cheeks, and a handsome face. He said: Do you know this? We said: No. He said: This is Isaac, peace be upon him. Then he opened another door and took out a white silk cloth and in it was a picture resembling Isaac, except that there was a mole on his lip. He said: Do you know this? We said: No. He said: This is Jacob, peace be upon him. Then he opened another door and took out a black silk cloth and in it was a picture of a white man with a handsome face, a hooked nose, and good stature, with a light on his face in which one could see piety, tending to redness. He said: Do you know this? We said: No. He said: This is Ishmael, the grandfather of your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then he opened another door and took out a white silk cloth and in it was a picture like the picture of Adam, as if his face were the sun. He said: Do you know this? We said: No. He said: This is Joseph, peace be upon him. Then he opened another door and took out a white silk cloth and in it was a picture of a red-skinned man with hairy legs, squinting eyes, a large belly, and stocky, wearing a sword. He said: Do you know this? We said no. He said: This is David, peace be upon him. Then he opened another door and took out a white silk cloth with a picture of a man with large buttocks and long legs riding a horse. He said: Do you know this? We said no. He said: This is Solomon, son of David, peace be upon them both. Then he opened another door and took out a black silk cloth with a white picture of him. There was a young man with a very black beard, much hair, handsome eyes and a handsome face. He said: Do you know this? We said no. He said: This is Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him. We said: Where did you get these pictures from? Because we know that it is as the prophets, peace be upon them, were depicted, because we saw the image of our Prophet, peace be upon him, like him. He said: Adam, peace be upon him, asked his Lord to show him the prophets from his descendants, so He sent down to him their images, and it was in the treasury of Adam, peace be upon him, at sunset. Then Dhul-Qarnayn extracted it from the sunset and gave it to Daniel. Then he said: By God, my soul is pleased with leaving my kingdom, and I was a slave to share your kingdom until I die. Then he granted us permission and gave us a good reward and we set out. When we came to Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, and we told him what he showed us and what he told us and what he granted us, Abu Bakr cried and said: Poor thing, if God wanted good for him, He would have done so. Then he said: The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, informed us that they and the Jews find the description of Muhammad, peace be upon him, with them. And thus the great Hafiz al-Bayhaqi, may God have mercy on him, included it in the book of Evidences of Prophethood, on the authority of al-Hakim, with permission, so he mentioned it and its chain of transmission is sound. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna told us, Uthman ibn Umar told us, Falih told us, on the authority of Hilal bin Ali, on the authority of Ata bin Yasar, said: I met Abdullah bin Amr and said: Tell me about the description of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Torah. He said: Yes, by God, he is described in the Torah as he is described in the Qur’an: O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner and a protection for the illiterate. You are My servant and Messenger, your name is Al-Mutawakkil. He is neither rude nor harsh. God will not take him until He establishes through him the crooked religion, so that they say, There is no god but God. And He opens through him covered hearts, deaf ears, and blind eyes. Ata said: Then I met Ka’b and asked him about that, and he did not differ a word except that Ka’b said what he had understood: He said covered hearts, deaf ears, and blind eyes. Al-Bukhari narrated it in his Sahih on the authority of Muhammad bin Sinan on the authority of Falih on the authority of Hilal bin Ali, and he mentioned with his chain of transmission something similar to it, and he added after his saying: He is neither rude nor harsh nor loud in the markets, and he does not repay evil for evil, but he pardons and forgives. And he mentioned the hadith of Abdullah bin Amr, then he said: It occurs in the speech of many of the predecessors that the Torah is used to refer to the books of the People of the Book, and something similar to this has been mentioned in some hadiths, and God knows best. Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Musa bin Harun told us, Muhammad bin Idris bin Warraq bin al-Hamidi told us, Muhammad bin Umar bin Ibrahim from the descendants of Jubayr bin Mut’im told us: Umm Uthman bint Saeed, my grandmother, told me on the authority of her father Saeed bin Muhammad bin Jubayr, on the authority of his father Muhammad bin Jubayr, on the authority of his father Jubayr bin Mut’im, who said: I went out as a merchant to Ash-Sham. When I was in the lowest part of Ash-Sham, a man from the People of the Book met me and said: Is there a man among you who is a prophet? I said: Yes. He said: Would you recognize his image if you saw it? I said: Yes. So he took me into a house in which there were images, but I did not see the image of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. While I was like that, a man from among them entered upon us and said: What are you doing? So we told him, and he took us to his house. As soon as I entered, I saw the image of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and there was a man holding the heel of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. I said: Who is this man holding his heel? He said: There was no prophet except that after him there was a prophet except this prophet, for there is no prophet after him and this caliph after him. And if the description of Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, Abu Dawud said: Umar bin Hafs Abu Amr Al-Dharee’ narrated to us, Hammad bin Salamah narrated to us, that Saeed bin Ayyas Al-Jariry informed them, on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaqiq Al-Uqaili, on the authority of Al-Aqra’, the muezzin of Umar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, who said: Umar sent me to the bishop, so I called him and Umar said to him: Do you find me in the book? He said: Yes. He said: How do you find me? He said: I find you a horn. Umar raised the whip and said: A horn of iron? He said: A horn of iron, a strong prince. He said: How do you find the one after me? He said: I find a righteous caliph, except that he prefers his relatives. Umar said: May God have mercy on Uthman, three times. He said: How do you find the one after him? He said: I find it rusty iron. He said: So Omar put his hand on his head and said: O Dafra, O Dafra. He said: O Commander of the Faithful, he is a righteous caliph, but when he succeeds, the sword is drawn and blood is shed. And the Almighty said: He enjoins upon them what is right and forbids them from what is wrong. This is the description of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the previous books, and this was his state, may God bless him and grant him peace. He only enjoins good and only forbids evil, as Abdullah bin Masoud said: When you hear God say, O you who believe, then listen to it, for it is good that you are commanded to do or evil that you are forbidden from. And the most important and greatest of that is what God sent him with, which is the command to worship Him alone, with no partner for Him, and the prohibition of worshipping anyone other than Him, as He sent all the messengers before him with, as God Almighty said: And We have certainly sent among every nation a messenger, [saying], ‘Worship God and avoid false deities.’ Imam Ahmad said: Abu Amir, who is Al-Aqdi Abdul Malik bin Amr, told us, Sulayman, who is Ibn Bilal, told us, on the authority of Rabia bin Abi Abdul Rahman, on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Saeed, on the authority of Abu Humayd and Abu Asid, may God be pleased with them, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “If you hear a hadith from me that your hearts recognize, your hair and skin soften to it, and you think it is close to you, then I am the one who is most deserving of it. But if you hear a hadith from me that your hearts reject, your hair and skin turn away from it, and you think it is far from you, then I am the one who is most distant from it.” Narrated by Imam Ahmad, may God be pleased with him, with a good chain of transmission, and none of the authors of books narrated it. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, on the authority of Abu Al-Bukhtari, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: If you hear a hadith from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then think of it as the most guided, the most agreeable, and the most pious. Then he narrated it on the authority of Yahya, on the authority of Ibn Saeed, on the authority of Misa’ar, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, on the authority of Abu Al-Bukhtari, on the authority of Abu Abdul Rahman, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: If you narrate from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, And he (peace be upon him) said a hadith, so they thought that he was the one who guided them, the most blessed, and the most pious. And his saying, And He has made lawful for them the good things and forbidden for them the bad things, meaning that He has made lawful for them what they had forbidden for themselves, such as the Baha’ir, the Sawa’ib, the Wasa’il, the Ham, and the like, which they had restricted for themselves, and He has forbidden for them the bad things. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, such as pork, usury, and what they had considered lawful of the forbidden foods that God the Most High had forbidden. Some scholars said that everything that God the Most High has permitted of foods is good and beneficial for the body and religion, and everything that He has forbidden is bad and harmful for the body and religion. This noble verse has been held by those who see rational goodness and badness, and this has been answered with what this place does not contain, and likewise those scholars who have gone as far as to argue with it have used it as evidence. However, the reference in the permissibility of foods that are not stated to be permissible or forbidden is to what the Arabs found pleasant in their state of luxury, and likewise in the aspect of prohibition to what they considered bad, and there is also a long discussion on this. And his saying, And removes from them their burden and the shackles which were upon them, meaning that he came with ease and tolerance, as the hadith was narrated through various chains of transmission on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said, I was sent with the easy-going Hanafi faith. And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to his two commanders, Muadh and Abu Musa al-Ash’ari, when he sent them to Yemen, Give good tidings and do not repel, make things easy and do not make them difficult, and cooperate and do not differ. And his companion Abu Barzah al-Aslami said, “I accompanied the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and witnessed his ease. The nations before us were restricted in their laws, so God made their affairs easy for this nation and made them easy for them. For this reason, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “God has forgiven my nation for what their souls have spoken to them as long as they did not say it or do it.” And he said, He has lifted from my nation mistakes, forgetfulness, and what they were forced to do. And for this reason he said, God guided this nation to say, “Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or make a mistake. Our Lord, and do not place upon us a burden like that which You placed upon those before us. Our Lord, and do not burden us with that which we have no ability to bear.” And pardon us and forgive us and have mercy upon us. You are our Master, so give us victory over the disbelieving people.” It is proven in Sahih Muslim that God Almighty said: After each question of this, I have done, I have done. And His statement, So those who believed in him, honored him, and supported him, meaning they glorified him and respected him. And His statement, And followed the light which was sent down with him, meaning the Qur’an and the revelation that he brought to convey to the people, those are the successful ones, meaning in this world and the hereafter.
7:158: God Almighty says to His Prophet and Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, Say O Muhammad, O people, and this is addressed to the red and the black, the Arab and the non-Arab, I am the Messenger of God to you all, meaning all of you. This is from his honor and greatness, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he is the Seal of the Prophets and that he was sent to all people, as God Almighty said: Say, God is a witness between me and you, and this Qur'an has been revealed to me that I may warn you thereby and whomever it reaches. And God Almighty said: And whoever disbelieves in it from the parties, the Fire is his promised destination. And God Almighty said: And say to those who were given the Scripture and to the unlettered, 'Have you submitted?' If they submit, then they are rightly guided; but if they turn away, then upon you is only the conveyance. The verses on this are many, and the hadiths on this are too numerous to list. It is known from the religion of Islam by necessity that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, is the Messenger of God to all people. Al-Bukhari, may God have mercy on him, said in his interpretation of this verse: Abdullah told us, Sulayman ibn Abd al-Rahman and Musa ibn Harun told us: Al-Walid ibn Muslim told us, Abdullah ibn al-Ala ibn Zayr told us, Yusr ibn Ubayd God told me, Abu Idris al-Khawlani told me, he said: I heard Abu al-Darda’, may God be pleased with him, say: There was a conversation between Abu Bakr and Umar, may God be pleased with them both, and Abu Bakr angered Umar, so Umar turned away from him angrily. Abu Bakr followed him and asked him to seek forgiveness for him, but he did not do so until he closed the door in his face. Abu Bakr went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu al-Darda’ said while we were with him, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: As for your companion, he has acted rashly, meaning angry and spiteful. He said: Omar regretted what he had done, so he came forward, greeted him, sat down next to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, the story. Abu Darda said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, became angry and Abu Bakr began to say: By God, O Messenger of God, I was the one who was wronged. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Are you leaving my companion for me? I said, O people, I am the Messenger of God to you all, and you said, ‘You lied.’ Abu Bakr said, ‘You have spoken the truth.’ It was reported only by Al-Bukhari. Imam Ahmad said: Abdul Samad told us: Abdul Aziz bin Muslim told us: Yazid bin Abi Ziyad told us: Muqsim told us: Ibn Abbas told us: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I have been given five things that no prophet before me was given. I do not say this out of pride. I have been sent to all people, both red and black. I have been aided by terror for a distance of a month’s journey. Spoils have been made lawful for me, as they were not made lawful for anyone before me. The earth has been made a place of prostration and purification for me. I have been given intercession, but I have delayed it for my nation on the Day of Resurrection. It is for those who do not associate anything with God.” A good chain of transmission, but they did not include it. Imam Ahmad also said: Qutaybah bin Saeed told us: Bakr bin Mudar told us: Ibn al-Haad told us: Amr bin Shuaib told us: His father told us: His grandfather told us: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: In the year of the Battle of Tabuk, he stood up at night to pray. Some of his companions gathered behind him to guard him. When he had finished praying, he turned to them and said: “I have been given five things tonight that no prophet before me was given. As for me, I was sent to all people in general, while those before me were only sent to their own people. I have been aided against the enemy by terror, even if there were a distance of journey between me and them.” A month that filled me with terror and made the spoils lawful for me to eat, and those before me used to venerate eating them and burn them. And the earth was made for me a place of prostration and purification. Wherever the time for prayer came, I would wipe myself and pray. Those before me used to venerate that, but they used to pray in their churches and synagogues. And the fifth is what I was told: Ask, for every prophet has asked, so I have postponed my asking until the Day of Resurrection, so it is for you and for those who bear witness that there is no god but God. It is also a good and strong chain of transmission, and they did not include it. And he also said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash`ari, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Whoever hears of me from my nation, whether a Jew or a Christian, and does not believe in me, will not enter Paradise. This hadith is in Sahih Muslim from another chain of transmission on the authority of Abu Musa, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, no one from this nation, whether a Jew or a Christian, hears of me and does not believe in me, except that he will enter the Fire. Imam Ahmad said: Hasan told us: Ibn Lahi’ah told us: Abu Yunus, who is Salim ibn Jubayr, told us: Abu Hurayrah told us: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, no one from this nation, whether Jewish or Christian, hears of me and then dies without believing in that with which I was sent, except that he will be among the people of the Fire.” Ahmad alone narrated it. Imam Ahmad said: Husayn ibn Muhammad told us: Isra’il told us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I was given five things: I was sent to the red and the black, the earth was made a place of prostration and purification for me, spoils were made lawful for me, and they were not made lawful for those who came before me, I was aided by terror for a distance of a month’s journey, and I was given intercession, and there is no prophet who did not ask for intercession. I have hidden my intercession, then I have made it for whoever dies from my nation who did not associate anything with God.” This is also a sound chain of transmission, and I have not seen them narrate it, and God knows best. There is a similar one from the hadith of Ibn Umar with a good chain of transmission as well. This hadith is also proven in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I was given five things that no one else was given. One of the prophets before me was aided by terror a month’s journey away, and the earth was made for me a place of prostration and purification, so whichever man of my nation is overtaken by the time of prayer, let him pray. Spoils of war were made lawful for me, but they were not made lawful for anyone before me. I was given intercession, and a prophet was sent to his people, but I was sent to all of mankind.” His statement, “To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. There is no god but He; He gives life and causes death.” This is an attribute of God Almighty in the statement of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, “Indeed, He who sent me is the Creator of all things, their Lord and their King. In whose hand is dominion and life and death, and His is the judgment.” His statement, So believe in God and His Messenger, the unlettered prophet. He informed them that he was the Messenger of God to them, then commanded them to follow him and believe in him. The unlettered prophet, meaning the one you were promised and given glad tidings of in the previous books, for he was described as such in their books. For this reason, He said, The unlettered prophet. His statement, The one who believes in God and His words, meaning his actions confirm his words, and he believes in what was revealed to him from his Lord. And follow him, meaning follow his path and follow his footsteps. That you may be guided, meaning to the straight path.
7:159: God Almighty says, informing about the Children of Israel, that among them is a group who follow the truth and act according to it, as God Almighty said: Among the People of the Scripture is a community standing, reciting the verses of God during the hours of the night, and they prostrate themselves. God Almighty also said: “And indeed, among the People of the Scripture are those who believe in God and in what has been revealed to you and what has been revealed to them, humbly submissive to God. They do not exchange the verses of God for a small price. Those will have their reward with their Lord. Indeed, God is swift in account.” God Almighty also said: “Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it - they believe in it. And when it is recited to them, they say, ‘We believe in it. Indeed, it is the truth from our Lord. Indeed, we were Muslims before it.’ Those will be given their reward twice for what they were patient.” The verse, and God Almighty also said: “Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it - when it is recited to them - fall upon their faces in prostration. And they say, ‘Glory be to our Lord. Indeed, the promise of our Lord has been fulfilled.’ And they fall upon their faces weeping, and it increases them in humility.” Ibn Jarir mentioned in his interpretation of it an amazing story, saying, Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told us. On the authority of Ibn Jurayj, his saying: And among the people of Moses is a community guiding with the truth and doing justice thereby. He said: It has reached me that when the Children of Israel killed their prophets and disbelieved, and they were twelve tribes, one tribe of them disavowed what they had done and apologized and asked God Almighty to separate them from them, so God opened for them a tunnel in the earth, so they traveled through it until they came out from behind China, and there they are monotheists, Muslims, facing our Qiblah. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said: That is what His saying: And We said after him to the Children of Israel, Dwell in the land, and when the promise of the Hereafter comes, We will bring you forth in droves. And the promise of the Hereafter is Jesus, son of Mary. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said: They traveled in the flock for a year and a half. Ibn Uyaynah said on the authority of Sadaqah Abi al-Hudhayl on the authority of al-Suddi: And among the people of Moses is a community guiding with the truth and doing justice thereby. He said: A people between you and them is a river of honey.
7:160: The explanation of all this is presented in Surat Al-Baqarah, which is Medinan, and this context is Meccan. We have pointed out the difference between this context and that, so there is no need to repeat it here. All praise and thanks be to God.

7:163: This context is an expansion of the Almighty’s saying: And you have certainly known those among you who transgressed on the Sabbath The verse says to His Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, And ask them meaning ask these Jews who are with you about the story of their companions who disobeyed God’s command, so His vengeance surprised them for their actions, transgression, and deceit in disobeying. And warn these people from concealing your description that they find in their books lest what happened to their brothers and predecessors befall them. This village is Ayla, and it is on the shore of the Red Sea. Muhammad bin Ishaq said on the authority of Dawud bin Al-Hussain on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the Almighty’s saying: And ask them about the town that was by the sea He said it is a town called Ayla between Madyan and At-Tur. And Ikrimah, Mujahid, Qatadah, and As-Suddi said the same. Abdullah bin Kathir Al-Qari said we heard that it is Ayla and it was said that it is Madyan, and this is a narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas. And Ibn Zayd said it is a town called Ma’ta between Madyan and ‘Aynunah. And His saying when they transgressed on the Sabbath meaning They transgress and disobey God’s command to them regarding it, by commanding them to do so at that time. When their fish come to them on their Sabbath day, as a regular pattern. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, meaning, they appear on the water. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, They appear from every place. Ibn Jarir said: His statement, “And on the Day when they will not be able to sleep, it will not come to them. Thus do We test them,” meaning, We test them by showing them fish on the surface of the water on the day when it is forbidden for them to catch it, and hiding it from them on the day when it is permissible for them to catch it. Thus do We test them, We test them, because of what they used to commit, meaning, by their transgression against the obedience of God and their departure from it. These are people who have contrived to violate the prohibitions of God by what they have taken of the apparent means, the meaning of which inwardly is taking the forbidden. The jurist, Imam Abu Abdullah Ibn Battah, may God have mercy on him, said: Ahmad Ibn Muhammad Ibn Muslim told us, Al-Hasan Ibn Muhammad Ibn Al-Sabah Al-Za’farani told us, Yazid Ibn Harun told us, Muhammad Ibn Amr told us, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Do not commit what the Jews committed, making permissible the prohibitions of God by the slightest tricks. This is a good chain of transmission, for this Ahmad Ibn Muhammad Ibn Muslim was mentioned by Al-Khatib in his history and he authenticated him, and the rest of his men are well-known and trustworthy, and Al-Tirmidhi authenticates many such chains of transmission.
7:164: God Almighty tells us about the people of this village that they became three groups: a group that committed the forbidden act and devised a scheme to catch fish on the Sabbath, as was explained in Surat Al-Baqarah; a group that forbade that and isolated themselves from it; and a group that remained silent and did not do it or forbid it, but it said to the one who denied it, Why do you preach to a people whom God will destroy or punish with a severe punishment? That is, you did not forbid them, and you knew that they had perished and deserved punishment from God, so there is no benefit in forbidding them. The one who denied it said to them, An apology to your Lord. Some of them read it in the nominative case as if it were an apology, and others read it in the accusative case, meaning we do that. An apology to your Lord, that is, in what He has taken from us of enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong. And perhaps they will fear God. They say, and perhaps because of this denial they will fear what they are in and leave it and return to God repentant. So if they repent, God will accept their repentance and have mercy on them. God the Almighty said: So when they forgot that by which they had been reminded, meaning when the doers refused to accept the advice, We saved those who forbade evil, and We seized those who did wrong, meaning they committed the sin, with a wretched punishment. So He stated the salvation of those who forbade and the destruction of the wrongdoers, and He was silent about those who remained silent, because the punishment is of the same kind as the deed, so they do not deserve praise to be praised, nor did they commit a great sin to be blamed. Despite this, the imams differed about them, were they among those who perished or among those who were saved, according to two opinions. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And when a group of them said, ‘Why do you preach to a people whom God is about to destroy or punish with a severe punishment?’ It is a village on the shore of the sea between Egypt and Medina, called Ayla, so God forbade them from whales on their Sabbath, and the whales used to come to them on their Sabbath lawfully on the shore of the sea, so when the Sabbath passed they were unable to overpower them, so as long as God willed continued. Then a group of them seized the whales on their Sabbath, so a group forbade them and said, You will take them. God has forbidden it to you on your Sabbath. But they only increased in transgression and rebellion. Another group began to forbid them. When that went on for a long time, a group of those who forbade them said, Do you know that these are a people upon whom the punishment has come due? Why do you preach to a people whom God is about to destroy? They were more angry for the sake of God than the other group, so they said, An excuse before your Lord, and perhaps they will fear God. And all of them forbade it. But when the wrath of God fell upon them, the two groups were saved: those who said, Why do you preach to a people whom God is about to destroy? and those who said, An excuse before your Lord. And God destroyed the people of His disobedience who took the whales, so He made them into monkeys. Al-Awfi narrated something close to this from Ibn Abbas. Hammad bin Zaid said from Dawud bin Al-Hussain from Ikrimah from Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, he said: I do not know whether those who said, Why do you preach to a people whom God is about to destroy were saved or not. He said: I kept on at him until I knew that they had been saved, so he clothed me with a robe. Abdul Razzaq said: Ibn Jurayj told us: A man told me on the authority of Ikrimah who said: I came to Ibn Abbas one day and he was crying and there was the Qur’an in his lap. I felt too anxious to come near him, but I kept on doing that until I came forward and sat down. I said: What makes you cry, O Ibn Abbas, may God make me your ransom? He said: These are the pages. He said: And it is in Surat Al-A’raf. He said: Do you know Ayla? I said yes. He said: There was a Jewish tribe there. Whales were driven to them on the Sabbath and then sank. They could not get over them until they had sunk after great toil and hardship. They would come to them on their Sabbath day, white and fat, like a churning mother, their backs butting against their bellies in their courtyards. They remained like that for a while. Then Satan inspired them and said: I only forbade you from eating it, taking it, and hunting it on the Sabbath, so take it on that day and eat it on any other day. A group of them said that, and another group said: Rather, you were forbidden from eating it, taking it, and hunting it on the Sabbath. They remained like that until the following Friday came. A group left with their children and women, and a group withdrew to the right and moved aside, and a group withdrew to the left and remained silent. The people on the right said: Woe to you, God! We forbid you from exposing yourself to God’s punishment. The people on the left said: Why do you preach to a people whom God is about to destroy or punish with a severe punishment? The people on the right said: As an excuse to your Lord, and perhaps they will fear God. That is, they will desist. Indeed, And if they do not desist, then we would rather have them not be afflicted or destroyed. And if they do not desist, then we have an excuse before your Lord. So they continued in sin, and the right-handers said, “You have done it, O enemies of God. By God, we will not let you spend the night in your city. By God, we do not see you wake up until God sends you down with a sinking or a stoning or some of the punishment He has.” So when they woke up, they knocked on the door and called out, but they were not answered. So they put up a ladder and climbed the city wall with a man. He turned to them and said, O servants of God, by God, monkeys are hostile and howl with tails. So they opened it and entered upon them, and the monkeys recognized their lineage from humans, but humans do not recognize their lineage from monkeys. So the monkeys would come to their human relatives, smell his clothes and cry, and he would say, Did we not forbid you from such-and-such? And they would say with their heads, Yes. Then Ibn Abbas recited, But when they forgot that by which they had been reminded, We saved those who had forbidden evil, and We seized those who did wrong with a wretched punishment. He said, I see that those who had been forbidden were saved, but I do not see the others. They mentioned that we see things that we disapprove of but do not speak about. He said: I said, may God make me your ransom. Don’t you see that they hate what they are doing and oppose them? And they said, Why do you preach to a people whom God will destroy? He said: So he ordered that I be dressed in two coarse garments. Mujahid narrated this from him. Ibn Jarir said: Yunus told us, Ashhab bin Abdul Aziz told us, on the authority of Malik, who said: Ibn Ruman claimed that the words of God Almighty: Their fish come to them on their Sabbath day as a regular custom, but on the day they do not observe the Sabbath, they do not come to them means: They used to come to them on the Sabbath, and when evening came, they would go away and nothing of them would be seen until the next Sabbath. So a man took a string and a peg and tied one of them to the water on the Sabbath. When Sunday night came, he took it and hung it up. The people smelled its smell, so they came to him and asked him about it, but he denied it. They kept on at him until he told them, It is the skin of a whale that we found. When the next Sabbath came, he did the same thing. I do not know, perhaps he said, He tied two whales. When Sunday night came, he took it and hung it up. They smelled its smell, so they came and asked him. He said to them, If you wish, you can do as I do. They said to him, What did you do? So he told them, so they did as he did until it became widespread. They had a city with a suburb that they closed off to them, so they were afflicted with the same transformation that afflicted them. Then their neighbors who were around them came to them, asking them what people ask for, and they found the city closed to them. So they called out, but they did not answer them, so they climbed over the wall on them, and behold, they were monkeys. The monkey began to approach, touching whoever it knew before that, and approaching him and touching him. We have already presented in Surat Al-Baqarah from the traces in the story of this city, what is convincing and sufficient, praise and thanks be to God. The second statement is that those who remained silent were among those who perished. Muhammad bin Ishaq said, on the authority of Dawud bin Al-Hussain, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said: They innovated the Sabbath, so they were afflicted with it, so whales were forbidden to them. So when it was the Sabbath, whales were made permissible for them to look at in the sea. When the Sabbath ended, they went away and were not seen until the next Sabbath. When the Sabbath came, they came back by law. So they remained as God willed them to remain like that. Then a man from them took a whale, pierced its nose, then struck a stake for it on the shore, tied it up, and left it in the water. When it was… The next day he took it, roasted it, and ate it. He did that while they were watching and did not disapprove, and none of them forbade him, except a group of them who forbade him until it became apparent in the markets, so he did it openly. He said: A group said to those who forbade them, Why do you preach to a people whom God is about to destroy or punish with a severe punishment? They said, An excuse before your Lord. They said, We disapprove of their deeds. “And perhaps they will fear God.” But when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We saved those who forbade evil, and We seized those who did wrong with a wretched punishment for what they used to do. But when they rebelled against what they had been forbidden, We said to them, Be apes, despised. Ibn Abbas said, “They were three: a third forbade it, a third said, “Why do you preach to a people whom God is about to destroy?” and a third were the people of sin. None was saved except those who forbade it, and the rest of them perished.” This is a good chain of transmission from Ibn Abbas, but referring back to the statement of Ikrimah regarding the salvation of those who kept quiet is more appropriate than saying this, because their condition became clear after that, and God knows best. The Almighty’s saying: And We seized those who did wrong with a wretched punishment indicates by implication that those who remained were saved. The word wretched has many readings, and according to Mujahid its meaning is severe. In another narration it means painful. Qatada said it means hurtful. All of them are similar, and God knows best. His saying disgraced means humiliated, contemptible, and disgraced.
