7:166: God Almighty tells us about the people of this village that they became three groups: a group that committed the forbidden act and devised a scheme to catch fish on the Sabbath, as was explained in Surat Al-Baqarah; a group that forbade that and isolated themselves from it; and a group that remained silent and did not do it or forbid it, but it said to the one who denied it, Why do you preach to a people whom God will destroy or punish with a severe punishment? That is, you did not forbid them, and you knew that they had perished and deserved punishment from God, so there is no benefit in forbidding them. The one who denied it said to them, An apology to your Lord. Some of them read it in the nominative case as if it were an apology, and others read it in the accusative case, meaning we do that. An apology to your Lord, that is, in what He has taken from us of enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong. And perhaps they will fear God. They say, and perhaps because of this denial they will fear what they are in and leave it and return to God repentant. So if they repent, God will accept their repentance and have mercy on them. God the Almighty said: So when they forgot that by which they had been reminded, meaning when the doers refused to accept the advice, We saved those who forbade evil, and We seized those who did wrong, meaning they committed the sin, with a wretched punishment. So He stated the salvation of those who forbade and the destruction of the wrongdoers, and He was silent about those who remained silent, because the punishment is of the same kind as the deed, so they do not deserve praise to be praised, nor did they commit a great sin to be blamed. Despite this, the imams differed about them, were they among those who perished or among those who were saved, according to two opinions. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And when a group of them said, ‘Why do you preach to a people whom God is about to destroy or punish with a severe punishment?’ It is a village on the shore of the sea between Egypt and Medina, called Ayla, so God forbade them from whales on their Sabbath, and the whales used to come to them on their Sabbath lawfully on the shore of the sea, so when the Sabbath passed they were unable to overpower them, so as long as God willed continued. Then a group of them seized the whales on their Sabbath, so a group forbade them and said, You will take them. God has forbidden it to you on your Sabbath. But they only increased in transgression and rebellion. Another group began to forbid them. When that went on for a long time, a group of those who forbade them said, Do you know that these are a people upon whom the punishment has come due? Why do you preach to a people whom God is about to destroy? They were more angry for the sake of God than the other group, so they said, An excuse before your Lord, and perhaps they will fear God. And all of them forbade it. But when the wrath of God fell upon them, the two groups were saved: those who said, Why do you preach to a people whom God is about to destroy? and those who said, An excuse before your Lord. And God destroyed the people of His disobedience who took the whales, so He made them into monkeys. Al-Awfi narrated something close to this from Ibn Abbas. Hammad bin Zaid said from Dawud bin Al-Hussain from Ikrimah from Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, he said: I do not know whether those who said, Why do you preach to a people whom God is about to destroy were saved or not. He said: I kept on at him until I knew that they had been saved, so he clothed me with a robe. Abdul Razzaq said: Ibn Jurayj told us: A man told me on the authority of Ikrimah who said: I came to Ibn Abbas one day and he was crying and there was the Qur’an in his lap. I felt too anxious to come near him, but I kept on doing that until I came forward and sat down. I said: What makes you cry, O Ibn Abbas, may God make me your ransom? He said: These are the pages. He said: And it is in Surat Al-A’raf. He said: Do you know Ayla? I said yes. He said: There was a Jewish tribe there. Whales were driven to them on the Sabbath and then sank. They could not get over them until they had sunk after great toil and hardship. They would come to them on their Sabbath day, white and fat, like a churning mother, their backs butting against their bellies in their courtyards. They remained like that for a while. Then Satan inspired them and said: I only forbade you from eating it, taking it, and hunting it on the Sabbath, so take it on that day and eat it on any other day. A group of them said that, and another group said: Rather, you were forbidden from eating it, taking it, and hunting it on the Sabbath. They remained like that until the following Friday came. A group left with their children and women, and a group withdrew to the right and moved aside, and a group withdrew to the left and remained silent. The people on the right said: Woe to you, God! We forbid you from exposing yourself to God’s punishment. The people on the left said: Why do you preach to a people whom God is about to destroy or punish with a severe punishment? The people on the right said: As an excuse to your Lord, and perhaps they will fear God. That is, they will desist. Indeed, And if they do not desist, then we would rather have them not be afflicted or destroyed. And if they do not desist, then we have an excuse before your Lord. So they continued in sin, and the right-handers said, “You have done it, O enemies of God. By God, we will not let you spend the night in your city. By God, we do not see you wake up until God sends you down with a sinking or a stoning or some of the punishment He has.” So when they woke up, they knocked on the door and called out, but they were not answered. So they put up a ladder and climbed the city wall with a man. He turned to them and said, O servants of God, by God, monkeys are hostile and howl with tails. So they opened it and entered upon them, and the monkeys recognized their lineage from humans, but humans do not recognize their lineage from monkeys. So the monkeys would come to their human relatives, smell his clothes and cry, and he would say, Did we not forbid you from such-and-such? And they would say with their heads, Yes. Then Ibn Abbas recited, But when they forgot that by which they had been reminded, We saved those who had forbidden evil, and We seized those who did wrong with a wretched punishment. He said, I see that those who had been forbidden were saved, but I do not see the others. They mentioned that we see things that we disapprove of but do not speak about. He said: I said, may God make me your ransom. Don’t you see that they hate what they are doing and oppose them? And they said, Why do you preach to a people whom God will destroy? He said: So he ordered that I be dressed in two coarse garments. Mujahid narrated this from him. Ibn Jarir said: Yunus told us, Ashhab bin Abdul Aziz told us, on the authority of Malik, who said: Ibn Ruman claimed that the words of God Almighty: Their fish come to them on their Sabbath day as a regular custom, but on the day they do not observe the Sabbath, they do not come to them means: They used to come to them on the Sabbath, and when evening came, they would go away and nothing of them would be seen until the next Sabbath. So a man took a string and a peg and tied one of them to the water on the Sabbath. When Sunday night came, he took it and hung it up. The people smelled its smell, so they came to him and asked him about it, but he denied it. They kept on at him until he told them, It is the skin of a whale that we found. When the next Sabbath came, he did the same thing. I do not know, perhaps he said, He tied two whales. When Sunday night came, he took it and hung it up. They smelled its smell, so they came and asked him. He said to them, If you wish, you can do as I do. They said to him, What did you do? So he told them, so they did as he did until it became widespread. They had a city with a suburb that they closed off to them, so they were afflicted with the same transformation that afflicted them. Then their neighbors who were around them came to them, asking them what people ask for, and they found the city closed to them. So they called out, but they did not answer them, so they climbed over the wall on them, and behold, they were monkeys. The monkey began to approach, touching whoever it knew before that, and approaching him and touching him. We have already presented in Surat Al-Baqarah from the traces in the story of this city, what is convincing and sufficient, praise and thanks be to God. (The second statement) is that those who remained silent were among those who perished. Muhammad bin Ishaq said, on the authority of Dawud bin Al-Hussain, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said: They innovated the Sabbath, so they were afflicted with it, so whales were forbidden to them. So when it was the Sabbath, whales were made permissible for them to look at in the sea. When the Sabbath ended, they went away and were not seen until the next Sabbath. When the Sabbath came, they came back by law. So they remained as God willed them to remain like that. Then a man from them took a whale, pierced its nose, then struck a stake for it on the shore, tied it up, and left it in the water. When it was… The next day he took it, roasted it, and ate it. He did that while they were watching and did not disapprove, and none of them forbade him, except a group of them who forbade him until it became apparent in the markets, so he did it openly. He said: A group said to those who forbade them, Why do you preach to a people whom God is about to destroy or punish with a severe punishment? They said, An excuse before your Lord. They said, We disapprove of their deeds. “And perhaps they will fear God.” But when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We saved those who forbade evil, and We seized those who did wrong with a wretched punishment for what they used to do. But when they rebelled against what they had been forbidden, We said to them, Be apes, despised. Ibn Abbas said, “They were three: a third forbade it, a third said, “Why do you preach to a people whom God is about to destroy?” and a third were the people of sin. None was saved except those who forbade it, and the rest of them perished.” This is a good chain of transmission from Ibn Abbas, but referring back to the statement of Ikrimah regarding the salvation of those who kept quiet is more appropriate than saying this, because their condition became clear after that, and God knows best. The Almighty’s saying: And We seized those who did wrong with a wretched punishment indicates by implication that those who remained were saved. The word wretched has many readings, and according to Mujahid its meaning is severe. In another narration it means painful. Qatada said it means hurtful. All of them are similar, and God knows best. His saying disgraced means humiliated, contemptible, and disgraced.
7:167: Ta'han is derived from the word adhan, meaning: to inform. This was said by Mujahid, and others said: to command. In the strength of the speech there is what conveys the meaning of an oath from this word, and for this reason it was followed by the lam in his saying He will send upon them meaning upon the Jews until the Day of Resurrection someone who will subject them to the worst of punishment meaning because of their disobedience and violation of God's commands and law and their deception of the forbidden things. It is said that Moses, peace be upon him, imposed a tax on them for seven years, and it was said thirteen years, and he was the first to impose a tax, then they were under the oppression of the kings of the Greeks, Chaldeans, and Chaldeans, then they moved to oppressing the Christians and humiliating them and taking from them the jizya and tax, then Islam and Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, came, so they were under his oppression and protection, paying the tax and jizya. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas in the interpretation of this verse: It is poverty and taking the jizya from them. Ali bin Abi Talha said on his authority: It is the jizya and the one who will subject them to the worst torment is Muhammad, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his nation until the Day of Resurrection. Saeed bin Jubair, Ibn Jurayj, As-Suddi and Qatadah said the same. Abdul Razzaq said on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Abdul Karim Al-Jazari on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, he said: It is recommended that the Nabataeans be sent to pay the jizya. I said: Then the end of their matter is that they will come out as supporters of the Antichrist, and the Muslims will kill them with Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, and that will be the end of time. His statement, Indeed, your Lord is swift in punishment, meaning to those who disobey Him and go against His law. And indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful, meaning to those who repent to Him and turn back. This is from the aspect of linking mercy with punishment so that despair does not occur. God often links encouragement and intimidation so that souls remain between hope and fear.
7:168: The Almighty mentions that He divided them into nations on the earth, i.e. groups and factions, as He said: “And We said after him to the Children of Israel, ‘Dwell in the land. Then, when the promise of the Hereafter comes, We will bring you in droves. ’” Among them are the righteous and among them are those who are not. That is, among them are the righteous and other than that, as the jinn said: “And among us are the righteous and among us are those who are not. We were divided into different paths.” And We tested them that is, We tested them with good and bad. That is, with ease and hardship, desire and fear, well-being and affliction that they might return. Then the Almighty said: Then there came after them a generation who inherited the Scripture, taking the goods of this lower world. The verse says: The Almighty says: Then there came after that generation, among whom are the righteous and the wicked, another generation, in whom there is no good, and they inherited the study of the Scripture, which is the Torah. Mujahid said: They are the Christians, and it may be more general than that. Taking the goods of this lower world. That is, they compensate for offering and spreading the truth with the goods of this worldly life, and they delay and promise themselves with repentance, and whenever something like the first appears to them, they fall. In it, and for this reason he said: And if an offer like it comes to them, they take it. And as Saeed bin Jubair said, they commit a sin and then seek forgiveness from God for it and confess to God, if the offer of that sin comes to them, they take it. Mujahid said in the words of God the Most High: They take the offer of this lower world, he said, nothing of this world is honored to them except that they take it, whether it is lawful or unlawful, and they wish for forgiveness. And they say, ‘We will be forgiven.’ And if an offer like it comes to them, they take it. Qatada said in the verse, “Yes, by God, they are bad offspring. “They inherited the Book,” after their prophets and messengers, God inherited it from them and entrusted it to them. And God the Most High said in another verse, Then there came after them a generation who neglected the prayer, the verse, he said, They take the offer of this lower world and say, ‘We will be forgiven.’ They wished from God hopes and deceptions that they were deceived by. And if an offer like it comes to them, they take it. Nothing distracts them and nothing prevents them from that. Whenever something from this world comes to them, they eat it, not caring whether it is lawful or unlawful. Al-Suddi said: His words, Then there came after them a generation to His words, And they were oblivious. What is in it? He said: The Children of Israel would not appoint a judge unless he took a bribe in the ruling. However, their best people gathered and some of them took covenants from others that they would not do that or take a bribe. So when a man among them was appointed a judge, he would take a bribe. It would be said to him, What is the matter with you, taking a bribe in the ruling? He says, He will forgive me, and the rest of the Children of Israel will criticize him for what he did. Then, when he dies or is removed, a man from those who used to criticize him is put in his place, and he takes bribes. He says, And if the others receive worldly goods, they will take them. God the Most High says, denouncing their actions, along with the covenant that was taken from them to make the truth clear to the people and not to conceal it, as He says, “And when God took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture, ‘You shall make it clear to the people and not conceal it,’ but they threw it behind their backs and exchanged it for a small price. How evil is that which they purchase.” Ibn Jurayj said, Ibn Abbas said, Was not a covenant taken from them in the Book, ‘You shall not say about God except the truth?’ He said, regarding their wish for God to forgive their sins, which they continue to commit and do not repent from. God the Most High says, “And the home of the Hereafter is better for those who fear God. Will you not then reason?” He encourages them with His abundant reward and warns them against His severe punishment, meaning, My reward and what I have is better. For those who fear the forbidden, abandon their own desires, and turn to obeying their Lord, Do you not reason? He says, Do not those who exchange the worldly goods for what I have have a mind that deters them from their foolishness and extravagance? Then the Almighty praised those who adhered to His Book, which leads them to follow His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as it is written in it, saying, And those who hold fast to the Book, meaning they hold fast to it, follow its commands, and abandon its prohibitions, “and establish prayer. Indeed, We will not allow to be lost the reward of the reformers.”

7:171: Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And when We raised the mountain above them, meaning We raised it, which is His statement, And We raised the mount above them with their covenant. Sufyan al-Thawri said on the authority of al-A'mash on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The angels raised it above their heads, which is His statement, And We raised the mount above them. Al-Qasim bin Abi Ayyub said on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Then Moses, peace be upon him, walked with them to the Holy Land and took the tablets after the anger had subsided from him and ordered them to do what God had ordered them to do of the duties, but it was too heavy for them and they refused to acknowledge it until God raised the mountain above them, as if it were a canopy. He said: The angels raised it above their heads. An-Nasa'i narrated it in full. Sunayd bin Dawud said in his interpretation on the authority of Hajjaj bin Muhammad on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abdullah, who said: This is a book, do you accept it with what is in it, for it explains what is permissible for you and what is forbidden to you, what is commanded you and what is forbidden to you? They said: Spread out to us what is in it, for if its obligations and limits are easy, we will accept it. He said: Accept it with what is in it. They said: No, not until we know what is in it, how its limits and obligations are. So they went back to him repeatedly. Then God inspired the mountain, so it was uprooted and rose into the sky until it was between their heads and the sky. Moses said to them: Do you not see what my Lord, the Almighty, says: If you do not accept the Torah and what is in it, I will throw you with this mountain? He said: Al-Hasan Al-Basri told me: When they looked at the mountain, each man fell prostrating on his left eyebrow and looked at the mountain with his right eye, fearing that it would fall on him. Likewise, today there is no Jew on earth who prostrates except on his left eyebrow. They say: This is the prostration by which the punishment was lifted. Abu Bakr said: When he spread out the tablets in which was the Book of God, which He wrote with His own hand, there remained on the face of the earth no mountain, tree, or stone that did not shake. Today there is no Jew on the face of the earth, young or old, to whom the Torah is recited, but he shakes and shakes his head, i.e. turns around, as God, the Almighty, says: And they will lower their heads toward you. And God knows best.
7:172: The Almighty informs us that He extracted the offspring of the children of Adam from their loins, bearing witness against themselves that God is their Lord and their King, and that there is no god but Him, just as He created them on that and made them like that. The Almighty said: “So direct your face toward the religion, inclining toward truth. [Adhere to] the nature of God upon which He has created mankind. There is no change in the creation of God.” And in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Every child is born upon the fitrah, and in another narration upon this religion, then his parents make him a Jew, a Christian, or a Zoroastrian, just as an animal is born whole. Do you see among them any with their ears cut off?” And in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Iyadh ibn Himar, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God says: I created My servants as monotheists, then the devils came to them and led them astray from their religion and prohibited for them what I had permitted for them.” And Imam Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him, said: Yunus ibn `Abd al-`Ala told us, Ibn Wahb told us, al-Sari ibn Yahya told me that al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan told them on the authority of al-Aswad ibn Sari` from Bani Saad said: I participated in four battles with the Messenger of God (peace be upon him). He said: The people took up their children after they had killed the fighters. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) was informed of that and he was upset with him. Then he said: What is the matter with people who take up their children? A man said: O Messenger of God, are they not the children of the polytheists? He said: “The best of you are the children of the polytheists. Indeed, no soul is born except that it is born upon the fitrah natural disposition, and it remains upon it until its language becomes clear to its parents, then its parents make it a Jew or a Christian.” Al-Hasan said: By God, God said in His Book: And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants (al-Baqarah 2:14). Imam Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Ismail bin Aliyah on the authority of Yunus bin Ubayd on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri on his authority. Al-Nasa’i included it in his Sunan on the authority of Hisham on the authority of Yunus bin Ubayd on the authority of Al-Hasan who said: Al-Aswad bin Sari’ told me and he mentioned it but he did not mention the statement of Al-Hasan Al-Basri and his recalling the verse at that time. There are hadiths about taking up the children from the loins of Adam (peace be upon him) and distinguishing them into the companions of the right and the companions of the left, and in some of them the testimony against them that God is their Lord. Imam Ahmad said: Hajjaj told us, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Abu Imran al-Joni, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “A man from the people of Hell will be asked on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:‘Do you think that if you had everything on the earth, would you ransom yourself with it?’ He will say: ‘Yes.’ He will say: ‘I wanted something easier from you than that. I took a covenant from you in the back of Adam that you would not associate anything with Me, but you refused except to associate anything with Me.’” They both included it in the two Sahihs on the authority of Shu`bah. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Husayn ibn Muhammad told us: Jarir, meaning Ibn Hazim, told us, on the authority of Kalthoum ibn Jabr, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God took the covenant from the back of Adam, peace be upon him, in Nu`man on the Day of Arafah, and brought forth from his loins every offspring He had created, and scattered them before Him, then He spoke to them directly, saying: ‘Am I not your Lord?’ They said: ‘Yes, we bear witness.’ This [hadith] was narrated by al-Nasa’i in the Book of Interpretation of his Sunan on the authority of Muhammad ibn `Abd al-Rahim Sa`iqah on the authority of Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Marwazi on his authority. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of Husayn ibn Muhammad on his authority, except that Ibn Abi Hatim made it a mursal. Al-Hakim included it in his Mustadrak on the authority of Husayn ibn Muhammad and others on the authority of Jarir ibn Hazim on the authority of Kalthoum ibn Jabr on his authority, and he said: Its chain of transmission is sound, but they did not include it. Muslim cited Kalthoum ibn Jabr as evidence, and this is what he said. `Abd al-Rahim narrated it on his authority. Al-Warith, on the authority of Kalthoum bin Jabr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, stopped it. Ismail bin Aliyah and Wakee’ narrated it likewise on the authority of Rabia bin Kalthoum, on the authority of Jabr, on the authority of his father, on his authority. Ata bin Al-Sa’ib, Habib bin Abi Thabit, and Ali bin Badhima narrated it likewise on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Al-Awfi and Ali bin Abi Talhah narrated it likewise on the authority of Ibn Abbas, so this is more and more authentic, and God knows best. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakee’ told us, my father told us, on the authority of Abu Hilal, on the authority of Abu Hamza Al-Dab’i, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: God brought forth the offspring of Adam from his back in the form of ants while he was in the filth of the water. He also said: Ali bin Sahl narrated to us, Damrah bin Rabi’ah narrated to us, Abu Mas’ud narrated to us, on the authority of Jarir, who said: Ibn Adh-Dahhak bin Muzahim died at the age of six days. He said: So he said: O Jabir, when you place my son in his grave, expose his face and untie his knots, for my son will be seated and questioned. So I did with him what he was commanded. When I finished, I said: May God have mercy on you, about what your son asks of whom he asks. He said: He asks about the covenant that he acknowledged in the loins of Adam. I said: O Abu Al-Qasim, what is this covenant that he acknowledged in the loins of Adam? He said: Ibn Abbas narrated to me: God wiped the loins of Adam and extracted from them every soul that He created until the Day of Resurrection. He took from them the covenant that they would worship Him and not associate anything with Him, and He guaranteed them sustenance. Then He returned them to his loins. The Hour will not come until the one to whom he gave the covenant is born on that day. Whoever among them attains the second covenant and fulfills it, the first covenant will benefit him. Whoever attains the second covenant and does not acknowledge it, the first covenant will not benefit him. Whoever dies young before attaining the second covenant dies upon the first covenant, according to the fitrah. All of these paths are what strengthen this. This is based on Ibn Abbas, and God knows best. Another hadith Ibn Jarir said: Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Walid told us, Ahmad ibn Abi Tayyiba told us, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Saeed, on the authority of al-Ajlah, on the authority of al-Dahhak, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants.” He said: He took from his back as a comb is taken from the head, and said to them: Am I not your Lord? They said: Yes. The angels said: We bear witness. This – lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, Indeed, we were of this unaware. This Ahmad ibn Abi Tayyiba is Abu Muhammad al-Jurjani, the judge of Qumis. He was one of the ascetics. Al-Nasa’i included him in his Sunan. Abu Hatim al-Razi said: His hadith should be written down. Ibn Adi narrated many strange hadiths. Abd al-Rahman ibn Hamza ibn Fahdi narrated this hadith on the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Mansur, and this is more authentic, and God knows best. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Ruh, he is Ibn Ubadah, told us, Malik told us, and Ishaq told us, Malik told us, on the authority of Zaid bin Abi Anisa, that Abdul Hamid bin Abdul Rahman bin Zaid bin Al-Khattab told him, on the authority of Muslim bin Yasar Al-Juhani, that Umar bin Al-Khattab was asked about this verse: And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants and made them testify of themselves, [saying], ‘Am I not your Lord?’ They said, ‘Yes.’ The verse. Umar bin Al-Khattab said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, being asked about it, and he said: “God created Adam, peace be upon him, then He wiped his back with His right hand and extracted from him his descendants. He said, ‘I created these for Paradise and they will do the deeds of the people of Paradise.’ Then He wiped his back and extracted from him his descendants. He said, ‘I created these for the Fire and they will do the deeds of the people of the Fire.’” A man said, O Messenger of God, what is the purpose of work? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When God creates a servant for Paradise, He employs him in the deeds of the people of Paradise until he dies doing one of the deeds of the people of Paradise, and He enters him into Paradise because of it. And when He creates a servant for Hell, He employs him in the deeds of the people of Hell until he dies doing one of the deeds of the people of Hell, and He enters him into Hell because of it.” And thus Abu Dawud narrated it on the authority of Al-Qa’nabi, Al-Nasa’i on the authority of Qutaybah, and Al-Tirmidhi in their Tafsir on the authority of Ishaq bin Musa on the authority of Ma’n and Ibn Abi Hatim on the authority of Yunus bin Abdul A’la on the authority of Ibn Wahb and Ibn Jarir on the authority of Ruh bin Ubadah and Sa’id bin Abdul Hamid bin Ja’far. And Ibn Hibban included it in his Sahih on the authority of Abu Mus’ab Al-Zubayri, all of them on the authority of Imam Malik bin Anas. Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a good hadith, and Muslim bin Yasar did not hear ‘Umar. This is what Abu Hatim and Abu Zur’ah said. Abu Hatim added: And between them was Nu’aym bin Rabi’ah. And what Abu Hatim said was narrated by Abu Dawud in his Sunan on the authority of Muhammad bin Musa on the authority of Baqiyah on the authority of ‘Umar bin Ja’tham Al-Qurashi on the authority of Zayd bin Abi Anisa on the authority of ‘Abd Al-Hamid bin ‘Abd Al-Rahman bin Zayd bin Al-Khattab on the authority of Muslim bin Yasar. Al-Juhani narrated on the authority of Na’im bin Rabi’ah who said: I was with Umar bin Al-Khattab and he was asked about this verse: And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants, so he mentioned it. Al-Hafiz Al-Daraqutni said: Umar bin Ja’tham was followed by Yazid bin Sinan Abu Farwah Al-Rahawi and their statement is more correct than the statement of Malik, and God knows best. I said: It appears that Imam Malik only omitted the mention of Na’im bin Rabi’ah intentionally because he was ignorant of the status of Na’im bin Rabi’ah and did not know him, as he is not known except in this hadith. For this reason he omitted the mention of a group of people whom he did not approve of. For this reason he sent many of the marfu’ hadiths and omitted many of the mawasul hadiths, and God knows best. Another hadith Al-Tirmidhi said when interpreting this verse: Abd bin Hamid told us, Abu Naim told us, Hisham bin Saad told us, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When God created Adam, He wiped his back, and from his back fell every soul that He would create from his offspring until the Day of Resurrection, and He placed between the eyes of every person of them a gleam of light. Then He showed them to Adam and said: ‘O Lord, who are these?’ He said: ‘These are your offspring.’ He saw a man among them and the gleam between his eyes pleased him. He said: ‘O Lord, who is this?’ He said: ‘This is a man from the last of the nations from your offspring, called David.’ He said: ‘O Lord, how long have you made his lifespan?’ He said: ‘Sixty years.’ He said: ‘O Lord, and I have given him forty years of my life.’ When Adam’s lifespan came to an end, the Angel of Death came to him and said: ‘Are there not forty years left of my lifespan?’ He said: ‘Did you not give them to your son David?’ He said: ‘So Adam denied, so his offspring denied, and Adam forgot, so his offspring forgot, and Adam sinned, so his offspring sinned.’” Then Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a good and authentic hadith. It has been narrated From other chains of transmission on the authority of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak on the authority of Abu Na’im al-Fadl ibn Dukayn on his authority and said: It is authentic according to the conditions of Muslim, although they did not include it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it in his Tafsir on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam on the authority of his father that he narrated on the authority of Ata’ ibn Yasar on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned something similar to what was mentioned above until he said: “Then he showed them to Adam and said: O Adam, these are your descendants, and among them were the leper, the albino, the blind, and all kinds of diseases. Adam said: O Lord, why have you done this to my descendants? He said: So that you may be grateful for my blessings. Adam said: O Lord, who are these whom I see as the most luminous of people? He said: These are the prophets, O Adam, from your descendants.” Then he mentioned the story of David something similar to what was mentioned above. Another hadith Abd al-Rahman ibn Qatada al-Nadri narrated on the authority of his father on the authority of Hisham ibn Hakim, may God be pleased with him, that a man asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, do deeds begin or has the decree already been decreed? He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God took the descendants of Adam from their backs, then made them testify against themselves, then poured them into His hands, then said: These are in Paradise and these are in Hell. So the people of Paradise are facilitated to do the deeds of the people of Paradise, and the people of Hell are facilitated to do the deeds of the people of Hell.” Narrated by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh through various chains of transmission on his authority. Another hadith Ja`far ibn al-Zubayr narrated, and he is weak, on the authority of al-Qasim, on the authority of Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When God created the creation and decreed the matter, He took the people of the right hand with His right hand and the people of the left hand with His left hand. He said: ‘O people of the right hand.’ They said: ‘At your service and pleasure.’ He said: ‘Am I not your Lord?’ They said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘O people of the left hand.’ They said: ‘At your service and pleasure.’ He said: ‘Am I not your Lord?’ They said: ‘Yes.’ Then He mixed them together. Someone said to Him: ‘O Lord, why have You mixed them together?’ He said: ‘They are doing deeds other than that, lest they say on the Day of Resurrection, ‘Indeed, we were unaware of this.’ Then He returned them to the loins of Adam.” Narrated by Ibn Mardawayh. Another trace Abu Ja`far al-Razi said on the authority of al-Rabi` ibn Anas on the authority of Abu al-`Aliyah on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka`b regarding the words of God Almighty: And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants (al-Baqarah 2:17), he said: Then He gathered them all together for Himself on that day, whatever would be from Him until the Day of Resurrection, and He made them in their forms, then He made them speak, and He took from them a covenant and a pact. And He made them testify of themselves, ‘Am I not your Lord?’ They said, ‘Yes.’ (al-Baqarah 2:17) He said: Then I call upon you the seven heavens and the seven earths, and I call upon you your father Adam, lest you say on the Day of Resurrection, ‘We did not know this.’ Know that there is no god but Me, and no lord but Me, and do not associate anything with Me, and that I will send to you messengers to warn you of My covenant and My pact, and I will send down to you My Book. They said: We testify that You are our Lord and our God. We have no lord but You, and we have no god but You. So they acknowledged their obedience to Him on that day, and He raised their father Adam and looked at them and saw among them the rich and the poor, and the beautiful in appearance and less than that, so He said: O Lord, if You made Your servants equal? He said: I wanted to thank and saw in them the prophets like lamps upon them light and they were singled out with another covenant of the message and prophethood, it is what God Almighty says: And when We took from the prophets their covenant the verse and it is what He says: So set your face toward the religion, inclining toward truth, the nature of God the verse and from that He said: This is a warner from the first warnings and from that He said: And we did not find for most of them any covenant the verse, narrated by Abdullah bin Imam Ahmad in Musnad of his father, and narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh in their commentaries from the narration of Abu Jaafar al-Razi with it and it was narrated from Mujahid, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubayr, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Suddi and more than one of the scholars of the Salaf contexts that agree with these hadiths, we were satisfied with citing them instead of going into length in all those narrations and with God is the helper. These hadiths indicate that God, the Almighty, extracted the offspring of Adam from his loins and distinguished between the people of Paradise and the people of Hell. As for bearing witness to them there that He is their Lord, it is only in the hadith of Kalthoum bin Jabr from Saeed bin Jubair from Ibn Abbas and in the hadith of Abdullah bin Amr. We have shown that they are suspended and not raised as mentioned above. Hence, some of the early and later scholars said that what is meant by this bearing witness is that He created them upon monotheism as mentioned above in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah and Iyad bin Himar Al-Majashi’i and in the narration of Al-Hasan Al-Basri from Al-Aswad bin Sari’. Al-Hasan interpreted the verse with this. They said: This is why He said: And when your Lord took from the children of Adam and did not say from Adam from their loins and did not say from his loins their offspring meaning He made their offspring generation after generation and century after century like the Almighty’s saying: And it is He who made you successors on the earth and He said: And He will make you successors on the earth and He said: Just as He created you from the offspring of another people then He said: “And He made them testify of themselves, ‘Am I not your Lord?’ They said: Yes” meaning He created them as witnesses to that. Saying to him in a state and a saying, and the testimony is sometimes by saying, as in His saying, They said, ‘We bear witness against ourselves’ verse, and sometimes it is a state, as in His saying, the Most High: It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of God while they bear witness against themselves of disbelief, meaning their state is a witness against them in that, not that they are saying that. And likewise His saying, the Most High: And indeed, He is, over that, a witness, just as the question is sometimes by saying and sometimes it is by state, as in His saying, And He gave you of all that you asked of Him, they said. And what indicates that what is meant by this is that He made this testimony an argument against them in polytheism. If this had happened as those who said said, then everyone would have mentioned it so that it would be an argument against him. If it is said that the Messenger’s (peace and blessings of God be upon him) informing them of it is sufficient for its existence, then the answer is that the deniers among the polytheists deny everything that the Messengers brought them of this and other things, and this was made an independent argument against them, so it indicates that it is the nature upon which they were created of acknowledging monotheism. For this reason, He said, lest you say, meaning lest you say on the Day of Resurrection, Indeed, we were of this, meaning monotheism, unaware. Or you say Our fathers only associated others with God.
