And when He creates a servant for Hell, He employs him in the deeds of the people of Hell until he dies doing one of the deeds of the people of Hell, and He enters him into Hell because of it.” And thus Abu Dawud narrated it on the authority of Al-Qa’nabi, Al-Nasa’i on the authority of Qutaybah, and Al-Tirmidhi in their Tafsir on the authority of Ishaq bin Musa on the authority of Ma’n and Ibn Abi Hatim on the authority of Yunus bin Abdul A’la on the authority of Ibn Wahb and Ibn Jarir on the authority of Ruh bin Ubadah and Sa’id bin Abdul Hamid bin Ja’far. And Ibn Hibban included it in his Sahih on the authority of Abu Mus’ab Al-Zubayri, all of them on the authority of Imam Malik bin Anas. Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a good hadith, and Muslim bin Yasar did not hear ‘Umar. This is what Abu Hatim and Abu Zur’ah said. Abu Hatim added: And between them was Nu’aym bin Rabi’ah. And what Abu Hatim said was narrated by Abu Dawud in his Sunan on the authority of Muhammad bin Musa on the authority of Baqiyah on the authority of ‘Umar bin Ja’tham Al-Qurashi on the authority of Zayd bin Abi Anisa on the authority of ‘Abd Al-Hamid bin ‘Abd Al-Rahman bin Zayd bin Al-Khattab on the authority of Muslim bin Yasar. Al-Juhani narrated on the authority of Na’im bin Rabi’ah who said: I was with Umar bin Al-Khattab and he was asked about this verse: And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants, so he mentioned it. Al-Hafiz Al-Daraqutni said: Umar bin Ja’tham was followed by Yazid bin Sinan Abu Farwah Al-Rahawi and their statement is more correct than the statement of Malik, and God knows best. I said: It appears that Imam Malik only omitted the mention of Na’im bin Rabi’ah intentionally because he was ignorant of the status of Na’im bin Rabi’ah and did not know him, as he is not known except in this hadith. For this reason he omitted the mention of a group of people whom he did not approve of. For this reason he sent many of the marfu’ hadiths and omitted many of the mawasul hadiths, and God knows best. Another hadith Al-Tirmidhi said when interpreting this verse: Abd bin Hamid told us, Abu Naim told us, Hisham bin Saad told us, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When God created Adam, He wiped his back, and from his back fell every soul that He would create from his offspring until the Day of Resurrection, and He placed between the eyes of every person of them a gleam of light. Then He showed them to Adam and said: ‘O Lord, who are these?’ He said: ‘These are your offspring.’ He saw a man among them and the gleam between his eyes pleased him. He said: ‘O Lord, who is this?’ He said: ‘This is a man from the last of the nations from your offspring, called David.’ He said: ‘O Lord, how long have you made his lifespan?’ He said: ‘Sixty years.’ He said: ‘O Lord, and I have given him forty years of my life.’ When Adam’s lifespan came to an end, the Angel of Death came to him and said: ‘Are there not forty years left of my lifespan?’ He said: ‘Did you not give them to your son David?’ He said: ‘So Adam denied, so his offspring denied, and Adam forgot, so his offspring forgot, and Adam sinned, so his offspring sinned.’” Then Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a good and authentic hadith. It has been narrated From other chains of transmission on the authority of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak on the authority of Abu Na’im al-Fadl ibn Dukayn on his authority and said: It is authentic according to the conditions of Muslim, although they did not include it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it in his Tafsir on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam on the authority of his father that he narrated on the authority of Ata’ ibn Yasar on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned something similar to what was mentioned above until he said: “Then he showed them to Adam and said: O Adam, these are your descendants, and among them were the leper, the albino, the blind, and all kinds of diseases. Adam said: O Lord, why have you done this to my descendants? He said: So that you may be grateful for my blessings. Adam said: O Lord, who are these whom I see as the most luminous of people? He said: These are the prophets, O Adam, from your descendants.” Then he mentioned the story of David something similar to what was mentioned above. Another hadith Abd al-Rahman ibn Qatada al-Nadri narrated on the authority of his father on the authority of Hisham ibn Hakim, may God be pleased with him, that a man asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, do deeds begin or has the decree already been decreed? He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God took the descendants of Adam from their backs, then made them testify against themselves, then poured them into His hands, then said: These are in Paradise and these are in Hell. So the people of Paradise are facilitated to do the deeds of the people of Paradise, and the people of Hell are facilitated to do the deeds of the people of Hell.” Narrated by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh through various chains of transmission on his authority. Another hadith Ja`far ibn al-Zubayr narrated, and he is weak, on the authority of al-Qasim, on the authority of Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When God created the creation and decreed the matter, He took the people of the right hand with His right hand and the people of the left hand with His left hand. He said: ‘O people of the right hand.’ They said: ‘At your service and pleasure.’ He said: ‘Am I not your Lord?’ They said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘O people of the left hand.’ They said: ‘At your service and pleasure.’ He said: ‘Am I not your Lord?’ They said: ‘Yes.’ Then He mixed them together. Someone said to Him: ‘O Lord, why have You mixed them together?’ He said: ‘They are doing deeds other than that, lest they say on the Day of Resurrection, ‘Indeed, we were unaware of this.’ Then He returned them to the loins of Adam.” Narrated by Ibn Mardawayh. Another trace Abu Ja`far al-Razi said on the authority of al-Rabi` ibn Anas on the authority of Abu al-`Aliyah on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka`b regarding the words of God Almighty: And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants (al-Baqarah 2:17), he said: Then He gathered them all together for Himself on that day, whatever would be from Him until the Day of Resurrection, and He made them in their forms, then He made them speak, and He took from them a covenant and a pact. And He made them testify of themselves, ‘Am I not your Lord?’ They said, ‘Yes.’ (al-Baqarah 2:17) He said: Then I call upon you the seven heavens and the seven earths, and I call upon you your father Adam, lest you say on the Day of Resurrection, ‘We did not know this.’ Know that there is no god but Me, and no lord but Me, and do not associate anything with Me, and that I will send to you messengers to warn you of My covenant and My pact, and I will send down to you My Book. They said: We testify that You are our Lord and our God. We have no lord but You, and we have no god but You. So they acknowledged their obedience to Him on that day, and He raised their father Adam and looked at them and saw among them the rich and the poor, and the beautiful in appearance and less than that, so He said: O Lord, if You made Your servants equal? He said: I wanted to thank and saw in them the prophets like lamps upon them light and they were singled out with another covenant of the message and prophethood, it is what God Almighty says: And when We took from the prophets their covenant the verse and it is what He says: So set your face toward the religion, inclining toward truth, the nature of God the verse and from that He said: This is a warner from the first warnings and from that He said: And we did not find for most of them any covenant the verse, narrated by Abdullah bin Imam Ahmad in Musnad of his father, and narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh in their commentaries from the narration of Abu Jaafar al-Razi with it and it was narrated from Mujahid, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubayr, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Suddi and more than one of the scholars of the Salaf contexts that agree with these hadiths, we were satisfied with citing them instead of going into length in all those narrations and with God is the helper. These hadiths indicate that God, the Almighty, extracted the offspring of Adam from his loins and distinguished between the people of Paradise and the people of Hell. As for bearing witness to them there that He is their Lord, it is only in the hadith of Kalthoum bin Jabr from Saeed bin Jubair from Ibn Abbas and in the hadith of Abdullah bin Amr. We have shown that they are suspended and not raised as mentioned above. Hence, some of the early and later scholars said that what is meant by this bearing witness is that He created them upon monotheism as mentioned above in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah and Iyad bin Himar Al-Majashi’i and in the narration of Al-Hasan Al-Basri from Al-Aswad bin Sari’. Al-Hasan interpreted the verse with this. They said: This is why He said: And when your Lord took from the children of Adam and did not say from Adam from their loins and did not say from his loins their offspring meaning He made their offspring generation after generation and century after century like the Almighty’s saying: And it is He who made you successors on the earth and He said: And He will make you successors on the earth and He said: Just as He created you from the offspring of another people then He said: “And He made them testify of themselves, ‘Am I not your Lord?’ They said: Yes” meaning He created them as witnesses to that. Saying to him in a state and a saying, and the testimony is sometimes by saying, as in His saying, They said, ‘We bear witness against ourselves’ verse, and sometimes it is a state, as in His saying, the Most High: It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of God while they bear witness against themselves of disbelief, meaning their state is a witness against them in that, not that they are saying that. And likewise His saying, the Most High: And indeed, He is, over that, a witness, just as the question is sometimes by saying and sometimes it is by state, as in His saying, And He gave you of all that you asked of Him, they said. And what indicates that what is meant by this is that He made this testimony an argument against them in polytheism. If this had happened as those who said said, then everyone would have mentioned it so that it would be an argument against him. If it is said that the Messenger’s (peace and blessings of God be upon him) informing them of it is sufficient for its existence, then the answer is that the deniers among the polytheists deny everything that the Messengers brought them of this and other things, and this was made an independent argument against them, so it indicates that it is the nature upon which they were created of acknowledging monotheism. For this reason, He said, lest you say, meaning lest you say on the Day of Resurrection, Indeed, we were of this, meaning monotheism, unaware. Or you say Our fathers only associated others with God.
7:174: The Almighty informs us that He extracted the offspring of the children of Adam from their loins, bearing witness against themselves that God is their Lord and their King, and that there is no god but Him, just as He created them on that and made them like that. The Almighty said: “So direct your face toward the religion, inclining toward truth. [Adhere to] the nature of God upon which He has created mankind. There is no change in the creation of God.” And in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Every child is born upon the fitrah, and in another narration upon this religion, then his parents make him a Jew, a Christian, or a Zoroastrian, just as an animal is born whole. Do you see among them any with their ears cut off?” And in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Iyadh ibn Himar, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God says: I created My servants as monotheists, then the devils came to them and led them astray from their religion and prohibited for them what I had permitted for them.” And Imam Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him, said: Yunus ibn `Abd al-`Ala told us, Ibn Wahb told us, al-Sari ibn Yahya told me that al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan told them on the authority of al-Aswad ibn Sari` from Bani Saad said: I participated in four battles with the Messenger of God (peace be upon him). He said: The people took up their children after they had killed the fighters. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) was informed of that and he was upset with him. Then he said: What is the matter with people who take up their children? A man said: O Messenger of God, are they not the children of the polytheists? He said: “The best of you are the children of the polytheists. Indeed, no soul is born except that it is born upon the fitrah natural disposition, and it remains upon it until its language becomes clear to its parents, then its parents make it a Jew or a Christian.” Al-Hasan said: By God, God said in His Book: And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants (al-Baqarah 2:14). Imam Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Ismail bin Aliyah on the authority of Yunus bin Ubayd on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri on his authority. Al-Nasa’i included it in his Sunan on the authority of Hisham on the authority of Yunus bin Ubayd on the authority of Al-Hasan who said: Al-Aswad bin Sari’ told me and he mentioned it but he did not mention the statement of Al-Hasan Al-Basri and his recalling the verse at that time. There are hadiths about taking up the children from the loins of Adam (peace be upon him) and distinguishing them into the companions of the right and the companions of the left, and in some of them the testimony against them that God is their Lord. Imam Ahmad said: Hajjaj told us, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Abu Imran al-Joni, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “A man from the people of Hell will be asked on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:‘Do you think that if you had everything on the earth, would you ransom yourself with it?’ He will say: ‘Yes.’ He will say: ‘I wanted something easier from you than that. I took a covenant from you in the back of Adam that you would not associate anything with Me, but you refused except to associate anything with Me.’” They both included it in the two Sahihs on the authority of Shu`bah. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Husayn ibn Muhammad told us: Jarir, meaning Ibn Hazim, told us, on the authority of Kalthoum ibn Jabr, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God took the covenant from the back of Adam, peace be upon him, in Nu`man on the Day of Arafah, and brought forth from his loins every offspring He had created, and scattered them before Him, then He spoke to them directly, saying: ‘Am I not your Lord?’ They said: ‘Yes, we bear witness.’ This [hadith] was narrated by al-Nasa’i in the Book of Interpretation of his Sunan on the authority of Muhammad ibn `Abd al-Rahim Sa`iqah on the authority of Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Marwazi on his authority. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of Husayn ibn Muhammad on his authority, except that Ibn Abi Hatim made it a mursal. Al-Hakim included it in his Mustadrak on the authority of Husayn ibn Muhammad and others on the authority of Jarir ibn Hazim on the authority of Kalthoum ibn Jabr on his authority, and he said: Its chain of transmission is sound, but they did not include it. Muslim cited Kalthoum ibn Jabr as evidence, and this is what he said. `Abd al-Rahim narrated it on his authority. Al-Warith, on the authority of Kalthoum bin Jabr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, stopped it. Ismail bin Aliyah and Wakee’ narrated it likewise on the authority of Rabia bin Kalthoum, on the authority of Jabr, on the authority of his father, on his authority. Ata bin Al-Sa’ib, Habib bin Abi Thabit, and Ali bin Badhima narrated it likewise on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Al-Awfi and Ali bin Abi Talhah narrated it likewise on the authority of Ibn Abbas, so this is more and more authentic, and God knows best. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakee’ told us, my father told us, on the authority of Abu Hilal, on the authority of Abu Hamza Al-Dab’i, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: God brought forth the offspring of Adam from his back in the form of ants while he was in the filth of the water. He also said: Ali bin Sahl narrated to us, Damrah bin Rabi’ah narrated to us, Abu Mas’ud narrated to us, on the authority of Jarir, who said: Ibn Adh-Dahhak bin Muzahim died at the age of six days. He said: So he said: O Jabir, when you place my son in his grave, expose his face and untie his knots, for my son will be seated and questioned. So I did with him what he was commanded. When I finished, I said: May God have mercy on you, about what your son asks of whom he asks. He said: He asks about the covenant that he acknowledged in the loins of Adam. I said: O Abu Al-Qasim, what is this covenant that he acknowledged in the loins of Adam? He said: Ibn Abbas narrated to me: God wiped the loins of Adam and extracted from them every soul that He created until the Day of Resurrection. He took from them the covenant that they would worship Him and not associate anything with Him, and He guaranteed them sustenance. Then He returned them to his loins. The Hour will not come until the one to whom he gave the covenant is born on that day. Whoever among them attains the second covenant and fulfills it, the first covenant will benefit him. Whoever attains the second covenant and does not acknowledge it, the first covenant will not benefit him. Whoever dies young before attaining the second covenant dies upon the first covenant, according to the fitrah. All of these paths are what strengthen this. This is based on Ibn Abbas, and God knows best. Another hadith Ibn Jarir said: Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Walid told us, Ahmad ibn Abi Tayyiba told us, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Saeed, on the authority of al-Ajlah, on the authority of al-Dahhak, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants.” He said: He took from his back as a comb is taken from the head, and said to them: Am I not your Lord? They said: Yes. The angels said: We bear witness. This – lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, Indeed, we were of this unaware. This Ahmad ibn Abi Tayyiba is Abu Muhammad al-Jurjani, the judge of Qumis. He was one of the ascetics. Al-Nasa’i included him in his Sunan. Abu Hatim al-Razi said: His hadith should be written down. Ibn Adi narrated many strange hadiths. Abd al-Rahman ibn Hamza ibn Fahdi narrated this hadith on the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Mansur, and this is more authentic, and God knows best. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Ruh, he is Ibn Ubadah, told us, Malik told us, and Ishaq told us, Malik told us, on the authority of Zaid bin Abi Anisa, that Abdul Hamid bin Abdul Rahman bin Zaid bin Al-Khattab told him, on the authority of Muslim bin Yasar Al-Juhani, that Umar bin Al-Khattab was asked about this verse: And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants and made them testify of themselves, [saying], ‘Am I not your Lord?’ They said, ‘Yes.’ The verse. Umar bin Al-Khattab said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, being asked about it, and he said: “God created Adam, peace be upon him, then He wiped his back with His right hand and extracted from him his descendants. He said, ‘I created these for Paradise and they will do the deeds of the people of Paradise.’ Then He wiped his back and extracted from him his descendants. He said, ‘I created these for the Fire and they will do the deeds of the people of the Fire.’” A man said, O Messenger of God, what is the purpose of work? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When God creates a servant for Paradise, He employs him in the deeds of the people of Paradise until he dies doing one of the deeds of the people of Paradise, and He enters him into Paradise because of it. And when He creates a servant for Hell, He employs him in the deeds of the people of Hell until he dies doing one of the deeds of the people of Hell, and He enters him into Hell because of it.” And thus Abu Dawud narrated it on the authority of Al-Qa’nabi, Al-Nasa’i on the authority of Qutaybah, and Al-Tirmidhi in their Tafsir on the authority of Ishaq bin Musa on the authority of Ma’n and Ibn Abi Hatim on the authority of Yunus bin Abdul A’la on the authority of Ibn Wahb and Ibn Jarir on the authority of Ruh bin Ubadah and Sa’id bin Abdul Hamid bin Ja’far. And Ibn Hibban included it in his Sahih on the authority of Abu Mus’ab Al-Zubayri, all of them on the authority of Imam Malik bin Anas. Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a good hadith, and Muslim bin Yasar did not hear ‘Umar. This is what Abu Hatim and Abu Zur’ah said. Abu Hatim added: And between them was Nu’aym bin Rabi’ah. And what Abu Hatim said was narrated by Abu Dawud in his Sunan on the authority of Muhammad bin Musa on the authority of Baqiyah on the authority of ‘Umar bin Ja’tham Al-Qurashi on the authority of Zayd bin Abi Anisa on the authority of ‘Abd Al-Hamid bin ‘Abd Al-Rahman bin Zayd bin Al-Khattab on the authority of Muslim bin Yasar. Al-Juhani narrated on the authority of Na’im bin Rabi’ah who said: I was with Umar bin Al-Khattab and he was asked about this verse: And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants, so he mentioned it. Al-Hafiz Al-Daraqutni said: Umar bin Ja’tham was followed by Yazid bin Sinan Abu Farwah Al-Rahawi and their statement is more correct than the statement of Malik, and God knows best. I said: It appears that Imam Malik only omitted the mention of Na’im bin Rabi’ah intentionally because he was ignorant of the status of Na’im bin Rabi’ah and did not know him, as he is not known except in this hadith. For this reason he omitted the mention of a group of people whom he did not approve of. For this reason he sent many of the marfu’ hadiths and omitted many of the mawasul hadiths, and God knows best. Another hadith Al-Tirmidhi said when interpreting this verse: Abd bin Hamid told us, Abu Naim told us, Hisham bin Saad told us, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When God created Adam, He wiped his back, and from his back fell every soul that He would create from his offspring until the Day of Resurrection, and He placed between the eyes of every person of them a gleam of light. Then He showed them to Adam and said: ‘O Lord, who are these?’ He said: ‘These are your offspring.’ He saw a man among them and the gleam between his eyes pleased him. He said: ‘O Lord, who is this?’ He said: ‘This is a man from the last of the nations from your offspring, called David.’ He said: ‘O Lord, how long have you made his lifespan?’ He said: ‘Sixty years.’ He said: ‘O Lord, and I have given him forty years of my life.’ When Adam’s lifespan came to an end, the Angel of Death came to him and said: ‘Are there not forty years left of my lifespan?’ He said: ‘Did you not give them to your son David?’ He said: ‘So Adam denied, so his offspring denied, and Adam forgot, so his offspring forgot, and Adam sinned, so his offspring sinned.’” Then Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a good and authentic hadith. It has been narrated From other chains of transmission on the authority of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak on the authority of Abu Na’im al-Fadl ibn Dukayn on his authority and said: It is authentic according to the conditions of Muslim, although they did not include it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it in his Tafsir on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam on the authority of his father that he narrated on the authority of Ata’ ibn Yasar on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned something similar to what was mentioned above until he said: “Then he showed them to Adam and said: O Adam, these are your descendants, and among them were the leper, the albino, the blind, and all kinds of diseases. Adam said: O Lord, why have you done this to my descendants? He said: So that you may be grateful for my blessings. Adam said: O Lord, who are these whom I see as the most luminous of people? He said: These are the prophets, O Adam, from your descendants.” Then he mentioned the story of David something similar to what was mentioned above. Another hadith Abd al-Rahman ibn Qatada al-Nadri narrated on the authority of his father on the authority of Hisham ibn Hakim, may God be pleased with him, that a man asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, do deeds begin or has the decree already been decreed? He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God took the descendants of Adam from their backs, then made them testify against themselves, then poured them into His hands, then said: These are in Paradise and these are in Hell. So the people of Paradise are facilitated to do the deeds of the people of Paradise, and the people of Hell are facilitated to do the deeds of the people of Hell.” Narrated by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh through various chains of transmission on his authority. Another hadith Ja`far ibn al-Zubayr narrated, and he is weak, on the authority of al-Qasim, on the authority of Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When God created the creation and decreed the matter, He took the people of the right hand with His right hand and the people of the left hand with His left hand. He said: ‘O people of the right hand.’ They said: ‘At your service and pleasure.’ He said: ‘Am I not your Lord?’ They said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘O people of the left hand.’ They said: ‘At your service and pleasure.’ He said: ‘Am I not your Lord?’ They said: ‘Yes.’ Then He mixed them together. Someone said to Him: ‘O Lord, why have You mixed them together?’ He said: ‘They are doing deeds other than that, lest they say on the Day of Resurrection, ‘Indeed, we were unaware of this.’ Then He returned them to the loins of Adam.” Narrated by Ibn Mardawayh. Another trace Abu Ja`far al-Razi said on the authority of al-Rabi` ibn Anas on the authority of Abu al-`Aliyah on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka`b regarding the words of God Almighty: And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants (al-Baqarah 2:17), he said: Then He gathered them all together for Himself on that day, whatever would be from Him until the Day of Resurrection, and He made them in their forms, then He made them speak, and He took from them a covenant and a pact. And He made them testify of themselves, ‘Am I not your Lord?’ They said, ‘Yes.’ (al-Baqarah 2:17) He said: Then I call upon you the seven heavens and the seven earths, and I call upon you your father Adam, lest you say on the Day of Resurrection, ‘We did not know this.’ Know that there is no god but Me, and no lord but Me, and do not associate anything with Me, and that I will send to you messengers to warn you of My covenant and My pact, and I will send down to you My Book. They said: We testify that You are our Lord and our God. We have no lord but You, and we have no god but You. So they acknowledged their obedience to Him on that day, and He raised their father Adam and looked at them and saw among them the rich and the poor, and the beautiful in appearance and less than that, so He said: O Lord, if You made Your servants equal? He said: I wanted to thank and saw in them the prophets like lamps upon them light and they were singled out with another covenant of the message and prophethood, it is what God Almighty says: And when We took from the prophets their covenant the verse and it is what He says: So set your face toward the religion, inclining toward truth, the nature of God the verse and from that He said: This is a warner from the first warnings and from that He said: And we did not find for most of them any covenant the verse, narrated by Abdullah bin Imam Ahmad in Musnad of his father, and narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh in their commentaries from the narration of Abu Jaafar al-Razi with it and it was narrated from Mujahid, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubayr, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Suddi and more than one of the scholars of the Salaf contexts that agree with these hadiths, we were satisfied with citing them instead of going into length in all those narrations and with God is the helper. These hadiths indicate that God, the Almighty, extracted the offspring of Adam from his loins and distinguished between the people of Paradise and the people of Hell. As for bearing witness to them there that He is their Lord, it is only in the hadith of Kalthoum bin Jabr from Saeed bin Jubair from Ibn Abbas and in the hadith of Abdullah bin Amr. We have shown that they are suspended and not raised as mentioned above. Hence, some of the early and later scholars said that what is meant by this bearing witness is that He created them upon monotheism as mentioned above in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah and Iyad bin Himar Al-Majashi’i and in the narration of Al-Hasan Al-Basri from Al-Aswad bin Sari’. Al-Hasan interpreted the verse with this. They said: This is why He said: And when your Lord took from the children of Adam and did not say from Adam from their loins and did not say from his loins their offspring meaning He made their offspring generation after generation and century after century like the Almighty’s saying: And it is He who made you successors on the earth and He said: And He will make you successors on the earth and He said: Just as He created you from the offspring of another people then He said: “And He made them testify of themselves, ‘Am I not your Lord?’ They said: Yes” meaning He created them as witnesses to that. Saying to him in a state and a saying, and the testimony is sometimes by saying, as in His saying, They said, ‘We bear witness against ourselves’ verse, and sometimes it is a state, as in His saying, the Most High: It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of God while they bear witness against themselves of disbelief, meaning their state is a witness against them in that, not that they are saying that. And likewise His saying, the Most High: And indeed, He is, over that, a witness, just as the question is sometimes by saying and sometimes it is by state, as in His saying, And He gave you of all that you asked of Him, they said. And what indicates that what is meant by this is that He made this testimony an argument against them in polytheism. If this had happened as those who said said, then everyone would have mentioned it so that it would be an argument against him. If it is said that the Messenger’s (peace and blessings of God be upon him) informing them of it is sufficient for its existence, then the answer is that the deniers among the polytheists deny everything that the Messengers brought them of this and other things, and this was made an independent argument against them, so it indicates that it is the nature upon which they were created of acknowledging monotheism. For this reason, He said, lest you say, meaning lest you say on the Day of Resurrection, Indeed, we were of this, meaning monotheism, unaware. Or you say Our fathers only associated others with God.
7:175: Abdul Razzaq said: On the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri, on the authority of al-A'mash and Mansur, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may God be pleased with him, regarding the words of God Almighty: And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he slipped out of them the verse, he said: He is a man from the Children of Israel called Balaam ibn Ba'oura. Shu'bah and others narrated it in this way on the authority of Mansur. Sa'id ibn Abi 'Aruba said on the authority of Qatada on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He is Saifi ibn al-Rahib. Qatada said: Ka'b said: He was a man from the people of Balqa' and he knew the Greatest Name and he was residing in Jerusalem with the tyrants. Al-A'wfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him: He is a man from the people of Yemen called Balaam. God gave him His signs, but he abandoned them. Malik ibn Dinar said: He was one of the scholars of the Children of Israel and his prayers were answered. They would put him forward in times of hardship. The Prophet of God, Moses, peace be upon him, sent him to the king of Madyan to call him to God, so he gave him a land and gave him, so he followed his religion and abandoned the religion of Moses, peace be upon him. Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said on the authority of Hisayn on the authority of Imran ibn Al-Harith on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He is Balaam bin Ba’oura, and this is what Mujahid and Ikrimah said. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Harith told me, Abdul Aziz told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: He is Balaam. Thaqeef said: He is Umayyah bin Abi Al-Salt. Shu’bah said on the authority of Ya’la bin Ata’ on the authority of Nafi’ bin Asim on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, regarding His statement, And recite to them the report of him to whom We gave Our signs 1:13, the verse, he said: He is your companion Umayyah bin Abi Al-Salt. It has been narrated from other sources on his authority, and it is authentically attributed to him. It seems that he only meant that Umayyah bin Abi Al-Salt resembled him, for he had attained much knowledge of the knowledge of the previous laws, but he did not benefit from his knowledge, for he lived during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his signs, signs, and miracles reached him, and they were apparent to everyone who had insight. Despite this, he met with him and did not follow him, and he turned to befriending, supporting, and praising the polytheists. He mourned the polytheists who fought at Badr with an eloquent elegy. May God curse him. It was mentioned in some hadiths that he who believed in his tongue but did not believe in his heart, has divine poetry, wisdom and eloquence, but God did not open his chest to Islam. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ibn Abi Namir told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Awar, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he slipped out of them, he said: He is a man who was given three supplications that were answered for him, and he had a wife with whom he had a child. She said, Give me one of them. He said, “You have one. What do you want?” She said, Pray to God to make me the most beautiful woman among the Children of Israel. So he prayed to God, and He made her the most beautiful woman among the Children of Israel. When she knew that there was no one like her among them, she turned away from him and wanted something else. So he prayed to God to make her a dog, and she became a dog. Then two prayers were made. Then her sons came and said, “We cannot stay here. Our mother has become a dog that people will taunt us with. So pray to God to return her to the state she was in.” So he prayed to God, and she returned to what she was, and the three prayers were made. She was called Al-Basoos. Strange. As for the well-known reason for the revelation of this noble verse, it is a man from the early generations in the time of the Children of Israel, as Ibn Masoud and others of the Salaf said. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He is a man from the city of the tyrants called Balaam, and he knew the greatest name of God. Abd al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam and others of the scholars of the Salaf said: His prayers were answered, and he did not ask God for anything except that He gave it to him. Stranger, even more distant, even mistaken is he who said: He had been given prophethood and then stripped himself of it. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of some of them, and it is not correct. Ali bin Abi Talha on the authority of Ibn Abbas: When Moses descended upon them, meaning the tyrants and those with him, his cousins and people came to him - meaning Balaam - and said: Moses is a man of iron and has many soldiers, and if he prevails over us he will destroy us, so pray to God to turn Moses and those with him away from us. He said: If I pray to God to turn Moses and those with him away, my world and my afterlife will be lost. So they kept on at him until he prayed against them, and God stripped him of what he was wearing. This is what God Almighty said: So he slipped away from it, and Satan pursued him 1:10. Al-Suddi said: When the forty years had passed, of which God said, It is forbidden to them for forty years, He sent Joshua bin Nun as a prophet. He called the Children of Israel and informed them that he was a prophet and that God had commanded him to fight the tyrants, so they pledged allegiance to him and believed him. A man from the Children of Israel called Balaam set out, and he was a scholar who knew the Greatest Hidden Name. He disbelieved, may God curse him, and went to the tyrants and said to them: Do not terrorize the Children of Israel, for if you go out to fight them, I will call down a curse upon them and they will perish. He had whatever he wanted of this worldly life with them, except that he was unable to approach women because of their great size, so he would marry a female donkey of his, and this is what God Almighty said: So he slipped out of her. God Almighty said: So Satan pursued him, meaning he took control of him and his affairs, so whatever he commanded him, he complied and obeyed. For this reason, He said: So he was among the astray, meaning among the perished, confused, and lost. A hadith was narrated in the meaning of this verse by Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la Al-Mawsili in his Musnad, where he said: Muhammad bin Marzouq narrated to us Muhammad bin Bakr on the authority of Al-Salt bin Bahram, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Jundub Al-Bajali in this mosque that Hudhayfah, meaning Ibn Al-Yaman, may God be pleased with him, narrated to him that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Among the things I fear for you is a man who recites the Qur’an until its brilliance is seen upon him and his cloak is Islam, which of them wills to be removed and cast behind his back, and attack his neighbor with the sword and accuse him of polytheism.” I said: O Prophet of God, which of the two is more deserving of polytheism, the one who is accused or the one who is accused? He said: Rather, the one who is accused. The chain of transmission is good. Al-Salt bin Bahram was one of the trustworthy people of Kufa and he was not accused of anything except Irja’. Imam Ahmad bin Hanbal, Yahya bin Ma’in, and others authenticated him. And the Almighty said: And if We willed, We could have elevated him thereby, but he clung to the earth and followed his own desire. The Almighty says: And if We willed, We could have elevated him thereby, meaning, We could have elevated him from the defilement of the filth of this world with the signs that We gave him, but he clung to the earth, meaning, he inclined toward the adornments and adornments of this worldly life and turned to its pleasures and delights, and it deceived him as it deceived others who were not people of insight and reason. Abu al-Rahawayh said about the Almighty’s statement: but he clung to the earth, he said: Satan appeared to him on a high place on the Baniyas Bridge, so the donkey prostrated to God and Balaam prostrated to Satan. And Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr and others said the same. Imam Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him, said: And from the story of this man was what Muhammad ibn Abd al-A`la told us, al-Mu`tamir told us on the authority of his father that he was asked about this verse: And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs, so he narrated on the authority of Sayyar that there was a man called Balaam and his prayers were answered. He said: And Moses came with the Children of Israel, wanting the land that In it was Balaam, or he said: Ash-Sham. He said: The people were terrified of him with great fear, so they came to Balaam and said: Pray to God against this man and his army. He said: Until I command my Lord, or until I am commanded. He said: So command to pray against them. It was said to him: Do not pray against them, for they are My servants and among them is their prophet. He said: So he said to his al-Nas 114:I have commanded my Lord to pray against them, and I have forbidden them. So they gave him a gift and he accepted it. Then they returned to him and said: Pray against them. He said: Until I command my Lord. So he commanded, but he did not command him to do anything. He said: I have been commanded, but he did not command me to do anything. They said: If your Lord had hated that you pray against them, He would have forbidden you as He forbade you the first time. He said: So he began to pray against them, and when he prayed against them, the prayer against his people came from his tongue, and when he wanted to pray for his people to be granted victory, he prayed for Moses and his army to be granted victory, or something like that, God willing. He said: So they said: We do not see you praying except against us. He said: It only comes from my tongue like this, and if I prayed against him also, I would not be answered, but I will guide you to a matter. Perhaps it will be their destruction. Indeed, God hates adultery, and if they commit adultery, they will perish. I hoped that God would destroy them, so they brought out the women to meet them, for they are a people traveling, so perhaps they will commit adultery and perish. He said: So they did, and they brought out the women to meet them. He said: The king had a daughter, and he mentioned her greatness, which God knows best. He said: Her father or Balaam said: Do not let me have power over anyone except Moses. He said: And they committed adultery. He said: Then the head of one of the tribes of the Children of Israel came to her and wanted to have sex with her, but she said: I will not have power over anyone except Moses: a man from the sons of Aaron, and he had a spear with him, so he thrust them. He said: And God supported him with strength, so he strung them together and raised them on his spear, and the people saw them - or something like that - He said: And God sent a plague upon them, and seventy thousand of them died. Abu Al-Mu'tamir said: Sayyar told me that Balaam rode his donkey until he reached Al-Ululi, or he said a road from Al-Ululi. He started hitting it but it would not move forward. It stood up to him and said: Why are you hitting me? Don't you see what is in front of you? Then Satan was before him. He said: So he descended and prostrated to him. God Almighty said: “And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he slipped out of them. So Satan pursued him, and he was among the deviators. And if We had willed, We could have elevated him thereby, but he clung to the earth and followed his own desire. So his example is that of the dog: if you chase him, he pants, or if you leave him, he pants. That is the example of the people who deny Our signs. So relate the story that perhaps they will give thought.” He said: So Sayyar told me this, and I do not know, perhaps something from someone else’s hadith has entered into it. I said He is Balaam, and it is said Balaam bin Ba’oura, and it is said Ibn Aber, and it is said Ibn Ba’our bin Shahtum bin Qushtum bin Mab bin Lot bin Haran, and it is said Ibn Haran bin Azar, and he lived in a village in Balqa. Ibn Asakir said: He is the one who knew the greatest name of God, but he slipped out of his religion. He is mentioned in the Qur’an. Then he mentioned from his story something similar to what we mentioned here, he mentioned it from Wahb and others, and God knows best. Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Sayyar said: On the authority of Salim Abu Al-Nadr, that he narrated that when Moses, peace be upon him, descended to the land of the Canaanites in the land of Ash-Sham, the people of Balaam came to him and said to him: This is Moses bin Imran among the Children of Israel. He has come to expel us from our country and kill us and make it the Children of Israel. We are your people and we have no home, and you are a man whose supplications are answered, so go out and supplicate to God against them. He said: Woe to you, the Prophet of God has with him the angels and the believers. How can I go and supplicate against them while I know from God what I know? They said to him: We have no home. So they kept on beseeching him and supplicating him until they tempted him, so he was tempted and rode his donkey towards the mountain that overlooked the army of the Children of Israel, which was Mount Hisban. After he had walked on it for some time, it lay down with him, so he got off it and hit it until he made it slip, then it stood up and he mounted it. It did not walk with him for long until it lay down with him and he hit it until he made it slip, so he gave it permission, so it spoke to him as an argument against him and said: Woe to you, Balaam, where are you going? Do you not see the angels in front of me preventing me from this path of mine? She went to the Prophet of God and the believers to pray against them, but he did not stop hitting her, so God let her go when he did that to her. She went with him until she brought him to the top of Hisban, over the army of Moses and the Children of Israel. He began to pray against them, and he did not pray against them for evil except that God turned his tongue to his people, and he did not pray for his people for good except that he turned his tongue to the Children of Israel. His people said to him: Do you know, O Balaam, what you are doing? He said: This is something I do not own, this is something that God has overcome. He said: His tongue stuck out and fell on his chest and he said to them: Now the world and the hereafter have gone from me and nothing remains but deceit and trickery, so I will deceive and scheme for you. Beautify the women and give them goods, then send them to the camp to sell them there and order them that no woman should withhold herself from a man who wants her, for if one man among them commits adultery, you will be spared them. So they did. When the women entered the camp, a Canaanite woman named Kasbi - the daughter of Tyre, the head of his nation - passed by a man from the leaders of the Children of Israel, who was Zimri, the son of Shallum, the head of the tribe of Simeon, the son of Jacob, the son of Isaac, the son of Abraham, peace be upon him. When he saw her, he was pleased, so he stood up, took her by the hand, and brought her to Moses and said: I think you will say this is forbidden to you? He said: Yes, it is forbidden to you, do not come near her. He said: By God, I will not obey you in this. So he entered his tent with her and fell upon her. God Almighty sent the plague upon the Children of Israel. Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron, was the one in charge of Moses and was absent when Zimri, son of Shallum, did what he did. He came while the plague was raging among them and reported the report. He took his spear, which was all iron. Then he entered the tent while they were lying down and strung them together with his spear. Then he went out with them, raising them to the sky, holding the spear in his arm and leaning his elbow on his waist and resting the spear on his jaw. He was the firstborn of Eleazar. He kept saying: O God, this is how we deal with those who disobey you and lift the plague. So he calculated how many of the Children of Israel had perished in the plague between the time Zimri struck the woman and Phinehas killed him. They found that seventy thousand of them had perished, and the one who underestimated them said twenty thousand in one hour of the day. From there, the Children of Israel would give Phinehas’ son from every sacrifice they had slaughtered the neck, the arm, the jaw, and the firstborn from all their wealth. And the same because he was the firstborn of his father, Eleazar. So regarding Balaam bin Ba’oura, God revealed: “And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he slipped out of them, so Satan pursued him, and he was among the deviators. And if We had willed, We could have elevated him thereby, but he clung to the earth and followed his own desire. So his example is like that of a dog: if you attack him, he pants, or if you leave him, he pants. That is the example of the people who deny Our signs. So relate the story that perhaps they will give thought.” And the Almighty’s saying: “So his example is like that of a dog: if you attack him, he pants, or if you leave him, he pants.” The commentators differed in its meaning. According to the context of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Abu al-Nadr, that Balaam’s tongue stuck out on his chest, so his likeness to a dog in its panting in both its states, whether it is rebuked or left alone, is apparent. And it was said that its meaning is that he became like him in his misguidance and his persistence in it and his lack of benefit to faith and lack of supplication like a dog in its panting in both its states: if you attack him or leave him, he pants in both states, so likewise this one does not benefit. By preaching and calling to faith or not, as God Almighty said: It is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them - they will not believe. “Ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them. If you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, God will not forgive them.” and the like. It was said that its meaning is that the heart of the disbeliever, hypocrite, and misguided person is weak and empty of guidance, so he is often obliged. This was expressed in this way, something similar was transmitted from Al-Hasan Al-Basri and others. God Almighty’s statement: So relate the stories that perhaps they will give thought. God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, So relate the stories that perhaps they meaning perhaps the Children of Israel who knew the state of Balaam and what happened to him in God’s misguidance and distancing him from His mercy, because he used God’s blessing upon him in teaching him the Greatest Name, which if he was asked by it, he would give, and if he was called by it, he would answer, in disobedience to his Lord. Rather, he called by it upon the party of the Most Merciful and the people of faith, the followers of His servant and Messenger at that time, the one who spoke to God, Moses, son of Imran, peace be upon him. For this reason, He said, Perhaps they will give thought, meaning that they would beware of being like him, for God had given them knowledge. And He distinguished them from the rest of the Arabs, and He placed in their hands the description of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, so that they would know it as they know their own sons. They are the people most deserving and most worthy of following him, supporting him, and backing him, as their prophets informed them of that and commanded them to do. For this reason, whoever among them disobeys what is in His Book and conceals it so that the servants do not know about it, God will make humiliation in this world connected to humiliation in the Hereafter. And His statement, Evil is the example of the people who deny Our signs, God Almighty says, Evil is the example of the people who deny Our signs, meaning, evil is their example that they are likened to dogs that have no concern except to obtain a meal or a desire. So whoever goes beyond the realm of knowledge and guidance and turns to his own desires and follows his whims becomes like a dog, and what an evil example he is. For this reason, it is established in the Sahih that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, We do not have a bad example, the one who takes back his gift is like a dog that returns to his vomit. And His statement, And they were wronging themselves, meaning, God did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves by turning away from following guidance and obeying their Master, and instead inclining to the abode of decay, and turning to obtaining pleasures and complying with whims.
