A hadith was narrated in the meaning of this verse by Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la Al-Mawsili in his Musnad, where he said: Muhammad bin Marzouq narrated to us Muhammad bin Bakr on the authority of Al-Salt bin Bahram, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Jundub Al-Bajali in this mosque that Hudhayfah, meaning Ibn Al-Yaman, may God be pleased with him, narrated to him that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Among the things I fear for you is a man who recites the Qur’an until its brilliance is seen upon him and his cloak is Islam, which of them wills to be removed and cast behind his back, and attack his neighbor with the sword and accuse him of polytheism.” I said: O Prophet of God, which of the two is more deserving of polytheism, the one who is accused or the one who is accused? He said: Rather, the one who is accused. The chain of transmission is good. Al-Salt bin Bahram was one of the trustworthy people of Kufa and he was not accused of anything except Irja’. Imam Ahmad bin Hanbal, Yahya bin Ma’in, and others authenticated him. And the Almighty said: And if We willed, We could have elevated him thereby, but he clung to the earth and followed his own desire. The Almighty says: And if We willed, We could have elevated him thereby, meaning, We could have elevated him from the defilement of the filth of this world with the signs that We gave him, but he clung to the earth, meaning, he inclined toward the adornments and adornments of this worldly life and turned to its pleasures and delights, and it deceived him as it deceived others who were not people of insight and reason. Abu al-Rahawayh said about the Almighty’s statement: but he clung to the earth, he said: Satan appeared to him on a high place on the Baniyas Bridge, so the donkey prostrated to God and Balaam prostrated to Satan. And Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr and others said the same. Imam Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him, said: And from the story of this man was what Muhammad ibn Abd al-A`la told us, al-Mu`tamir told us on the authority of his father that he was asked about this verse: And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs, so he narrated on the authority of Sayyar that there was a man called Balaam and his prayers were answered. He said: And Moses came with the Children of Israel, wanting the land that In it was Balaam, or he said: Ash-Sham. He said: The people were terrified of him with great fear, so they came to Balaam and said: Pray to God against this man and his army. He said: Until I command my Lord, or until I am commanded. He said: So command to pray against them. It was said to him: Do not pray against them, for they are My servants and among them is their prophet. He said: So he said to his al-Nas 114:I have commanded my Lord to pray against them, and I have forbidden them. So they gave him a gift and he accepted it. Then they returned to him and said: Pray against them. He said: Until I command my Lord. So he commanded, but he did not command him to do anything. He said: I have been commanded, but he did not command me to do anything. They said: If your Lord had hated that you pray against them, He would have forbidden you as He forbade you the first time. He said: So he began to pray against them, and when he prayed against them, the prayer against his people came from his tongue, and when he wanted to pray for his people to be granted victory, he prayed for Moses and his army to be granted victory, or something like that, God willing. He said: So they said: We do not see you praying except against us. He said: It only comes from my tongue like this, and if I prayed against him also, I would not be answered, but I will guide you to a matter. Perhaps it will be their destruction. Indeed, God hates adultery, and if they commit adultery, they will perish. I hoped that God would destroy them, so they brought out the women to meet them, for they are a people traveling, so perhaps they will commit adultery and perish. He said: So they did, and they brought out the women to meet them. He said: The king had a daughter, and he mentioned her greatness, which God knows best. He said: Her father or Balaam said: Do not let me have power over anyone except Moses. He said: And they committed adultery. He said: Then the head of one of the tribes of the Children of Israel came to her and wanted to have sex with her, but she said: I will not have power over anyone except Moses: a man from the sons of Aaron, and he had a spear with him, so he thrust them. He said: And God supported him with strength, so he strung them together and raised them on his spear, and the people saw them - or something like that - He said: And God sent a plague upon them, and seventy thousand of them died. Abu Al-Mu'tamir said: Sayyar told me that Balaam rode his donkey until he reached Al-Ululi, or he said a road from Al-Ululi. He started hitting it but it would not move forward. It stood up to him and said: Why are you hitting me? Don't you see what is in front of you? Then Satan was before him. He said: So he descended and prostrated to him. God Almighty said: “And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he slipped out of them. So Satan pursued him, and he was among the deviators. And if We had willed, We could have elevated him thereby, but he clung to the earth and followed his own desire. So his example is that of the dog: if you chase him, he pants, or if you leave him, he pants. That is the example of the people who deny Our signs. So relate the story that perhaps they will give thought.” He said: So Sayyar told me this, and I do not know, perhaps something from someone else’s hadith has entered into it. I said He is Balaam, and it is said Balaam bin Ba’oura, and it is said Ibn Aber, and it is said Ibn Ba’our bin Shahtum bin Qushtum bin Mab bin Lot bin Haran, and it is said Ibn Haran bin Azar, and he lived in a village in Balqa. Ibn Asakir said: He is the one who knew the greatest name of God, but he slipped out of his religion. He is mentioned in the Qur’an. Then he mentioned from his story something similar to what we mentioned here, he mentioned it from Wahb and others, and God knows best. Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Sayyar said: On the authority of Salim Abu Al-Nadr, that he narrated that when Moses, peace be upon him, descended to the land of the Canaanites in the land of Ash-Sham, the people of Balaam came to him and said to him: This is Moses bin Imran among the Children of Israel. He has come to expel us from our country and kill us and make it the Children of Israel. We are your people and we have no home, and you are a man whose supplications are answered, so go out and supplicate to God against them. He said: Woe to you, the Prophet of God has with him the angels and the believers. How can I go and supplicate against them while I know from God what I know? They said to him: We have no home. So they kept on beseeching him and supplicating him until they tempted him, so he was tempted and rode his donkey towards the mountain that overlooked the army of the Children of Israel, which was Mount Hisban. After he had walked on it for some time, it lay down with him, so he got off it and hit it until he made it slip, then it stood up and he mounted it. It did not walk with him for long until it lay down with him and he hit it until he made it slip, so he gave it permission, so it spoke to him as an argument against him and said: Woe to you, Balaam, where are you going? Do you not see the angels in front of me preventing me from this path of mine? She went to the Prophet of God and the believers to pray against them, but he did not stop hitting her, so God let her go when he did that to her. She went with him until she brought him to the top of Hisban, over the army of Moses and the Children of Israel. He began to pray against them, and he did not pray against them for evil except that God turned his tongue to his people, and he did not pray for his people for good except that he turned his tongue to the Children of Israel. His people said to him: Do you know, O Balaam, what you are doing? He said: This is something I do not own, this is something that God has overcome. He said: His tongue stuck out and fell on his chest and he said to them: Now the world and the hereafter have gone from me and nothing remains but deceit and trickery, so I will deceive and scheme for you. Beautify the women and give them goods, then send them to the camp to sell them there and order them that no woman should withhold herself from a man who wants her, for if one man among them commits adultery, you will be spared them. So they did. When the women entered the camp, a Canaanite woman named Kasbi - the daughter of Tyre, the head of his nation - passed by a man from the leaders of the Children of Israel, who was Zimri, the son of Shallum, the head of the tribe of Simeon, the son of Jacob, the son of Isaac, the son of Abraham, peace be upon him. When he saw her, he was pleased, so he stood up, took her by the hand, and brought her to Moses and said: I think you will say this is forbidden to you? He said: Yes, it is forbidden to you, do not come near her. He said: By God, I will not obey you in this. So he entered his tent with her and fell upon her. God Almighty sent the plague upon the Children of Israel. Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron, was the one in charge of Moses and was absent when Zimri, son of Shallum, did what he did. He came while the plague was raging among them and reported the report. He took his spear, which was all iron. Then he entered the tent while they were lying down and strung them together with his spear. Then he went out with them, raising them to the sky, holding the spear in his arm and leaning his elbow on his waist and resting the spear on his jaw. He was the firstborn of Eleazar. He kept saying: O God, this is how we deal with those who disobey you and lift the plague. So he calculated how many of the Children of Israel had perished in the plague between the time Zimri struck the woman and Phinehas killed him. They found that seventy thousand of them had perished, and the one who underestimated them said twenty thousand in one hour of the day. From there, the Children of Israel would give Phinehas’ son from every sacrifice they had slaughtered the neck, the arm, the jaw, and the firstborn from all their wealth. And the same because he was the firstborn of his father, Eleazar. So regarding Balaam bin Ba’oura, God revealed: “And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he slipped out of them, so Satan pursued him, and he was among the deviators. And if We had willed, We could have elevated him thereby, but he clung to the earth and followed his own desire. So his example is like that of a dog: if you attack him, he pants, or if you leave him, he pants. That is the example of the people who deny Our signs. So relate the story that perhaps they will give thought.” And the Almighty’s saying: “So his example is like that of a dog: if you attack him, he pants, or if you leave him, he pants.” The commentators differed in its meaning. According to the context of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Abu al-Nadr, that Balaam’s tongue stuck out on his chest, so his likeness to a dog in its panting in both its states, whether it is rebuked or left alone, is apparent. And it was said that its meaning is that he became like him in his misguidance and his persistence in it and his lack of benefit to faith and lack of supplication like a dog in its panting in both its states: if you attack him or leave him, he pants in both states, so likewise this one does not benefit. By preaching and calling to faith or not, as God Almighty said: It is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them - they will not believe. “Ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them. If you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, God will not forgive them.” and the like. It was said that its meaning is that the heart of the disbeliever, hypocrite, and misguided person is weak and empty of guidance, so he is often obliged. This was expressed in this way, something similar was transmitted from Al-Hasan Al-Basri and others. God Almighty’s statement: So relate the stories that perhaps they will give thought. God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, So relate the stories that perhaps they meaning perhaps the Children of Israel who knew the state of Balaam and what happened to him in God’s misguidance and distancing him from His mercy, because he used God’s blessing upon him in teaching him the Greatest Name, which if he was asked by it, he would give, and if he was called by it, he would answer, in disobedience to his Lord. Rather, he called by it upon the party of the Most Merciful and the people of faith, the followers of His servant and Messenger at that time, the one who spoke to God, Moses, son of Imran, peace be upon him. For this reason, He said, Perhaps they will give thought, meaning that they would beware of being like him, for God had given them knowledge. And He distinguished them from the rest of the Arabs, and He placed in their hands the description of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, so that they would know it as they know their own sons. They are the people most deserving and most worthy of following him, supporting him, and backing him, as their prophets informed them of that and commanded them to do. For this reason, whoever among them disobeys what is in His Book and conceals it so that the servants do not know about it, God will make humiliation in this world connected to humiliation in the Hereafter. And His statement, Evil is the example of the people who deny Our signs, God Almighty says, Evil is the example of the people who deny Our signs, meaning, evil is their example that they are likened to dogs that have no concern except to obtain a meal or a desire. So whoever goes beyond the realm of knowledge and guidance and turns to his own desires and follows his whims becomes like a dog, and what an evil example he is. For this reason, it is established in the Sahih that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, We do not have a bad example, the one who takes back his gift is like a dog that returns to his vomit. And His statement, And they were wronging themselves, meaning, God did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves by turning away from following guidance and obeying their Master, and instead inclining to the abode of decay, and turning to obtaining pleasures and complying with whims.
7:177: Abdul Razzaq said: On the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri, on the authority of al-A'mash and Mansur, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may God be pleased with him, regarding the words of God Almighty: And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he slipped out of them the verse, he said: He is a man from the Children of Israel called Balaam ibn Ba'oura. Shu'bah and others narrated it in this way on the authority of Mansur. Sa'id ibn Abi 'Aruba said on the authority of Qatada on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He is Saifi ibn al-Rahib. Qatada said: Ka'b said: He was a man from the people of Balqa' and he knew the Greatest Name and he was residing in Jerusalem with the tyrants. Al-A'wfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him: He is a man from the people of Yemen called Balaam. God gave him His signs, but he abandoned them. Malik ibn Dinar said: He was one of the scholars of the Children of Israel and his prayers were answered. They would put him forward in times of hardship. The Prophet of God, Moses, peace be upon him, sent him to the king of Madyan to call him to God, so he gave him a land and gave him, so he followed his religion and abandoned the religion of Moses, peace be upon him. Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said on the authority of Hisayn on the authority of Imran ibn Al-Harith on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He is Balaam bin Ba’oura, and this is what Mujahid and Ikrimah said. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Harith told me, Abdul Aziz told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: He is Balaam. Thaqeef said: He is Umayyah bin Abi Al-Salt. Shu’bah said on the authority of Ya’la bin Ata’ on the authority of Nafi’ bin Asim on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, regarding His statement, And recite to them the report of him to whom We gave Our signs 1:13, the verse, he said: He is your companion Umayyah bin Abi Al-Salt. It has been narrated from other sources on his authority, and it is authentically attributed to him. It seems that he only meant that Umayyah bin Abi Al-Salt resembled him, for he had attained much knowledge of the knowledge of the previous laws, but he did not benefit from his knowledge, for he lived during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his signs, signs, and miracles reached him, and they were apparent to everyone who had insight. Despite this, he met with him and did not follow him, and he turned to befriending, supporting, and praising the polytheists. He mourned the polytheists who fought at Badr with an eloquent elegy. May God curse him. It was mentioned in some hadiths that he who believed in his tongue but did not believe in his heart, has divine poetry, wisdom and eloquence, but God did not open his chest to Islam. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ibn Abi Namir told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Awar, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he slipped out of them, he said: He is a man who was given three supplications that were answered for him, and he had a wife with whom he had a child. She said, Give me one of them. He said, “You have one. What do you want?” She said, Pray to God to make me the most beautiful woman among the Children of Israel. So he prayed to God, and He made her the most beautiful woman among the Children of Israel. When she knew that there was no one like her among them, she turned away from him and wanted something else. So he prayed to God to make her a dog, and she became a dog. Then two prayers were made. Then her sons came and said, “We cannot stay here. Our mother has become a dog that people will taunt us with. So pray to God to return her to the state she was in.” So he prayed to God, and she returned to what she was, and the three prayers were made. She was called Al-Basoos. Strange. As for the well-known reason for the revelation of this noble verse, it is a man from the early generations in the time of the Children of Israel, as Ibn Masoud and others of the Salaf said. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He is a man from the city of the tyrants called Balaam, and he knew the greatest name of God. Abd al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam and others of the scholars of the Salaf said: His prayers were answered, and he did not ask God for anything except that He gave it to him. Stranger, even more distant, even mistaken is he who said: He had been given prophethood and then stripped himself of it. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of some of them, and it is not correct. Ali bin Abi Talha on the authority of Ibn Abbas: When Moses descended upon them, meaning the tyrants and those with him, his cousins and people came to him - meaning Balaam - and said: Moses is a man of iron and has many soldiers, and if he prevails over us he will destroy us, so pray to God to turn Moses and those with him away from us. He said: If I pray to God to turn Moses and those with him away, my world and my afterlife will be lost. So they kept on at him until he prayed against them, and God stripped him of what he was wearing. This is what God Almighty said: So he slipped away from it, and Satan pursued him 1:10. Al-Suddi said: When the forty years had passed, of which God said, It is forbidden to them for forty years, He sent Joshua bin Nun as a prophet. He called the Children of Israel and informed them that he was a prophet and that God had commanded him to fight the tyrants, so they pledged allegiance to him and believed him. A man from the Children of Israel called Balaam set out, and he was a scholar who knew the Greatest Hidden Name. He disbelieved, may God curse him, and went to the tyrants and said to them: Do not terrorize the Children of Israel, for if you go out to fight them, I will call down a curse upon them and they will perish. He had whatever he wanted of this worldly life with them, except that he was unable to approach women because of their great size, so he would marry a female donkey of his, and this is what God Almighty said: So he slipped out of her. God Almighty said: So Satan pursued him, meaning he took control of him and his affairs, so whatever he commanded him, he complied and obeyed. For this reason, He said: So he was among the astray, meaning among the perished, confused, and lost. A hadith was narrated in the meaning of this verse by Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la Al-Mawsili in his Musnad, where he said: Muhammad bin Marzouq narrated to us Muhammad bin Bakr on the authority of Al-Salt bin Bahram, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Jundub Al-Bajali in this mosque that Hudhayfah, meaning Ibn Al-Yaman, may God be pleased with him, narrated to him that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Among the things I fear for you is a man who recites the Qur’an until its brilliance is seen upon him and his cloak is Islam, which of them wills to be removed and cast behind his back, and attack his neighbor with the sword and accuse him of polytheism.” I said: O Prophet of God, which of the two is more deserving of polytheism, the one who is accused or the one who is accused? He said: Rather, the one who is accused. The chain of transmission is good. Al-Salt bin Bahram was one of the trustworthy people of Kufa and he was not accused of anything except Irja’. Imam Ahmad bin Hanbal, Yahya bin Ma’in, and others authenticated him. And the Almighty said: And if We willed, We could have elevated him thereby, but he clung to the earth and followed his own desire. The Almighty says: And if We willed, We could have elevated him thereby, meaning, We could have elevated him from the defilement of the filth of this world with the signs that We gave him, but he clung to the earth, meaning, he inclined toward the adornments and adornments of this worldly life and turned to its pleasures and delights, and it deceived him as it deceived others who were not people of insight and reason. Abu al-Rahawayh said about the Almighty’s statement: but he clung to the earth, he said: Satan appeared to him on a high place on the Baniyas Bridge, so the donkey prostrated to God and Balaam prostrated to Satan. And Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr and others said the same. Imam Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him, said: And from the story of this man was what Muhammad ibn Abd al-A`la told us, al-Mu`tamir told us on the authority of his father that he was asked about this verse: And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs, so he narrated on the authority of Sayyar that there was a man called Balaam and his prayers were answered. He said: And Moses came with the Children of Israel, wanting the land that In it was Balaam, or he said: Ash-Sham. He said: The people were terrified of him with great fear, so they came to Balaam and said: Pray to God against this man and his army. He said: Until I command my Lord, or until I am commanded. He said: So command to pray against them. It was said to him: Do not pray against them, for they are My servants and among them is their prophet. He said: So he said to his al-Nas 114:I have commanded my Lord to pray against them, and I have forbidden them. So they gave him a gift and he accepted it. Then they returned to him and said: Pray against them. He said: Until I command my Lord. So he commanded, but he did not command him to do anything. He said: I have been commanded, but he did not command me to do anything. They said: If your Lord had hated that you pray against them, He would have forbidden you as He forbade you the first time. He said: So he began to pray against them, and when he prayed against them, the prayer against his people came from his tongue, and when he wanted to pray for his people to be granted victory, he prayed for Moses and his army to be granted victory, or something like that, God willing. He said: So they said: We do not see you praying except against us. He said: It only comes from my tongue like this, and if I prayed against him also, I would not be answered, but I will guide you to a matter. Perhaps it will be their destruction. Indeed, God hates adultery, and if they commit adultery, they will perish. I hoped that God would destroy them, so they brought out the women to meet them, for they are a people traveling, so perhaps they will commit adultery and perish. He said: So they did, and they brought out the women to meet them. He said: The king had a daughter, and he mentioned her greatness, which God knows best. He said: Her father or Balaam said: Do not let me have power over anyone except Moses. He said: And they committed adultery. He said: Then the head of one of the tribes of the Children of Israel came to her and wanted to have sex with her, but she said: I will not have power over anyone except Moses: a man from the sons of Aaron, and he had a spear with him, so he thrust them. He said: And God supported him with strength, so he strung them together and raised them on his spear, and the people saw them - or something like that - He said: And God sent a plague upon them, and seventy thousand of them died. Abu Al-Mu'tamir said: Sayyar told me that Balaam rode his donkey until he reached Al-Ululi, or he said a road from Al-Ululi. He started hitting it but it would not move forward. It stood up to him and said: Why are you hitting me? Don't you see what is in front of you? Then Satan was before him. He said: So he descended and prostrated to him. God Almighty said: “And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he slipped out of them. So Satan pursued him, and he was among the deviators. And if We had willed, We could have elevated him thereby, but he clung to the earth and followed his own desire. So his example is that of the dog: if you chase him, he pants, or if you leave him, he pants. That is the example of the people who deny Our signs. So relate the story that perhaps they will give thought.” He said: So Sayyar told me this, and I do not know, perhaps something from someone else’s hadith has entered into it. I said He is Balaam, and it is said Balaam bin Ba’oura, and it is said Ibn Aber, and it is said Ibn Ba’our bin Shahtum bin Qushtum bin Mab bin Lot bin Haran, and it is said Ibn Haran bin Azar, and he lived in a village in Balqa.
