Then he mentioned from his story something similar to what we mentioned here, he mentioned it from Wahb and others, and God knows best. Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Sayyar said: On the authority of Salim Abu Al-Nadr, that he narrated that when Moses, peace be upon him, descended to the land of the Canaanites in the land of Ash-Sham, the people of Balaam came to him and said to him: This is Moses bin Imran among the Children of Israel. He has come to expel us from our country and kill us and make it the Children of Israel. We are your people and we have no home, and you are a man whose supplications are answered, so go out and supplicate to God against them. He said: Woe to you, the Prophet of God has with him the angels and the believers. How can I go and supplicate against them while I know from God what I know? They said to him: We have no home. So they kept on beseeching him and supplicating him until they tempted him, so he was tempted and rode his donkey towards the mountain that overlooked the army of the Children of Israel, which was Mount Hisban. After he had walked on it for some time, it lay down with him, so he got off it and hit it until he made it slip, then it stood up and he mounted it. It did not walk with him for long until it lay down with him and he hit it until he made it slip, so he gave it permission, so it spoke to him as an argument against him and said: Woe to you, Balaam, where are you going? Do you not see the angels in front of me preventing me from this path of mine? She went to the Prophet of God and the believers to pray against them, but he did not stop hitting her, so God let her go when he did that to her. She went with him until she brought him to the top of Hisban, over the army of Moses and the Children of Israel. He began to pray against them, and he did not pray against them for evil except that God turned his tongue to his people, and he did not pray for his people for good except that he turned his tongue to the Children of Israel. His people said to him: Do you know, O Balaam, what you are doing? He said: This is something I do not own, this is something that God has overcome. He said: His tongue stuck out and fell on his chest and he said to them: Now the world and the hereafter have gone from me and nothing remains but deceit and trickery, so I will deceive and scheme for you. Beautify the women and give them goods, then send them to the camp to sell them there and order them that no woman should withhold herself from a man who wants her, for if one man among them commits adultery, you will be spared them. So they did. When the women entered the camp, a Canaanite woman named Kasbi - the daughter of Tyre, the head of his nation - passed by a man from the leaders of the Children of Israel, who was Zimri, the son of Shallum, the head of the tribe of Simeon, the son of Jacob, the son of Isaac, the son of Abraham, peace be upon him. When he saw her, he was pleased, so he stood up, took her by the hand, and brought her to Moses and said: I think you will say this is forbidden to you? He said: Yes, it is forbidden to you, do not come near her. He said: By God, I will not obey you in this. So he entered his tent with her and fell upon her. God Almighty sent the plague upon the Children of Israel. Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron, was the one in charge of Moses and was absent when Zimri, son of Shallum, did what he did. He came while the plague was raging among them and reported the report. He took his spear, which was all iron. Then he entered the tent while they were lying down and strung them together with his spear. Then he went out with them, raising them to the sky, holding the spear in his arm and leaning his elbow on his waist and resting the spear on his jaw. He was the firstborn of Eleazar. He kept saying: O God, this is how we deal with those who disobey you and lift the plague. So he calculated how many of the Children of Israel had perished in the plague between the time Zimri struck the woman and Phinehas killed him. They found that seventy thousand of them had perished, and the one who underestimated them said twenty thousand in one hour of the day. From there, the Children of Israel would give Phinehas’ son from every sacrifice they had slaughtered the neck, the arm, the jaw, and the firstborn from all their wealth. And the same because he was the firstborn of his father, Eleazar. So regarding Balaam bin Ba’oura, God revealed: “And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he slipped out of them, so Satan pursued him, and he was among the deviators. And if We had willed, We could have elevated him thereby, but he clung to the earth and followed his own desire. So his example is like that of a dog: if you attack him, he pants, or if you leave him, he pants. That is the example of the people who deny Our signs. So relate the story that perhaps they will give thought.” And the Almighty’s saying: “So his example is like that of a dog: if you attack him, he pants, or if you leave him, he pants.” The commentators differed in its meaning. According to the context of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Abu al-Nadr, that Balaam’s tongue stuck out on his chest, so his likeness to a dog in its panting in both its states, whether it is rebuked or left alone, is apparent. And it was said that its meaning is that he became like him in his misguidance and his persistence in it and his lack of benefit to faith and lack of supplication like a dog in its panting in both its states: if you attack him or leave him, he pants in both states, so likewise this one does not benefit. By preaching and calling to faith or not, as God Almighty said: It is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them - they will not believe. “Ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them. If you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, God will not forgive them.” and the like. It was said that its meaning is that the heart of the disbeliever, hypocrite, and misguided person is weak and empty of guidance, so he is often obliged. This was expressed in this way, something similar was transmitted from Al-Hasan Al-Basri and others. God Almighty’s statement: So relate the stories that perhaps they will give thought. God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, So relate the stories that perhaps they meaning perhaps the Children of Israel who knew the state of Balaam and what happened to him in God’s misguidance and distancing him from His mercy, because he used God’s blessing upon him in teaching him the Greatest Name, which if he was asked by it, he would give, and if he was called by it, he would answer, in disobedience to his Lord. Rather, he called by it upon the party of the Most Merciful and the people of faith, the followers of His servant and Messenger at that time, the one who spoke to God, Moses, son of Imran, peace be upon him. For this reason, He said, Perhaps they will give thought, meaning that they would beware of being like him, for God had given them knowledge. And He distinguished them from the rest of the Arabs, and He placed in their hands the description of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, so that they would know it as they know their own sons. They are the people most deserving and most worthy of following him, supporting him, and backing him, as their prophets informed them of that and commanded them to do. For this reason, whoever among them disobeys what is in His Book and conceals it so that the servants do not know about it, God will make humiliation in this world connected to humiliation in the Hereafter. And His statement, Evil is the example of the people who deny Our signs, God Almighty says, Evil is the example of the people who deny Our signs, meaning, evil is their example that they are likened to dogs that have no concern except to obtain a meal or a desire. So whoever goes beyond the realm of knowledge and guidance and turns to his own desires and follows his whims becomes like a dog, and what an evil example he is. For this reason, it is established in the Sahih that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, We do not have a bad example, the one who takes back his gift is like a dog that returns to his vomit. And His statement, And they were wronging themselves, meaning, God did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves by turning away from following guidance and obeying their Master, and instead inclining to the abode of decay, and turning to obtaining pleasures and complying with whims.
7:178: God Almighty says: Whoever God guides, none can misguide him, and whoever He misguides, he has certainly failed, lost, and gone astray. For God Almighty, whatever He wills will happen, and whatever He does not will will not happen. For this reason, it was stated in the hadith of Ibn Masoud: “Indeed, all praise is due to God. We praise Him, seek His aid, ask for His guidance, and ask His forgiveness. We seek refuge in God from the evils of our souls and the badness of our deeds. Whoever God guides, none can misguide him, and whoever God misguides, none can guide him. I bear witness that there is no god but God alone, without partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger.” The hadith in its entirety was narrated by Imam Ahmad, the scholars of Sunan, and others.
7:179: God Almighty says: And We have certainly created for Hell meaning We created and made for Hell many of the jinn and mankind meaning We prepared them for it and the deeds of its people they will do, for when God Almighty wanted to create the creation He knew what they would do before they came into being, so He wrote that down with Him in a book fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth, as was reported in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God determined the measures of creation fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth, and His Throne was over the water. In Sahih Muslim also: From the hadith of Aisha bint Talha, from her aunt Aisha, the Mother of the Believers, may God be pleased with her, that she said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was invited to the funeral of a boy from the Ansar, so I said: O Messenger of God, blessed is he, a bird from the birds of Paradise, he did not do evil nor did he reach it, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Or something else, O Aisha, God created Paradise and created its people while they were in the loins of their fathers, and He created Hell and created its people while they were in the loins of their fathers.” And in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Ibn Masoud: Then God sends an angel to him and he is commanded with four words, and he writes down his provision, his life span, his deeds, and whether he will be wretched or happy. And it was mentioned that when God extracted the descendants of Adam from his loins and made them into two groups, the people of the right and the people of the left, He said: These are for Paradise and I do not care, and these are for Hell and I do not care. And the hadiths on this are many, and the issue of destiny is great, and this is not the place to elaborate on it. And the Almighty’s saying: They have hearts with which they do not understand, and they have eyes with which they do not see, and they have ears with which they do not hear means not… They benefit from some of these organs that God made a cause of guidance, as God Almighty said: And We gave them hearing and sight and hearts, but their hearing and sight and hearts availed them nothing when they denied the signs of God verse, and God Almighty said: Deaf, dumb, and blind, so they will not return verse regarding the hypocrites. And He said about the disbelievers, Deaf, dumb, and blind, so they do not understand. They were not deaf, dumb, or blind except to guidance, as God Almighty said, “And if God had known any good in them, He would have made them hear. And if He had made them hear, they would have turned away while they were averse.” And He said, For indeed, it is not the eyes that are blind, but blind are the hearts which are within the breasts. And He said, “And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful - We appoint for him a devil, and he is to him a companion. And indeed, they avert them from the way, while they think that they are guided.” And God Almighty said, Those are like livestock, meaning those who do not hear the truth, nor understand it, nor see guidance, like the grazing livestock that do not benefit from these senses except in what sustains them in the outward appearance of worldly life, as God Almighty said, And the example of those who disbelieve is like the example of one who calls to that which hears nothing but a call and a cry. That is, their example when they are called to faith is like the example of livestock when their shepherd calls them, they do not hear anything but his voice, and do not understand what he says. And for this reason He said about these people, Rather, they are more astray, meaning than the animals, because they may respond to their shepherd if he becomes familiar with them, even if they do not understand his speech, unlike these people, and because they do what they were created for, either by their nature or by being subjugated, unlike the disbeliever, for he was only created to worship God and make Him One, so he disbelieved in God and associated others with Him. And for this reason, whoever obeys God from among the humans is more honorable than his like from the angels in his afterlife, and whoever disbelieves in Him from among the humans, the animals are more perfect than him. And for this reason, the Most High said, “Those are like livestock, rather, they are more astray. It is those who are the heedless.”
7:180: On the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "God has ninety-nine names, one hundred minus one. Whoever counts them will enter Paradise. He is odd and loves odd numbers." They included it in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Abu al-Zinad, on the authority of al-A'raj, on his authority. Al-Bukhari narrated it on the authority of Abu al-Yaman, on the authority of Shu'ayb, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Abu al-Zinad, on his authority. Al-Tirmidhi included it in his Jami', on the authority of al-Jawzjani, on the authority of Safwan ibn Salih, on the authority of al-Walid ibn Muslim, on the authority of Shu'ayb, and he mentioned with his chain of transmission something similar. He added after his statement: He loves odd numbers: He is God, other than whom there is no god, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, the King, the Holy, the Peace, the Faithful, the Guardian, the Almighty, the Compeller, the Majestic, the Creator, the Maker, the Fashioner, the Forgiving, the Subduer, the Giver, the Provider, the Opener, the Knowing, the Constrictor, the Expander, the Abaser, the Exalter, the Honorer, the Humiliator, the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing, the Judge, the Just, the Kind, the All-Aware, the Forbearing, the Great, the Forgiving, the Appreciative, the High, the Great, the Preserver, the Honorer, the Reckoner, the Majestic. The Generous, the Watchful, the Responsive, the Vast, the Wise, the Loving, the Glorious, the Resurrector, the True Witness, the Trustee, the Strong, the Firm, the Guardian, the Praiseworthy, the Counting, the Beginner, the Restorer, the Giver of Life, the Giver of Death, the Living, the Self-Sustaining, the Finder, the Glorious, the One, the Unique, the Eternal, the Able, the Powerful, the Forerunner, the Delayer, the First, the Last, the Manifest, the Hidden, the Guardian, the Most High, the Righteous, the Accepter of Repentance, the Avenger, the Forgiving, the Compassionate, the Owner of the Kingdom, the Possessor of Majesty and Honor, the Just, the Gatherer, the Rich, the Enricher, the Preventer, the Harmful, the Beneficial, the Light, the Guide, the Incomparable, the Eternal, the Inheritor, the Rightly Guided, the Patient.” Then Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a strange hadith, and it has been narrated from other sources on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, and we do not know in many of the narrations the mention of names except in this hadith, and Ibn Hibban narrated it in his Sahih on the authority of Safwan with it. Ibn Majah narrated it in his Sunan through another chain of transmission on the authority of Musa ibn Uqbah on the authority of Al-A’raj on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He listed the names in a manner similar to what was mentioned above, with additions and subtractions. What a group of hadith scholars relied on is that the listing of the names in this hadith is inserted into it. Rather, that is as Al-Walid ibn Muslim and Abd Al-Malik ibn Muhammad Al-San’ani narrated on the authority of Zuhair ibn Muhammad, that he heard from more than one of the people of knowledge that they said that, meaning that they collected them from the Qur’an. It was also narrated on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, and Abu Zayd Al-Lughawi, and God knows best. Then let him know that the beautiful names are not limited to ninety-nine, as evidenced by what Imam Ahmad narrated in his Musnad on the authority of Yazid bin Harun, on the authority of Fadil bin Marzuq, on the authority of Abu Salamah al-Juhani, on the authority of al-Qasim, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “No one has ever been afflicted with worry or sadness and said: O God, I am Your servant, the son of Your female servant, my forelock is in Your hand, Your command over me is carried out, and Your judgment over me is just. I ask You by every name that is Yours, with which You have named Yourself, or revealed in Your Book, or taught to any of Your creation, or kept to Yourself in the knowledge of the unseen with You, to make the Noble Qur’an the life of my heart, the light of my chest, the dispeller of my sadness, and the remover of my worry, except that God removes his sadness and worry and replaces it with joy.” It was said: O Messenger of God, should we not learn it? He said, Yes, everyone who hears it should learn it. Imam Abu Hatim ibn Hibban al-Busti included it in his Sahih with a similar wording. The jurist Imam Abu Bakr al-Arabi, one of the Imams of the Maliki school, mentioned in his book al-Ahwadhi in his commentary on al-Tirmidhi that some of them collected from the Qur’an and Sunnah a thousand names of God. And God knows best. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the words of God the Almighty: And leave those who blaspheme concerning His names, he said: The blasphemy of the blasphemer is that they invoke Al-Lat among the names of God. Ibn Jurayj said on the authority of Mujahid: And leave those who blaspheme concerning His names, he said: They derived Al-Lat from God, and Al-Uzza from Al-Aziz. Qatada said: They blaspheme and associate partners with God in His names. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Blasphemy is denial. The root of blasphemy in the speech of the Arabs is deviation from the intended path, inclination, injustice and deviation. From this comes the word lahd in the grave, because it deviates toward the direction of the qiblah from the direction of the grave.
7:181: God Almighty says: And among those We have created meaning some of the nations is a nation who uphold the truth in word and deed guiding with the truth they say it and call to it and doing justice thereby they act and judge. It has been reported in the narrations that what is meant by this nation mentioned in the verse is this Muhammadan nation. Saeed said on the authority of Qatada in his interpretation of this verse: It has reached me that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say when he recited this verse This is for you and the people before you have been given something similar “And among the people of Moses is a nation guiding with the truth and doing justice thereby.” Abu Ja`far al-Razi said on the authority of al-Rabi` ibn Anas regarding the words of God Almighty: And among those We have created is a nation who guide with the truth and do justice thereby, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Among my nation are people who are on the truth until Jesus, son of Mary, descends whenever he descends. And in the two Sahihs on the authority of Mu`awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A group of my nation will continue to be victorious upon the truth, and they will not be harmed by those who let them down or those who oppose them until the Hour comes. And in another narration: Until God’s command comes and they are still like that. And in another narration: And they are in Syria.
7:182: God the Almighty says: And those who deny Our signs - We will lead them on gradually from where they do not know. This means that He will open for them the doors of provision and ways of living in this world until they are deceived by what they are in and believe that they are on something, as God the Almighty says: "But when they forgot that by which they had been reminded, We opened to them the doors of every [good] thing until, when they rejoiced in what they had been given, We seized them suddenly, and at once they were in despair. So He cut off the last remnant of the people who did wrong. And praise be to God, Lord of the worlds." For this reason God the Almighty says: And I will grant them respite meaning I will grant them respite, meaning I will prolong what they are in, Indeed, My plan is firm meaning strong and severe.
7:183: God the Almighty says: And those who deny Our signs - We will lead them on gradually from where they do not know. This means that He will open for them the doors of provision and ways of living in this world until they are deceived by what they are in and believe that they are on something, as God the Almighty says: "But when they forgot that by which they had been reminded, We opened to them the doors of every [good] thing until, when they rejoiced in what they had been given, We seized them suddenly, and at once they were in despair. So He cut off the last remnant of the people who did wrong. And praise be to God, Lord of the worlds." For this reason God the Almighty says: And I will grant them respite meaning I will grant them respite, meaning I will prolong what they are in, Indeed, My plan is firm meaning strong and severe.
7:184: God the Almighty says: Have these disbelievers not considered "that their companion" meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, "is not mad meaning he is not mad, rather he is truly the Messenger of God, calling to the truth He is only a clear warner" meaning apparent to whoever has a mind and a heart that understands and comprehends, as God the Almighty says: "And your companion is not mad" and God the Almighty says: "Say, "I only admonish you of one thing: that you stand before God in pairs or individually and then reflect. There is no madness in your companion. He is only a warner to you before a severe punishment" He says: I only ask you to stand up sincerely for God, without fanaticism or stubbornness in pairs or individually meaning: together and separately, then reflect on this one who came to you with the message from God, whether he is mad or not, for if you do that, it will become clear to you and become apparent that he is truly and truthfully the Messenger of God. Qatada bin Di'amah said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was on Al-Safa and called the Quraysh, and he began to strike them thigh by thigh, saying, O sons of so-and-so, O sons of so-and-so, and he warned them of God’s punishment and the events of God. Then one of them said, This companion of yours is mad; he kept making noise until morning, or until morning. Then God Almighty revealed: “Have they not considered? There is no madness in their companion. He is only a clear warner.”
7:185: God the Almighty says: Have these deniers of Our signs not looked at God's dominion and authority in the heavens and the earth, and in what He has created in them, so that they may ponder that and take heed from it, and know that this is for the One who has no equal or likeness, and from the actions of the One for whom worship and pure religion should be only for Him, so that they may believe in Him and believe in His Messenger, and turn to His obedience, and renounce rivals and idols, and beware that their appointed times may have drawn near and they may perish in their disbelief and be subject to God's punishment and painful chastisement. And His statement, Then in what statement after this will they believe? means, then in what frightening, warning, and terror after the warning and terror of Muhammad, may God's prayers and peace be upon him, which he brought to them from God in the verses of His Book will they believe if they do not believe in this statement that Muhammad brought to them from God the Almighty? Imam Ahmad narrated: On the authority of Hasan bin Musa, Affan bin Muslim, and Abd al-Samad bin Abd al-Warith, all of them on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid bin Jadaan, on the authority of Abu al-Salt, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I saw such and such on the night of my ascension. When we reached the seventh heaven, I looked above me and saw thunder, lightning, and thunderbolts. I came upon a people whose stomachs were like houses, in which were snakes that could be seen from outside their stomachs. I said: Who are these, O Gabriel? He said: These are the usurers. When I descended to the lowest heaven and looked below me, I saw a thunderstorm, smoke, and sounds. I said: What is this, O Gabriel? He said: These are the devils hovering over the eyes of the children of Adam so that they do not contemplate the kingdom of the heavens and the earth. If it were not for that, they would have seen wonders.” Ali bin Zaid bin Jadaan has some strange sayings. Then God the Almighty said:
7:186: God Almighty says: Whoever is destined to go astray, no one will guide him, and if he looks at himself in what he looks at, it will not suffice him at all. And he whom God intends to test, you will not possess for him anything from God. And as God Almighty said: Say, ‘Look at what is in the heavens and the earth.’ But signs and warners do not avail a people who do not believe.
7:187: God Almighty says: They ask you about the Hour as God Almighty said: People ask you about the Hour It was said that it was revealed about the Quraysh, and it was said about a group of Jews, and the first is more likely because the verse was revealed in Mecca, and they were asking about the time of the Hour, ruling out its occurrence and denying its existence, as God Almighty said: And they say, 'When will this promise be, if you should be truthful?' And God Almighty said: "Those who do not believe in it urge it on, while those who believe are fearful of it and know that it is the truth. Unquestionably, those who dispute about the Hour are in extreme error." And His saying, When will it be anchored? Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Its end, meaning when will it be its final destination and when will be the last period of this world, which is the beginning of the time of the Hour. “Say, ‘The knowledge thereof is only with my Lord. None can reveal its time except Him.’” God Almighty commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he was asked about the time of the Hour, to refer its knowledge to God Almighty, for He is the One who will reveal its time, meaning He knows the details of its matter and when it will be, specifically. None knows that except He Almighty. For this reason He said, Its burden is heavy upon the heavens and the earth. Abd al-Razzaq said on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatadah regarding His saying, Its burden is heavy upon the heavens and the earth, he said: Its knowledge is heavy upon the people of the heavens and the earth because they do not know. Muammar said: Al-Hasan said: When it comes, it will be heavy upon the people of the heavens and the earth, meaning: it will be too great for them. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the words of God Almighty: It is heavy in the heavens and the earth, he said: There is nothing in creation that will not be affected by harm on the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Jurayj said: It is heavy in the heavens and the earth, he said: When it comes, the heaven will split and the stars will scatter, the sun will be rolled up, and the mountains will move, and what God Almighty said will happen, so that is its weight. Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him, chose that what is meant is the weight of knowledge of its time on the people of the heavens and the earth, as Qatadah said, and it is as they said, like the words of God Almighty: It will not come to you except suddenly, and that does not negate the weight of its coming on the people of the heavens and the earth, and God knows best. Al-Suddi said: It is heavy in the heavens and the earth meaning: It is hidden in the heavens and the earth, so no close angel or sent prophet knows when it will rise. It will not come to you except suddenly its rising will take them by surprise. Qatada said about the Almighty’s statement: It will not come to you except suddenly God has decreed that It will not come to you except suddenly He said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God used to say: The Hour will stir up people, while a man is fixing his cistern, a man is watering his livestock, a man is setting out his merchandise in the market, lowering his scales and raising them. Al-Bukhari said: Abu Al-Yaman told us, Shu`ayb told us, Abu Al-Zinad told us, on the authority of `Abd Al-Rahman, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The Hour will not come until the sun rises from the West. When it rises and the people see it, they will all believe. At that time, no soul will benefit from its faith if it did not believe before or earn any good through its faith. The Hour will come while two men have spread their garments between them, but they will neither buy it nor fold it. The Hour will come while a man has taken the milk of his she-camel away, but he will not eat it. The Hour will come while he is cleaning his trough, but he will not water it. The Hour will come while a man has raised his food to his mouth, but he will not eat it.” Muslim said in his Sahih: Zuhayr bin Harb told me, Sufyan bin `Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Zinad, on the authority of Al-A`raj, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, and he transmitted it, saying: The Hour will come while a man is milking his she-camel, but the vessel will not reach his mouth until the Hour comes. Two men are selling a garment, but they will not sell it until the Hour comes. A man... He rubs his basin and does not come out until you get up. And his saying, They ask you as if you were aware of it, the commentators differed about its meaning. It was said that its meaning is as Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, They ask you as if you were aware of it, meaning: As if there is affection between you and them, as if you were their friend. Ibn Abbas said: When the people asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the Hour, they asked him the question of people as if they thought that Muhammad was aware of them, so God revealed to him that its knowledge was with Him alone and He kept it to Himself, so God did not inform any close angel or messenger about it. Qatada said: Quraysh said to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: There is kinship between us and you, so confide in us, when is the Hour? God Almighty said: They ask you as if you were knowledgeable about it. This is also narrated on the authority of Mujahid, Ikrimah, Abu Malik, and As-Suddi. This is one statement, and the correct one is narrated on the authority of Mujahid from the narration of Ibn Abi Nujayh and others: They ask you as if you were knowledgeable about it. He said: You were knowledgeable about it until you knew its time. This is also what Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: They ask you as if you were knowledgeable about it. He said: As if you were knowledgeable about it, but you did not know it. “Say: Its knowledge is only with God.” Muammar said on the authority of some of them: As if you are aware of it as if you are knowledgeable about it. Abdurrahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said: As if you are aware of it as if you are knowledgeable about it, and God has hidden its knowledge from His creation, and he recited: Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour 1:13. This statement is more correct in this regard than the first, and God knows best. That is why He said: “Say: Its knowledge is only with God, but most people do not know.” That is why when Gabriel, peace be upon him, came in the form of a Bedouin to teach people about their religion, he sat with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the seat of a questioner seeking guidance. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked him about Islam, then about faith, then about ihsan, then he said: When is the Hour? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: The one asked about it does not know more than the one asking, meaning I do not know it more than you, and no one knows it more than anyone else. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour 1:13. In another narration, he asked him about the signs of the Hour, so he explained to him the signs of the Hour, then he said, In five that none knows but God, and he recited this verse, and in all of this he would say to him after every answer: You have spoken the truth, and for this reason the companions were amazed at this questioner asking him and believing him, then when he left, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, This is Gabriel, he came to you to teach you your religion, and in another narration he said, And he did not come to me in any form except that I recognized him in it except this form of his. I have mentioned this hadith with its chains of transmission and wording from the Sahihs, Hassans, and Musnads at the beginning of my commentary on Al-Bukhari, praise and thanks be to God. When that Bedouin asked him and called him in a loud voice, saying, O Muhammad, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him, Come here, in a voice similar to his own. He said, O Muhammad, when is the Hour? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him, Woe to you! The Hour is coming, but you have not prepared for it. He said, I have not prepared for it much prayer or fasting, but I love God and His Messenger. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him, A person will be with those he loves. The Muslims have never rejoiced at anything as much as they rejoiced at this hadith. This has many chains of transmission in the two Sahihs and elsewhere on the authority of a group of the Companions on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that he said, A person will be with those he loves. It is mutawatir among many of the memorizers of hadith who are proficient in hadith. It states that when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was asked about something that they did not need to know, he would guide them to what was most important for them, which was to prepare for it to happen and get ready for it before it came, even if they did not know when it would happen. For this reason, Muslim said in his Sahih: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Usamah narrated to us on the authority of Hisham on the authority of his father on the authority of Aisha may God be pleased with her, she said: When the Bedouins came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) they would ask him about the Hour: When will the Hour be? He would look at the youngest of them and say, If this young man lives, he will not be overtaken by old age until your Hour comes upon you, meaning by that their death which will lead them to the intermediate state of the Hereafter. Then Muslim said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah told us, Yunus ibn Muhammad told us, on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas, that a man asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the Hour, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, If this young man lives, perhaps old age will not overtake him until the Hour comes. This is narrated only by Muslim. Hajjaj bin Al-Sha’ir told me, Sulayman bin Harb told us, Hammad bin Zaid told us, Saeed bin Abi Hilal Al-Masry told us, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him, that a man asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saying: When will the Hour come? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was silent for a while, then he looked at a young boy from Azd Shanu’ah who was in front of him and said: This Umar will not reach old age until the Hour comes. Anas said: That boy is of my age. He said: Harun bin Abdullah told us, Affan bin Muslim told us, Hammam told us, Qatada told us, on the authority of Anas, who said: A young boy of Al-Mughirah bin Shu’bah passed by, and he was of my age. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If this one is delayed, old age will not reach him until the Hour comes. Al-Bukhari narrated it in the Book of Etiquette in his Sahih on the authority of Amr bin Asim, on the authority of Hammam bin Yahya, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas, that a man from the desert said: O Messenger of God, when is the Hour? He mentioned the hadith, and at the end of it: A young boy of Al-Mughira bin Shuba passed by and he mentioned him. This generality in these narrations is based on the restriction to your time in the hadith of Aisha, may God be pleased with her. Ibn Jurayj said: Abu al-Zubayr told me that he heard Jabir ibn Abdullah say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say a month before he died: “You ask me about the Hour, but its knowledge is with God alone. I swear by God that there is not a soul on the face of the earth today that will live to be a hundred years old.” Narrated by Muslim. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Ibn Umar, something similar is narrated. Ibn Umar said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, only meant the end of that century. Imam Ahmad said: Hisham told us, Al-Awam told us, on the authority of Jabalah bin Suhaim, on the authority of Muthir bin Afara, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “On the night of my Night Journey, I met Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, and they discussed the matter of the Hour. He said: They referred their matter to Abraham, peace be upon him, and he said: I have no knowledge of it. They referred their matter to Moses, and he said: I have no knowledge of it. They referred their matter to Jesus, and Jesus said: As for its occurrence, no one knows about it except God Almighty. And among what my Lord Almighty has entrusted to me is that the Antichrist will emerge. He said: And with me are two sticks, and when he sees me he will melt like lead. He said: Then God Almighty will destroy him when he sees me, until the trees and stones will say: O Muslim, there is an unbeliever beneath me, so come and kill him. He said: Then God Almighty will destroy them, and then the people will return to their lands and homelands. He said: Then at that time Gog and Magog will emerge, and they will swarm from every hill, and they will tread upon their lands, and they will not come upon anything except that they will destroy it, and They do not pass by any water without drinking it. He said: Then the people come back to me and complain about them, so I call upon God Almighty against them, so He destroys them and makes them die until the earth becomes filthy with the stench of their stench, meaning it stinks. He said: Then God Almighty sends down rain and sweeps away their bodies until He throws them into the sea. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid bin Harun said: Then the mountains will be blown away and the earth will be stretched out like a hide. Then he returned to the hadith of Hisham, saying: In what my Lord, the Almighty, has entrusted to me, if that is the case, then the Hour will be like a pregnant woman whose people do not know when she will surprise them with her birth, at night or during the day. Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Bandar on the authority of Yazid bin Harun on the authority of Al-Awam bin Hawshab with his chain of transmission similarly. These are the greatest of the resolute messengers who do not have knowledge of the exact time of the Hour. Rather, they referred the matter to Jesus, peace be upon him, so he spoke about its signs because he will descend at the end of this nation, implementing the rulings of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he will kill the Antichrist, and God will cause the destruction of Gog and Magog by the blessing of his supplication. So he informed him of what God, the Almighty, informed him of. Imam Ahmad said: Yahya bin Abi Bakr told us, Ubayd bin Iyad bin Laqeet told us, he said: I heard my father mention on the authority of Hudhayfah who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about the Hour, and he said: “Its knowledge is with my Lord, the Almighty and Majestic. None can reveal its time except Him. But I will inform you of its signs and what will be before it. Before it, there will be tribulation and chaos.” They said: O Messenger of God, we know about the tribulation, but what is the chaos? He said: In the language of the Abyssinians, it means killing. He said: And there will be discord among the people, and hardly anyone will recognize anyone. None of the authors of the six books narrated it from this source. And Wakee’ said: Ibn Abi Khalid told us on the authority of Tariq bin Shihab who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, kept mentioning the matter of the Hour until the verse was revealed: “They ask you about the Hour: when is its appointed time?” And Al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Isa bin Yunus on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid with it, and this is a good and strong chain of transmission. So this unlettered Prophet, the master of the Messengers and their Seal, Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is the Prophet of Mercy, the Prophet of Repentance, the Prophet of the Epic, the Last, the One Who Follows, and the Gatherer at whose feet the people will be gathered, with his saying in what is proven from him in the Sahih from the hadith of Anas and Sahl bin Sa’d, may God be pleased with them both, I and the Hour were sent like these two, and he joined his index finger and the one next to it. And with all of this, God commanded him to refer the knowledge of the time of the Hour to Himself if he was asked about it, so He said: “Say: Its knowledge is only with God, but most people do not know.”
7:188: God the Almighty commanded him to entrust matters to Him, and to inform about himself that he does not know the future unseen and has no knowledge of any of that except what God has informed him of, as God the Almighty said: He is the Knower of the unseen, and He reveals His unseen to none (al-An`am 2:10). And His statement, And if I knew the unseen, I would have increased in goodness, Abd al-Razzaq said on the authority of al-Thawri on the authority of Mansur on the authority of Mujahid, And if I knew the unseen, I would have increased in goodness, he said: If I knew when I would die, I would have done a righteous deed. Ibn Abi Nujayh narrated the same on the authority of Mujahid, and Ibn Jurayj said the same, and there is a view in it because the work of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was continuous, and in another narration: If he did a deed, he would have recorded it, so all of his work was on the same pattern as if he was looking to God the Almighty in all his circumstances, unless what is meant is that he guides others to prepare for that, and God knows best. And the best in this is what al-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And if I knew the unseen, I would have increased in goodness, meaning money. In another narration: I would have known that if I bought something I would make a profit from it, so I would not sell anything without making a profit from it. And no harm has touched me and poverty has not befallen me. Ibn Jarir said: Others said: The meaning of this is that if I knew the unseen, I would have prepared for the barren year with a fertile one and for the time of high prices with cheap things, so I would have prepared for it with cheap things. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: And no harm has touched me means: I would have avoided what would be of evil before it happened and guarded against it. Then he informed that he is only a warner and a bringer of good tidings, meaning a warner of the punishment and a bringer of good tidings to the believers of Paradise, as God the Almighty said: We have only made it easy in your language that you may give good tidings thereby to the righteous and warn thereby a hostile people.
7:189: God the Almighty points out that He created all people from Adam, peace be upon him. And that He created from him his wife Eve, and then people spread out from them, as God the Almighty said: "O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of God is the most righteous of you." And God the Almighty said: O mankind, fear your Lord, who created you from one soul and created from it its mate 3:13, and He said in this noble verse: And made from it its mate that he might dwell in tranquility with her, meaning to be intimate with her and live with her, as God the Almighty said: And among His signs is that He created for you from yourselves mates that you may dwell in tranquility with them, and He put between you affection and mercy 3:13. There is no greater affection between two souls than that between spouses. For this reason God the Almighty mentioned that the magician may, through his trickery, reach a separation between a man and his wife. Then when he covers her 3:13, she bears a light burden 3:13. This is the beginning of pregnancy, and the woman does not feel pain from it. Rather, it is the sperm, then the clot, then the lump of flesh. And his saying, So she passed by him Mujahid said: She continued carrying him. Something similar was narrated from Al-Hasan, Ibrahim Al-Nakha'i and Al-Suddi. Maymun bin Mihran said from his father: She took him lightly. Ayoub said: I asked Al-Hasan about his saying, So she passed by him He said: If I were an Arab man, I would know what it is, it is only so she continued with him. Qatadah said: So she passed by him Her pregnancy became clear. Ibn Jarir said: Its meaning is she continued with the water, she stood and sat with it. Al-Awfi said from Ibn Abbas: She continued with him and then doubted whether she was pregnant or not? So when she became heavy meaning she became heavy with her pregnancy. Al-Suddi said: The child grew in her belly. They called upon God, their Lord, 'If You give us a righteous one' meaning a healthy human being, as Ad-Dahhak said from Ibn Abbas: They feared that he would be an animal. And Abu Al-Bukhtari and Abu Malik said the same: They feared that he would not be a human. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: If You give us a boy, we will surely be among the grateful. But when He gave them both a good son, they attributed to Him partners in what He had given them. So exalted is God above what they associate with Him.” The commentators mention here traces and hadiths that I will cite and explain what is in them, then we will follow that with explaining the correct hadith in that, God willing, and in Him is trustworthy. Imam Ahmad said in his Musnad: Abd Al-Samad told us: Umar bin Ibrahim told us, Qatadah told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Samurah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “When Eve gave birth, Satan circled around her, and she did not have a child who would live. He said: Name him Abd Al-Harith, for he will live. So she named him Abd Al-Harith, and he lived. That was from the inspiration and command of Satan.” And thus Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Muhammad bin Bashar on the authority of Bandar on the authority of Abd Al-Samad bin Abd Al-Warith on his authority, and Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in his interpretation of this verse on the authority of Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna on the authority of Abd Al-Samad on his authority, and he said: This is a good and strange hadith that we do not know except from the hadith of Umar bin Ibrahim, and some of them narrated it on the authority of Abd Al-Samad and he did not… He raised it, and Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak from the hadith of Abd Al-Samad, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, then he said: This hadith has a sound chain of transmission, and they did not include it. Imam Abu Muhammad bin Abi Hatim narrated it in his interpretation on the authority of Abu Zur’ah Al-Razi on the authority of Hilal bin Fayyad on the authority of Umar bin Ibrahim on his authority with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. And likewise, Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Ibn Mardawayh narrated it in his interpretation from the hadith of Shadh Ibn Fayyad from Umar Ibn Ibrahim, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. I said: Shadh is Hilal, and Shadh is his nickname. The point is that this hadith is defective for three reasons: One that this Umar Ibn Ibrahim is from Basra, and Ibn Ma’een authenticated him, but Abu Hatim Al-Razi said: He cannot be relied upon. But Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of Al-Mu’tamir from his father from Al-Hasan from Samurah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. And God knows best. Second that it has been narrated from Samurah himself, but it is not with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, as Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Abd Al-A’la told us, Al-Mu’tamir told us from his father, Bakr Ibn Abd God Ibn Sulayman Al-Taymi told us from Abu Al-Ala Ibn Al-Shakheer from Samurah Ibn Jundub, who said: Adam named his son Abd Al-Harith. Third that Al-Hasan himself interpreted the verse differently, so if he had this chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet from Samurah, he would not have deviated from it. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakee’ told us, Sahl bin Yusuf told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Al-Hasan: They made for Him partners in what He gave them. He said: This was with some of the people of religions and was not with Adam. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told us, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar, who said: Al-Hasan said: He meant by it the descendants of Adam and those who associated partners with God after him, meaning they made partners for Him in what He gave them. Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Sa'id told us on the authority of Qatada, who said: Al-Hasan used to say: They are the Jews and Christians, God gave them children and they became Jews and Christians. These are authentic chains of transmission on the authority of Al-Hasan, may God be pleased with him, that he interpreted the verse in this way, and it is one of the best interpretations and the most appropriate way to interpret the verse. If this hadith had been preserved in his possession from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he would not have deviated from it, nor would anyone else, especially with his fear of God and his piety. This indicates that it is attributed to the Companion, and it is possible that he received it from some of the People of the Book who believed among them, such as Ka'b or Wahb ibn Munabbih and others, as will be explained, God willing, except that we are innocent of the responsibility of the marfu' (upon him be peace) hadith, and God knows best. As for the narrations, Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yasar said on the authority of Dawud bin Al-Hussain on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Eve used to give birth to children for Adam, peace be upon him, and he would worship them for God and name them Abdullah and Ubaidullah and the like, and then death would befall them. Then Satan came to them and said: If you had named him with something other than what you named him, he would have lived. He said: So she gave birth to a man for him and he named him Abdul Harith. In this regard, God revealed His saying: “It is He who created you from one soul and created from it its mate that he might find tranquility in her. Then when he covered her, she conceived a light burden and passed by with it. But when it became heavy, they both cried out to God, their Lord, ‘If You should give us a good [child], we will surely be among the grateful.’ But when He gave them both a good [child], they ascribed to Him partners in what He had given them.” to the end of the verse. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying about Adam: “It is He who created you from one soul and created from it its mate that he might find tranquility in her. Then when he covered her, she conceived a light burden and passed by with it.” She doubted whether she was pregnant or not? So when she became heavy, they both called upon God, their Lord, [saying], ‘If You should give us a good child, we will surely be among the grateful.’ Then Satan came to them and said, Do you know what will be born to you? Or do you know whether it will be a beast or not? And he made falsehood seem good to them. Indeed, it is clear error. Before that, she had given birth to two boys who died. Then Satan said to them, If you do not name him by my name, he will not come out sound and will die as the first one died. So they named their son Abd al-Harith. This is what God the Most High said, But when He gave them both a good child, they ascribed to Him partners in what He had given them. Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak said on the authority of Sharik on the authority of Khasif on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, And when He gave them both a righteous woman, they ascribed to Him partners in what He had given them, he said: God Almighty said, “It is He who created you from one soul and created from it its mate that he might dwell in tranquility with her. But when he had covered her” Adam, she conceived, so Satan, may God curse him, came to them and said, “I am your companion who brought you out of Paradise. Either you obey me or I will make for him two camel horns and he will come out of your belly and split it open, or I will do this and I will do that,” frightening them. So they named him Abd Al-Harith, but they refused to obey him, so he came out dead. Then the second woman became pregnant, so he came to them again and said, “I am your companion who did what I did. Either you do that or I will do that,” frightening them. But they refused to obey him, so he came out dead. Then the third woman became pregnant, so he came to them again and mentioned it to them, and they were overcome by the love of a child, so they named him Abd Al-Harith. So that is what God Almighty said, They ascribed to Him partners in what He had given them, narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. This trace was received from Ibn Abbas from his companions, such as Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubair, and Ikrimah, and from the second class, Qatada, Al-Suddi, and more than one of the predecessors and a group of the successors, and from the interpreters of the later generations, groups that cannot be counted, and it seems - and God knows best - that its origin was taken from the People of the Book, for Ibn Abbas narrated it from Abi bin Kaab, as Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it: My father told us, Abu Al-Jamahir told us, Saeed told us, meaning Ibn Bashir, from Uqbah, from Qatada, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, from Abi bin Kaab, who said: When Eve became pregnant, Satan came to her and said to her: Will you obey me and your child will be safe, name him Abdul-Harith, but she did not do so, so he was born and died, then she became pregnant and he said to her the same thing but she did not do so, then she became pregnant for the third time, so he came to her and said: If you obey me, he will be safe, otherwise he will be an animal, so he feared them and they obeyed. These traces appear - and God knows best - to be traces of the People of the Book. It has been authenticated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said, If the People of the Book tell you something, do not believe them or disbelieve them. Then their reports are divided into three categories. Some of them we know to be authentic based on evidence from the Book of God or the Sunnah of His Messenger. Some of them we know to be false based on evidence to the contrary from the Book and the Sunnah as well. Some of them are silent, so it is the one permitted to narrate, based on his saying, peace be upon him, Narrate from the Children of Israel and there is no blame. This is the one that is neither believed nor disbelieved based on his saying, Do not believe them or disbelieve them. This trace is from the second or third category, and there is a problem with it. As for the one who narrated it from a Companion or a Follower, he sees it as being from the third category. As for us, we follow the school of thought of Al-Hasan Al-Basri, may God have mercy on him, in this, and that what is meant by this context is not Adam and Eve, but rather what is meant by that are the polytheists from his descendants. It is like a digression from mentioning a person to a species, like his saying, And We have certainly adorned the lowest heaven with lamps. The verse, and it is known that the lamps, which are the stars with which the heaven is adorned, are not the ones that… It is thrown away, but this is a digression from the person of the lamps to their type, and there are parallels to this in the Qur’an, and God knows best.

In this regard, God revealed His saying: “It is He who created you from one soul and created from it its mate that he might find tranquility in her. Then when he covered her, she conceived a light burden and passed by with it. But when it became heavy, they both cried out to God, their Lord, ‘If You should give us a good [child], we will surely be among the grateful.’ But when He gave them both a good [child], they ascribed to Him partners in what He had given them.” to the end of the verse. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying about Adam: “It is He who created you from one soul and created from it its mate that he might find tranquility in her. Then when he covered her, she conceived a light burden and passed by with it.” She doubted whether she was pregnant or not? So when she became heavy, they both called upon God, their Lord, [saying], ‘If You should give us a good child, we will surely be among the grateful.’ Then Satan came to them and said, Do you know what will be born to you? Or do you know whether it will be a beast or not? And he made falsehood seem good to them. Indeed, it is clear error. Before that, she had given birth to two boys who died. Then Satan said to them, If you do not name him by my name, he will not come out sound and will die as the first one died. So they named their son Abd al-Harith. This is what God the Most High said, But when He gave them both a good child, they ascribed to Him partners in what He had given them. Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak said on the authority of Sharik on the authority of Khasif on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, And when He gave them both a righteous woman, they ascribed to Him partners in what He had given them, he said: God Almighty said, “It is He who created you from one soul and created from it its mate that he might dwell in tranquility with her. But when he had covered her” Adam, she conceived, so Satan, may God curse him, came to them and said, “I am your companion who brought you out of Paradise. Either you obey me or I will make for him two camel horns and he will come out of your belly and split it open, or I will do this and I will do that,” frightening them. So they named him Abd Al-Harith, but they refused to obey him, so he came out dead. Then the second woman became pregnant, so he came to them again and said, “I am your companion who did what I did. Either you do that or I will do that,” frightening them. But they refused to obey him, so he came out dead. Then the third woman became pregnant, so he came to them again and mentioned it to them, and they were overcome by the love of a child, so they named him Abd Al-Harith. So that is what God Almighty said, They ascribed to Him partners in what He had given them, narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. This trace was received from Ibn Abbas from his companions, such as Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubair, and Ikrimah, and from the second class, Qatada, Al-Suddi, and more than one of the predecessors and a group of the successors, and from the interpreters of the later generations, groups that cannot be counted, and it seems - and God knows best - that its origin was taken from the People of the Book, for Ibn Abbas narrated it from Abi bin Kaab, as Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it: My father told us, Abu Al-Jamahir told us, Saeed told us, meaning Ibn Bashir, from Uqbah, from Qatada, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, from Abi bin Kaab, who said: When Eve became pregnant, Satan came to her and said to her: Will you obey me and your child will be safe, name him Abdul-Harith, but she did not do so, so he was born and died, then she became pregnant and he said to her the same thing but she did not do so, then she became pregnant for the third time, so he came to her and said: If you obey me, he will be safe, otherwise he will be an animal, so he feared them and they obeyed. These traces appear - and God knows best - to be traces of the People of the Book. It has been authenticated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said, If the People of the Book tell you something, do not believe them or disbelieve them. Then their reports are divided into three categories. Some of them we know to be authentic based on evidence from the Book of God or the Sunnah of His Messenger. Some of them we know to be false based on evidence to the contrary from the Book and the Sunnah as well. Some of them are silent, so it is the one permitted to narrate, based on his saying, peace be upon him, Narrate from the Children of Israel and there is no blame. This is the one that is neither believed nor disbelieved based on his saying, Do not believe them or disbelieve them. This trace is from the second or third category, and there is a problem with it. As for the one who narrated it from a Companion or a Follower, he sees it as being from the third category. As for us, we follow the school of thought of Al-Hasan Al-Basri, may God have mercy on him, in this, and that what is meant by this context is not Adam and Eve, but rather what is meant by that are the polytheists from his descendants. It is like a digression from mentioning a person to a species, like his saying, And We have certainly adorned the lowest heaven with lamps. The verse, and it is known that the lamps, which are the stars with which the heaven is adorned, are not the ones that… It is thrown away, but this is a digression from the person of the lamps to their type, and there are parallels to this in the Qur’an, and God knows best.
7:191: This is a denial from God to the polytheists who worshipped other than God, from rivals, idols and statues, which are created by God, are man-made and manufactured, do not possess any command, do not harm or benefit, do not see or support their worshippers, rather they are inanimate and do not move, do not hear or see, and their worshippers are more perfect than them in their hearing, sight and strength, and for this reason He said: Do they associate with Him that which does not create anything and they are created? That is, do they associate with Him from the deities that do not create anything and are not able to do so, as God the Almighty said: "O mankind, an example is presented, so listen to it. Indeed, those you invoke besides God could never create a fly, even if they banded together for that purpose. And if the fly should steal from them something, they could not rescue it from it. Weak are the pursuer and the pursued. They do not esteem God with His true esteem. Indeed, God is Powerful and Exalted in Might." God the Almighty informed us that if all their gods banded together, they would not be able to create a fly. Rather, if the fly stole from them something of insignificant food and flew away, they would not be able to rescue it from it. So who is this in His description? How can he be worshipped to be provided for and supported? That is why God Almighty said: He does not create anything, but they are created. That is, they are created and made, as Al-Khalil said: Do you worship what you carve? verse. Then the Almighty said: And they are not able to help them meaning their worshippers nor can they help themselves meaning they are not able to help themselves from those who want to harm them, just as Abraham, peace be upon him, used to break the idols of his people and humiliate them to the utmost degree, as the Almighty informed us about in His statement: So he struck them with his right hand and the Almighty said: So he made them into fragments, except for one of their biggest, that perhaps they would return to it and just as Muadh ibn Amr ibn al-Jamuh and Muadh ibn Jabal, may God be pleased with them, were two young men who had converted to Islam when the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, came to Medina. They used to attack the idols of the polytheists at night, break them, destroy them, and use them as firewood for the widows so that their people would take heed and see for themselves. Amr ibn al-Jamuh, who was a leader among his people, had an idol that he worshipped and perfumed. They used to come at night, turn it over his head, and smear it with dung. Then Amr ibn al-Jamuh would come and see what had been done to it, so he would wash it, perfume it, and put it on his head. He had a sword and said to him: Win, then they did the same thing again, and he did the same thing again, until they took him once and paired him with a dead dog, and lowered him by a rope into a well there, so when Amr ibn al-Jamuh came and saw that, he looked and knew that what he was on of religion was false, and he said: By God, if you were a god, you and the dog would not be in the same horn. Then he converted to Islam and his conversion was good, and he was killed as a martyr on the day of Uhud, may God be pleased with him and make Paradise his abode. His saying, And if you call them to guidance, they will not follow you, the verse, means that these idols do not hear the call of those who call upon them, and it is the same to them who calls upon them and who pushes them aside, as Abraham said, O my father, why do you worship that which does not hear and does not see and does not avail you at all? Then God Almighty mentioned that they are slaves like their worshippers, that is, creatures like them. Rather, people are more perfect than them because they hear, see and strike, while those do not do any of that. His saying, Say, ‘Call upon your partners,’ the verse, means seek their help against me, do not delay me for the blink of an eye, and strive your best. Indeed, my ally is God, who has sent down the Book, and He is the Guardian of the righteous, meaning God is sufficient for me and He is my supporter, and upon Him I rely and to Him I turn, and He is my guardian in this world and the hereafter, and He is the guardian of every righteous person after me. This is like what Hud, peace be upon him, said when his people said to him, We say nothing except that some of our gods have afflicted you with evil. He said, Indeed, I bear witness. God, and bear witness that I am innocent of what you associate with Him. So plot against me all together and then give me no respite. Indeed, I have put my trust in God, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature but that He holds it by the forelock. Indeed, my Lord is on a straight path. And like the words of Abraham, “Have you seen what you used to worship? You and your forefathers of old. Indeed, they are an enemy to me, except for the Lord of the worlds, Who created me and He guides me.” The verses, and like his words to his father and his people, “Indeed, I am innocent of what you worship. Except for He who created me, for He will guide me.” And He made it a word remaining among his descendants that perhaps they would return. And His saying, And those you call upon besides Him, to the end of the verse, confirms what came before, except that it is in the form of address, which is in the form of the third person. That is why He said, They are not able to help you, nor are they able to help themselves. And His saying, “And if you call them to guidance, they do not hear. And you see them looking at you, but they do not see.” Like His saying, If you call upon them, they do not hear your call. And His saying, And you see them looking at you, but they do not see, He only said, looking at you, meaning they meet you with visualized eyes as if they were watching, even though they are inanimate. That is why He treated them as if they were rational, because they are in the form of a human being, and you see them looking at you, so He expressed it with the pronoun of rational being. Al-Suddi said: What is meant by this are the polytheists. Something similar was narrated from Mujahid, but the first is better, and it is the choice of Ibn Jarir, and Qatada said the same.
