7:199: Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas that his statement, Take what is easy means take what you are forgiven from their money and whatever they bring you, take it. This was before the revelation of Bara'ah with the obligatory charity and its details and what the charity ends with, said Al-Suddi. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Take what is easy means spend the surplus. Saeed bin Jubair said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Take what is easy means the surplus. Abdur-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said regarding his statement, Take what is easy, God commanded him to forgive and pardon the polytheists for ten years, then He commanded him to be harsh with them. Ibn Jarir chose this statement. More than one person said on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement, Take what is easy, he said: from the morals and actions of people without spying. Hisham bin Urwa said on the authority of his father: God commanded the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to forgive people’s behavior. In another narration, he said: Take what you have been forgiven of from their behavior. In Sahih al-Bukhari, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of his father Urwa, on the authority of his brother Abdullah bin al-Zubayr, he said: It was only revealed: Take forgiveness from people’s behavior. In another narration, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Umar, and in another narration, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, that they both said the same for you. And God knows best. In the narration of Saeed bin Mansour, on the authority of Abu Muawiyah, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Wahb bin Kaysan, on the authority of Abu Al-Zubayr: Take forgiveness. He said: It is from the morals of people, and by God, I will take it from them as long as I keep company with them. This is the most famous of the sayings, and what is supported by what was narrated by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim, both of them: Yunus told us, Sufyan told us, he is Ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of my mother, he said: When God Almighty revealed to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Take forgiveness, enjoin what is right, and turn away from the ignorant, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What is this, O Gabriel? He said: God has commanded you to forgive those who wrong you, give to those who deprive you, and connect with those who cut you off. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it in writing on the authority of Abu Yazid Al-Qaratisi, on the authority of Asbagh bin Al-Faraj, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of my mother, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, something similar. This is a mursal in any case, and corroborating evidence has been narrated for it from other sources. It has been narrated with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the authority of Jabir and Qais bin Saad bin Ubadah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Ibn Mardawayh attributed them both to him. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Al-Mughira told us, Muadh bin Rifa’ah told us, Ali bin Yazid told me, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abi Umamah Al-Bahili, on the authority of Uqbah bin Amir, may God be pleased with him, who said: I met the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I began by taking his hand and saying: O Messenger of God, tell me about the best deeds. He said: O Uqbah, connect with those who cut you off, give to those who deprive you, and turn away from those who wrong you. Al-Tirmidhi narrated something similar on the authority of Ubayd God bin Zahr on the authority of Ali bin Yazid, and he said: It is good. I said: But Ali bin Yazid and his sheikh Al-Qasim Abu Abd Al-Rahman are weak. Al-Bukhari said: His saying, Accept forgiveness, enjoin what is right, and turn away from the ignorant. Al-Aref means what is known. Abu Al-Yaman told us, Shuaib told us on the authority of Al-Zuhri, Ubaidullah bin Abdullah bin Utbah told me that Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: Uyaynah bin Hisn bin Hudhayfah came and stayed with his nephew Al-Hurr bin Qays, and he was one of the men whom Umar brought close to him. The reciters were the companions of Umar’s gatherings and consultations, whether they were old or young. Uyaynah said to his nephew: O nephew, you have a position with this emir, so ask permission for me to see him. He said: I will ask permission for you to see him. Ibn Abbas said: Al-Hurr asked permission for Uyaynah, and Umar gave him permission. When he entered upon him, he said: This is it, O son of Al-Khattab. By God, you do not give us enough and you do not judge between us with justice. Umar became angry until he was about to smite him, but Al-Hurr said to him: O Commander of the Faithful, God Almighty said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Accept forgiveness, enjoin what is right, and turn away from the ignorant, and this is one of the ignorant. By God, Umar did not go beyond it when he recited it to him, and he was standing at The Book of God Almighty, and it was narrated exclusively by Al-Bukhari. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus bin Abdul A’la narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, Malik bin Anas narrated to me, on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Nafi’, that Salim bin Abdullah bin Umar passed by a caravan of the people of Ash-Sham, and it had a bell, so he said: This is forbidden. They said: We know this better than you. Only a large bell is disliked, but as for something like this, there is nothing wrong with it. Salim remained silent and said: And turn away from the ignorant. Al-Bukhari’s statement: The known custom, was stated by Urwah bin Az-Zubayr, As-Suddi, Qatadah, Ibn Jarir, and others. Ibn Jarir narrated that it is said: I gave him a known and a known person, all of which means the known. He said: And God commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to command His servants to do good, and this includes all acts of obedience and to turn away from the ignorant. And even though it was a command to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, it is a discipline for His creation to tolerate those who wronged them and transgressed against them, not to turn away from those who were ignorant of the right that is due from God, nor to forgive those who disbelieved in God and were ignorant of His Oneness, and he is at war with the Muslims. Saeed bin Abi Aruba said on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, Adopt forgiveness, enjoin what is right, and turn away from the ignorant, he said: These are morals that God commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to do and guided him to them. Some of the wise men took this meaning and cast it in two verses that contain alliteration, and he said: Take forgiveness and enjoin what is right as you were commanded and turn away from the ignorant. And in speech for all people, it is preferable for the ignorant to be soft Some scholars said: People are of two types: a good man, so take what he has forgiven you of his goodness and do not burden him beyond his capacity or what embarrasses him. As for a bad man, then order him to do good. If he persists in his misguidance and is stubborn with you and continues in his ignorance, then turn away from him, for perhaps that will turn back his plot, as God the Almighty said: “Repel evil with that which is best. We know best what they describe. And say, ‘My Lord, I seek refuge in You from the insinuations of the devils. And I seek refuge in You, my Lord, lest they be present.’” And God the Almighty said: “And not equal are the good deed and the evil. Repel evil with that which is best, and thereupon he between whom and you there was enmity will become as though he was a devoted friend. And none is granted it except those who are patient, and none is granted it except one having great good fortune.” That is, this commandment: “But if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan, then seek refuge in God. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.” And He also said in this noble surah: “But if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan, then seek refuge in God. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.” So these three verses are in Al-A’raf, Al-Mu’minoon, and Ha-Mim As-Sajdah, and there is no fourth, for He God the Almighty, guides in them to treat the disobedient among mankind with kindness and in the best manner, for that will prevent him from his rebellion, by His permission, the Almighty. For this reason, He said, Then he between whom and you there was enmity will become as though he was a devoted friend. Then God the Almighty guides to seek refuge in Him from the devil of the jinn, for if kindness will not prevent him from you, and he only wants your destruction and ruin completely, then he is a clear enemy to you and to your father before you. Ibn Jarir said in his interpretation of His statement, But if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan, or if Satan angers you with an anger that prevents you from turning away from the ignorant person and makes you punish him, Then seek refuge in God, meaning: seek refuge in God from his suggestion, For He is All-Hearing, All-Knowing, He hears the ignorance of the ignorant person towards you and seeking refuge in Him from his suggestion and other than that from the speech of His creation, nothing of it is hidden from Him, He knows how to remove from you the suggestion of Satan and other matters of His creation. Abdul Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said: When the verse Adopt forgiveness, enjoin what is right, and turn away from the ignorant was revealed, he said: O Lord, what about anger? So God revealed: “But if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan, then seek refuge in God. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.” I said: The hadith of the two men who insulted each other in the presence of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was mentioned before, and one of them became so angry that his nose was rolling with anger. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “I know a word that if he said it, what he feels would go away. I seek refuge in God from Satan, the accursed.” It was said to him, and he said: I have no madness. The origin of evil is corruption, either through anger or something else. God the Most High said: “And tell My servants to say that which is best. Indeed, Satan induces dissension among them.” Seeking refuge is seeking refuge, support, and protection from evil. As for seeking refuge, it is in seeking good, as Abu Tayyib al-Mutanabbi said in his poetry: O He in Whom I seek refuge in what I hope for and in Whom I seek refuge from what I fear. People do not mend a bone that you break, nor do they weaken a bone that you mend. We have presented the hadiths of seeking refuge at the beginning of the interpretation, which makes it unnecessary to repeat them here.
7:200: Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas that his statement, Take what is easy means take what you are forgiven from their money and whatever they bring you, take it. This was before the revelation of Bara'ah with the obligatory charity and its details and what the charity ends with, said Al-Suddi. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Take what is easy means spend the surplus. Saeed bin Jubair said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Take what is easy means the surplus. Abdur-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said regarding his statement, Take what is easy, God commanded him to forgive and pardon the polytheists for ten years, then He commanded him to be harsh with them. Ibn Jarir chose this statement. More than one person said on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement, Take what is easy, he said: from the morals and actions of people without spying. Hisham bin Urwa said on the authority of his father: God commanded the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to forgive people’s behavior. In another narration, he said: Take what you have been forgiven of from their behavior. In Sahih al-Bukhari, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of his father Urwa, on the authority of his brother Abdullah bin al-Zubayr, he said: It was only revealed: Take forgiveness from people’s behavior. In another narration, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Umar, and in another narration, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, that they both said the same for you. And God knows best. In the narration of Saeed bin Mansour, on the authority of Abu Muawiyah, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Wahb bin Kaysan, on the authority of Abu Al-Zubayr: Take forgiveness. He said: It is from the morals of people, and by God, I will take it from them as long as I keep company with them. This is the most famous of the sayings, and what is supported by what was narrated by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim, both of them: Yunus told us, Sufyan told us, he is Ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of my mother, he said: When God Almighty revealed to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Take forgiveness, enjoin what is right, and turn away from the ignorant, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What is this, O Gabriel? He said: God has commanded you to forgive those who wrong you, give to those who deprive you, and connect with those who cut you off. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it in writing on the authority of Abu Yazid Al-Qaratisi, on the authority of Asbagh bin Al-Faraj, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of my mother, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, something similar. This is a mursal in any case, and corroborating evidence has been narrated for it from other sources. It has been narrated with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the authority of Jabir and Qais bin Saad bin Ubadah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Ibn Mardawayh attributed them both to him. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Al-Mughira told us, Muadh bin Rifa’ah told us, Ali bin Yazid told me, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abi Umamah Al-Bahili, on the authority of Uqbah bin Amir, may God be pleased with him, who said: I met the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I began by taking his hand and saying: O Messenger of God, tell me about the best deeds. He said: O Uqbah, connect with those who cut you off, give to those who deprive you, and turn away from those who wrong you. Al-Tirmidhi narrated something similar on the authority of Ubayd God bin Zahr on the authority of Ali bin Yazid, and he said: It is good. I said: But Ali bin Yazid and his sheikh Al-Qasim Abu Abd Al-Rahman are weak. Al-Bukhari said: His saying, Accept forgiveness, enjoin what is right, and turn away from the ignorant. Al-Aref means what is known. Abu Al-Yaman told us, Shuaib told us on the authority of Al-Zuhri, Ubaidullah bin Abdullah bin Utbah told me that Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: Uyaynah bin Hisn bin Hudhayfah came and stayed with his nephew Al-Hurr bin Qays, and he was one of the men whom Umar brought close to him. The reciters were the companions of Umar’s gatherings and consultations, whether they were old or young. Uyaynah said to his nephew: O nephew, you have a position with this emir, so ask permission for me to see him. He said: I will ask permission for you to see him. Ibn Abbas said: Al-Hurr asked permission for Uyaynah, and Umar gave him permission. When he entered upon him, he said: This is it, O son of Al-Khattab. By God, you do not give us enough and you do not judge between us with justice. Umar became angry until he was about to smite him, but Al-Hurr said to him: O Commander of the Faithful, God Almighty said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Accept forgiveness, enjoin what is right, and turn away from the ignorant, and this is one of the ignorant. By God, Umar did not go beyond it when he recited it to him, and he was standing at The Book of God Almighty, and it was narrated exclusively by Al-Bukhari. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus bin Abdul A’la narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, Malik bin Anas narrated to me, on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Nafi’, that Salim bin Abdullah bin Umar passed by a caravan of the people of Ash-Sham, and it had a bell, so he said: This is forbidden. They said: We know this better than you. Only a large bell is disliked, but as for something like this, there is nothing wrong with it. Salim remained silent and said: And turn away from the ignorant. Al-Bukhari’s statement: The known custom, was stated by Urwah bin Az-Zubayr, As-Suddi, Qatadah, Ibn Jarir, and others. Ibn Jarir narrated that it is said: I gave him a known and a known person, all of which means the known. He said: And God commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to command His servants to do good, and this includes all acts of obedience and to turn away from the ignorant. And even though it was a command to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, it is a discipline for His creation to tolerate those who wronged them and transgressed against them, not to turn away from those who were ignorant of the right that is due from God, nor to forgive those who disbelieved in God and were ignorant of His Oneness, and he is at war with the Muslims. Saeed bin Abi Aruba said on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, Adopt forgiveness, enjoin what is right, and turn away from the ignorant, he said: These are morals that God commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to do and guided him to them. Some of the wise men took this meaning and cast it in two verses that contain alliteration, and he said: Take forgiveness and enjoin what is right as you were commanded and turn away from the ignorant. And in speech for all people, it is preferable for the ignorant to be soft Some scholars said: People are of two types: a good man, so take what he has forgiven you of his goodness and do not burden him beyond his capacity or what embarrasses him. As for a bad man, then order him to do good. If he persists in his misguidance and is stubborn with you and continues in his ignorance, then turn away from him, for perhaps that will turn back his plot, as God the Almighty said: “Repel evil with that which is best. We know best what they describe. And say, ‘My Lord, I seek refuge in You from the insinuations of the devils. And I seek refuge in You, my Lord, lest they be present.’” And God the Almighty said: “And not equal are the good deed and the evil. Repel evil with that which is best, and thereupon he between whom and you there was enmity will become as though he was a devoted friend. And none is granted it except those who are patient, and none is granted it except one having great good fortune.” That is, this commandment: “But if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan, then seek refuge in God. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.” And He also said in this noble surah: “But if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan, then seek refuge in God. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.” So these three verses are in Al-A’raf, Al-Mu’minoon, and Ha-Mim As-Sajdah, and there is no fourth, for He God the Almighty, guides in them to treat the disobedient among mankind with kindness and in the best manner, for that will prevent him from his rebellion, by His permission, the Almighty. For this reason, He said, Then he between whom and you there was enmity will become as though he was a devoted friend. Then God the Almighty guides to seek refuge in Him from the devil of the jinn, for if kindness will not prevent him from you, and he only wants your destruction and ruin completely, then he is a clear enemy to you and to your father before you. Ibn Jarir said in his interpretation of His statement, But if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan, or if Satan angers you with an anger that prevents you from turning away from the ignorant person and makes you punish him, Then seek refuge in God, meaning: seek refuge in God from his suggestion, For He is All-Hearing, All-Knowing, He hears the ignorance of the ignorant person towards you and seeking refuge in Him from his suggestion and other than that from the speech of His creation, nothing of it is hidden from Him, He knows how to remove from you the suggestion of Satan and other matters of His creation. Abdul Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said: When the verse Adopt forgiveness, enjoin what is right, and turn away from the ignorant was revealed, he said: O Lord, what about anger? So God revealed: “But if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan, then seek refuge in God. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.” I said: The hadith of the two men who insulted each other in the presence of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was mentioned before, and one of them became so angry that his nose was rolling with anger. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “I know a word that if he said it, what he feels would go away. I seek refuge in God from Satan, the accursed.” It was said to him, and he said: I have no madness. The origin of evil is corruption, either through anger or something else. God the Most High said: “And tell My servants to say that which is best. Indeed, Satan induces dissension among them.” Seeking refuge is seeking refuge, support, and protection from evil. As for seeking refuge, it is in seeking good, as Abu Tayyib al-Mutanabbi said in his poetry: O He in Whom I seek refuge in what I hope for and in Whom I seek refuge from what I fear. People do not mend a bone that you break, nor do they weaken a bone that you mend. We have presented the hadiths of seeking refuge at the beginning of the interpretation, which makes it unnecessary to repeat them here.
7:201: The Almighty tells us about the righteous among His servants who obeyed Him in what He commanded and left what He forbade them from, that if a specter touches them means they are afflicted by it. Others read it as ta’if, and a hadith has been narrated about it. They are two well-known readings. It was said that they have one meaning, and it was said that there is a difference between them. Some of them interpreted it as anger, and some of them interpreted it as the devil’s touch with epilepsy and the like, and some of them interpreted it as the thought of sin, and some of them interpreted it as the occurrence of sin. His saying remember means God’s punishment, His abundant reward, His promise, and His threat, so they repented, turned back, sought refuge in God, and returned to Him soon after. Then behold, they see means they have become upright and recovered from what they were in. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh mentioned here the hadith of Muhammad bin Amr on the authority of Abu Salamah on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: A woman came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and she was possessed by a ghost and said: O Messenger of God, pray to God to heal me. He said: If you wish, I will pray to God and He will heal you, and if you wish, be patient and there will be no reckoning upon you. She said: Rather, I will be patient and there will be no reckoning upon me. More than one of the people of Sunnah narrated it, and they have it. She said: O Messenger of God, I suffer from epilepsy and I am uncovered, so pray to God to heal me. He said: If you wish, I will pray to God to heal you, and if you wish, be patient and you will have Paradise. She said: Rather, I will be patient and I will have Paradise, but pray to God that I not be uncovered. So he prayed for her and she was not uncovered. Al-Hakim included it in his Mustadrak, and he said: It is authentic according to the conditions of Muslim, but they did not include it. Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir mentioned in the biography of Amr bin Jami’ in his history that a young man was worshipping in the mosque, and a woman fell in love with him and invited him to herself, and she kept on at him until he almost entered the house with her, so he mentioned this verse: Indeed, those who fear God - when an impulse touches them from Satan, they remember [God] and at once they have insight. So he fell unconscious, then he came to and repeated it, and he died. Omar came and offered his condolences to his father, who had been buried at night, so he went and prayed at his grave with those with him, then Omar called out to him and said: O young man, And for him who fears standing before his Lord are two Gardens. So the young man answered him from inside the grave: O Omar, my Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, has given them to me in Paradise twice. And the Almighty’s saying: And their brothers support them means the brothers of the devils among mankind, like His saying: Indeed, the wasteful are brothers of the devils and they are their followers and listeners, those who accept their commands and support them in error, meaning the devils help them in sins and make them easy for them and make them seem good to them. Ibn Kathir said: The extension of increase means that they increase them in error, meaning ignorance and foolishness. Then they do not stop. It was said that its meaning is that the devils extend the people and do not stop in their actions with that, as Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas in his statement: And their brothers extend them in error and then do not stop. He said: Neither do the people stop what they do, nor do the devils hold back from them. It was said that its meaning is as Al-Awfi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas in his statement: They extend them in error and then do not stop. He said: They are the jinn who inspire their human allies and then do not stop. He said: They do not get tired. And Al-Suddi and others said the same, that the devils mean that they extend their human allies and do not get tired of supporting them in evil, because that is their nature and disposition. They do not stop. They do not slacken in it nor do they cease from it, as God the Almighty said: Have you not seen that We have sent the devils upon the disbelievers, inciting them with [excessive] incitement? Ibn Abbas and others said: They incite them to sins with incitement.

7:203: Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the Almighty’s statement: They said, ‘Why did you not choose it?’ He said: Why did you not receive it? And he said another time: Why did you not create it and establish it? Ibn Jarir said on the authority of Abdullah bin Kathir on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And when you do not bring them a sign, they say, ‘Why did you not choose it?’ He said: Why did you not require it? They said: You extract it from yourself. And this is what Qatada, As-Suddi, and Abd Al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said, and Ibn Jarir chose it. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Why did you not choose it? He said: I received it from God Almighty. Ad-Dahhak said: Why did you not choose it? He said: Why did you not take it and bring it from the sky? The meaning of the Almighty’s saying: And if you do not bring them a sign is a miracle and a miracle, like the Almighty’s saying: If We will, We can send down upon them from the sky a sign, and their necks would remain humbled to it. They said to the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace: Why do you not exert yourself in seeking signs from God so that we may see them and believe in them? God Almighty said to him: Say, ‘I only follow what is revealed to me from my Lord.’ That is, I do not precede Him in anything, but rather I follow what He has commanded me to do, so I comply with what He reveals to me. If He sends a sign, I accept it, and if He prevents it, I do not ask Him for it in the first place unless He gives me permission to do so, for He is All-Wise, All-Knowing. Then He guided them to the fact that this Qur’an is the greatest of miracles, the clearest of indications, and the truest of arguments and proofs, so He said: This is insight from your Lord and guidance and mercy for a people who believe.
7:204: When the Almighty mentioned that the Qur’an is insight for the people and guidance and mercy, the Almighty commanded us to listen to it when it is recited out of respect and reverence for it, not as the polytheistic infidels of Quraysh used to do when they said, Do not listen to this Qur’an and speak noisily during it, the verse. However, this is confirmed in the obligatory prayer when the imam recites loudly, as Muslim narrated in his Sahih from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash’ari, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, The imam is only appointed to be followed, so when he says takbir, then say takbir, and when he recites, then listen. And the people of Sunan narrated it likewise from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah as well, and Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj also authenticated it, but he did not include it in his book. Ibrahim ibn Muslim al-Hijri said on the authority of Abu ‘Iyad on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: They used to talk during the prayer, so when this verse was revealed, And when the Qur’an is recited, then listen to it, and the other verse, they were commanded to listen. Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Abu Bakr bin Ayyash told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Al-Musayyab bin Rafi’, who said: Ibn Mas’ud said: We used to greet one another during prayer, then the Qur’an came: And when the Qur’an is recited, listen to it and be silent that you may receive mercy. He also said: Abu Kurayb told us, Al-Muharibi told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, on the authority of Bashir bin Jabir, who said: Ibn Mas’ud prayed and heard some people reciting with the imam, so when he finished he said: Is it not time for you to understand, is it not time for you to reason? And when the Qur’an is recited, listen to it and be silent, as God has commanded you. He said: Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, Hafs told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, who said: This verse was revealed about a young man from the Ansar. Whenever the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) recited something, he would recite it, then the verse was revealed: And when the Qur’an is recited, listen to it and be silent. Imam Ahmad and the Sunan scholars narrated from the hadith of Az-Zuhri on the authority of Abu Ukaymah Al-Laythi on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) finished a prayer in which he had recited aloud and said, Did any of you recite with me just now? A man said, Yes, O Messenger of God. He said, I say, why should I dispute with the Qur’an? The people stopped reciting with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in the prayers in which he had recited aloud when they heard that from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). At-Tirmidhi said: This is a hasan hadith, and Abu Hatim Al-Razi authenticated it. Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak said on the authority of Yunus on the authority of Al-Zuhri: He said: No one behind the Imam should recite in what the Imam recites aloud. The Imam’s recitation is sufficient for them even if they do not hear his voice, but they should recite in secret to themselves in what he does not recite aloud, and it is not permissible for anyone behind him to recite with him in what he recites aloud, secretly or publicly, because God Almighty said: And when the Qur’an is recited, listen to it and be silent that you may receive mercy. I said: This is the doctrine of a group of scholars that the follower is not required in the prayer recited aloud to recite what the Imam recites aloud, neither Al-Fatihah nor anything else. This is one of the two opinions of the Shafi’is, and it is the old one like the doctrine of Malik and a narration from Ahmad bin Hanbal, for what we mentioned from the previous evidence. He said in the new one: He recites Al-Fatihah only during the silences of the Imam, and this is the opinion of a group of the Companions and the Followers and those who came after them. Abu Hanifa and Ahmad bin Hanbal said: The follower is not required to recite at all in the secret or the aloud prayers, based on what was mentioned in the hadith: Whoever has an Imam, his recitation is a recitation for him. This hadith was narrated by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad on the authority of Jabir. It is attributed to the Prophet, and it is in the Muwatta of Malik on the authority of Wahb bin Kaysan on the authority of Jabir, and this is more authentic. This issue is discussed in detail in other places, and Imam Abu Abdullah al-Bukhari devoted a separate book to it, and he chose the obligation of reading behind the imam in both silent and audible prayers, and God knows best. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, And when the Qur’an is recited, listen to it and be silent, meaning in the obligatory prayer. This was also narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Mughaffal. Ibn Jarir said: Hamid bin Mas’adah told us, Bishr bin al-Mufaddal told us, al-Jariri told us on the authority of Talhah bin Ubaidullah bin Kuraiz, who said: I saw Ubaid bin Umair and Ata bin Abi Rabah talking, and the narrator was narrating, so I said: Do you not listen to the remembrance and deserve what is promised? He said: They looked at me and then returned to their conversation. He said: I repeated it and they looked at me and returned to their conversation. He said: I repeated it a third time. He said: They looked at me and said: That is only in prayer. And when the Qur’an is recited, listen to it and be silent, and this was also said by Sufyan al-Thawri on the authority of Abu Hisham Ismail bin Katheer on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement, And when the Qur’an is recited, listen to it and be silent, he said: In prayer. This was also narrated by more than one person on the authority of Mujahid. Abdul Razzaq said on the authority of Al-Thawri on the authority of Laith on the authority of Mujahid, who said: There is no problem if a man recites outside of prayer and speaks. And this is what Saeed bin Jubair, Al-Dahhak, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Qatadah, Al-Sha’bi, Al-Suddi, and Abdul Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said: What is meant by that is during prayer. Shu'bah said on the authority of Mansur: I heard Ibrahim bin Abi Hamza narrating that he heard Mujahid say about this verse: And when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and be silent. He said: In the prayer and the sermon on Friday. Ibn Jurayj narrated something similar on the authority of Ata'. Hisham said on the authority of Ar-Rabi' bin Subaih on the authority of Al-Hasan who said: In the prayer and when remembering God. Ibn Al-Mubarak said on the authority of Baqiyyah: I heard Thabit bin Ajlan say: I heard Saeed bin Jubair say about His statement: And when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and be silent. He said: Listening is on the Day of Sacrifice, the Day of Fitr, and on Friday and in what the imam recites aloud in the prayer. This is the choice of Ibn Jarir that what is meant by that is listening in the prayer and in the sermon, as came in the hadiths about the command to listen behind the imam and during the sermon. Abd Al-Razzaq said on the authority of Ath-Thawri on the authority of Laith on the authority of Mujahid that he disliked that if the imam passed by a verse of fear or a verse of mercy, anyone behind him should say anything. He said: Silence. Mubarak bin Fadalah said on the authority of Al-Hasan: If you sit for the Qur'an, then listen to it. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Saeed, a client of Banu Hashim, told us, Ibad bin Maysarah told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever listens to a verse from the Book of God, a double good deed will be written for him, and whoever recites it, it will be a light for him on the Day of Resurrection. This was reported only by Imam Ahmad, may God Almighty have mercy on him.
7:205: God the Almighty commands us to remember Him often at the beginning and end of the day, just as He commanded us to worship Him at these two times in His statement: And glorify the praises of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting. This was before the five daily prayers were made obligatory on the Night of the Isra’, and this verse is Meccan. He said here: in the morning, which is the beginning of the day, and asl is the plural of asil, just as ayman is the plural of yameen. As for His statement, in humility and fear, it means remember your Lord in your soul with desire and fear and in speech, not out loud. That is why He said, and without out loud speech. Thus, it is preferable that the remembrance not be a call and that it be loud and eloquent. That is why when they asked the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), they said: Is our Lord near so that we may confide in Him, or is He far so that we may call out to Him? So God the Almighty revealed: “And when My servants ask you concerning Me - indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me.” In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari may God be pleased with him, he said: The people raised their voices in supplication during some journeys, so the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to them: "O people, be gentle with yourselves, for you are not calling upon one who is deaf or absent. Indeed, the One You are calling upon is All-Hearing, Near, Nearer to each one of you than the neck of his mount." This verse may be intended as in the words of God the Almighty: And do not recite your prayer aloud, nor in a low voice, but seek a way between that. For when the polytheists heard the Qur'an, they would curse it, and curse the One Who revealed it, and curse the One Who brought it. So God the Almighty commanded him not to recite it aloud so that the polytheists would not harm him, and not to recite it in a low voice from his companions so that they would not hear him, and to take a way between speaking aloud and whispering. This is what he said about this noble verse: And do not recite aloud in the mornings and the evenings, and do not be among the heedless. Ibn Jarir and before him Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam claimed that what is meant by it is an order to the listener of the Qur'an while listening to remembrance in this manner. This is far-fetched and contradicts the listening that is commanded. Then what is meant by that is in prayer as mentioned above, or in prayer and the sermon, and it is known that listening in that case is better than remembrance with the tongue, whether it is secretly or aloud. So what they said was not followed in, rather what is meant is to encourage frequent remembrance from the servants in the morning and evening, lest they be among the heedless. For this reason, He praised the angels who glorify Him night and day without slackening, as He said, Indeed, those who are with your Lord are not too proud to worship Him 1:13. Rather, He mentioned this to them so that they might be followed in their frequent obedience and worship. For this reason, He prescribed prostration for us here when He mentioned their prostration to God Almighty, as came in the hadith, Do you not line up as the angels line up before their Lord, completing the rows, first to the next, and standing close together in the row? This is the first prostration in the Qur’an from which it is prescribed for its reciter and listener to prostrate by consensus. It was mentioned in a hadith narrated by Ibn Majah on the authority of Abu al-Darda’ on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he counted it among the prostrations of the Qur’an.
